## ENGINE-THROTTLE-EVENT-STEP: a throttle that settles inside one recorder step replays up to 0.05 off [FILED 2026-11-23 from the ghost-fx-3 air flight `2026-11-23_1201`; OPEN; low (recorded data is immutable)]

What: the recorder writes an EngineThrottle event only when the throttle has moved more than 0.05 since the last one (`FlightRecorder.EngineAndRcs.cs`), so a slow spool to 0.29 ends on a recorded 0.25. Where stock's curve or per-frame threshold is steep the ghost shows it: RAPIER in air mode at 30 % `fx-far` flame real 20746, event ghost 321 (its trail draws nothing), Whiplash 18000 / 15002. The start route, seeded at 0.30, reads 20816 and 17945. A recorded flight cannot be changed; a settled-throttle event would be a recorder change for new flights.

## ~~GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-WRONG-SOURCE~~: the ghost's nozzle glow follows the wrong signal on the Whiplash, the wet Panther and seven ReStock boosters, and ReStock's RCS glow is missing [FILED 2026-11-23 from `ghost-fx-3`'s `2026-11-23_1201`, PPS-12b `2026-11-23_1656`, PP-10 `2026-11-23_1712` and `_1718` / `_1725`; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-6`, flown `2026-11-23_1927` / `_1934` / `_1940` / `_1946`; low (visual only)]

What, `color-blob-px` event / start route: `turboFanEngine` burn-full bottom 16355 / 0 (stock), 16356 / 0 (ReStock); `turboJet` burn-full-m2 bottom 18271 / 1, 18272 / 1; ReStock `Mite` burn-full bottom 10530 / 10531, side-a 1704; ReStock `linearRcs` top 7279 / 7279. PP-9 `2026-11-23_1749` adds the six other boosters, event bottom: Thoroughbred 8476, `restock-srb-mallet-1` 3402, Pollux 2962, Clydesdale 2499, Shrimp 2106, `restock-srb-striker-1` 976.

1. Jets. `TRJ_Heat` and `TurboJetHeat` are the only FXModuleAnimateThrottle clips of stock-minimal, modded-restock and modded-compat without `dependOnThrottle` (ModuleManager.ConfigCache of each), and stock (decompiled `FixedUpdate`) then reads `vessel.ctrlState.mainThrottle`, not the engine's throttle. The parity rig runs engines on the independent throttle (`PartParityFxDriver.AuthorVesselNode`) with the vessel's at 0, so stock's target is 0; the ghost took the engine's recorded power. The regression is the rig's case only: with the main throttle up (the ordinary flight) stock's bell heats as the ghost's does, so dropping the glow would have been wrong. Ruled out: the layer / weight mix of several clips on one part (in both `.mu` files only the heat clip animates `_EmissiveColor`; the nozzle clips move transforms and a light's colour or intensity), and a clip that runs but does not show (the start route's ghost, built from a snapshot taken after the 23 s press, is dark too, so the part persisted an `animState` of about 0; a hidden clip would have persisted 0.25). Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.ResolveVesselThrottleSource`. A glow that follows the vessel's throttle divides the recorded power by the thrust limiter (an engine on the main throttle runs at throttle x limiter), and when its engines ignore the main throttle (saved `independentThrottle`, or a throttle lock) its target while they run is the snapshot's `CTRLSTATE mainThrottle`.
2. Boosters. ReStock spells `includedRenderers` / `excludedRenderers` on 26 parts; stock's `OnLoad` reads the singular keys, so on the seven where both modules write `_EmissiveColor` (Mite, Shrimp, Thoroughbred, Clydesdale, Pollux, `restock-srb-mallet-1`, `restock-srb-striker-1`) heatColor (0.025 or 0.05 /s) and throttleColor (1 /s) both write the whole bell. Stock's Update shows the last one, throttleColor, which the ghost played (its log: `bound=1 ['throttleColor' colors=3 ... ramp=0@1]`). KSPCommunityFixes' Update (decompiled) writes only while its ramp moves, so from the first second on heatColor's ramp shows, and once both stand the last FXModuleThrottleEffects call. Measured on the pictures (emission goes with the square): the real bell stood at 0.157 in PPS-12b and 0.316 in PP-9, 0.025 /s x 6.3 s and 12.6 s, the core mesh with it, which rules out that the plural filter is honoured (the core would be at 1) and that the ghost mis-times one module's ramp. Fix: `ResolveThrottleGlowWritersUnder` keeps the other writers of a material, `GhostPlaybackLogic.ShownNozzleGlow` picks the one stock shows.
3. `linearRcs`. Neither of the glow paths: ReStock's own `ModuleRestockRCSGlow` (decompiled Restock.dll, six parts) sets `_TintColor` on the first mesh under each thruster transform to its curves at `thrustForces[i] / thrusterPower` every physics step, which for one nozzle is the recorded power. Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.BuildReStockRcsGlow`, one-nozzle parts only (`linearRcs`, `RCSLinearSmall`); the four blocks wait on RCS-PER-NOZZLE-RECORDING. The material is listed in `CollectGhostOwnedMaterials`, so the reentry glow neither re-clones it nor loses the part.

Limits: a throttle mode, limiter or main throttle changed in flight is not recorded (the snapshot's stands); an end-of-recording snapshot gives no vessel throttle (the recorded power stands in, as before); a booster's start route stays hot (PARTPARITY-START-ROUTE-RAMP-NOT-RELOADED).

Tests: `GhostNozzleGlowTests` (Vessel throttle, ReStock RCS glow, `Overlap_*`).

Flown (main 82dc51fb, DLL ede21f49, evidence `<umbrella>/logs/flights/fx-fly/`; 16c and 16d INVALID on controls only, their specs plan none; recompute 0 mismatches, no `[Parsek][ERROR]`). `color-blob-px`, event / start route: PPS-16a `2026-11-23_1927` PASS (stock air) and PPS-16b `_1934` PASS (ReStock air), four controls ok each, `turboFanEngine` burn-full bottom 16355 / 0 and 16356 / 0 -> 0 / 0, `turboJet` burn-full-m2 18271 / 1 and 18272 / 1 -> 1 / 1: the bells agree, cold against cold, as the rig's reading says (PARTPARITY-VESSEL-THROTTLE-NOT-DRIVEN; nothing here measures the ordinary hot bell). Every other glow reading as in the headers; ReStock RAPIER 30 % still reads event bottom 10010 (start 0, ENGINE-THROTTLE-EVENT-STEP). PPS-16c `_1940` (ReStock orbit): event 0 on all seven boosters (Pollux side-b 1, Shrimp bottom 1), `linearRcs` top 7279 / 7279 -> 0 / 0 (pass), `RCSLinearSmall` 2 / 2; `toroidalAerospike`, LV-T91 (6), ionEngine, RAPIER and `liquidEngine2` unchanged. The boosters' start routes stay hot (Mite bottom 10531), as filed. PPS-16d `_1946` (stock orbit): 13 of 13 pass.

## ~~GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-SPLIT-RAMP~~: a ghost that begins at a split starts its ReStock bell at the wrong heat [FILED 2026-11-23 from the PP-9 `2026-11-23_1749` start routes (owner: "Yes, both"); FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-7`; live: the code ran on six dropped boosters (`2026-11-23_2156`), their bell heat not seen in game; low (visual only, modded)]

What: 40 PP-9 cases fail on the start-route bell (`toroidalAerospike` up to 128022 px): the ghost built from a snapshot taken mid-burn stands at the hot end, the real bell is mid-ramp.

Stock after a load (decompiled `ModuleColorChanger` / `FXModuleThrottleEffects`): `animState` (a bool) and `FXModuleThrottleEffects.state` are the only persisted fields; `Start()` sets `currentRateState = animState ? 1 : 0` (KSPCommunityFixes' Start postfix shows it at once). So a save taken mid-burn loads with the bell at the HOT end, and the ghost built from it is what stock shows after that load. The rig's real side is not reloaded, so the 40 cases compare two different vessels (PARTPARITY-START-ROUTE-RAMP-NOT-RELOADED).

Which recordings start mid-burn (322 recordings with `.prec.txt` under `harness/fixtures/saves`; an engine running within 0.6 s of the start): 39. 27 launches, all with a snapshot taken before the ignition (PRELAUNCH, engine off) and an engine-off seed first, so the ramp starts at 0; 3 rows the optimizer cut, which replay their earlier rows (#2795); one Re-Fly row lit after its snapshot; 8 debris pieces whose running engines are separation motors (ReStock gives `sepMotor1` no glow). Nothing starts too hot. A switch, a Re-Fly or an F9 loads the vessel, so the hot end is right there.

The mirror is the ordinary case: 147 of the 322 (139 dropped stages, 8 controlled pieces) begin at a split with an engine that has just stopped. The snapshot's switch is off, so the bell started cold; replaying the parent's events at 0.05 /s it stands at 0.93 (median; counted from 0.1 up).

Fix: `GhostPlaybackLogic.SettleRampsAtSplit` (at bind, only for a ghost with a ramping glow). A row that begins at an Undock / EVA / JointBreak / Breakup with one parent (a Re-Fly attempt excluded) takes the ramp its engine's recorded events give, replayed from the first row of the line through optimizer cuts and earlier splits; a part keeps its persistentId through a split. No events: the snapshot's end, as before. Clip glows (`FXModuleAnimateThrottle`) persist their level and are untouched. Nothing recorded changes.

Not covered, by choice: a docked vessel's bell still warm from before the dock (two parents), a switch to a vessel in the physics bubble (nothing was loaded, the ghost takes the switch's end), a re-aimed loop row (GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-REAIM-HISTORY).

Tests: `GhostNozzleGlowTests` (`Split_*`; `Split_ARecordedBoosterTakesItsRampFromTheAscent` replays three boosters of `duna-one-recorded`).

Flown: PPS-17c `2026-11-23_2156` (throwaway, modded-restock, DLL 1d211ee6, evidence `<umbrella>/logs/flights/ghost-fx-7/`), a Kerbal X ascent, Rewind-to-Launch and replay: `Nozzle glow at a split` fired for each of the six `Kerbal X Debris` ghosts with rows=1 ramps=2/2, headUT 30.9 and splitUT 61.5 / 63.7 / 65.9, no `[Parsek][ERROR]`. The heat each bell started at is not in the log: the per-glow line is rate limited and only the first pair (ramp 0.000, engines off for 17 s, so 0 either way) printed. The flown recordings replayed offline through the same code give 0 / 0.625 / 0.580 (before: 0 / 0 / 0). The split line now prints the hottest ramp; that build has not flown. Run verdict PARSEK-FAIL on `recordings.count 9 > max 8`, a bound copied from GPOS-1 (stock): the ninth is the "Kerbal X Probe" row the optimizer cut where it left the atmosphere. PPS-17b `_2152` (modded-restock): event-route bells at most 2 px on Mite, `liquidEngine2`, RAPIER, `ionEngine` and `toroidalAerospike` at every power flown; the start routes stay hot as filed (Mite bottom 10530, aerospike 132302, RAPIER 24966, `liquidEngine2` side-a 10635). Its controls are absent by spec, so it is INVALID on controls only.

## PARTPARITY-START-ROUTE-RAMP-NOT-RELOADED: the parity start route compares a loaded ghost with a real bell that was never loaded [FILED 2026-11-23 from `ghost-fx-7`; OPEN; instrument, low]

What: the start-route ghost is built from a snapshot of the real part while it burns. For ReStock's ramping `ModuleColorChanger` that snapshot means the hot end (stock's own load, GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-SPLIT-RAMP), while the real part on the stand is mid-ramp: 40 PP-9 plume cases fail on `color-blob-px` of the start route alone, bells right on the event route.

Fix (not started), either: let the real bell arrive (hold until the ramp stands, up to 40 s a case at 0.025 /s) before the start snapshot; or save and reload the real vessel before the start-route picture; or report the start route's bell on a ramping part as a known difference. No ghost change makes these right: the only data that says where a ramp stood is the engine events before the snapshot, and the rig's start route has none.

## ~~GHOST-LES-NO-PLUME~~: a stock launch escape tower burns without a plume on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-7 `2026-11-23_1732` (`LaunchEscapeSystem` full: real core 1485 / 1482 / 10277 / 2010 px on side-a / side-b / bottom / far, ghost 0); FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-7`, flown `2026-11-23_2149`; low (visual only, stock)]

What: stock draws five `Squad/FX/LES_Thruster` emitters (one per `thrustTransform`) by the engine's thrust (`powerEffectName = running_closed`), dark below 5 %, so it burns on abort and on jettison. The ghost drew nothing; ReStock's tower passed.

Cause: `EngineFxBuilder.TryBuildEngineFX` skipped the part by name since 2026-03-16 (8185c6817): "excessive particles at playback distance, the nozzle glow is enough". The part has no `FXModuleAnimateThrottle`, so there was no glow either; the excess is likely that time's rules (fixed emission, the size boost; inferred, not measured), which GHOST-ENGINE-FX-STOCK-RULES replaced with stock's own curves. Real: 235 particles over the five nozzles.

Fix: the skip is gone; the tower goes through the same EFFECTS path as every engine. An unlit tower (on the pad, on a jettisoned piece) stays dark: its recording seeds an engine-off event, which also keeps the zero-event auto-start off (287 of 287 fixture recordings with an engine carry one).

Tests: `EngineFxBuilderTests` (`LaunchEscapeTower_*`, `TryBuildEngineFx_NamesNoPartButTheRapier`), `OrphanEngineFxAutoStartTests` (`*_AnUnlitEscapeTowersSeed_*`).

Flown: PPS-17a `2026-11-23_2149` (throwaway, stock-minimal, DLL 1d211ee6, INVALID on controls only, its spec plans none; recompute 0 mismatches, no `[Parsek][ERROR]`), core px real / ghost side-a 1469 / 1473, side-b 1477 / 1463, bottom 10345 / 10387, far 2015 / 2015, far length and width 1.00 / 1.01, 237.8 / 235.1 particles, 5 of 5 emitters, `pass`. Mite, `liquidEngine2`, RAPIER, `ionEngine` and `toroidalAerospike`: 9 of 9 other cases `pass`, the missing-system lists as in PP-7 (flameout and spark systems that do not render). ReStock's tower (PPS-17b `_2152`) still passes, 14191 / 14451.

## ~~GHOST-LEGACY-FX-KEEP-POSITION~~: the Mainsail's two vernier flames burn at the main nozzle on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-7 `2026-11-23_1732`; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-6`, flown `2026-11-23_1946`; low (visual only, stock)]

What: `liquidEngineMainsail.v2` at 30 % side-b flame width 0.381 (full throttle 1.00, the main flame hides it). Stock's two `fx_exhaustFlame_yellow_mini` sit at (0.04, -1.01, 1.85) and (-0.04, 1.01, 1.85) under the thrust transform, the ghost's both at the engine's `fxOffset` (0, 0, 2.18).

Cause (decompiled): the two keys end in `true`, which makes `PartLoader` add `(Keep Pos)` to the object's name, and `ModuleEngines.AutoPlaceFXGroup` gives a system so named its authored position instead of `fxOffset`. The only `fx_*` keys under `Squad/Parts` and `SquadExpansion` that end so are the Mainsail's four (two flames, two lights); ReStock drops them.

Fix: `EngineFxBuilder.LegacyFxLocalPosition`. Tests: `GhostFxStockPlacementTests`. Flown: PPS-16d `2026-11-23_1946`, 30 % side-b width 0.381 -> 0.991, core 4900 / 3943 -> 4896 / 4994, side-a origin 16 -> 0 px, both powers pass, `fxDiffers` empty.

## PARTPARITY-VESSEL-THROTTLE-NOT-DRIVEN: no parity case burns an engine on the vessel's main throttle [FILED 2026-11-23 from `ghost-fx-6`; OPEN; instrument, low]

What: the FX rig authors `independentThrottle = True` and leaves the case vessel's `ctrlState.mainThrottle` at 0, so anything stock drives by the vessel's throttle stays at rest on the real side: today the Whiplash's and the wet Panther's heat clips (`TRJ_Heat`, `TurboJetHeat`). Their cases judge a cold bell against a cold bell; the ordinary flight, bell hot on both sides, is not measured.

Seen 2026-11-23: PPS-16a / PPS-16b (`2026-11-23_1927` / `_1934`) read 0 px on both bells against the cold real side (16355 to 18272 px before GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-WRONG-SOURCE), which agrees with the rig's reading and measures nothing about the ordinary case.

Fix (not started): also author `CTRLSTATE { mainThrottle = <the case's throttle> }` on the case vessel (the independent throttle stays, so nothing else moves) and expect both bells hot.

## GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-REAIM-HISTORY: a re-aimed loop row cut at a burn's end starts with a cold nozzle [FILED 2026-11-23 from the `ghost-fx-2` review; OPEN; low (visual only)]

What: a row the optimizer cut carries the head row's start snapshot, so `GhostPlaybackLogic.BindNozzleGlows` replays the earlier chain rows' engine events to find the nozzle's level at the cut. The walk needs a `Recording`; a re-aimed loop member is a `ReaimedTrajectory` wrapper, so it gets none and the nozzle starts at the snapshot's level, cooled.

Fix (not started): give the wrapper's base recording to the walk.

## PARTPARITY-FX-ORBIT-FINDINGS-2026-11-23: what the first full orbit FX sweeps found, by cluster [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-7 `2026-11-23_1027` (stock-minimal), PP-9 `2026-11-23_1050` (modded-restock) and PP-8 `2026-11-23_1232` (modded-compat); OPEN as the index of the entries below; report-only lanes, nothing here is ruled on]

Verdicts (report-only; the E.4 thresholds are starting guesses). PP-7, 128 cases: 34 pass / 33 warn / 60 fail / 1 error. PP-9, 165 cases: 28 / 74 / 61 / 2, re-judged under the weak-core rule (design E.4) 28 / 71 / 64 / 2. PP-8, 165 cases: 27 pass / 21 warn / 20 fail / 2 error / 95 reference (would be 42 fail / 53 warn). Re-judged under the per-entry cap (design E.4, "FX instrument fixes"): PP-7 34 / 16 / 77 / 1, PP-9 28 / 7 / 128 / 2, PP-8 27 / 7 / 34 / 2 and 95 reference (would be 95 fail). Every run: controls ok, press ok, complete, recompute 0 mismatches, no `[Parsek][ERROR]`. PP-7 and PP-9 flew one DLL (sha256 prefix 002a3fc9, main plus `ghost-fx-2`), PP-8 a later one (e2a66a0f: main with #2795 and #2797 plus this branch's instrument changes). Evidence: `<umbrella>/logs/flights/p8-f6/` (sweeps, KSP logs, viewer site `viewer/index.html`).

The headline: ReStock's own plumes match. Stock's legacy plumes do not: 42 full-thrust cases, core 0.80, far length 0.82; 30 at 30 % thrust, core 2.26, width 1.41, far length 2.09 (2 of 30 within 25 %).

## ~~GHOST-FLAME-Z-DIRECTION~~: the small `_Z` engine flames point sideways on a ghost and read as a ball at the nozzle [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-7 `2026-11-23_1027`; FIXED 2026-11-23 by GHOST-ENGINE-FX-STOCK-RULES (branch `ghost-fx-3`, flown on two of the four parts) and, for the separation motors, branch `ghost-fx-4`, all flown `2026-11-23_1651`; low (visual only)]

What: `smallRadialEngine` and `.v2`, `liquidEngineMini.v2` (Spark) and `LiquidEngineRV-1` draw `fx_exhaustFlame_yellow_tiny_Z`. The inventories differ in the emission direction (and in size, as everywhere): real `dir=(0.0,1.0,0.0)`, ghost `dir=(0.0,0.0,-1.0)` (local to the same parent). In the pictures stock draws a flame 2 to 5 nozzles long and the ghost a round glow at the nozzle: core 12933 / 1565 px (`smallradialengine.v2--orange--burn-full--0fb37a96`, length 0.15), Spark length 0.46, RV-1 0.35. ReStock draws its own plume there and matches.

Cause (re-derived against main with #2798): the four parts name the flame in a PREFAB_PARTICLE node with no `localRotation`, which stock (`PrefabParticleFX.OnInitialize`, decompiled) reads as identity. The ghost ran the parent-up heuristic instead (`EngineFxBuilder.ResolvePrefabParticleLocalRotation`), which answers -90 degrees about X when the mount's up is far from world up: (0,1,0) turned to the read (0,0,-1). `ghost-fx-3` loads stock's exact asset for an EFFECTS entry and puts it on stock's identity, and flew it: `2026-11-23_1209` `smallRadialEngine.v2` and `2026-11-23_1225` Spark read dir (0,1,0) on both sides. `smallRadialEngine` and `LiquidEngineRV-1` are the same node and code path. The same change covers the `fx_smokeTrail_veryLarge` axis on the 10 ReStock engines and boosters.

Fix (`ghost-fx-4`): the one legacy direction still off, `Size1p5.Tank.05`'s separation motors (PP-7: real (0,0,-1) on every nozzle, ghost (0,1,0) and (0,0.7,-0.7)). `ModuleEngines.AutoPlaceFXGroup` (decompiled) sets a legacy system to identity and `Rotate(-90,0,0)` under its own thrust transform; the ghost carried the `fx_*` child's part-frame rotation over, which only agrees when the nozzle points down the part. `EngineFxBuilder.LegacyFxLocalRotation`. Every other legacy system of PP-7 already read (0,0,-1). The heuristic stays for a substitute that is not stock's own asset; the plumes Parsek added to nine engines are gone (GHOST-ENGINE-ADDED-PLUMES).

Flown: PPS-12a `2026-11-23_1651` (stock-minimal, DLL f2fd0df2, INVALID on controls only: the spec plans none). Side-a length PP-7 -> now: `smallRadialEngine` 0.148 -> 0.993, side-b lateral -103 -> -0.0 px; `.v2` 0.146 -> 1.061, -112 -> -0.0; Spark 0.465 -> 1.005, -140 -> 0.0; RV-1 0.352 -> 1.038, -65 -> 0.0. `Size1p5.Tank.05` far smoke width 0.432 -> 1.054, core-iou 0.349 -> 0.86, pass. `fxDiffers` empty on all five. What is left on the four tiny flames is `warn` on hue L1 (0.12 to 0.47) and origin (8 to 38 px) of sparse particles.

What: `lightsDiffer` reads `count real=1 ghost=0` on 28 stock cases, `real=3` on 4 and `real=2` on 2 (34 cases): the legacy engines' `fx_exhaustLight_*` `Light`. ReStock parts carry none, so PP-9 reads 0. Reported only (E.4).

## ~~GHOST-FX-MODEL-SCALE~~: a ghost's engine and RCS effects ignore the model's scale and draw 1.25 times too large [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-7 `2026-11-23_1027` and PP-9 `2026-11-23_1050`; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-4`, flown `2026-11-23_1651` / `_1656` (the engines' first nozzle and the legacy systems came with `ghost-fx-3`); low (visual only)]

What: the real effect system sits under a model scaled 0.8 (0.64 where two nested transforms are), the ghost's under 1.0. Stock: `liquidEngine`, `liquidEngine2`, `RAPIER` (0.80 -> 1.00) and `sepMotor1` (3.53 -> 4.42). ReStock: `RAPIER`, `restock-engine-125-valiant`, `linearRcs`, `RCSBlock.v2` and the `restock-rcs-*` blocks (0.64 or 0.80 -> 1.00). It shows as a larger plume: ReStock RAPIER full core 55234 / 73716 px, width 1.32; `restock-rcs-single-mini-1` length 1.58; Valiant width 1.24.

Cause (decompiled `TransformExtension.NestToParent`, `ModelMultiParticleFX.OnInitialize`): stock parents an effect keeping its WORLD scale, so on a part rescaled by 1.25 the instance's local scale is 0.8. 0.64 is not two nested transforms: the second and later mounts get `Instantiate` of the FIRST instance after it was nested, so its local 0.8 becomes the copy's world scale and 0.8 / 1.25 = 0.64 (RAPIER and RCSBlock.v2: one 0.80, the rest 0.64; Poodle's last mount, scaled 0.5, reads 2.00). Other variants' mounts count: stock nests an instance under them too. The ghost parented without keeping the world scale. `ghost-fx-3` already fixed the legacy systems and EFFECTS prefabs (flown: `sepMotor1` 3.53 / 3.53), and gave every model instance 0.8, the later nozzles included.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.NestedModelFxScale` (pure: the mounts' prefab scales and the node's `localScale`), used by the engine and the RCS builder for MODEL_MULTI_PARTICLE nodes; SmokeScreen's `_PERSIST` node keeps what it had. Found with it and fixed: the RCS builder read `localOffset`, a key stock's `ModelMultiParticleFX` has not, and not `localPosition`, which it has (12 ReStock parts sat 0.1 to 0.15 m off, 6 lacked their 0.015 m; the -188 px origin of `restock-rcs-single-mini-1`). Tests: `GhostFxStockPlacementTests`.

Flown: PPS-12a `2026-11-23_1651` (stock-minimal) and PPS-12b `_1656` (modded-restock), DLL f2fd0df2, both INVALID on controls only. ReStock, before -> now: RAPIER full width 1.316 / 1.344 -> 0.970, bottom area 1.596 -> 1.002; Valiant width 1.244 -> 0.909, bottom area 1.364 -> 1.004; `linearRcs` origin 30 / 24 px and bottom area 1.542 -> no reason left, `fxDiffers` 2 -> 0; `restock-rcs-single-mini-1` origin -187 / -188 px -> pass; the other rcs systems now sit at the real position and, on the single-variant blocks, at the real scale (0.80 / 0.80). On `RCSBlock.v2` and the two multi blocks `fxDiffers` still pairs a real 0.80 with a ghost 0.64: the pairing is by order, the real side lists every variant's systems (36 on `RCSBlock.v2`, two of them 0.80 and 34 at 0.64) and the ghost the 8 it builds, all 0.64, so it is the pairing and not the scale. Stock: `liquidEngine` / `liquidEngine2` full hue 0.398 / 0.444 -> 0.004 / 0.012, 30 % length 1.549 / 1.481 -> pass; `sepMotor1` pass but for hue. The pictures of PPS-12a, PPS-12b and PPS-14a were pruned by the results retention (the newest 6 sweeps stay); their sidecars are in `automation/results-archive/`.

## ~~GHOST-RESTOCK-NOZZLE-GLOW~~: a ReStock engine's nozzle and bell do not glow on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-9 `2026-11-23_1050`; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-4`, flown `2026-11-23_1656` / `_1749`; the boosters with two glow writers went to GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-WRONG-SOURCE; low (visual only, modded)]

What: 94 of 102 PP-9 plume cases fail or warn on `color-blob-px` at the bottom view (and about 50 on a side view): the real bell glows orange while it burns, the ghost's stays cold metal (`toroidalaerospike--trussmount--burn-full--fcaf5be7` 123810 px, `liquidenginelv-t91--cap--burn-full--24c349fb` 37868). Stock nozzles now match (`ghost-fx-2`: `FXModuleAnimateThrottle` / `FXModuleAnimateRCS` clips; PP-7 reads 0 to 58 px there), but ReStock drives the glow with `ModuleColorChanger` (`heatColor` / `throttleColor`, 52 modded parts, design E.1), which `GhostVisualBuilder.NozzleGlow` does not read. It is the one thing that keeps most matching ReStock plumes from `pass`.

Cause (config and decompile): ReStock replaces FXModuleAnimateThrottle with stock's `FXModuleThrottleEffects` (101 on the install, all responseSpeed 1, dependOnThrottle) that calls `SetScalar` on a `ModuleColorChanger` by `moduleID`: `heatColor` (`_EmissiveColor`, animRate 0.025, 0.05 or 0.1) and `throttleColor` (animRate 1). All are `useRate`, so `SetScalar` is a switch (`animState` from 0.5) and the module's `Update` shows `currentRateState`, a ramp of `animRate` per second: a bell takes 10 to 40 s to heat and as long to cool. KSPCommunityFixes (both modded profiles and stock-minimal carry it) replaces that `Update` with one that writes only while the ramp moves, so once it stands the setter's level shows.

Measured on PP-9's own pictures (curves are linear in all four channels, so emission goes with the square): at 30 % the bell reads 0.300 of its full colour curve on 37 of 37 engines whose side view shows the bell, the setter's level; at full it reads the ramp, `toroidalAerospike` 0.621 = 0.05 /s x 12.4 s, SSME 0.275 and `microEngine.v2` 0.312 at 0.025 /s. So the setter's write comes before the module's own (the other order would read 1.0 at full).

Fix: `BuildColorChangerInfos` marks a colour changer an FXModuleThrottleEffects names (`ColorChangerPattern.ThrottleGlow`; a cabin light toggle or a heat shield char keeps its writer) and samples its curves; `GhostVisualBuilder.BuildThrottleGlows` turns it into a `NozzleGlowInfo` on the material clones it already had, driven by the recorded engine power through the nozzle-glow walk (`GhostPlaybackLogic.NozzleGlow`, closed form in the recorded UT, writes only when the level moved). A part whose only glow is a colour changer keeps the reentry glow. Two ReStock engines (`restock-srb-anvil`, `restock-srb-castor`) author `shaderProperty = _EmisiveColor` (a typo). Checked 2026-11-23 on modded-restock: the property list of neither .mu (`restock-srb-anvil-1`, `restock-engine-srb-pollux-1`) holds it, both hold `_EmissiveColor`, and nothing else under `GameData` or `KSP_x64_Data` names it. Compressed shader bundles cannot be searched and neither part was read in flight, so that they stay dark in stock and on the ghost is likely, not measured. The KSPCommunityFixes rule is read off the Harmony owner of `ModuleColorChanger.Update`, so a ReStock install without it shows stock's ramp. Tests: `GhostNozzleGlowTests` (Throttle glow region).

Known limit: stock does not persist where the ramp stood, only `animState`, so a ghost whose snapshot was taken with the engine running starts at the hot end (as stock's own load does). The start-route ghosts of PP-9 read brighter than the real bell 12 s into its burn for that reason: the rig's real side is not reloaded (PARTPARITY-START-ROUTE-RAMP-NOT-RELOADED). A recording that begins at a split, where stock loads nothing either, takes the ramp from the events before it (GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-SPLIT-RAMP).

Flown: PPS-12b `2026-11-23_1656` and the full lane PP-9 `_1749` (modded-restock), event-route `color-blob-px` before -> now: `toroidalAerospike` full 32783 / 32782 / 101512 -> 1, 30 % 1504 / 1497 / 688 -> 1; LV-T91 bottom 37868 / 36718 -> 6 / 0; SSME 37620 -> 2 / 1; `microEngine.v2` 13312 -> 0; `ionEngine` 36399 / 36086 -> 0; Poodle 5252 / 5209 -> 2; Valiant, RAPIER and boar at most 8 px. Of PP-9's 102 plume cases the event route fails on the bell on 9 (94 failed or warned before): seven ReStock boosters whose renderer filters are spelled so stock does not read them (Clydesdale 0 -> 2499, Pollux 0 -> 2962, Thoroughbred 4665 -> 8476, Mite 9607 -> 10514, Shrimp 1513 -> 2106, mallet 3292 -> 3402, striker 865 -> 976: worse with this branch, GHOST-NOZZLE-GLOW-WRONG-SOURCE), `restock-engine-caravel-1` (48958 -> 2951) and `MassiveBooster` (1089 -> 466). The known limit shows as filed: the start-route ghost's bell stands at the hot end, 40 of the 50 PP-9 plume fails.

## ~~GHOST-LIGHT-COOKIE~~: a ghost lamp's light is a plain disc where stock's has a pattern [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-9 `2026-11-23_1050`; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-4`, flown `2026-11-23_1656` / `_1749`; low (visual only)]

What: the plate pictures of `GrapplingDevice`, `smallClaw` and `restock-claw-625-1` differ (82804, 55775 and 66661 px) though intensity, colour, range and spot angle agree: the real light has ring-shaped falloff and the ghost's is a uniform disc (mean plate luminance 8.6 against 20.7). Inferred, not read: the light's `cookie` texture is not copied (no `cookie` read in `Source/Parsek/Ghost/`). Every other lamp's plate passes.

Cause: it is the cookie, but copying the prefab's would have changed nothing. Exactly these three parts carry ReStock's `ModuleRestockEnhancedLight` with a `cookiePath` (the other lamps' is commented out); its `OnStart` (decompiled Restock.dll) sets `GameDatabase.GetTexture(cookiePath)`, wrap mode clamp, on every Light its ModuleLights drive. A `.mu` light has no cookie, so the prefab the ghost copies has none.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.ResolveReStockLightCookie` reads the module's `cookiePath` off the prefab and the Lights ModuleLight drives get the same texture; every Light also takes the prefab's `cookie` and `cookieSize`.

Flown: PPS-12b `2026-11-23_1656`, plate `color-blob-px` before -> now, both routes: `GrapplingDevice` 82804 -> 0, `smallClaw` 55775 -> 0, `restock-claw-625-1` 66661 -> 0, `spotLight1` 0 -> 0; all pass, and all 17 plates of PP-9 `_1749` pass.

## PARTPARITY-FX-INSTRUMENT-2026-11-23: what the FX sweeps found about their own instrument [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-7, PP-8 and PP-9; FIXED 2026-11-23 on branch `fx-instrument` except the two open lines, the C# half flown 2026-11-23 on PP-5 to PP-10; low (tooling)]

The numbers behind each fix are in design E.4, "FX instrument fixes". The C# half flew on PP-7 `2026-11-23_1732`, PP-9 `_1749` and PP-8 `_1811`: no setup fault on any of them (`stripLight1` plate error -> pass on all three; `telescopicLadderBay` on the modded installs excluded, 165 -> 164 cases), `fx-not-plateaued` 10 -> 1 (PP-7), 10 -> 6 (PP-9) and 10 -> 7 (PP-8), `fx.layers` read after the warm-up, and every control ok. The air real-vs-real control at 16 samples a side read the Flea's far / side width 0.973 / 1.033 (PP-10) and 1.008 / 0.951 (PP-5), line 1.30: no INVALID(parity-controls) on the three air lanes. Sweep seconds, now against before: PP-7 897 / 906, PP-9 1198 / 1243, PP-8 1218 / 1254.

- ~~Plate sized from the spot angle.~~ FIXED (`PlateSizeM`, the smaller of the cone and the range). `stripLight1` (`spotAngle` 170) gets an 89 m plate at 3 m, so the real side lights 1.1 % (stock) or 0.5 % (ReStock) of it, under the 2 % floor: setup fault `plate-not-lit` on every install, though real and ghost agree (0 px). 
- ~~No Light behind the ModuleLight.~~ FIXED (`fx-no-light`). `telescopicLadderBay` on ReStock has no `Light` behind its `ModuleLight` (`real[]` on the settle line), so its plate case is always `plate-not-lit`.
- ~~Convergence.~~ FIXED in the judge: the cap is per entry, and every capped fail that a settled entry, the body or the structure carried stands (PP-7 17, PP-9 64, PP-8 14 cases and 53 would-be moved `warn` to `fail`, nothing else moved). `Samples` stays 16: 32 would cost 7 to 12 minutes a lane and leave most of it. `fx-unsettled` capped a fail to warn on 70 of 165 cases on PP-9 (67 under the weak-core rule), 70 of 165 on PP-8 (would-be verdicts included) and 17 of 128 on PP-7: ReStock's particles are sparse and large, so 16 samples per view do not settle length and width within 10 %. A fail under the cap read `warn`.
- ~~Read too early.~~ FIXED (read after the warm-up; the judged missing / extra lists keep their read). `fx.layers` is read before the ghosts' emitters have a material, so KSPParticleEmitter flames are listed under `smoke` there (PARTPARITY-FX-AIR-FIRST-READINGS-2026-11-23, Instrument); the measures classify each frame. ## ~~GHOST-SMOKE-RIDES-ACTIVE-VESSEL~~ (was PARTPARITY-ORBIT-SRB-SMOKE-NOISE): a ghost's world-space smoke rode along with the active vessel, so a booster ghost sat in a ball of its own smoke [FILED 2026-11-23 from PP-8 / PP-9 as instrument noise; the owner saw it on the pictures 2026-11-24; FIXED 2026-11-24, branch `srb-smoke`]

What a player saw: beside his own ghost in the air, or with a vessel in orbit, every ReStock booster ghost hid in a ball or column of grey smoke the real booster does not draw, and stock smoke trails spread out around the ghost instead of behind it. The parity instrument read it as `smoke-extra` on 12 boosters of PP-8 / PP-9; this entry called it noise on the real side, inferred from the Krakensbane shear. Wrong: the real side was right, the ghost was not.

Cause (IL of `FloatingOrigin.setOffset` and `EffectBehaviour.OffsetParticles`): while Krakensbane or continuous mode is on, stock moves every registered world-space particle by minus (origin offset + frame velocity * dt) each physics step, 45 m at orbital speed, so smoke stays where it was emitted; a `KSPParticleEmitter`'s particles also drift back by `(rb.velocity + frameVelocity) * Random * dt` (mean one half more). It finds a part's systems through the Part (`ModelMultiParticleFX` / `ModelParticleFX`, FXGroups) or stock's `FXPrefab`; a ghost has no Part, and `StripKspFxControllers` destroys `FXPrefab`. So nothing moved a ghost's smoke, and it kept the active vessel's velocity. Stock's own loops for plain systems (FXGroups, PREFAB_PARTICLE) move nothing: the particle is a copy that is never written back, and `FXPrefab`'s registration does the plain shift; KSPCommunityFixes' `FloatingOriginPerf` replaces `setOffset` with one that writes both the shift and the drift. This also answers E0's open question (why the real world-space particles drift kilometres in orbit).

Fix: `Source/Parsek/Ghost/GhostWorldSpaceEmitter.cs`, one component on every world-space system of a ghost FX clone (`FXPrefab` stays stripped, so nothing moves twice), registered exactly while it is enabled, moved in the `setOffset` postfix with stock's rule: the shift always, the drift for an emitter-fed system and, when KSPCommunityFixes patches `setOffset`, for a plain one. The drift velocity is read off the ghost's own motion plus the shifts; a jump (loop restart) is rejected by taking the slower of two readings. Nothing happens while the active vessel is parked (no shift), as for a real vessel seen from there.

Proof (throwaway lanes SMK-1 to SMK-6, kept with their rig in `<umbrella>/logs/flights/srb-smoke/`): free burns recorded by the real recorder, the ghost replayed from the same recording at the same UT and camera, before (registration removed) and after. Orbit, 9 ReStock boosters, smoke within 20 m of the nozzle of about 280 particles: real 2 to 4 on all 27 shots, before 34 to 294, after 2 to 4; spread across the plume real 2.9 to 3.4 km, after 2.9 to 3.3 km. Air, a real booster of the same kind 42 m beside the ghost (mean distance behind the nozzle): Hammer +5 s before 6.3 m, after 73.1 m, real in the same instant 67.9 m; Flea +7 s 6.5 / 136.6 / 138.0 m. Stock `fx_smokeTrail_medium` beside a Flea +7 s: before 165 m, after 473 m, real 466 m.

The standing flow STAYS (owner ruling 2026-11-24; do not remove it without asking). `WorldSpaceEmitterFloorSpeed` gives a ReStock booster ghost's smoke 6 m/s exhaust-ward (commit d75cf8f27, 2026-06-12, made for the static showcase, where the asset's own 0 to 1 m/s "gathers in one point"). The real part does gather: a real Hammer held still in the air reads 1.0 m mean behind the nozzle (4.8 m at most), the flowing ghost 5.8 m (15.7 m); without the flow the ghost reads 1.0 / 4.9 m and the showcase shows a ball of smoke at each booster (both photographed, `showcase/` and `air-restock-nofloor/` in the flight folder; removal 97e052a12, reverted). Its limit, tightened with the ruling: the flow counts the ghost's own speed (`GhostWorldSpaceEmitter.StandingFlow`, smoke leaves at 6 m/s minus the ghost's speed when that is above its own), so only a booster that burns standing still differs from the real one and nothing from 6 m/s up is touched. Before that it reached launched flights too: Hammer +3 / +5 / +7 s 30.9 / 73.1 / 118.5 m with it, 25.3 / 68.7 / 114.6 m without, real beside it 25.0 / 67.9 / 114.5 m.

Parity lanes on the fixed build (PP-9 `2026-11-24_2040` and `_2145`, PP-10 `_2101`, PP-7 `_2120`, PP-5 `_2137`, MC-2 `_2144` PASS; DLL 7164781e except `_2040` / `_2101`, which flew the build without the standing flow): ReStock booster smoke on PP-9, 10 boosters times 4 views, views with a ghost core of 256 px or more 40 of 40 before, 1 and 0 of 40 after (real 0, 0, 2); the instrument's own 95th-percentile spread across the axis real 155 / ghost 155 m on the Thumper (before 1.7 m). Verdicts against main `2026-11-24_0735` / `_0758` / `_0628` (pass / warn / fail): PP-9 68 / 31 / 65 -> 71 / 27 / 66, PP-7 105 / 19 / 4 -> 103 / 23 / 2, PP-10 2 / 5 / 7 -> 2 / 6 / 6, PP-5 2 / 5 / 7 -> 2 / 5 / 7, every control ok; the cases that moved the wrong way are flame-layer flicker at the rate two runs of one build show (PP-9 9 worse / 8 better / 2 to fail between `_1749` and `_0735`, 8 / 9 / 4 here) and two smoke views, see the next entry. `ctl-fx-smoke-dropped` was built on the defect (a ghost that keeps its smoke at the nozzle in orbit) and now switches the mover off on its own ghosts.

Not changed: a ghost watched from a parked vessel draws its trail without the drift (as stock draws a real vessel from there), so it is denser than the one its pilot saw.

## PARTPARITY-ORBIT-SMOKE-PUFF-NOISE: in orbit a fresh smoke puff lands in the near box now and then, on either side, so a booster's orbit smoke view can read `smoke-missing` or `smoke-extra` once in a while [FILED 2026-11-24 from PP-9 `_2040` / `_2145`; OPEN; low (tooling)]

What: the puffs of the newest rendered frame sit at the nozzle until the next physics step carries them off, and a view counts them when a sample falls in that gap. After GHOST-SMOKE-RIDES-ACTIVE-VESSEL both sides do it alike: of 80 booster smoke views 1 had a ghost core (Flea side-a 924 px) and 2 a real one (Flea side-a 808, Thumper bottom 2279; the Thumper read 29 and 197 px there in the two runs before). With both halves settled the Thumper's bottom view reads `smoke-missing` and fails (PP-9 `_2145`); `smallRadialEngine.v2` at 30 % reads the same `smoke-extra` on its bottom view as before the fix and fails now that the cap for unsettled views no longer hides it. Fix: do not judge the smoke layer of an orbit case whose sides draw world-space smoke unless both cores pass the minimum in both halves, or make it a visible known-unjudged. Until then read a single orbit smoke reason on a booster as this.

## GHOST-TRANSIENT-FX-RIDE-ACTIVE-VESSEL: the ghost FX Parsek builds itself (explosion smoke, part puffs, launch dust, the reentry fire) are world-space and do not follow the floating origin [FILED 2026-11-24 while fixing GHOST-SMOKE-RIDES-ACTIVE-VESSEL; FIXED 2026-11-26, branch `ghost-fx-9`, flight pending; low (visual only)]

What: `GhostVisualBuilder.TransientFx.cs` and the reentry fire (`GhostVisualBuilder.HeatAndReentryFx.cs`) create their particle systems with `simulationSpace = World` and nothing moves them when the origin shifts, so beside a flying active vessel they drift along with it for their 1 to 4 s.

Cause (source, and the 1.12.5 decompile of `FloatingOrigin.setOffset` / `FXMonger.offsetPositions`): six world-space systems are Parsek's own, none on a stock list: the built explosion's fireball and its smoke child (`SpawnExplosionFx`, unparented, the smoke bursts 0.1 s after the spawn), the part puff's smoke and sparks (`SpawnPartPuffFx`, unparented, on every ghost Decoupled event and the destroyed-part fallback), launch dust (`TryBuildLaunchDust`, under the ghost root) and the reentry fire (`BuildReentryFireParticleSystem`, under the ghost root); the EVA jetpack plume is local-space. Stock moves a plain system it holds in `FloatingOrigin.particleSystems` (an `FXPrefab` registers one) by the shift alone, also under KSPCommunityFixes' `FloatingOriginPerf`. Not Parsek's: the flight ghost explosion is stock's own `FXMonger.Explode`, which stock moves itself (object and particles) while the active vessel is under 10 km radar altitude (`altToStopMovingExplosions`), as for a real explosion; the built explosion stands in only with the pause menu open, when `FXMonger` refuses, and in the KSC scene.

Fix: `GhostWorldSpaceEmitter.AttachOwn`, the same component GHOST-SMOKE-RIDES-ACTIVE-VESSEL put on the cloned FX, on each of the six systems: registered exactly while enabled, shifted in the `setOffset` postfix with stock's rule for a plain registered system (no drift), and an unparented root (puff, built explosion) has its own transform moved too, as `FXMonger.offsetPositions` moves a stock explosion's, so the smoke burst it has not emitted yet leaves from the right place. A system that already carries one is skipped (`ShouldAttach`), so nothing is moved twice; a non-drifting system now skips the per-frame motion read. The reentry streaks become the hull moving away from fire left in the air, which is what they were tuned to while the viewer stood still. Tests: `GhostWorldSpaceEmitterTests` (attach rule; the four attach sites and the six world-space systems pinned from source, so a new one reds until attached).

## ~~GHOST-SRB-SPARKS-MISSING~~: a solid booster's ghost drew its flame and smoke but not its exhaust sparks [FILED 2026-11-24 from the srb-smoke flights; FIXED 2026-11-26, branch `ghost-fx-9`; low (visual only)]

What: the real Flea and Hammer draw `fx_exhaustSparks_yellow` in the air (SMK-3 `viewerReal` stats: 79 to 89 world-space particles, renderer on), the ghost had no such system (PP-7 `fxMissing=[fx_exhaustSparks_yellow<thrustTransform]` on every stock booster). In orbit both draw none: the prefab carries a `SmokeTrailControl`, which stock (and the ghost's `GhostSmokeTrailFade`) hides in vacuum, so PP-7 reads the real entry `rendered: false`.

Cause: the legacy `fx_*` child loop in `EngineFxBuilder` (and the Waterfall pristine path `PristinePartFxResolver.ParseLegacyFxKeys`) skipped every name containing `sparks` as a transient effect. The solid boosters (Flea, Hammer, Thumper, Kickback, Thoroughbred, Clydesdale, Shrimp, Mite) name `fx_exhaustSparks_yellow` in their `running` group, and stock's running `FXGroup` burns it with the flame; a flameout's sparks carry the word flameout.

Fix: `EngineFxBuilder.IsTransientLegacyFx` leaves out flameout and debris effects by name and sparks only when stock's running or power group does not hold them; the clone takes the legacy running rule like the flame and, world-space with its `FXPrefab` stripped, the floating-origin mover. Tests: `EngineFxBuilderTests.IsTransientLegacyFx_*`, `PristinePartFxResolverTests.ParseLegacyFxKeys_*`.

## PARTPARITY-FX-FIRST-READINGS-2026-11-23: what the first FX sweep (P8 F3 acceptance) saw on the ghosts [FILED 2026-11-23; OPEN; triage belongs to the P8 F6 reading runs, nothing judged yet]

Run `2026-11-23_0728`, stock-minimal, orbit, one part per label (evidence `<umbrella>/logs/flights/p8-f3/`). The FX thresholds are starting guesses, so these are readings, not verdicts. RAPIER figures are the closed cycle, before #2792 reached the branch DLL: provisional.

- ~~Body glow.~~ FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-2` (RCS blocks with more than one nozzle excepted, RCS-PER-NOZZLE-RECORDING). Engine and RCS nozzles glowed on the real part while they fired and stayed dark on both ghost routes: LV-T45, ion engine, RAPIER and RCSBlock.v2 (bottom-view `color-blob-px` 25568, 31016, 118378 and 8308). Cause: stock heats them with `FXModuleAnimateThrottle` / `FXModuleAnimateRCS`, which move the clip's time toward the throttle (the nozzle's force) by `responseSpeed * 25 * dt` a physics step (time constant 40 s on the LV-T45, 4 s on the RCS, 0.07 s on the ion engine); the ghost built the clip's colours but only `ThermalAnimation*` events wrote them, and only `ModuleAnimateHeat` records those. Now `GhostVisualBuilder.BuildNozzleGlows` samples the clip at 17 times and `GhostPlaybackLogic.UpdateNozzleGlows` drives it from the recorded engine / RCS power as a pure function of UT, from the level the snapshot persisted (`animState`) at its `lastUT`; a row cut off an earlier one replays the earlier rows' events first. A ModuleAnimateHeat part now takes its clip's own colours at 0 / 0.5 / 1 (`BuildClipHeatMaterialStates`, over the nozzle glow's clip sampler, every Animation that holds the clip, as `ModuleAnimationSetter.AnimStartup`); the generic ramp stays for a clip that animates no colour. ## ~~GHOST-RCS-DARK-AFTER-FX-SUPPRESSION~~: a ghost that comes out of FX suppression while its RCS fires shows no RCS puffs until the next RCS event [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part parity P8 E0 spike (`docs/dev/design-part-ghost-parity.md` E.12 U2; PPS-8a `2026-11-22_2144`, PPS-8b `2026-11-22_2151`); FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-fixes`; low (visual only)]

What: `GhostPlaybackEngine.StopVisualFxForFrame` (every suppressed frame, and the hidden prime of a freshly built ghost) calls `GhostPlaybackLogic.StopAllRcsFx`, which disables every RCS particle renderer, and then `StopAllRcsEmissions`. On the first unsuppressed frame `RestoreAllRcsEmissions` restores only modules with an ENABLED renderer (its `wasActive` test), so it restores none and clears `rcsSuppressed`. The ghost stays dark until its recording's next RCS event. Engines do not have this gap: `RestoreActiveEngineFx` restarts them from the last recorded power. Evidence: an `RCSBlock.v2` ghost built from a recording with one `RCSActivated` event at power 0.157 drew 0 particles and 0 enabled renderers after the production priming, on stock and ReStock; a direct `SetRcsEmission` with the same power then drew 4 (stock) or 8 (ReStock) renderers.

Player-visible: a ghost holding a steady RCS translation (a docking approach) shows no puffs once it has been out of FX range or hidden and comes back, and none at all when it is first built mid-burn.

Fix: `RestoreAllRcsEmissions` re-lights every module with recorded power through `SetRcsEmission` (the existing `CollectDeferredRcsPowerRestores` set over `rcsInfos[*].currentPower`), the way `RestoreActiveEngineFx` restarts engines, instead of testing the renderer state `StopAllRcsFx` had just cleared. Re-applying the recorded power writes the same S1 magnitude the event wrote, so the in-game `RcsPlumeMagnitudeSurvivesSuppressAndRestore` round trip still holds. The log line now reads `Restored RCS emissions for N of M modules from recorded power`. Tests: `GhostFxSmokeAndRcsRestoreTests`. Live proof (E0 spike harness on the fix, throwaway branch): PPS-8a `2026-11-22_2253` `U2 ghost reach rcsblock-v2: productionPath alive=33 renderersOn=4` (before `alive=0 renderersOn=0`), `rcsblock-01-small` `alive=35 renderersOn=4`; on ReStock (modded-compat) PPS-8b `2026-11-22_2259` both blocks `alive=48 renderersOn=8` (before `alive=0 renderersOn=0`). Evidence: `<umbrella>/logs/flights/ghost-fx-fixes/`.

## ~~GHOST-SMOKE-IN-VACUUM~~: a ghost engine draws its smoke trail in vacuum, where stock hides it [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part parity P8 E0 spike (`docs/dev/design-part-ghost-parity.md` E.12 U8; PPS-8a `2026-11-22_2144`, PPS-8c `2026-11-22_2149`); FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-fixes`; low (visual only)]

What: in orbit the real stock legacy engines (LV-T45, LV-T30, Hammer, nuclear engine) keep their `fx_smokeTrail_*` particle system playing but with its renderer disabled, so no smoke is drawn (no smoke coverage in the sweep camera on any of the four stock legacy engines tried). Their ghosts draw the trail: `fx-far` smoke core 9832 px on the LV-T45 ghost and 27120 px on the Hammer ghost, 0 on the real sides. In the air (1600 m over KSC) the real smoke draws and the ghost's matches it in placement (the Hammer's trails differ in length only). The ghost RAPIER drew an alpha-blended smoke trail too, a separate cause (GHOST-RAPIER-AIR-SMOKE-SUBSTITUTE).

Stock rule (decompiled `SmokeTrailControl.Update`, KSP 1.12.5, a MonoBehaviour on every legacy `fx_smokeTrail_*` prefab): each flight frame `airDensity = Mathf.InverseLerp(fadeEndDns, fadeStartDns, (float)FlightGlobals.ship_dns)` (defaults 0.001362253 / 0.06089431, about 34 km / 15 km on Kerbin); above 0.001 it writes the material's `_TintColor` (white with alpha `Lerp(0, maxAlpha, airDensity)`, or a per-channel lerp from `fadedColor` to `maxAlpha` when `fadeToColor`) and enables the renderer, otherwise it disables the renderer. The ghost build stripped the component (`StripKspFxControllers`), because its `ship_dns` is the ACTIVE vessel's density, so nothing faded the ghost's trail.

Fix: the strip now captures each `SmokeTrailControl`'s own values and renderer into `EngineGhostInfo.smokeTrailFades`, and `GhostPlaybackLogic.UpdateEngineSmokeTrailFades` (last call of `ApplyFrameVisuals`' unsuppressed branch) applies the same rule from the air density at the ghost's own playback altitude (`lastInterpolatedBodyName` / `lastInterpolatedAltitude`, the body's base pressure and temperature curves, as reentry FX use). It returns at once unless an engine with a captured fade is lit; density is cached per 10 m; the tint and renderer are written only when a 32-level quantized fade changes; an emission write (`SetEngineEmissionWithOutcome`) and `RestoreGhostFidelity` re-hide a trail the fade hid; the material instance the first tint write makes is registered in `state.materials`. KSC playback does not run the fade (its smoke is unchanged). Tests: `GhostFxSmokeAndRcsRestoreTests`. Live proof (E0 spike harness on the fix, throwaway branch): orbit PPS-8a `2026-11-22_2253` ghost `fx-far` smoke core16 0 px on LV-T45, Hammer, nuclear engine, LV-T30 and RAPIER (before 9832 / 27120 / 9959 px); air PPS-8c `2026-11-22_2256` (1600 m, density 1.007) the Hammer ghost still draws, core16 28867 px (before 28287, real 36658); ReStock PPS-8b `2026-11-22_2259` stock-model engines read 0 px too. The ReStock Hammer's `restock-fx-srb-smoke-1` carries no `SmokeTrailControl` and its real renderer stays ON in orbit (U5 `rend=True`), so it is not this rule; its orbit difference (ghost 7106 px, real near 0) is the Krakensbane shear of E.12 U8. Evidence: `<umbrella>/logs/flights/ghost-fx-fixes/`.

Not fixed here: the ghost RAPIER's air smoke (GHOST-RAPIER-AIR-SMOKE-SUBSTITUTE, fixed 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-rapier-smoke`). It was Parsek's own `fx_smokeTrail_large` substitute for the RAPIER's additive trail; the fade above covered only the substitute, so the real trail's own fade component is handled there.

## ~~GHOST-RAPIER-AIR-SMOKE-SUBSTITUTE~~: the ghost RAPIER drew a grey smoke trail instead of the RAPIER's own additive trail [FILED 2026-11-23 from GHOST-SMOKE-IN-VACUUM's PPS-8c re-flight `2026-11-22_2256`; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-rapier-smoke`; low (visual only)]

What: `EngineFxBuilder` stripped the RAPIER's `fx_smokeTrail_aeroSpike` entry (named by both modes' EFFECTS, `rapierEngine.cfg`) and drew an alpha-blended `fx_smokeTrail_large` on its place. On ReStock, where that tuning stands down, the `fxPrefabFallbacks` alias `fx_smokeTrail_aeroSpike -> fx_smokeTrail_large` did the same unless a live RAPIER had put the real asset in the loaded-objects scan (PPS-8d `2026-11-22_2154` ghost drew the exact asset, PPS-8b `_2259` the substitute).

Misread corrected: the entry used to say stock's RAPIER draws no smoke trail in the air (PPS-8c real `smoke` core16 0 px, ghost 33635). It does: the real `fx_smokeTrail_aeroSpike` (104 particles alive, renderer on) has shader `KSP/Particles/Additive (Soft)`, so the spike's layer split files it under `flame`, and 0 px in the `smoke` layer only says no ALPHA-BLENDED trail. Owner ruling: drop the stand-in, match stock.

Fix: the RAPIER's own trail loads stock's exact builtin `Effects/fx_smokeTrail_aeroSpike` (`GhostVisualBuilder.FindBuiltinEffectsPrefab`, a RAPIER-only lookup; the shared `TryResolveFxPrefabExact` has no `Effects/` and the alias still serves other parts, e.g. the RestockWaterfallExpansion jets), on identity rotation as stock `PrefabParticleFX.OnInitialize` does (the exhaust re-aim turned it sideways on ReStock, the 2026-02 "dark, perpendicular" report behind the substitute), without the #383 size boost. The white-flame fallback and its anchor are unchanged (`TryAddRapierWhiteFlame`). The asset fades by `FXFadeByPressure`, not `SmokeTrailControl` (the only prefab that does): stock's component reads the active vessel's density and switches the renderer, so `StripKspFxControllers` captures its thresholds as a visibility-only fade and `UpdateEngineSmokeTrailFades` drives it from the ghost's own altitude. Tests: `EngineFxBuilderTests` (own trail, never the substitute, white flame). Emission scaling is not copied (stock scales the rate by the config curve with power).

Live proof (E0 spike harness on the fix, throwaway branch, DLL sha256 prefix eeb3b147, evidence `<umbrella>/logs/flights/ghost-rapier-smoke/`): stock air PPS-8c `2026-11-23_0646`, core16 px real / ghost, flame side-a 32550 / 38237 (before 32705 / 6312), far 3520 / 5635 (before 3433 / 105), bottom 27846 / 30153 (before 27854 / 7832); smoke 0 / 0 in every view (before ghost 22154 / 33635 / 29213). The trail runs along the exhaust and in the real trail's colour. Orbit PPS-8a `_0648` and PPS-8b `_0654`: `Smoke trail fade: ... density=0 drawn=0 hidden=1`, ghost renderer off as on the real side. ReStock air PPS-8d `_0651`: the ghost trail is straight along the exhaust (before, sideways) and the ghost resolves the exact asset; smoke 0 / 0. In PPS-8a / 8b the active vessel is at the ghost's altitude, so those lanes prove capture and hiding, not the wrong-vessel case.

Left open: GHOST-RAPIER-TRAIL-EXTENT.

## ~~GHOST-RAPIER-TRAIL-EXTENT~~: the ghost RAPIER's trail is longer and wider than the real one in the air [FILED 2026-11-23 from PPS-8c `2026-11-23_0646`; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `ghost-fx-3` (GHOST-ENGINE-FX-STOCK-RULES); low (visual only)]

Cause and fix: the real trail keeps its world scale on a part rescaled 1.25 (local scale 0.8; the ghost's was 1), emits by the config curve and loses part of every frame's emission to stock's per-step `Play()`. Flight `2026-11-23_1201`: far flame core 26946 real / 27338 ghost, length 1.00, width 1.01.

Far view, logged flame extents: ghost rows 31-258 and columns 236-275 against real 31-219 and 239-272 (about 21 % longer, 18 % wider; inside P8's 25 % / 30 % fail limits, over its warn limits). 131 ghost trail particles alive against 104 real. The prefab (`resources.assets`, lifetime 1 to 2 s, rate 90, speed 30) alone does not explain it and the cause is not established; the config's `emission` / `speed` curves, which stock applies every frame and the ghost does not, are the first suspect. On a RestockWaterfallExpansion install the real RAPIER's spool trail uses that pack's own offset, speed and lifetime (`RapierRWE.cfg`), while the ghost uses ReStock's, so its trail is shorter and fatter there.


## ~~PARITY-RESTOCK-MASK-ROOT-PART~~: the part parity sweep photographed ReStock depth masks as opaque cyan discs on the real part [FILED 2026-11-22 from PP-2 `2026-11-22_0045_PP-2-part-parity-modded` (86 x `Module ModuleRestockDepthMask threw during OnStart: System.NullReferenceException` at `Component.get_gameObject` <- `UpdateAllMaterials`, 59 cases capped at warn `depth-mask`); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `part-parity-restock-mask`; low (automation-only; the real side of 74 modded cases was not the part a player sees)]

What: on the ReStock install the REAL picture of every part with a `ModuleRestockDepthMask` (intakes, jets, RCS blocks, claws, InfraredTelescope, ...) showed the mask mesh with its authored placeholder material, so those cases compared a cyan disc against the ghost (which skips masks by owner ruling 2026-11-22) and were capped at warn.

Root cause (not Parsek): every sweep case vessel is ONE part, so the case part is the vessel's ROOT part. Stock `ProtoPartSnapshot.Load(vesselRef, loadAsRootPart: true)` (decompiled, KSP 1.12.5, `<umbrella>/logs/decompile/2026-11-22-restock-mask/ProtoPartSnapshot.cs`) instantiates the prefab, moves the clone's children under the vessel's GameObject, adds a fresh `Part` and fresh modules there (`part.AddModule(moduleName)`), copies every public field across by reflection, sets `part.partTransform = vesselRef.transform`, and `ConfigurePart` then `DestroyImmediate`s the clone (`rootPartPrefab`). ReStock resolves `bodyTransformObject` only in `OnLoad` at part compilation, and every ReStock patch leaves `bodyTransform` empty, so it is the part's own transform: the copied reference names the destroyed clone root (the mask transforms survive, they were reparented). The sweep's own diagnostic proved it on all 74 cases: `live: body=destroyed masks=[in-part] shader=alive prefab: body=in-part masks=[in-part] shader=alive`. Ruled out: Parsek touching the prefab (the prefab module is intact in every case, the first throw precedes any ghost build of that part, no Parsek patch on part loading), KSPCF (FastLoader, FasterPartFindTransform, MemoryLeaks, PartParsingPerf read; none changes this path).

Normal play (ReStock's defect, reported here only): any vessel whose ROOT part carries a ReStock depth mask shows the cyan mask whenever it is loaded from its saved state (scene change, quickload, switching to it, coming into physics range), for example a spent stage whose root is an RCS block or a jet, a claw-rooted probe, or a Parsek spawn of such a recording. A part that is not the root keeps its live clone and works. Nothing in Parsek causes or can fix it short of patching ReStock; the upstream fix is to resolve the transforms in `OnStart`.

Fix (sweep only, `Source/Parsek/TestCommands/PartParityDepthMaskRepair.cs`, design `docs/dev/design-part-ghost-parity.md` 4.2 step 0): before the real renderers are read, every module whose name contains `DepthMask` is checked by reflection (no compile-time reference to ReStock); when its body or a mask is not a live transform under the part, or its shader is dead, the transforms are resolved on the live part as the module's own `OnLoad` does and its `UpdateAllMaterials` re-runs. One `[PartParity]` summary line per such case (Warn when a module stayed unrepaired); sidecar flags `depth-mask-repaired:<count>` and `depth-mask-unrepaired:<count>`. A module that stays unrepaired (missing members, no mask or shader on the live part, a throwing re-run) makes the case the setup fault `depth-mask-unrepaired` (an `error`, C# `TestCommandPartParitySweep.SetupDepthMaskUnrepaired` and Python `SETUP_DEPTH_MASK_UNREPAIRED`), never a ghost fail. The `depth-mask` warn cap is dropped from `harness/lib/partparity.py`. The module's `onVariantApplied` / `onPartRepaired` handlers (which would requeue the ghost once it is parented under the part) cannot fire during capture: a module repaired for a dead transform threw before subscribing them, and `PartParityDepthMaskEventGateTests` reds on a capture-path file naming either event, `SetVariant` or `ApplyVariant`. Pure logic in `PartParityDepthMaskRepairTests`.

Proof: PP-2 `2026-11-22_1157_PP-2-part-parity-modded_run2` PASS attempt 1 (automation DLL sha256 prefix 5b83e100): the repair line fired on all 74 cases (86 modules, matching the 86 throws), and the 59 formerly capped cases all pass on their pictures; the lane read 1510 cases pass 1458 / warn 50 / fail 2 (was 1392 / 115 / 3). The flown build re-checked the repaired mask shader by name and so logged `airScoop` (shader `Depth Mask`) as `not-depth-shaded` though its pictures pass; that post-run check is gone (the update sets the shader or throws). The review follow-ups (that change, the `depth-mask-unrepaired` setup fault, both flag counts, the Warn line, the event gate) are unflown. PP-1 not re-flown: no stock part has a depth-mask module (the repair returns before touching anything) and the stock run `_0033` had no `depth-mask` entry, so removing the cap changes no stock verdict.

## ~~SEAM-ENDPOINT-LENS-FORBID-ON-PHASE-LOCKED-MOON-LOOPS~~: player-loop lanes forbid an outside-SOI seam reading that a phase-locked moon replay produces by design [FILED 2026-11-22 from GS-13's first flight, run 2026-11-22_0456; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `seam-lens` (the oracle, not the specs); low (latent lane red, no product defect)]

GS-13-mun-v3-chain-loop-replay's first flight raised `seam-endpoint-outside-soi` once (Kerbin->Mun seam, ratio 1.0526 against `SeamEndpointOracle.DefaultRatioTolerance` 1.005, `clock=baked seed=faithful-seed loopShift=280142.5`). Root cause (read-only investigation, verified in the log): a same-parent moon transfer replays faithful (`factory chain ... reaimed=False`) under PhaseLock (`PhaseLock APPLIED ... zeroDrift=yes`), and its cadence leaves the Mun a phase residual by design: 280142.527 s minus two Mun periods is 2173.8 s (5.63 deg, about 1179 km, 0.485 of the SOI), inside `MissionPeriodicity.ToleranceSecondsFor` (SOI / Mun speed, about 4478 s) per `docs/dev/done/plans/zero-drift-reschedule.md`. The oracle's 1.005 is calibrated for re-aimed arcs (its own comment says faithful loop replays read higher). Split rule version 3 only made the lens reachable: the transfer piece now starts before the SOI seam, so the hand-off frame lands on the pre-seam conic and the lens measures (`evaluated=1`); V6M's `outsideSoi=0` is a lens that never measured (`evaluated=0 ... skip.no-cross-body-successor=1`).

Lane census (re-read on origin/main c01fe82f8): the outside-SOI forbid sits on V6M-mun-player-loop, V7M-minmus-player-loop, V14M-ike-player-loop and V21M-mun-minmus-player-loop. V4-player-loop-workflow carries no such forbid (its header names `outsideSoi=[1-9]` only as an unflown inversion control), and V8F-eve-loop-faithful REQUIRES raises (Sun->Eve 47.5-203.2, Kerbin->Mun 4.80), all far above the widest faithful tolerance (2.005), so the fix cannot move it.

Fix: `SeamEndpointOracle.ResolveRatioTolerance` gives a FAITHFUL seed (the Director's seed is the covering recorded segment) read on the shifted `baked` clock the destination's bounded PhaseLock residual: residual = `MissionPeriodicity.CircularPhaseError(seamUT - recordedSeamUT, destination orbit period)` (the shift the clock mapping applied), bound = `MissionPeriodicity.ToleranceSecondsFor` of the destination's Orbital constraint (SOI / mean orbital speed, the band PhaseLock schedules inside), tolerance = `DefaultRatioTolerance + residual x speed / SOI` when residual <= bound. A faithful seed outside the band (`faithful-unlocked`), one on a `raw` / `assumed-live` clock (`faithful-unshifted-clock`: the conic was not moved by the shift, so there is no residual; the creation-frame raw readings stay visible), one with no body data, a re-aimed seed and a seedless or non-loop sample keep 1.005 unchanged. The oracle stays primitive-only (naming Missions types put it in the type knot, `test_archview` 437 -> 439); `MapRenderProbe.ResolveSeamRatioTolerance` reads period / speed / SOI through `FlightGlobalsBodyInfo` and the band through `ToleranceSecondsFor`; the `seam-endpoint-outside-soi` line now carries `tolSource=` and `phaseResidual=`, and a reading the default would have raised that the allowance absorbs prints `seam-endpoint phase-lock allowance: ... ratio= tol= tolSource=phase-lock phaseResidual=` (Verbose, rate-limited per pid). GS-13's numbers: residual 2173.7 s, tolerance about 1.4904, ratio 1.0526 passes. Unit: `SeamEndpointOracleTests.FaithfulSeed_*` / `ReaimedSeed_KeepsTheDefaultUnchanged`. GS-13 restores the forbid and requires the allowance line; V6M's header no longer claims a phase-locked moon replay has no drift. Live proof 2026-11-22 (automation DLL sha256 prefix cd638021): GS-13 `2026-11-22_1215` PASS attempt 1 with `seam-endpoint phase-lock allowance: ... ratio=1.0526 tol=1.4904 tolSource=phase-lock phaseResidual=2173.8s` and census `evaluated=1 outsideSoi=0`; V6M `_1220`, V7M `_1221`, V14M `_1222`, V21M `_1222`, V4 `_1224` and V8F `_1225` all PASS attempt 1 (V8F's required raises unchanged: Sun->Eve at `tolSource=default`, Kerbin->Mun 4.8024 at `tolSource=faithful-unlocked`, residual 58763.9 s).

## ~~OPTIMIZER-SPLITS-LIVE-REFLY-PROVISIONAL~~: the split pass cut a NotCommitted Re-Fly provisional once the marker was gone [FILED 2026-11-22 (lane RF-12W, run 2026-11-22_0423, PARSEK-FAIL(expectation)); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `rsr-lane-repins`; medium (a session's provisional loses its terminal to an unnamed row)]

Symptom: RF-12W's `KerbalRecoveryOnSupersede` skipped with "Provisional ... is not a valid supersede target (null TerminalState)". The in-game test `JournalFinisherMarkerPresentVariant` runs the merge-journal finisher against the live session; the finisher clears the marker and runs the optimizer pass, and with the marker gone the pass's `deferredActiveReFlyId` deferral no longer covered the provisional, which was still NotCommitted. Split rule version 3 (stamped on the Re-Fly provisional) cuts it at its atmosphere exit, and the split moves the terminal state, crew end states and VesselDestroyed onto a fresh-id second half that neither the marker nor the supersede commit names. The last pass of the lane (2026-11-17, before version 3) made no cut.

Fix: `RecordingOptimizer.FindSplitCandidatesForOptimizer` keeps every NotCommitted recording whole (one Verbose summary `kept N NotCommitted recording(s) whole`), mirroring `MergeInto`'s NotCommitted refusal and ERS's NotCommitted skip; such a recording is cut on a later pass once its merge commits it. The Re-Fly splitter (`RecordingTreeSplitter`, which calls `SplitAtUT` directly) is unaffected. Unit: `RecordingOptimizerTests.FindSplitCandidatesForOptimizer_NotCommittedRecording_KeptWhole`. Live proof: RF-12W re-flown on the fixed DLL.

## ~~TEST-ISOLATION-FLAKES-2026-11-21~~: two xUnit facts failed in filtered runs on state an earlier class left behind [FILED 2026-11-21 (both green in the full suite, red in some filtered subsets); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `rsr-test-flakes`; test-only, no production change; low (test noise only)]

What (1): `MergeDialogTests.RunOptimizationPass_NoRecordings_NoFlushLog` assumes an empty committed list, but `MergeDialogTests` had no setup reset and `RecordingStoreTests` reset only in its constructor, so the last `RecordingStoreTests` fact's committed recordings were still in `RecordingStore` when the next class ran. Reproduced with `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~RecordingStoreTests|FullyQualifiedName~MergeDialogTests"` (the preceding fact was `SanitizeNonLoopableLoopPlayback_LeavesLoopableAlone`; the optimizer pass flushed its dirty recordings and the `FlushDirtyFiles` line failed `Assert.DoesNotContain`). Several `MergeDialogTests` facts also seed the store without clearing it.

What (2): `ParsekScenarioOnLoadStepOrderTests.InSessionSpaceCenterLoad_CommitThrows_KeepsTheScheduledRestore` patches the ghost-only commit route to throw, which a headless load takes only while `ParsekScenario.IsAutoMerge` reads off. With no settings installed that getter returns the process-lifetime cache `ParsekScenario.cachedAutoMerge`, which it also latches on every read of a real settings instance. `MergeFlowDecisionTests`' `AutoMerge(true)` facts latched it ON; their Dispose nulled `ParsekSettings.CurrentOverrideForTesting` but not the cache, so the next load took the full-fidelity route, the prefix never threw and the `[ERROR][Scenario] ... threw InvalidOperationException` line was missing. Reproduced with `--filter "FullyQualifiedName~MergeFlowDecisionTests|FullyQualifiedName~ParsekScenarioOnLoadStepOrderTests"`.

Fix: `RecordingStoreTests` resets the store in a Dispose too, and `MergeDialogTests` resets it in a constructor and a Dispose. `MergeFlowDecisionTests.ResetAll` also calls `ParsekScenario.SetCachedAutoMergeForTesting(false)` (the leaker; that line alone turns the second filter green), and `ParsekScenarioOnLoadStepOrderTests.ResetStatics` pins the same cache off, because every `new ParsekSettings()` defaults `autoMerge` to true and 14 other test files install one. The cache stays out of the session reset by design (`scripts/session-reset-allowlist.txt`).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-REPLAY~~: the replay of a stage the player stopped watching: falls to the ground, chutes, crew, final orbits, takeovers, stock's fate (owner rulings 2026-11-18 / 2026-11-21) [FILED 2026-11-18 by the review "Simulated flight after switching away" (`docs/handoff/abandoned-stage-replay/`, code read at main e705fc5); SCOPE ruling 2026-11-21: fix every finding (D1, C1, B1-B12, B14, P1, R1-R4 and the lower-impact list L1-L9); BUILT 2026-11-21 on the integration branch `abandoned-stage-replay` (work packages on `asr-*` branches, one closed entry per finding below, review C and the two final reviews closed in ABANDONED-STAGE-STOCK-FATE and ABANDONED-STAGE-FINAL-REVIEWS), xUnit; lanes ASR-1..ASR-7 and ASR-9 (ASR-FINAL-FLIGHT-2026-11-21); OPEN: the follow-ups from ABANDONED-STAGE-REALCHUTE-LOADED on]

Contract: `docs/parsek-recording-finalization-design.md` (Behavior, Consumer Paths, Edge Cases 8-10, 16 and 26-39). Stock fact (decompiled `Vessel.cs`, KSP 1.12.5): a packed, non-active vessel that is not landed or splashed and is outside the active vessel's pack range is deleted with its crew killed (`MurderCrew`) when `mainBody.GetPressure(altitude) > 1.0` kPa; an unloaded vessel below the terrain is deleted too; this runs only in FLIGHT (`Vessel.CheckKill` needs an active vessel), and it fires no terminal event. "The deletion line" below is that 1 kPa altitude of the body (about 25 km on Kerbin), not the atmosphere top.

Current owner rulings (V, 2026-11-18 review cards and 2026-11-21 in-session; a later ruling replaces the one it names):

| Id | Date | Ruling |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q1a | 2026-11-18 | After KSP deletes an ignored stage in the air, the replay keeps falling to where it would hit. |
| Q1b | 2026-11-18 | If KSP still has the stage, save the predicted crash anyway; if the player flies it again, drop the prediction and record it for real. |
| Q2 | 2026-11-18 | A predicted fall ends with the explosion at ground / water impact, not at the deletion height. |
| Q3 | 2026-11-18 | A grazing orbit crashes only if its low point is below the deletion line, on the first pass; otherwise it stays Orbiting and spawns. |
| Q4 | 2026-11-18 | A stage left with parachutes open descends at chute speed and ends Landed / Splashed where it comes down. |

| Q4d | 2026-11-21 ~20:25 | Replaces Q4b. A chuted craft stock deletes (crew killed) is recorded as stock decided: Destroyed, crew dead, nothing spawned. Its ghost descends under its chutes and ends quietly at the ground (no explosion). The Re-Fly offer stays (Q4c). A chuted craft stock still has keeps Landed / Splashed + spawn. |
| Q5 | 2026-11-18 | No drag: predicted falls stay a plain Kepler arc. |
| Q6b | 2026-11-21 | Breakup: crew die only if KSP destroyed the part they were in; a capsule that survives as its own piece keeps them alive. |

Any recovery of the launch-matched vessel overrides a predicted Destroyed, before or after its predicted UT (the vessel survived, P-STOCK); a predicted touchdown yields only to a recovery before the touchdown; a confirmed crash stays final. |

A predicted touchdown stays only for an in-flight commit after which the player keeps flying (the stock-fate pass then follows stock). |

| L2 | 2026-11-21 | Above 10x warp a crashing ghost plays its explosion when it is close enough to be seen; a far ghost just ends. |
| L5 | 2026-11-21 | A gap over 30 s before the predicted path: the ghost slides across it, no freeze, no jump. |
