| R4c | 2026-11-24 | "A dropped stage's predicted fall plays in mission loops but does not count toward loop timing." Timing (span, cadence, overlap cap, Auto, first-play floor, period snapping, the KSC / Tracking Station clock, the supply-route clock and origin span) reads the recorded span: the latest non-predicted UT over the members. In flight the fall plays to its impact, overlapping the next launches and its own next copies; copies past the 20 cap end quietly, the cadence is never raised. KSC and the Tracking Station draw one copy, cut at the next relaunch. Same for a recording with no tail, spawns, first runs and R4b as before. |
| P-STOCK | 2026-11-21 ~20:15 | Parsek's committed endings and crew outcomes must not contradict stock's background simulation; no live-game override. |
| P-LEAVE | 2026-11-21 ~20:25 | Stock warns that leaving flight in the atmosphere loses the vessel, so a predicted crash with crew dead at commit agrees with stock; a prediction stock later contradicts (vessel alive after the crash UT) is dropped like a Q1b takeover. Q9 (make the live game match) is CLOSED by P-STOCK / Q4d / P-LEAVE. |

Interpretations taken without asking (micro-choices): the periapsis floor (`OrbitClearance`, operator ruling 2026-09-27 "any orbit Parsek calls Orbiting will spawn" kept) is max(deletion line, highest terrain), read by commit, inference, finalizer and spawn safety alike; an arc whose low point is below the line but above the ground ends Destroyed at its first periapsis; a bound FLYING coast clear of the floor is a stable orbit; the horizon cap is 50 Kerbin years; a final orbit ends after a 60 s settle span on it; a Sun hyperbola ends SubOrbital and spawns on its path (ruling Q10, SPAWN-ESCAPE-TRAJECTORY-NEVER-SPAWNS); a member a quickload finds dropped is never made spawnable; an airless orbit grazing the peaks that stock keeps on rails is taken back from a predicted crash to SubOrbital (P-STOCK); a craft seen in the game after the commit that later vanishes with no recovery, termination or merge row was deleted by stock (P-STOCK); the stock-fate pass runs in FLIGHT only, because stock deletes nothing anywhere else.

New persisted markers, all additive (no format or generation bump, absent = false / old behaviour): `terminalPredicted`, `terminalRemnantSurvives`, `quietEnd`, `stockHeldUT` and the `RECOVERED_CREW` child node on the recording, and `TrackSectionSource.Predicted` (= 3) on a track section.

## ~~LOOP-TIMING-READ-THE-PREDICTED-FALL~~: a looped mission's span, period and supply-route clock included a dropped stage's predicted fall [FILED + FIXED 2026-11-24 from GS-12 `2026-11-23_2013` (PARSEK-FAIL), branch `loop-timing-predicted-falls`, owner ruling R4c; xUnit `MissionLoopFallTimingTests`, `LoopFallPlaybackTests`, `LoopFallEndTests`, `RouteBackingMissionTests`, `RouteBuilderTests`; lanes GS-12 (re-cut) and LF-3 (new) FLOWN GREEN `2026-11-24_0228`]

**Seen:** since ABANDONED-STAGE-D1 a dropped stage keeps its predicted fall (minutes, days, or the 50-year horizon), and the loop unit took its span from the members' drawn ends: GS-12's 150 s loop of a 110 s flight read `span 109.86 -> 301.46`, `cadence=305` instead of 150, and the 5 s stage was raised to 20 s by span/20. The same span set the first-play floor (a loop waited for the fall to end), the Space Center and Tracking Station clock, a supply route's cadence, and refused a shuttle route whose dropped stage's fall outlived a dock (`origin-span-mismatch`).
**Fix:** `PredictedEndingTakeover.ResolveRecordedEndUT` (Recording module) is the one reading of "last non-predicted UT": the recording's end when it has no predicted tail (an explicit end past the last sample stays recorded time), else the last real sample, section or non-predicted orbit segment. Every tail shape is a predicted orbit segment (a fall, an escape followed to its final orbit with the settle span, a ground-scan or horizon cap, a predicted coast that stays up), a predicted track section (a chute descent), or a predicted Destroyed end UT with no segment; a piece with predicted data only holds no recorded time. `MissionLoopUnitBuilder.ComputeTimingSpanEndUT` makes `LoopUnit.SpanEndUT` from it (window-clipped), so the cadences, the overlap cap, the floor, the periodicity windows (`ComputeTimingMemberWindows`), re-aim, the Missions period cell and the route clock follow with no change of their own; `MissionCompositionNode.TimingEndUT` does the same for the route's origin-span check and start trim. `LoopUnit.RenderSpanEndUT` carries the drawn end and the member windows keep their tails.
- Flight: a falling member of a uniform unit that does not overlap itself is drawn as one copy per launch on the unit's cadence (`UpdateUnitMemberFallSchedule`, over the existing overlap path), so it plays to its impact while the rest keeps its single span-clock copy; in a self-overlapping unit it is on that path already. `ResolveOverlapCadence(keepCadence)` never raises a fall's cadence, and copies past the 20 cap end with no explosion (`Fall copy ended quietly at the copy cap`, `MeshDestroyed ... reason=fall copy cap`). In a unit with a relaunch schedule, loiter cuts, holds or the descent trigger the fall plays on through the wait and an older cycle's fall is kept beside the next one (`UpdateNonUniformFall`); with the launch alignment engaged (re-aim), one copy, cut at the next relaunch, because the overlap list belongs to the boundary secondary there. The flight map draws the same copies (`LoopUnitSet.DrawsFallCopies`).
- Where a fall ends (review finding B1): a launch period longer than the fall leaves a gap with no copy. Once the newest launch's copy is past its own end (`HasOverlapCopyEnded`) it joins the overlap list, which expires it there with its ending (explosion, watch hold; `Fall copy reached its end before the next launch`), and its cycle is not drawn again, so the mesh and the flight map agree (`EndNewestFallCopy`; members and debris, and the Space Center's self-overlap path). Before that the copy was held at its end until the next launch, the wreck sliding on the ground and the explosion a period late. The watch clock stops following it too. The same ending applies to a member or debris of a self-overlapping unit whose predicted tail ends INSIDE the span (`EndsInPredictedTail`); one whose end is recorded keeps the old hold (OVERLAP-PRIMARY-HELD-PAST-ITS-RECORDED-END). Debris of a non-uniform unit whose fall ends in the wait gets its ending as well, where it vanished.
- High warp (review finding B2): above 50x `UpdateNonUniformFall` ends the older launches' copies and an older primary; they stayed alive, undriven and visible. A uniform fall whose copy ends while hidden is dropped instead of exploding after the warp (`DropEndedFallAtWarp`); the watched ghost is never dropped.
- A loop edited while its falls are in the air (review finding B3): the Missions window sets the period without re-stamping the loop anchor, so the rebuilt unit is live on the next frame and the old cycle numbers name other launches. A copy numbered above the newest launch had a negative phase and hung at the separation point for hours; on a shorter period one read as ended would have exploded on the edit frame. Every fall copy now carries its own clock (`GhostPlaybackState.fallClockOffsetUT`, the live UT of recorded UT 0 for its cycle); a copy whose clock moved more than 0.5 s, or whose cycle is above the newest launch (or equal to it beside the slot), ends quietly (`IsStaleFallCopy`, `Fall copy ended quietly the loop's schedule changed under it`, `MeshDestroyed ... reason=fall schedule changed`) and the new schedule draws its own copies. Uniform and non-uniform units, debris, self-overlapping units with a predicted end and the Space Center's self-overlap path; a rebuild that moves nothing (a trim, an unrelated commit, the same route schedule rebuilt) keeps every copy, and the first run's fall, on the real clock, is untouched. Fall copies an edit leaves with no path to drive them go too (`DropUndrivenFallCopies`). The flight map lists copies from the schedule alone, so it needed nothing. Copies with a recorded end keep the old demotion (a cycle above the newest is still clamped at its start there; see OVERLAP-PRIMARY-HELD-PAST-ITS-RECORDED-END).
- First run: a loop may now start while the first run's fall is still in the air; in flight that ghost keeps falling on the real clock beside the copies (`TryKeepFirstRunFall`), where the old floor waited for it. A scene load after the anchor does not redraw it.
- Debris: debris with a predicted tail past the span end plays to its impact in flight (per launch in a uniform unit, else through the wait to the next relaunch) and changes no timing; recorded debris past the span end is cut as before. KSC and the Tracking Station draw no loop debris.
- KSC / Tracking Station: the single copy plays its fall through the wait and the next relaunch cuts it (`TryExtendRenderIntoFall`). A self-overlapping unit keeps drawing one copy per launch there, falls included, as it did.
- Logs: `MissionLoopUnit:` keeps every token (`span` / `spanDur` / `cadence` / `overlapCadence` / `overlaps` now read the recorded span) and gains `renderSpanEnd= fallMembers= fallOverlaps=` only when a member falls past it; `missionconfig applied:` gains `renderSpanSeconds=`.

**Not changed (product questions, not decided here):** a copy whose end is recorded is still held at it between launches (OVERLAP-PRIMARY-HELD-PAST-ITS-RECORDED-END); the map and Tracking Station do not turn a looped predicted path with the planet (R4b covers the flight mesh and the KSC ghost), and a span-clock copy at KSC that ends inside the wait still ends with no explosion, as every span-clock member's end did.

## LOOP-FALL-KSC-TS-SINGLE-COPY: looped predicted falls at the Space Center, the Tracking Station and on the map are drawn less fully than in flight [FILED 2026-11-24 from LOOP-TIMING-READ-THE-PREDICTED-FALL's "KSC / Tracking Station" and "Not changed" notes; OPEN, product, low, for 1.0.4 or later]

Left open by owner ruling R4c (option C), which fixed loop timing and the flight scene:
- **Fall cut short:** in a loop that does not overlap itself, the Space Center and the Tracking Station draw one copy, and the next relaunch cuts its fall (`TryExtendRenderIntoFall`); in flight each launch's fall plays to its impact (`UpdateUnitMemberFallSchedule`). A self-overlapping loop draws one copy per launch there, falls included.
- **No explosion:** a span-clock copy at the Space Center whose fall ends inside the wait ends with no explosion. Every span-clock member's end did so before, so it is not new.
- **Map path:** the map and the Tracking Station do not turn a looped predicted path with the planet (R4b covers the flight mesh and the KSC ghost only).

Related: OVERLAP-PRIMARY-HELD-PAST-ITS-RECORDED-END (copies with a recorded end, built on `loop-own-end`, held for 1.0.4).

## OVERLAP-PRIMARY-HELD-PAST-ITS-RECORDED-END: in an overlapping loop a ghost with a RECORDED end is held at that end until the next launch [FILED 2026-11-24 from the review of LOOP-TIMING-READ-THE-PREDICTED-FALL; OPEN, owner question; low; RULED 2026-11-24 (owner): every copy ends at its own recorded end, as falls do, no parked landed copy; built on branch `loop-own-end`, HELD for 1.0.4, not in 1.0.3]

**Cause:** `UpdateOverlapPlayback` (and `ParsekKSC.UpdateOverlapKsc`) clamps its newest cycle's playback UT to the recording's end and only expires OLDER cycles, so a member, debris or standalone loop whose own length is shorter than the launch cadence stays drawn at its last frame until the next launch; in flight its explosion comes only then, the watch clock stays on it, and the flight map lists no copy meanwhile. Reachable in a self-overlapping mission for every stage or debris shorter than the period (GS-12 stage 1's shape before R4c: 57 s debris at a 150 s cadence). The code is the same on main before the branch (9559614ea); the archived GS-12 log starts its loop lines at stage 2 (cadence 30, under the debris' 57 s), so it shows none.
**Done:** recordings whose end is PREDICTED no longer do this (LOOP-TIMING-READ-THE-PREDICTED-FALL). Nothing changed for a recording without a predicted tail: R4c promises those stay as they were, so `SelfOverlappingDebris_EndsWhenPredicted_IsHeldWhenRecorded` / `SelfOverlappingMember_...` (`LoopFallEndTests`) pin the hold.
**Same path, same scope line:** raising the period of a self-overlapping mission leaves copies with a recorded end numbered above the newest launch; they are clamped at their start until the schedule reaches that number, as on main. Falls end quietly instead (LOOP-TIMING-READ-THE-PREDICTED-FALL, B3).
**Question for the owner:** should a copy with a recorded end also end at its end (explode or vanish) instead of standing there until the next launch? The change is to pass `endAtOwnEnd: true` at the remaining `UpdateOverlapPlayback` / `UpdateOverlapKsc` calls.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-D1~~: every ignored spent stage exploded in mid-air at the moment Parsek stopped watching it [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding D1, high, design); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-destroy` 14250a907, with c219f487e and 9d1694dd4; xUnit `BackgroundRecorderTests`, `RecordingFinalizationCacheProducerTests`; lanes ASR-1 / ASR-5 read the debris and the probe core ending at the ground; GS-8 / GS-9 re-pinned for the probe core's Destroyed ending 2026-11-23, branch `lane-repins-1023`; RF-14 re-pinned 2026-11-24 for the same ending (slot 1 promoted `crashed`, not `stableLeafUnconcluded`), branch `lane-repins3-1124`]

**Cause:** `ResolveBackgroundEndTerminalUT` (`BackgroundRecorder.Finalization.cs`) returned min(predicted terminal UT, close UT) for a Destroyed ending, so a debris time limit, unload, parent close or warp cut the tail to the close (GS-7: a 20 ms tail), and the design's edge case 16 said so.
**Fix:** a background close (debris time limit, unload, parent close, confirmed destruction) keeps the cache's Destroyed / Landed / Splashed terminal UT when it is at or after the close, so the tail runs to impact. An Orbiting / SubOrbital ending is kept too when the cache carries a predicted segment past the close (a Q8 final orbit, c219f487e from review A); when an ending is pulled back to the close the cache's far `TerminalOrbit` is dropped so the applier stamps the last retained segment's orbit. The switch-close stamp passes `retainPredictedTailPastEnd=false`, so a tail never overlaps the continuation. A close after an ending the cache already predicted (a deletion Parsek did not see) is clamped to that ending (9d1694dd4).

## ~~PARENT-ANCHORED-TAIL-HIDDEN-IN-FLIGHT~~: a dropped stage's ghost was hidden for its whole predicted fall in flight and ended with no explosion [FILED 2026-11-23 from the release flights on main 08445c153 (GS-8 `2026-11-23_0840`, GS-9 `2026-11-23_0850`); high (rulings Q1a / Q2 did not hold for the stages they were written for); FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `predicted-tail-flight`; xUnit `ParentAnchoredPredictedTailTests`; FLOWN 2026-11-23 on GS-8 `2026-11-23_1119` and GS-9 `2026-11-23_1133`, every fall token met (both red only on the live-at-quit pins, widened since and not re-flown); GS-7 `2026-11-23_1119` and GS-6 `2026-11-23_1129` PASS with their tails drawn]

**Seen:** the ghost of a parent-anchored recording is hidden from the frame its recorded sections end and stays hidden until its recording ends, although the recording carries a predicted tail (ABANDONED-STAGE-D1).
- GS-8, dropped probe core `728e31c5` (sections end 298.42, predicted segment 298.43-616.52, Destroyed): drawn as `Predicted-tail orbit playback ... ut=298.30`, then `recorded-relative-retired: reason=parent-anchored-debris-outside-relative-coverage coverageReason=no-covering-section ... playbackUT=298.44` every frame to the quit at UT 329; `engine-frame-iter` goes from `out:vis=T ... zone=Physics rdist=25m` to `out:vis=F retired=T zone=Physics rdist=35m`, beside the watched ghost.
- GS-9, core `e4dead26` (predicted segment 140.32-331.64): the same from UT 140.34, at rdist=126m, in both cycles. GS-6 `2026-11-23_0842` (PASS): the same on its core from UT 235.82.
- All six boosters (both lanes): hidden from about UT 112.4-114.6 to their impact (114.3-123.3), then `MeshDestroyed reason=parent-anchored debris outside relative coverage at endpoint`; no explosion at any impact (the only `ExplosionFx` lines are two nose cones destroyed at about UT 67 in each replay).

**Cause:** `DebrisRelativePlaybackPolicy.ShouldRetireFromDiagnostic` retires on `no-covering-section`, a predicted tail lies past every track section, and `GhostPlaybackEngine.RenderInRangeGhost` / `PositionGhostAtRecordingEndpoint` (and the loaded-position, loop, watch and world-position paths) asked it BEFORE the orbit-tail dispatch (`ShouldUseOrbitTailPlayback`). The rule predates the predicted tails and keys on `ParentAnchorRecordingId != null`, so it covered debris and controlled-decoupled children alike, the population of ABANDONED-STAGE-D1. `ParsekKSC` and `GhostMapPresence.StateVectors` were never affected: they ask the policy only with a covering Relative section in hand, and KSC dispatches the tail first. The ASR lanes read the recorded data and never replay in flight, so nothing saw it.
**Fix:** the engine wrapper every flight caller goes through, `ShouldRetireParentAnchoredDebrisOutsideRecordedRelativeCoverage` (and its `ShouldSkipRecordedRelativeResolver...` twin), no longer retires a UT past the last track section that the recording's own predicted tail draws (`IsInAcceptedPredictedTail`, diagnostic reason `covered-by-predicted-tail`). It reads the dispatch's own finders (a predicted segment holding the UT, the bridged gap of up to 30 s before it, the L5 slide from a last point a section holds), so an accepted UT is never positioned from flat points. Unchanged and still retired: before the first section, between sections, inside a section its frames do not cover, past the tail's end, a recorded (non-predicted) segment, an empty parent id; loop-anchored chains keep their own path. The endpoint follows: its coverage UT is the tail's end, so the ghost is posed there and `TriggerExplosionIfDestroyed` runs. The tail's continuity blend no longer reads a flat point past a Relative section as lat/lon/alt for a parent-anchored recording (`MayAnchorContinuityOnFlatPoint`). New line `[Anchor] parent-anchored predicted tail: ... active=T` (Verbose, 5 s per recording), written after the frame's activation.
**Flown:** GS-8 `2026-11-23_1119` (the fix's DLL, MISSION-OK): nine `parent-anchored predicted tail` lines, all `active=T` (the six boosters from UT 112.24, the Probe at UT 298.38), six `Stock FXMonger.Explode` lines for the boosters (UT 113.84-122.58) each followed by `MeshDestroyed ... reason=playback completed`, no `recorded-relative-retired` past a last section, and `engine-frame-iter` reading `out:vis=T retired=F` for the Probe until the watch hold ended (UT 301.38; from there it is 226 km from the pad and hidden by the distance LOD, not retired). PARSEK-FAIL(expectation) on the live-at-quit pins alone: `ParsekFlight.OnDestroy` logged the Probe ghost's `reason=engine teardown` 0.5 s after `flushandquit: Application.Quit`, a line `2026-11-23_0840` never reached. GS-9 `2026-11-23_1133`: the same in both cycles (six explosions each, the Probe `active=T` at UT 140.86) and red on the same quit teardown alone. GS-7 `_1119` PASS (six boosters and the Probe explode) and GS-6 `_1129` PASS (six boosters, the Probe `active=T`); in none of the four does a booster or a Probe read `recorded-relative-retired` past its last section. Both lanes now allow exactly that line (GS-8 destroyLines 9 or 10, GS-9 15 or 16, Probe 1 or 2; any other destroy of that recording, or one before the quit line, reds).
**Gate:** GS-8 and GS-9 require the `active=T` line for the Kerbal X Probe (both cycles in GS-9) and exactly six `Stock FXMonger.Explode for ghost #<i> "Kerbal X Debris"` lines per replay, and forbid the endpoint-coverage ending of a booster; offline the two pre-fix logs above red on exactly those, the same logs rewritten to the fixed shape pass, and so do `_1119` and `_1133` as flown. No in-game cell: one in the `GhostPlayback` category moves the tallies of every lane that pins it.

## ~~DEBRIS-GHOST-HANGS-PAST-THE-SAMPLING-RANGE~~: a dropped booster's ghost hung in the air for half a minute, then jumped kilometres down to its fall [FILED 2026-11-23 from the GS-8 log `2026-11-23_0840` while fixing PARENT-ANCHORED-TAIL-HIDDEN-IN-FLIGHT; FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `debris-sampling-range`; FLOWN GS-8 `2026-11-23_1954`, GS-9 `2026-11-23_2007` PASS: 0 jump lines, 0 `interval=none`; xUnit `DebrisFallContinuityTests`, `VesselUnloadStateTests`, `ProximityRateSelectorTests`, `DebrisParentSamplingCeilingTests`, `BackgroundPhysicsFrameUnitsTests`]

**Seen:** booster `0e77736b`: the background recorder stopped sampling past 2.3 km (`Sample rate changed: ... dist=2304m interval=none`, last sample UT 78.92, alt 6026 m) while the vessel stayed loaded, and its Absolute section stayed open to UT 112.46 (`frames=38 duration=41.50s`), so the replay held the ghost at the last sample (`rdist=5953m` from UT 79 to 112), then moved it 4357 m in one frame onto the on-rails conic at UT 112.48 (alt 1672 m). The predicted tail that follows (UT 112.50-114.45) was extrapolated from the 78.92 sample, not from the conic's end (`recovered sub-surface live-orbit fallback ... pointUT=78.920`), so a second jump followed where the tail starts. All six boosters of that run share the shape. MEASURED with the tail drawn (GS-8 `2026-11-23_1119`, `AfterUpdate ... dM`): ghosts #2-#5 jumped 4.2-4.4 km onto the conic, then 0.95-1.01 km onto the tail 1-2 frames later; #6 jumped 4.1 km and 4.1 km, #7 3.9 km and 0.29 km. EVA-4 `2026-11-15_0948` shows the same silence over 131 s of a chute descent (UT 225.26-357.02).

**Cause, two halves:** (1) `ProximityRateSelector` had a silent band from 2.3 km, but stock simulates a flying vessel out to 22.5 km (`VesselRanges` flying: unload 22500, pack 25000; sub-orbital packs at 10000). (2) At 22.5 km stock unloads the booster without having packed it, so `onVesselGoOnRails` fires inside `Vessel.Unload()`, after the part list was cleared and before `SetLoaded(false)`: the vessel read loaded with no parts, `IsLiveVesselAlive` called it dead, and its good live conic was discarded for an extrapolation from the last recorded sample (todo UNLOAD-READ-AS-DESTRUCTION).
**Fix:** a loaded, unpacked vessel is sampled until it goes on rails. Past 2.3 km: floor 2 s (`FarInterval`), 1 s for parent-anchored debris (`BeyondRangeDebrisInterval`), ceiling the configured maximum, and the attitude trigger takes the motion floor (with the foreground floor a tumbling booster sampled every 0.215 s). A vessel parked on the surface out there rests after one sample (`ShouldRestSamplingBeyondRange`). The open Absolute section of a loaded vessel takes one closing frame where it ends: on rails, debris end, destruction, commit (`BuildSectionClosingFrame`). Mid-unload the vessel reads alive, so the tail is extrapolated from the live orbit the conic was cut from and starts where the conic ends. No format change; recordings made before this keep their shape.
**Cost:** GS-8's six boosters spent 33.7 / 33.7 / 33.2 / 33.4 / 32.6 / 32.6 s loaded past the range, so at most 200 extra samples and 6 closing frames per Kerbal X launch, about 5 KB per booster sidecar (14.6 KB before) and 30 KB per launch. A debris piece is bounded by its 60 s limit.
**Gate:** GS-8 and GS-9 forbid a frame that moves a ghost 100 m or more where its own speed predicts under 10 m (`phase=AfterUpdate ... reason=large-delta`); offline it matches exactly the 12 (`_1119`), 6 (`_0840`), 24 (`_1133`) and 12 (`_0850`) jumps of this defect and no other line. Not flown.

## ~~UNLOAD-READ-AS-DESTRUCTION~~: a craft stock unloaded while it flew, or that landed more than 2.5 km away, was read as destroyed, and its stored vessel lost every part [FOUND AND FIXED 2026-11-23 while fixing DEBRIS-GHOST-HANGS-PAST-THE-SAMPLING-RANGE, branch `debris-sampling-range`; FLOWN GS-8 `2026-11-23_1954`, GS-9 `2026-11-23_2007`, EVA-4 `2026-11-23_2015` PASS: mid-unload guard fires, 0 `identity lost` lines; xUnit `VesselUnloadStateTests`]

**Cause:** inside stock `Vessel.Unload()` the part list is cleared before `GoOnRails()` and `SetLoaded(false)` (decompiled), so the background recorder's `onVesselGoOnRails` handler met a vessel that reads loaded with no parts. Three readers took that for destruction: `IdentityLossClassifier.IsRecordedIdentityLost` sealed a controlled craft Destroyed at its unload (EVA-4 `2026-11-15_0440` and `_0948`: the pod touched down under its chute, `Jumping Flea Unloaded`, then `Recorded controllable identity lost on go-on-rails: ... survivingParts=0 sit=LANDED ... classifying as Destroyed`, which also judges its crew lost); `IsLiveVesselAlive` discarded its live conic; and `TryBackupSnapshot` called `BackupVessel()`, which rebuilds the protoVessel from the live parts, so stock's freshly taken snapshot was replaced by one with NO parts and the craft was saved empty. That last one is read off the code; the second refresh of every GS-8 booster, after the unload, still reading "not alive" (it needs proto parts > 0) agrees with it.
**Fix:** `VesselUnloadState.IsMidUnload` (stock's internal `isUnloading` flag, loaded, zero parts, a protoVessel with parts, not DEAD). The liveness read, the identity check and `RemnantSurvives` treat such a vessel as unloaded (its proto snapshots); `TryBackupSnapshot` reads its protoVessel and never calls `BackupVessel()`. A vessel whose last part really died (flag clear) reads exactly as before.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B1~~: a probe-cored stage KSP deleted out of range exploded where it was last seen [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B1, high); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-destroy` 14250a907; xUnit `RecordingFinalizationCacheProducerTests`, `BackgroundRecorderTests`]

**Cause:** the `background_destroy` refresh replaced the cache with "Destroyed now, no segments" and stamped the recording eagerly, so the confirmed-destruction apply was refused `RejectedAlreadyFinalized` (GS-10 / GS-11 logs: `eagerRecordingStamp=True`).
**Fix:** a destroy refresh of a packed, airborne vessel is a stock on-rails deletion: it runs the normal extrapolation, coerces the ending to Destroyed (a touchdown read as impact, no fall = Destroyed now), and skips the eager stamp; the recorder prefers the fresh fall, then the previous cache's fall, then Destroyed now. The confirmed apply lands the tail and sets `VesselDestroyed`. Loaded crashes are unchanged. A chuted craft is ABANDONED-STAGE-CHUTES (Q4d).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B3~~: a predicted fall that started above the air stopped at the atmosphere top [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B3, high); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `abandoned-stage-replay` 31832c443; xUnit `BallisticExtrapolatorTests`, `AbandonedStageDeletionAltitudeTests`, `SceneExitFinalizationIntegrationTests`]

**Fix:** `BallisticExtrapolator.FindLocalCutoff` has no atmosphere-top stop: surface impact first (`reason=surface-impact`), then the deletion periapsis (`reason=deletion-periapsis`). `ExtrapolationBody` carries `DeletionAltitude` and `PeriapsisFloorAltitude` (`TryBuildExtrapolationBodies`); the scene-exit re-entry clip and the horizon Orbiting downgrade read the floor (rulings Q2, Q5).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B5~~: an on-rails suborbital or escaping stage missing at commit was labelled Orbiting [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B5, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `abandoned-stage-replay` 31832c443; xUnit `RecordingFinalizationCacheProducerTests`, `OrbitClearanceRulingTests`]

**Fix:** `RecordingFinalizationCacheProducer.TryBuildFromStableOrbitSegment` checks the periapsis floor: an on-rails conic that is unbound or under the floor is extrapolated into a predicted tail and its real ending instead of a hard-coded Orbiting. `OrbitClearance` (floor = max(deletion line, highest terrain), `ComputeDeletionAltitude` bisection cached per body) is read by commit classification (`RecordingTree.IsBoundOrbitClearOfFloor`), spawn safety (`TerminalOrbitSpawnSafety.Evaluate`), the Re-Fly auto-seal preview, the finalizer and the cache.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B6~~: a vessel KSP only unloaded replayed as an explosion [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B6, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-destroy` 14250a907; xUnit `BackgroundRecorderTests`]

**Fix:** the false-destroy branch of `ParsekFlight.DeferredDestructionCheck` takes back a Destroyed stamp the destroy refresh wrote eagerly and drops that refresh's cache before the recorder re-attaches.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B8~~: a stage starting in the air with its low point above ground circled inside the atmosphere for 50 years [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B8, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `abandoned-stage-replay` 31832c443, 9475d9f35, 834f2bddc; xUnit `AbandonedStageDeletionAltitudeTests`, `AbandonedStageAccuracyTests`, `BallisticExtrapolatorTests`]

**Fix:** a low point between the deletion line and the ground ends Destroyed at the first periapsis pass (ruling Q3); one above the line is a stable orbit. `ShouldExtrapolate` reads the floor for bound ORBITING, SUB_ORBITAL (9475d9f35, no more horizon-cap Warn for a periapsis between the line and the atmosphere top) and FLYING coasts (834f2bddc: clear of the floor = not extrapolated, read Orbiting from the orbit evidence); ESCAPING is always followed. The producer's "packed in atmosphere -> Destroyed now" fallback applies only below the deletion line.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-C1~~: a crewed stage the player ignored killed or kept its kerbals by accident of path, not by rule [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding C1, high); FIXED 2026-11-21, branches `asr-crew` 70d3e56e7, `asr-crew2` 06c3fed1e, `asr-crew3` bdeb64cd6 / 8beef2e79 / 611aad14a, `asr-edgefix` f05f243cb, `asr-fix-recovery` c6afcc383; xUnit `PredictedCrashCrewTests`, `CrewPartFateTests`, `EffectiveLeafFinalizationTests`, `TakeoverCrewRecommitTests`, `RecoveredPredictedEndingTests`, `RecoveryOverridesPredictedCrashTests`; lanes ASR-1 / ASR-5 read the crew-death line of the abandoned crewed stack]

**Rule (Q6c, Q6b, Q12b, Q13b, Q4d, Q14):** a Destroyed ending kills the crew, predicted or confirmed (`InferCrewEndState` and the ghost-only chain handoff), with the death hold; a reputation penalty row exists only when stock took one. `Recording.TerminalPredicted` (key `terminalPredicted`) still marks a prediction: the takeover, playback, the stock-fate pass and the recovery rule read it. Identity loss over a remnant KSP keeps (`MarkDestroyedAtTerminal(vesselSurvives)` = `IdentityLossClassifier.RemnantSurvives`) stamps `terminalRemnantSurvives`; only that flag sends the crew through the per-part check (seat by part persistentId from the end, else start snapshot; Dead only when a Destroyed / ParachuteDestroyed part death names his part or the end snapshot dropped him; a seat a Breakup / JointBreak child took is read as carried away). A crewed breakup piece is always recorded (`ShouldRecordDebris` crewCount). Recovery: ABANDONED-STAGE-RECOVERY.
**Fix history (approach changed):** 70d3e56e7 first answered Aboard for a predicted crash (ruling Q6); bdeb64cd6 reverted that to Dead (Q6c). 8beef2e79: a same-id replace after a takeover (`ShouldRefreshCrewRowsOnReplace`) retires the predicted crash's KerbalAssignment rows and its death penalty (`LedgerOrchestrator.RetireTakenOverPredictedCrashCrewRows`). f05f243cb (review B2): a recovered breakup remnant keeps Dead the kerbal whose part stock destroyed. c6afcc383: a kerbal the recovery names (`RECOVERED_CREW`) is Recovered even when his start seat is a destroyed part (an IVA transfer). Old recordings (no key) keep Dead.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B4~~: a far Switch-To, Commit Flight or post-crash merge froze a still-falling sibling [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B4, medium-high); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-crew` 70d3e56e7; xUnit `InFlightCommitOptimizationTests`, `SwitchIntentPatchSmokeTests`, `ReFlyConclusionChainHeadFinalizeTests`; GPOS-1 re-pinned 8 -> 9 2026-11-24, branch `lane-repins3-1124`: the probe core's predicted fall makes its space half longer than the 5 s floor, so the optimizer cuts it at its atmosphere exit, as it does at a scene exit (RF-9)]

**Fix:** an in-flight commit runs the lifetime finalizer for a live non-active leaf, and for the active leaf when the pre-switch Merge abandons it (`CommitTreeFlightAbandoningActiveVessel`, the far Switch-To Case B), or a fresh Destroyed cache when it declines, before the situation stamp (ruling Q1b). A plain CommitTree keeps the active vessel's live situation stamp by design (ASR-4's reading: the active crewed stack ends SubOrbital).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-P1~~: coming back to a stage still falling showed its ghost and the real vessel at once, and flying it again kept the predicted crash [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding P1, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branches `asr-rerecord` 699ae8c89, `asr-crew3` c07cb2d1b / 8beef2e79 / 081b8dd37 / 7509f579c, `asr-reconcile` 66a4dccf4, `asr-edgefix` 6d9ebfcee / 1b55c3c74 / 38f7c2028 / dc44e0a7e, `asr-fix-recon` 15d4128d4; xUnit `PredictedEndingTakeoverTests`, `PredictedTakeoverCoastTests`, `PredictedTailSceneHideTests`, `PredictedCrashReconcilerTests`, `PredictedTakeoverAfterEndTests`, `MergePartnerTakeoverTests`; lane ASR-6 (TS Fly takeover, never flown)]

**Fix (ruling Q1b, P-STOCK, P-LEAVE):** `PredictedEndingTakeover.DropPredictedEndingForTakeover` drops the predicted segments past the cut, the predicted terminal, `TerminalPredicted`, `VesselDestroyed`, terminal orbit / surface metadata, an explicit end past the cut and the crew answer (Recovered / Docked / Boarded never touched; one `[PredictedTakeover]` Info line). Return paths: committed-tree restore (TS Fly, KSC marker Fly, far Switch-To, alarm Jump, the 1 Hz restore; the clone only, so a Discard keeps the committed copy), the intent consume (committed-clone parent, BG member, and route 14 `ended-recording-takeover` for a vessel whose ended recording in the live tree holds a prediction), background promotion, committed resume and the post-switch fresh start. Coast keep (c07cb2d1b): when the live vessel is on the predicted conic at the takeover (stored element frame, tolerance max(250 m, 1e-4 r)) the cut is the takeover UT and the kept segments lose `isPredicted`; off the conic, on another body or with no evidence the cut is the last real sample. After the predicted end (6d9ebfcee, dc44e0a7e): flying a vessel the replay spawned at a predicted Landed / Splashed / Orbiting / SubOrbital ending keeps the whole tail as history (a `Predicted` section becomes `Background`, `keptDescentSections=N`) and drops only the ending; a vessel alive after its predicted crash is dropped as before; `HasPredictedEnding` decides from provenance (review B1: a real Landed ending is never read as predicted, the explicit-end clue serves Destroyed only). Dock, claw grab and EVA board (1b55c3c74) are takeovers: in the live tree the partner leaf is resolved (`PredictedTakeoverLeaf.ResolveInTree`) and becomes the merge's second parent; against an earlier committed mission `TreeCommitService.TakeOverPredictedEndingsOfMergePartners` drops the partner's prediction at the merge UT at commit time and re-derives its crew rows. A surviving breakup remnant (`TerminalRemnantSurvives`) is never a predicted ending for a takeover or a merge partner (15d4128d4, final reviews). Playback hides a ghost on its predicted tail while the launch-matched vessel exists, in FLIGHT and at the Space Center (`GhostPlaybackLogic.ShouldHidePredictedTailGhostForScene`); map presence already refused it. The reconciler (66a4dccf4, `PredictedCrashReconciler` pure + `PredictedCrashReconcilerHost`, FLIGHT only since 15d4128d4): a predicted crash whose vessel stock still holds, seen twice 2 s apart after crashUT + 10 s, not active, not in physics in the air and whose conic no longer reaches the deletion line, is replaced by a committed clone with the prediction dropped and the live ending stamped; a vessel stock removed confirms the prediction (no change), a recovery or termination row reads `RemovedByPlayer` (c6afcc383); a confirmed crash is never reopened. Predicted touchdowns and final orbits: ABANDONED-STAGE-STOCK-FATE.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-CHUTES~~: a stage left under open parachutes replayed as a crash or vanished in mid-air [FILED 2026-11-18 (review edge case, ruling Q4); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-chutes` 834f2bddc..69f2812ab (ee07250cd, 8f13eed0c, 61b144fb7, 69f2812ab), `asr-edgefix` 1d7fa1fe3 / 6fac5f839 / dc44e0a7e, `asr-semichute` 7668f1913; xUnit `ParachuteDescentTests`, `UnfinishedFlightClassifierTests`, `ParachuteProtoModuleReadTests`; lanes ASR-2 (Q14 shape), ASR-7 (in-flight commit, the craft lands in range)]

**Fix (Q4, Q10b, Q11, Q4c, Q4d):** a live vessel (loaded, packed or unloaded) in an atmosphere with a parachute DEPLOYED or SEMIDEPLOYED gets a predicted descent instead of the drag-free fall: `ParachuteDescentLiveReader` reads the chutes (deploymentState / deployAltitude loaded; for an unloaded vessel every persisted chute module through `ParachuteProtoModuleRead.TryReadCanopy` / `ClassifyProtoModule`: ModuleParachute, ModuleEvaChute and RealChute's RealChuteModule, PREDEPLOYED / LOWDEPLOYED -> SEMIDEPLOYED, most open canopy wins) and the pure `ParachuteDescentPlanner` keeps the body-fixed lat / lon and descends at constant speed: deployed at the measured rate, semi-deployed at the measured rate down to the largest full-deploy altitude (stock 500 m), then the full-canopy rate. An armed, stowed or cut chute does not count (Q10b). The touchdown is judged on the estimated full-canopy rate (7668f1913): `v_land = v * 1/sqrt(clamp(drag/weight, 0.1, 10)) * sqrt(D_now / D_full) * sqrt(rho_here / rho_ground)`, D the open chutes' summed stock drag (semiDeployedDrag / fullyDeployedDrag, prefab for unloaded vessels), drag/weight from stock `Vessel.perturbation` over gravity (unpacked loaded vessels only, else terminal speed assumed), densities `body.GetDensity` at the vessel and at the ground; the 7 m/s default stays only when nothing can be scaled (`landingSource=default-*` on the `Chute descent predicted` line). Survives only at or below `MaxSafeLandingRate` = 12 m/s (Q11), else Destroyed at ground impact. Survived: Landed on the terrain (root height above the lowest part added) or Splashed at sea level on an ocean body; the touchdown is written into the end snapshot so the spawn sits where the replay lands. Representation: one Absolute, Atmospheric `TrackSectionSource.Predicted` section from the last authored UT to the ending, the same points in the flat list; predicted-data readers skip it (`TryGetLastAuthoredUT`, the debris persistence walk), a repair or new descent replaces it, a takeover drops it, a keep after the predicted end turns it into `Background`. Q4c: a predicted touchdown chain tip stays an Unfinished Flight (`reason=predictedTouchdown`, `TerminalKindClassifier` InFlight, a safe stable retry for supersede). Q4d: a chuted craft stock deletes ends Destroyed, crew dead, no spawn, its descent kept as the tail with the sparse key `quietEnd` (`Recording.QuietDestroyedEnd`): the ghost comes down and ends with no explosion (flight, KSC, manual preview). The harness endings block reads a predicted section as an extension of the end, not watched samples (61b144fb7). Leaving the flight scene with the craft still in the air: ABANDONED-STAGE-Q14; stock deleting a committed touchdown later: ABANDONED-STAGE-STOCK-FATE. RealChute (loaded and unloaded, canopy area for the estimate): ABANDONED-STAGE-REALCHUTE-LOADED. Open: ABANDONED-STAGE-CHUTE-ESTIMATE-GAPS.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-PACKED-IN-ATMOSPHERE~~: a stage packed by warp inside the atmosphere held still, then exploded [FILED 2026-11-18 (review, the warp path of the two-stage table; V 2026-11-21: record what the game simulates); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-railsatmo` 9d1694dd4 + 1dd8c8930; xUnit `BackgroundOnRailsAtmosphereConicTests`, `EccentricOrbitOptimizerInvariantTests`, characterization goldens]

**Fix:** stock moves a packed vessel on its drag-free conic until it deletes, unpacks or hands it to the player, so `InitializeOnRailsState` opens the conic below the atmosphere top too (`ResolveOnRailsInitialPayload`; a vessel on the pad still opens none). The span carries one fixed label, `BackgroundOnRailsState.packedInsideAtmosphere` (set at open, kept through warp checkpoints and time-jump re-captures, cleared at an SOI change): its checkpoint sections are Atmospheric, so it adds no optimizer split candidate and cannot toggle per orbit; no TrackSection or hysteresis is added to the on-rails state. `RefreshOnRailsFinalizationCache` keeps the live-vessel cache for such a span (chutes, predicted fall) and rebuilds from the conic only when the cache is missing, empty or failed. The load-time clip against physical sections still relabels ExoBallistic, so committed flights are untouched.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B2~~: a vessel the player flew and left, an EVA kerbal or an undocked craft vanished mid-coast [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B2, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35; xUnit `AbandonedStageAccuracyTests`, `SceneExitFinalizationIntegrationTests`]

**Fix:** only the active vessel has a patched-conic solver (decompiled `Vessel.MakeActive` / `MakeInactive`), so the live-orbit fallback no longer turns a LIVE vessel (`IsLiveVesselAlive`: not DEAD, parts left) into "Destroyed now": it follows the live orbit to its natural ending. An open parachute declines the drag-free tail (ABANDONED-STAGE-CHUTES takes it). The unconfirmed case keeps the `NoSolverStart` classification.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B7~~: Commit Flight left the background recorder subscribed to the committed tree [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B7, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-crew2` f9836f014; xUnit `MergeFlowDecisionTests` (a source gate pins every drop site)]

**Fix:** `ReleaseBackgroundRecorderAfterInFlightCommit` runs `DiscardWithoutPersist` (unsubscribe, no flush; `FinalizeAllForCommit` already flushed) before the recorder is dropped.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B9~~: a tail rebuilt from a recorded point started sideways and its crash site drifted about 1 deg per minute of age [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B9, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35; xUnit `AbandonedStageAccuracyTests`]

**Fix:** an orbit rebuilt from a recorded body-fixed sample (recovery start and the predicted-tail reseed) shifts its node back by 360 * age / rotationPeriod (`ComputeHistoricalRotationLanShiftDegrees`).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B10~~: moon encounters in the tail were often missed [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B10, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35; xUnit `AbandonedStageAccuracyTests`, `BallisticExtrapolatorTests`]

**Fix:** a child SOI entry is searched only inside the child's radial band (child Pe - SOI .. Ap + SOI), sampled at most one SOI of relative motion apart, every near local minimum refined to the closest approach (golden section), budget 16384 samples per child per conic.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B11~~: a Mun stage with its low point among the peaks got no tail or flew through mountains [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B11, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35; xUnit `AbandonedStageAccuracyTests`]

**Fix:** a closed conic whose low point is below the highest terrain scans later periapsis passes (only the stretch below the highest terrain, with the body turning under it) for an impact, budget 8192 samples; `ShouldExtrapolate` reads the floor, not sea level.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B12~~: a pending maneuver node discarded the coast before it [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B12, medium-low); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35; xUnit `SceneExitFinalizationIntegrationTests`]

**Fix:** the stock patches up to the node are kept and the unburned coast is propagated from there, instead of dropping the whole chain.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-B14~~: a probe still beside its parent could end Landed at a nonsense spot and spawn there [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding B14, low-medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-crew2` f9836f014; xUnit `RelativeEndpointInferenceTests`]

**Fix:** `InferTerminalStateFromTrajectory`, `HasOnlySubOrbitalFallbackEvidence`, `PopulateTerminalPositionFromLastPoint` and `TryCaptureTerrainHeightFromLastTrajectoryPoint` read the last flat point through `FlatPointFrameDispatch` (`TryResolveLastPointBodyFixed`): a Relative metre offset is replaced by its body-fixed shadow, or refused.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-R1~~: the map and Tracking Station icon froze at the last recorded point for the whole tail [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding R1, high; limited by ruling Q7 to flights shown on the map / TS); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-render` 2bc7ec83a; xUnit `PredictedTailRenderTests`]

**Fix:** the flight map and Tracking Station markers resolve the tail segment the flight mesh rides (`GhostPlaybackLogic.TryFindTailSegment` / `TryGetTailWorldPosition`); the TS time gate accepts "points or tail" (`IsInsidePointsOrTail`).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-R2~~: on the map, a crash flight's coast had no line under its icon [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding R2, high; Q7 applies); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-render` 2bc7ec83a; xUnit `GhostTrajectoryPolylineBuildTests`]

**Fix:** the forward pass draws the arc the head sits on when the member has no map vessel and its ending can never get one (crash / landing), `ShouldForwardDrawCurrentArc`. Contract: `docs/dev/design-map-ts-render-architecture.md` appendix.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-R3~~: at the Space Center the ghost hung in the sky during the tail and exploded there [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding R3, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-render` 2bc7ec83a; xUnit `PredictedTailRenderTests`]

**Fix:** the KSC ghost follows the tail (`TryResolveKscTailPose`, branch `orbit-tail`) with the flight ghost's continuity blend off the last point and the segment's orbital-frame attitude, so the explosion plays at the ground.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-R4~~: looped replay teleported the ghost at the tail start every cycle and missed the crash site [FILED 2026-11-18 (review finding R4, medium); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-render` 2bc7ec83a (teleport) and `asr-render2` 1aa334d3e (ruling R4b); xUnit `PredictedTailRenderTests`, `PredictedTailPlanetTurnTests`, `PredictedTailSlideTests`]

**Fix:** loop cycles past the last point ride `PositionFromOrbit` (carrying the continuity blend), and a loop state never reuses a continuity offset cached under another cycle's body rotation. R4b: a predicted path that ends on the ground on the same body (Destroyed, Landed, Splashed) is turned with the planet by the replay offset (playback UT minus now, plus the phasing derotation of its points), read each frame from the body's own surface frame, never cached; position, continuity anchor, attitude and surface velocity turn together, and a turned pose is re-applied body-fixed after floating-origin shifts. Orbiting tails and non-loop ghosts are unchanged; the map / TS markers read non-loop UTs.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L1~~: an SOI bounce used up the 8-crossing budget [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35; xUnit `BallisticExtrapolatorTests`]

**Fix:** the reverse crossing at an SOI transition instant is always suppressed, so a refined crossing landing a hair outside no longer bounces the state to the cap.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L2~~: above 10x warp a crashing ghost vanished without its explosion [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-render2` a663ac279 (ruling L2); xUnit `ExplosionFxTests`]

**Fix:** pure `GhostPlaybackLogic.ShouldPlayExplosionFx`: the explosion plays at any warp for a watched ghost or one whose cached view distance is inside the unwatched mesh LOD cutoff (50 km), at the KSC inside the 25 km cull range; a far ghost just ends.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L3~~: a tumbling stage's spin froze in the tail [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35; xUnit `AbandonedStageAccuracyTests`]

**Fix:** the live vessel's spin is stamped on every predicted segment (`OrbitSegment.angularVelocity` contract), without PersistentRotation.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L4~~: debris exploded at its first lost part and skipped the rest of its tail [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-render` 2bc7ec83a; xUnit `ExplosionFxTests`]

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L5~~: a gap over 30 s before the tail froze the ghost with flames playing, then jumped [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-render2` 496b28fff (ruling L5); xUnit `PredictedTailSlideTests`, `GhostPlaybackEngineTests`]

**Fix:** the ghost slides from the last recorded point to the predicted path's start along the great circle between the two body-relative directions (monotone cubics on angle and radius seeded from the endpoint velocities, no overshoot, no dip below the lower radius); the orbit is evaluated only at its own start, the slide carries no velocity (no stale FX) and the attitude eases between the two. Flight mesh, flight world-position resolver, map / TS markers and the KSC ghost (branch `orbit-tail-slide`). A last point in a Relative section, on another body, or a recorded next segment keeps the old hold.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L6~~: the 50-year horizon was counted in Earth years [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35]

**Fix:** counted in KSP's calendar year (`KSPUtil.dateTimeFormatter.Year` via `ExtrapolationLimits.calendarSecondsPerYear`, default 426 days); now only the cap for unresolved cases (ruling Q8).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L7~~: terrain below sea level was treated as sea level [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-accuracy` 9475d9f35]

**Fix:** on a body without an ocean the fall ends at the real ground below the datum (`ExtrapolationBody.TerrainBelowDatum` / `MinTerrainAltitude`), the sub-surface start guard sits that much lower; ocean bodies still stop at the sea.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L8~~: an F9 quickload dropped every guess and closed missing members SubOrbital in mid-air [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-quickload` 4c50a04ac; xUnit `QuickloadFinalizationCacheTests`, `BackgroundRecorderCharacterizationTests`]

**Fix:** `EnsureBackgroundRecorderAttached` forces one cache refresh per live member right after the missing-member check (`BackgroundRecorder.RebuildFinalizationCachesAfterRestore`, one `Restore cache rebuild:` line). `CloseMissingBackgroundMembersAtLoad`: a member whose evidence was SubOrbital builds a cache from its recorded data (the last orbit segment, or the orbit reseeded off the last sample with the historical rotation) and applies it like a missing-vessel commit; Orbiting / Landed / Splashed predictions are not adopted (a removed vessel is never made spawnable); open parachute, Relative-only sample and missing body facts keep the old stamp (summary `followedRecordedTail=N`). The cache stays in memory; no OnLoad step added.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-L9~~: a SubOrbital crewed stage left its crew aboard open-ended, and an escaping stage flew 50 years and never spawned [FILED 2026-11-18 (review lower-impact item); SETTLED 2026-11-21 by rulings Q8 + Q6c; FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-finalorbit` c695b197f + c219f487e; xUnit `FinalConicEndingTests`, `BackgroundRecorderTests`]

**Fix (Q8):** `BallisticExtrapolator.Extrapolate` stops on the first final conic: bound, periapsis strictly above the floor (`OrbitClearance.IsBoundOrbitClear`), inside the SOI, no surface event and no sphere change within one period; the tail ends Orbiting after `FinalConicSettleSeconds` (60 s, at most a quarter period) of it (`reason=stable-conic`). An open conic around a body with no parent (the Sun) with no child sphere ahead ends SubOrbital the same way (`reason=final-escape`) and spawns on its path (ruling Q10). When propagation started at the last stock patch's end and ended on that conic, the ending moves to the patch start (`TryMoveFinalConicEndingToPatchStart`). `stopOnFinalConic: false` keeps follow-to-the-horizon for `EscapeTrajectoryTerminal.ResolveAtUT`. Encounters after the first period are not predicted (the spawned vessel meets them in stock). Covered: V's scenario 2026-11-21 (an escaping stage committed and rewound before it reaches the Sun SOI ends Orbiting the Sun and spawns there).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-STOCK-FATE~~: a predicted touchdown or final orbit stock later deleted was still spawned, with its crew alive (review C) [FILED 2026-11-21 by review C (one blocker: a predicted chute touchdown committed while the craft is loaded is never squared with stock deleting it later, `Vessel.CheckKill` fires no terminal event); FIXED 2026-11-21, branches `asr-touchdown` 9bbae1472 / 9a6b278b1 / 2496ba23a, `asr-followups` 5a7a1929e, `asr-fix-recon` 15d4128d4 / 5d43376d9; xUnit `PredictedTouchdownStockFateTests`, `StockFateReconcileReviewFixTests`, `PredictedEndingRecoveryFollowupTests`, the OnLoad step and token goldens; in-game `OrbitSpawnClearance` spawn-gate live-lookup cell (029a82896); lane ASR-7]

**Fix (P-STOCK, Q4d, Q8):** `PredictedTouchdownStockFate` (pure, plus guarded live guid / clock reads) and the reconciler host's touchdown pass, FLIGHT only. A committed predicted touchdown or predicted final orbit (Q8 final orbits are stamped `TerminalPredicted` by the applier and the scene-exit finalizer since 15d4128d4) is judged against the live game: (a) down (landed / splashed): left as committed; (b) gone, held by stock in this timeline, no recovery / termination row, no live dock or boarding, confirmed twice 2 s apart: stock deleted it, `PredictedCrashReconciler.ApplyStockDeletion` commits a clone as Q4d's shape (Destroyed, not predicted, `quietEnd` after the descent, end UT kept, crew Dead, slot open as for a crash); (c) a touchdown still in the air on rails past the touchdown + 10 s, clear of the deletion line: `ApplyContradiction` drops it and the ending follows the live vessel; a held final orbit is compared with stock's orbit and dropped the same way when stock holds it elsewhere (ABANDONED-STAGE-HELD-FINAL-ORBIT-NOT-COMPARED). Discriminator: `Recording.StockHeldVesselUT` (sparse key `stockHeldUT`), stamped in place only from a live read of the current stock state (CommitTree while the craft is in the game, and every pass that finds it) and cleared by every time-travel load to a stock state older than the stamp (`ForgetStockHeldVesselsAfterTimeTravel`, at both time-travel break sites of OnLoad), so a rewound timeline carries no stamp and its replay spawns the craft as before. Spawn gate: `ShouldSpawnAtRecordingEnd` refuses a stamped predicted ending whose craft is gone, and `RunSpawnDeathChecks` clears an adopted one stock deleted with no death counted (5a7a1929e); the live lookup `IsVesselWithGuidLive` reads only `FlightGlobals.Vessels` in FLIGHT (protoVessels keeps a vessel `Vessel.Die` removed until the next save, so the gate failed open, final reviews), remnants excluded. The same-id replace retires the touchdown's Aboard rows. The KSC runs no pass (stock deletes nothing there; the spawn gate holds).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-Q14~~: a chuted craft still in the air when the player left the flight scene kept a predicted touchdown stock would never honour (owner ruling Q14) [FILED 2026-11-21 by the final reviews (the chute fate depended on scene order); RULED 2026-11-21 ~23:20 ("Decided at the exit"); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-fix-exit` 1fa2e6913 / e37552366; xUnit `SceneExitChuteDescentTests`; lanes ASR-2, RF-1, RF-C1, RF-L2, RB-4, RB-5, RF-4, QL-7 re-pinned (3d15a4b96 / a8b167775), not yet re-flown]

**Fix:** step 3c of `FinalizeTreeRecordingsAfterFlush`, `PredictedTouchdownStockFate.ApplyFlightSceneLeave` (handed the tree's recording list, so the type knot stays at 437), runs at a scene exit (Space Center, Tracking Station, main menu) and at the pre-switch Merge of a far Switch-To (`leavesFlightScene`): every predicted chute touchdown becomes Destroyed, not predicted, crew dead, quiet end after the descent, no spawn, slot open as a crash. A craft whose live vessel is already Landed / Splashed keeps its ending; a too-fast descent stays an exploding crash; an in-flight commit after which the player keeps flying keeps the forecast for ABANDONED-STAGE-STOCK-FATE. Log: `[Extrapolator] Chute descent at scene exit: ... outcome=mission-lost|kept-touched-down`.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-RECOVERY~~: recovering a stage Parsek predicted a crash for left the crash and killed the crew [FILED 2026-11-21 (WP7; final reviews: a recovery after the predicted crash UT never revived the crew, D-d / C3, and recovered crew read their start seat, so an IVA transfer read Dead); FIXED 2026-11-21, branches `asr-crew3` 611aad14a, `asr-edgefix` f05f243cb / e5bd6ffd7, `asr-followups` 5a7a1929e, `asr-fix-recovery` c6afcc383; xUnit `RecoveredPredictedEndingTests`, `PredictedEndingRecoveryFollowupTests`, `RecoveryOverridesPredictedCrashTests`, `UnfinishedFlightsMembershipTests`]

**Fix (Q13b):** live recording: `CanOverwriteTerminalState(existingPredicted)` lets a Recovered overwrite a predicted Destroyed (both recovery stamp sites: TS / KSC recover through `UpdateRecordingsForTerminalEvent`, in-flight Recover through `InFlightRecoveryRequest`), clears `VesselDestroyed` and re-infers the crew Recovered. Committed recording: `PredictedEndingRecovery` (pure, launch guid only) converts a clone (prediction dropped as a takeover, Recovered at the recovery UT) and `ParsekScenario.ApplyRecoveryOfCommittedPredictions` commits it through `TreeCommitService.CommitTree` before the ledger rows (same-id replace retires the death rows and penalty). A predicted Destroyed follows any recovery of its launch, before or after the predicted UT (`IsRecoveryInsidePredictedEnding`); a predicted touchdown only before its touchdown; a confirmed crash, a recovery before the last real sample, a live session's tree and a Re-Fly session are left alone (logged). `Recording.RecoveredCrewNames` (sparse `RECOVERED_CREW` node): the crew stock recovered, read from the ProtoVessel at `OnVesselRecovered` and from the live vessel when the in-flight Recover arms; `PopulateCrewEndStates` reads a named kerbal Recovered even when his start seat is a destroyed part. A recovery before a predicted touchdown closes the crew hold at the recovery (`KerbalsModule.RecoveryHoldEndUT`, measured from the predicted descent start). The crash pass reads a recovery or termination row as `RemovedByPlayer`, never as stock confirming the crash. A recovered breakup remnant keeps Dead the kerbal whose part stock destroyed (f05f243cb); recovering a replay-spawned vessel seals its open Re-Fly row (e5bd6ffd7, test).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-NOSOLVER-UNLOADED~~: an unloaded probe core alive on rails was finalized Destroyed at the scene exit and its tail lost [FILED 2026-11-21 from flight `asr-final` (ASR-1: the core unloaded at 93.7 km on a sub-orbital arc, Destroyed at the exit UT, tail discarded at the commit); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-nosolver` d280a7272; xUnit `AbandonedStageNoSolverTests`]

**Fix:** stock `Vessel.Unload` empties `vessel.parts`, so `IsLiveVesselAlive` read every unloaded vessel as dead and the B2 live coast never ran for it; liveness now reads the protoVessel's part snapshots for an unloaded vessel (pure `IsVesselAliveCore`). The scene-exit apply now starts every predicted segment at the last authored UT (as the cache apply does), so `SessionMerger`'s predicted-suffix rule no longer drops a tail rebuilt from an earlier recorded point.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-FINAL-REVIEWS~~: the two final whole-diff reviews (Opus 5.5 High, Fable 5.2 High, 2026-11-21 ~23:15) [FILED 2026-11-21 (V ~22:20: design, code and coverage reviewed together); every converged finding FIXED 2026-11-21 by fix packages A-D]

Converged blockers and design findings (ids Opus C1-C3, Fable C1-C2, D-a..D-f; only D-d / C3 is named one-to-one in the ruling log), each with its fix:

- The Tracking Station reconciler host never ran (stock's `CheckKill` needs an active vessel): host removed, the pass is FLIGHT-only (15d4128d4).

- Map / TS tail markers formatted log lines, built keys and allocated a closure per frame: `VerboseRateLimitedComposed` with a struct, keys built once per recording, plain-loop body lookup (25481a28f; the two TS key caches tagged `process` in `lifetimes.toml`).
- The docs were behind WP13-WP15: this docs pass.
- Coverage: the lanes the reviews asked for are ASR-6 / ASR-7 / ASR-9 (authored) and ABANDONED-STAGE-LANES-OWED (ASR-8, the crash-contradiction lane).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-REALCHUTE-LOADED~~: a LOADED RealChute stage is not read as under chutes [FILED 2026-11-21 from WP11 (`asr-edgefix`); low (RealChute installs only); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `realchute-parts`; xUnit `RealChuteLiveReadTests`; in-game check OWED]

`ParachuteProtoModuleRead` read RealChute's `RealChuteModule` from the persisted proto module of an UNLOADED vessel only; the loaded half of `ParachuteDescentLiveReader` read `ModuleParachute` (and its subclass `ModuleEvaChute`). A RealChute stage still loaded when Parsek stopped watching it was predicted to fall and crash.

**Fix:** on a loaded part with no `ModuleParachute`, `RealChuteLiveRead` finds a module whose type (or a base) is named `RealChuteModule` and reads, by reflection over public fields only (no RealChute reference, no RealChute method run), its `parachutes` list and each canopy's `depState`, `deploymentAlt`, `preDeployedDiameter` and `deployedDiameter` into the node shape RealChute persists (one `PARACHUTE` child per canopy; field names from RealChute's `Parachute.cs` / `RealChuteModule.cs`, master 5a2824c). Loaded and unloaded parts then share one pure read (`ParachuteProtoModuleRead.TryReadCanopy`, most open canopy wins). The full-canopy estimate now has RealChute drag too: `TryReadRealChuteCanopyArea` sums the open canopies' area (PREDEPLOYED at its pre-deployed diameter, LOWDEPLOYED / DEPLOYED at the deployed one; full = deployed), one Cd assumed for every canopy. `OpenChuteTally.CombineDrag` keeps the stock drag and RealChute area sums apart (different units): RealChute only reads `chuteDragSource=realchute-area`, a vessel with both kinds open reads `mixed` (NaN, the estimate falls back), a stock-only vessel reads the stock sums as before (`stock`). A vessel with a RealChute module logs a `RealChute read:` Verbose line (rate-limited per vessel, a changed count prints at once) (`source=loaded-reflection|proto-node`, modules, open canopies, areas); a module reflection cannot read (another RealChute version's shape) logs `RealChute module not readable: ... reason=` (Warn, rate-limited) and its canopies read as not open. Stock installs carry no `RealChuteModule`, so their reads are unchanged apart from the new `chuteDragSource=stock` token on the `Chute descent predicted` line. **Owed:** one in-game check on the modded-compat install (RealChute is not in its profile): a RealChute stage left under an open canopy shows `RealChute read: ... source=loaded-reflection ... openModules=1` and a `Chute descent predicted` line instead of a crash; no RealChute lane exists. Known limit (review): on a flight-scene load RealChute's `Parachute.Initialize` resets a staged canopy to STOWED until its next update re-deploys it (up to about a second), so a read inside that window sees no open canopy and falls back to the drag-free fall.

## ABANDONED-STAGE-MERGE-PARTNER-COAST-RELOAD: the commit-time dock / board takeover loses the merged vessel's orbit across a reload [FILED 2026-11-21 from WP11 (1b55c3c74); low; OPEN]

`RecordingTree.MergePartnerCoastEvidence` (the merged vessel's orbit at the merge, read by the coast-keep rule) is in memory only, never serialized. A commit after a reload falls back to cutting the partner at its last real sample, so its replay loses the coast between that sample and the merge. Fix if it matters: persist it as an additive tree key, or re-derive it from the merge recording's first sample.

## ABANDONED-STAGE-MANY-BOOSTERS-COST: the cost of many abandoned boosters at once is not measured [FILED 2026-11-18 (review edge case "Many staged boosters"); OPEN]

Each background vessel refreshes its cache (a full tail guess) every 5 s, now with the moon-band search and the peaks scan. One measurement on a many-booster craft (frame time and the refresh summary counts) settles it.

## ABANDONED-STAGE-ASTEROID-AND-MULTI-SOI-LOOP: asteroid capture and looped tails that cross more than one SOI are not checked [FILED 2026-11-21 (gameplay edge-case review); OPEN]

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-SEMICHUTE-RATE~~: semi-deployed chutes were judged on a fixed 7 m/s full-canopy rate, so they always landed [FILED 2026-11-21 from WP4 (ASR-2's reading `canopy=SemiDeployed ... rate2=7.00`); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `asr-semichute` 7668f1913; xUnit `ParachuteDescentTests`]

**Fix:** the touchdown is judged on the full-canopy rate estimated from the measured descent by the terminal-speed law (formula in ABANDONED-STAGE-CHUTES), so a heavy stage under one drogue, or a craft on Duna, crashes. Remaining gaps: ABANDONED-STAGE-CHUTE-ESTIMATE-GAPS.

## ABANDONED-STAGE-CHUTE-ESTIMATE-GAPS: the full-canopy estimate ignores non-chute drag, RealChute materials and stock-plus-RealChute vessels [FILED 2026-11-21 from WP4b (7668f1913); low; OPEN]

RealChute canopies are now scaled by their open canopy area (ABANDONED-STAGE-REALCHUTE-LOADED), with one drag coefficient assumed for every canopy (canopies of different RealChute materials are weighted by area only), and a vessel with stock and RealChute chutes both open reads no drag (`chuteDragSource=mixed`, the 7 m/s default for a semi-deployed one). The estimate also counts only the chutes' drag: a draggy stage (fins, a heat shield) lands slower than predicted. Fix if a case matters: read each RealChute canopy's material Cd (`MaterialsLibrary`), and add the vessel's measured non-chute drag share from `Vessel.perturbation` before the chutes opened.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-CREWED-SUBORBITAL-RESERVED~~: a crewed stage ending SubOrbital at the horizon cap or a scan-budget miss keeps its crew reserved for good [FILED 2026-11-21 from WP3b / `asr-fix-recovery` (pinned as held open-ended in `RecoveryOverridesPredictedCrashTests`); SETTLED 2026-11-22 by ruling Q15; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `suborbital-crew`; xUnit `GroundScanEndOrbitTests`, `FinalConicEndingTests`, `RecoveryOverridesPredictedCrashTests`]

Q8 would spawn such a stage on its final orbit, but the spawn safety check refuses a conic that dips below the terrain, so the recording never spawns and its crew stay Aboard with no end. Only a bound conic whose low point sits between the ground under its track and the highest peak reaches it (Mun, Minmus and other airless bodies; Duna, whose peaks top its deletion line).

**Fix (Q15):** when the later-pass ground scan (`FindLaterPassTerrainImpact`) finds no impact, it reports where it stopped checking: the horizon or sphere exit when it read every pass, else (budget of 8192 samples, about 170 passes) the end of the last pass read plus the 60 s settle, held before the next stretch under the peaks so the vessel is above every peak there. `Extrapolate` ends the conic there (`reason=ground-scan-end`, `ExtrapolationResult.endedAtGroundScanEnd`) unless a child sphere comes first or the conic leaves its sphere before then; `stopOnFinalConic: false` still runs to the horizon. The finalizer, the live-vessel cache and the on-rails cache keep that Orbiting past the periapsis floor, and the recording carries the new sparse marker `groundScanEnd` (`Recording.GroundScanEndOrbit`, only beside a predicted Orbiting; codec, copy, split, merge and cache carry it). `TerminalOrbitSpawnSafety.Evaluate` skips the floor for that one marker (`reason=ground-scan-end-orbit`; the atmosphere-band deferral still applies); every other reader keeps the floor. The crew stay Aboard on the spawned vessel. The ending is `TerminalPredicted`, so the stock-fate pass (edge case 37) turns it into a loss when stock deletes the craft. A ground-scan-end ending pulled back to a background close, and a member stock dropped from the save, keep the old SubOrbital verdict. Not changed: the reconciler's return of a stock-held peak-grazing orbit from a predicted crash to SubOrbital (edge case 34) keeps the live vessel's own situation.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-HELD-FINAL-ORBIT-NOT-COMPARED~~: a predicted final orbit stock still holds is never compared with stock's real orbit [FILED 2026-11-21 from `asr-fix-recon` (15d4128d4); low; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `final-orbit-reconcile`; xUnit `HeldFinalOrbitReconcileTests`, `StockFateReconcileReviewFixTests`]

The stock-fate pass left a held Q8 final orbit alone. If stock's on-rails orbit differed from the predicted one (an encounter the prediction missed, a patch it did not see), the replay still spawned the vessel on the predicted orbit.

**Fix (P-STOCK, the direction this entry already named):** the stock-fate pass compares every held predicted final orbit with stock's live orbit (`HeldFinalOrbitComparison`, pure). The reference is the predicted segment that covers the pass UT; past the last predicted segment it is the final conic propagated on, up to one period after its start for a closed conic (the span the predictor checked for sphere changes; an encounter after it is the vessel's own future, design edge case 26), with no limit for an open conic around the Sun. Past the end only a last segment no longer than the 60 s settle span counts as a final conic: a tail cut at the SOI transition cap ends at a crossing the predictor found itself, so stock in the next body there is not compared (review). Before the prediction starts the pass is due again at its start. Both conics are propagated in their stored element frame (KSP-native elements, `TwoBodyOrbit.TryCreateFromSegmentStoredFrame`, no Zup and no live frame read) with the live body's gravity. Verdicts: another body, the ground, or a position miss over max(1 km, 1% of the distance from the body centre) differs; within it agrees; no live orbit, before the prediction or past the horizon is not compared. The 1% keeps stock's own noise (the sphere-change frame timing and the physics seconds before packing, about 1e-3 after a long heliocentric coast) and still catches another body, a burn or a missed encounter. A vessel in physics is not judged (`StockStillSimulating`). A difference seen on two passes 2 s apart is `Contradicted` and goes through the contradicted-touchdown path: `PredictedCrashReconciler.ApplyContradiction` (now accepting a predicted final orbit, `predictionContradicted` so the tail past the end is never kept) drops the prediction at the last real sample and stamps the live vessel's ending on a committed clone. Agreeing or not compared: left as committed (`FinalOrbitHeld` / `FinalOrbitNotCompared`, both on the pass summary); the pass is due again 10 s after the next predicted conic change (`PredictedTouchdownPassResult.NextDueUT`, merged into the host's due UT). Log: `Held final orbit differs from stock: ... verdict=Differs reason=... miss=... tolerance=...` (InfoRateLimited per recording and reason) and `Predicted final orbit contradicted by stock:` on the apply. Known shape, as for a contradicted touchdown: the ending is stamped at the last real sample with the live orbit, so a replay after a rewind places the vessel on stock's conic at that UT, around the live body even when stock reached it later.

## ABANDONED-STAGE-CRASH-PASS-SKIPPED-RECOVERY: a recovery skipped while a Re-Fly was active is never converted later [FILED 2026-11-21 from `asr-fix-recovery` (c6afcc383); low; OPEN]

`PredictedEndingRecovery` leaves a Re-Fly session's tree alone, and nothing replays the skipped recovery after the session ends, so the committed predicted crash stays (the crash pass reads the recovery row as `RemovedByPlayer` and does not confirm it, but does not convert it either). Fix: let the crash pass convert a predicted Destroyed whose launch has a recovery row, through the same `PredictedEndingRecovery` clone.

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-SPLITATSECTION-EXTRA-SAMPLE~~: the optimizer split dropped a predicted tail when a section opened on the previous section's sample (or an extra sample) [FILED 2026-11-21 from WP15 (`asr-nosolver`); SEEN 2026-11-22 in flight `asr-final3` ASR-1 / ASR-5; FIXED 3a35c3ae3 (branch `asr-splittail`)]

Flight `asr-final3`: the probe core's predicted fall survived the commit and the tree merge, then `SplitAtSection` (atmosphere / space) wrote both halves `predictedOrbitSegments=0`: the space section starts at the cut but its first sample is the atmosphere section's last one, so the flat list of the second half held one sample fewer than its sections, the tail-preserving sync refused and the rebuild from sections dropped the predicted segment (it lives only in the flat list). Fix: `TrajectoryTextSidecarCodec.TrySyncFlatTrajectoryFromTrackSectionsPreservingPredictedOrbitTail`, called by `SplitAtSection` after the existing sync, rebuilds from the sections and re-appends the trailing predicted segments that start at or after the recorded sections' end; the second half keeps the fall, its end UT and terminal, the first half none (`flatSync=.../track-sections-preserved-predicted-orbit-tail:N`). The merge pass's mirror bug (it dropped `RecoveredCrewNames` when the later half ended Recovered) fixed in the same commit. Tests `AbandonedStageSplitTailTests` (flight shape, extra seam sample, clean control, no tail, merge crew carry).

## ~~ABANDONED-STAGE-TAKEOVER-REPREDICT~~: after a takeover the next in-flight commit re-predicted the taken-over stage's rows [FILED 2026-11-22 from flight `asr-final3` ASR-6; FIXED 82231e4d9 (branch `asr-splittail`)]

After `Predicted ending dropped for takeover` on the probe core and a continuation bound to the same pid, the next in-flight CommitTree ran the B4 lifetime finalizer on the chain head (`IsNonFinalChainSegmentInTree` compared the head's end, its section end at the cut, with the successor's first SAMPLE, which sits before the cut) and on the taken-over row (its standalone continuation has no branch point), stamping a predicted Destroyed on a vessel the player was flying. Fix: `ChainSuccessorBoundaryUT` reads the successor's first section start when later; `HasSameVesselContinuationInTree` (same launch, the tree's active recording or a recording starting at the row's end, 1 s) makes an in-flight commit skip the lifetime finalizer for such a row and stamp the live situation (log `continues in '<id>'`); scene exits unchanged. Tests `AbandonedStageTakeoverRepredictTests` (10 cells).

Log it at Verbose when the existing ending matches the cache. The GS-7 `MergeTree: boundary discontinuity=~9.8 km ... unrecorded-gap ... Kerbal X Probe dt=~22 s` is also pre-existing (2026-11-08 / 2026-11-15 runs): the gap between the probe's last background sample and the recording started at the switch to it.

## RP-QUICKSAVE-LOST-ON-IMMEDIATE-SCENE-EXIT: a separation the player leaves the flight from at once loses its Re-Fly rewind point [FILED 2026-11-22 from ASR-8 flight 1 `2026-11-22_1150_ASR-8-armed-chute-stage-falls-drag-free` (PASS; automation DLL sha256 prefix 9f5e7a52, branch `asr8-armed-chute` on origin/main c01fe82f8); OPEN; low (needs a decouple and a scene exit within a fraction of a second)]

What: the seam decoupled at 13:51:17.445 and ExitToSpaceCenter ran ~0.15 s later, while the split was still in the crash-coalescer window. The exit's persist save flushed it (`Pending splits flushed (OnSave)`), so `RewindPointAuthor.Begin` ran INSIDE that OnSave (`RewindPoint begin: rp=rp_3c1ce66a... slots=2`, `RewindPoints saved: 1`) and started its one-frame-deferred quicksave coroutine on `ParsekScenario`. The scene change destroyed the scenario before the deferred frame, so the coroutine died silently: no `[RewindSave] Wrote`, and not the `Aborted mid-coroutine` rollback either (that guard only runs if the coroutine resumes). The RP rode the in-session handoff to the Space Center, both crashed slots were promoted `CommittedProvisional` against it, and the same load's sweep reaped it (`Cleaned missing rewind-point quicksave: rp=rp_3c1ce66a...`, `Reaped ... slots=2`).

Player impact: a separation followed at once by leaving the flight has no Re-Fly point, though the classifier opened its slots (`reason=crashed`). The end state is clean (no orphan file, no stale row), only the slot is lost.

Fix direction (not started): author the quicksave synchronously when `Begin` is reached from OnSave / a scene-exit flush (the flight is still loaded there), or roll the RP back at scenario destroy when its deferred write never ran, so no slot is promoted against a point that will not exist. ASR-8 now dwells 5 s at 1x before its exit, so the lane flies the ordinary path; a lane for this edge would drop the dwell and expect the quicksave written.
