## ~~PARTPARITY-REAL-VS-REAL-ONE-PIXEL~~: the noise-floor control can read bad on a single colour pixel [FILED 2026-11-22 from the modded-restock smoke flight `2026-11-22_2141_PPX-0-modded-restock-smoke` (a local uncommitted lane, branch `p8-modded-restock-profile`); FIXED 2026-11-23, branch `part-parity-p5-gate`; xUnit `PartParitySweepPlanTests.Control_RealVsReal`; low (instrument only)]

What: `ctl-real-vs-real` (the real `fuelTankSmallFlat`, ReStock model, rendered as both sides) read `outcome=bad ... detail=difference in bottom`, so the run was INVALID(parity-controls) although every mask was identical in all four views (iou 1, 0 real-only / ghost-only px) and the only difference was `colorOverPx=1`, `colorBlobPx=1` in the `bottom` view (`colorBlockMax` 0.06). The same lane, re-provisioned with the next reference DLL and flown again 6 minutes later (`2026-11-22_2147`), read controls ok. So two renders of the same real part can differ by one colour pixel, and the control's judge counts any colour blob. Evidence: `<umbrella>/logs/flights/p8-p1-ppx0-2026-11-22_2141/` (sidecar, atlas, KSP.log, result JSON).

Fix (P5, branch `part-parity-p5-gate`): the judge (`PartParitySweepPlan.JudgeControl`) still needs identical masks in every view, but allows up to `RealVsRealColorNoisePx = 8` overlap pixels per view over the colour threshold (an eighth of the 64 px colour warn line); the required outcome reads `identical masks, colours within 8 px of noise`. Measured over the results archive: 1 of 216 archived `ctl-real-vs-real` views had any colour pixel over the threshold (this one, 1 px). An armed part parity lane must not flake INVALID on render noise. Flown: every P5 reading, check and mutation run (design Appendix F) read controls ok on the fixed judge.

## ~~GHOST-AIRBRAKE-START-NOT-DEPLOYED~~: a recording that starts with an airbrake deployed shows it stowed at its first frame [FILED 2026-11-22 from the P6 state engine's first live runs (branch `part-parity-p6-s3`, harness runs `2026-11-22_1411` / `_1419` / `_1428_S3L-part-parity-states-local`, a local uncommitted acceptance spec; design `docs/dev/design-part-ghost-parity.md` D.5); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-light-airbrake`; low]

What: `airbrake1--default--deployed`: the event route (stowed snapshot + the polled `DeployableExtended midx=0`) matches the real part (iou 1.0 in every view), but the start route (the deployed snapshot + its start seeds) reads `not-reached` with `startFirstFrame.atTarget = false` (start iou 0.39 `side-a`, 0.06 `top`). The log shows why: `Spawn baseline: stowed 1/1 deployable(s)` for the deployed snapshot, then the seed `DeployableExtended (aeroSurface)` starts the deploy transition at the first frame, so a recording that starts with the brakes out (a split TIP, a Re-Fly, a station) draws them folding out over the clip. The snapshot baseline reads no `ModuleAeroSurface.deploy`.

Seen again 2026-11-22 on both orbit state lanes (`airbrake1--default--deployed--65d4f96a`, PP-3 `2026-11-22_1656` and PP-4 `2026-11-22_1644`: start route shape blob 33770 px, 42.8 % on `side-a`).

Fix: the snapshot baseline reads the persisted `deploy` of `ModuleAeroSurface` / `ModuleControlSurface` (stock `ModuleControlSurface.deploy` is `isPersistant`, and `ModuleAeroSurface.OnSave` writes it again; KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) into `SnapshotPartBaseline.surfaceDeployed` (`GhostVisualBuilder.TryClassifySnapshotSurfaceDeploy`, the live classifier's reading: `deploy` decides, a deploy whose first finite `aeroDeployAngle` / `deployAngle` is under 0.5 deg reads stowed). It is kept only when the surface will own the part's one deployable info, as the builder decides (no `ModuleDeployablePart`, gear, ladder, cargo bay or animation group on the part; the aero surface before the control surface), and `ResolveSnapshotBaselineActions` takes it as the last arm of the deployable cascade, so the ghost spawns deployed at once and the start seed `DeployableExtended (aeroSurface)` finds it already there instead of folding it out. No recorded data or save key added. xUnit: `SnapshotBaselineParserTests` (`SurfaceDeploy_*`), `SnapshotBaselineApplicationTests` (`ResolveActions_SurfaceDeploy*`, `ApplySnapshotBaselines_SurfaceDeployed_SpawnsTheAirbrakeDeployed`).

## ~~GHOST-LIT-SPOTLIGHT-LENS~~: a lit spot light's lens is drawn in a different colour on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from the same P6 runs; CLOSED 2026-11-22, no ghost defect: the stock cases are the sweep photographing the real lamp mid-fade, the ReStock cases are GHOST-WATERFALL-LIGHT-FX-MISSING; low]

What: `spotlight1--default--lit` (stock-minimal): both judged routes reach `lit` (`lightPlaybackStates.isOn`), shape matches (iou 0.9998), but S4's judge reads colour fails `color-blob-px side-a=17070`, `bottom=48844` on both routes; the stowed case and `mk1pod.v2` cabin light pass. The capture rig switches every scene light off (design D3), so this is the lens / flare emission. Evidence: `<umbrella>/logs/flights/s3-2026-11-22_1428/` (atlas and sidecar under `s3st6/`).

Diagnosis (branch `ghost-light-airbrake`): the ghost writes stock's SETTLED lens emissive (`lightColor`, flare tint white) and that is right. Stock `ModuleLight.FixedUpdate` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) fades the lens `_EmissiveColor` as `Lerp(black, lightColor, currentTime / lightBrightenSpeed)` in game seconds, and every stock light cfg sets `lightBrightenSpeed = 2.5`, while the state driver settles a light case for 1 s. So the real lamp is photographed part-way through its fade. Measured from the PP-3 `_1656` atlases (ghost minus stowed over real minus stowed, per channel): `spotlight1` 1.87 (captured about 1.34 game s after the press, 2.5 / 1.34 = 1.87), `spotlight2` 2.35, `spotlight1.v2` 1.82, `spotlight2.v2` 2.23, `spotlight3` 2.02, `striplight1` 1.85; `domelight1` and `navlight1`, photographed 5 to 7 s after their press, read 1.0. The modded `navlight1--dark` (1.22) and `striplight1--dark` (1.15) are the same timing. The other four modded cases (`spotlight1--dark`, `spotlight1.v2--dark`, `spotlight2.v2--dark`, `spotlight3--dark`, plus the `groundlight1` / `groundlight2` lit cases) differ for another reason: the real part carries Waterfall light FX the ghost does not draw (GHOST-WATERFALL-LIGHT-FX-MISSING).

Fix: none in the ghost. Its lens snaps to the settled colour where stock fades over 2.5 s; transcribing the fade would put per-frame material writes on every ghost light for a short transient, which the design principle rules out. The instrument fix, settling a light case for at least its module's `lightBrightenSpeed` before the photograph, is handed to the sweep instrument work (`PartParityStateDriver`'s light settle, design D.1 / D.3).

Also 2026-11-22 (PP-3 `2026-11-22_1656` / PP-4 `2026-11-22_1644`, both routes, `state-invisible` unless noted): stock `spotlight1`, `spotlight1.v2--basic`, `spotlight2`, `spotlight2.v2--basic`, `spotlight3--basic`, `striplight1--basic` (colour blobs 2348 to 47340 px); modded `spotlight1--dark`, `spotlight1.v2--dark`, `spotlight2.v2--dark` (also a 14.6 % shape blob on `bottom`), `spotlight3--dark`, `striplight1--dark`, `navlight1--dark` (PP-4 `_1644` and `_1718`). Every lit lens or emitter differs, not only the spot light's.

## GHOST-WATERFALL-LIGHT-FX-MISSING: a lit light's Waterfall flare and beam are not drawn on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from GHOST-LIT-SPOTLIGHT-LENS (PP-4 `2026-11-22_1718`, modded-compat); OPEN; low (modded installs with a Waterfall light pack only)]

What: on modded-compat, `StockWaterfallEffects` / `RestockWaterfallExpansion` add Waterfall effects to the stock lights (`Templates/Stock/Lights/stock-spotlight-1..4.cfg`, `stock-floodlight-1.cfg`, `stock-gearlight.cfg`): a billboard flare (`Waterfall_FX_lightFlare_0/.../fx-billboard-generic-1/Billboard`) and a beam (`Waterfall_FX_1lightFx_0/.../fx-cylinder/Cylinder`). The real lit part shows the flare glowing over the lamp face; the ghost has no Waterfall renderers (structure `missingOnGhost`, `nonVisual = fx`), so it shows the bare lit lens. Cases: `spotlight1--dark--lit` (colour blob 111165 px), `spotlight1.v2--dark--lit` (79771), `spotlight2.v2--dark--lit` (83607), `spotlight3--dark--lit` (149171, side-a), `groundlight1--default--lit` (57643), `groundlight2--default--lit` (4349); `memlander` / `mk1-3pod` carry the same FX nodes with no visible difference. Evidence: sidecars in `<umbrella>/automation/results-archive/2026-11-22_1718_PP-4-part-parity-states-modded/partparity/pp4/`, atlases in `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/p6-s6/img/3/`.

Fix: not started. Ghosts draw no Waterfall effect today (`WaterfallCompat.cs` only recovers the stock FX a Waterfall pack deletes). A fix would build the light template's Waterfall meshes on the ghost and drive them from the light's on state; weigh the per-ghost cost against how rarely a lit light is seen up close.

## ~~PARTPARITY-STOWED-POSE-NOT-STOWED: the stowed sweep photographs a lone landing gear deployed and a Mk2 cargo bay open~~ [FILED 2026-11-22 from the same P6 runs; DONE 2026-11-22, P6 S8; low]

What: a one-part vessel authored with no persistent module values starts at each field's initial value: `ModuleWheelDeployment` starts Deployed (the seed logs `Seeded already-deployed gear: 'GearSmall'`) and a `ModuleCargoBay` whose `closedPosition = 1` (the Mk2 / Mk3 bays) starts open at `animTime = 0`. The P6 state cases author the stowed pose (`PartParityStateDriver.AuthorStowedPose`: `stateString = Retracted`; `animTime = closedPosition` with the matching `animSwitch`) and refuse a press whose target already reads reached, but the stowed PP-1 / PP-2 cases (`PartParityCaseAuthoring.AuthorVesselNode`) still photograph those parts in the target pose, so their "stowed" rows are not stowed.

Fix (P6 S8, branch `part-parity-p6-s8`): `PartParityCaseAuthoring.AuthorStowedPose` writes the stowed pose into every stowed case's authored part (`stateString = Retracted` on each `ModuleWheelDeployment`; a `ModuleCargoBay`'s `ModuleAnimateGeneric` deploy module at `animTime = closedPosition` with the matching `animSwitch`), one Verbose `authored stowed pose` line per case; the state driver's pose for its gear / bay case is the same helper restricted to the pressed module. Case ids unchanged (the stowed-id pin passes). Evidence: a local PP-1 reading run limited to the gear, legs and bays (`2026-11-22_1803`, stock-minimal, 7 filtered steps, 18 cases, automation DLL sha256 prefix 4282a6db) photographs every gear and leg retracted and the Mk2 / Mk3 bays and ramp closed, real and ghost alike, against the P3 run `2026-11-22_0033` (gear deployed, bays open). Verdicts: the six gear / legs and the rover wheel `warn` -> `pass` (they no longer droop in free fall), the Mk2 / Mk3 bays stay `pass`, `mk3cargoramp` `pass` -> `warn` (a 60 px shape blob on side-a). Pictures and viewer: `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/p6-s8/` (`sweeps/pp1g`, `viewer/`).

## GHOST-FAIRING-OPEN-TOP-SEAM: an open-top procedural fairing's ghost lacks a thin panel seam line the live one shows [FILED 2026-11-22 from the P6 S8 FGV context runs; OPEN; low]

What: `fairingsize2--white--stowed--fgv-3-open-top--9dd2b1aa` (FGV's open-top configuration, intact) reads `warn` on both S8 reading runs (`2026-11-22_1758` and `_1806` of a local `contexts=fgv states=all` spec, stock-minimal): IoU 1.0 in every view, a 140 px colour blob on side-a only (8 px on side-b), a thin vertical seam line at one panel edge that the live stock panels show and the ghost's stock-panel shell does not. Every other FGV case reads `pass`; FGV-1 does not measure pixels, so it passes the same craft.

Investigated 2026-11-22 (branch `ghost-deploy-fixes`), not fixed: the geometry is not the difference. The ghost's shell runs stock's own panel builder with the arguments stock's flight path uses (decompiled `ModuleProceduralFairing.SpawnMeshes`: `SetupPanelArray`, `Spawn`, `BuildMesh(triangulate: true, panel one ring below)`; `GhostVisualBuilder.TryBuildStockFairingPanels` does the same), the silhouettes match (IoU 1.0) and the structure lists no transform or mesh-shape difference. Read off the `_1806` atlas, the blob is a one-pixel diagonal line along one panel edge (x 72 to 79, y 52 to 395 of side-a): the real pixel is darker (about 143,137,122) where the ghost's is (about 176,170,156), the rest of the panel is pixel-identical. So it is edge shading, which points at the panel MATERIAL (stock gives every panel its own `FairingsFlightMat` instance and applies the variant to each; the ghost shares one cached clone per part, variant and role, the structure's only `materialDiffers` entries), not the mesh. Next step needs a live dump of both panel materials at that seam (shader, keywords, main and bump textures with tiling / offset / wrap and filter mode) before a fix can be chosen; low, one view, one configuration.

## ~~PARTPARITY-SUN-TRACKER-CAP~~: a real sun-tracking panel is still slewing at the 10 s tracking cap [FILED 2026-11-22 from the same P6 runs; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `part-parity-p6-s6` (PP-3 re-flight `2026-11-22_1656`); low]

What: `solarpanels4--default--deployed` captures tagged `still-tracking` on every run: the real pivot still turns about 2.4 deg per 0.5 s at the cap (`sun tracker still moving at the cap`), so it sits 17 to 20 deg short of the ghost's aim (the ghost slews at 20 deg/s) and the views read warn / fail on the panel's edge. The cap is S1's `SunTrackerCapSeconds` (design D.3). PP-3's first full flight `2026-11-22_1634` showed it on all nine tracking panels (every one tagged `still-tracking`, 1 to 14 deg short; 8 of 9 failed).

Fix: stock slews the pivot by `Quaternion.Lerp(current, aim, deltaTime * trackingSpeed)` (decompiled `ModuleDeployablePart`, `trackingSpeed` 0.25 on every stock tracking panel), an exponential approach that needs about 21.4 s from 180 deg to meet the still rule; `SunTrackerCapSeconds` 10 -> 25 (the wave admission bound with a tracker 56.7 -> 71.7 s). Re-flight `2026-11-22_1656`: no panel still tracking (settled 0.5 to 17.8 s after the done signal), real and ghost aim within 0.1 to 1.4 deg; 3 of 9 panels still fail on small shape blobs (`solarpanels1` 489 px, `solarpanelox10c` 147 px: the real pivot stops about 1 deg short of the ghost's aim), the rest pass or warn. PP-4 flew before the re-pin.

## ~~GHOST-CHUTE-CANOPY-AIM~~: a deployed parachute's ghost canopy points a different way from the live one [FILED 2026-11-22 from the P6 air lanes' first flights (branch `part-parity-p6-s7`, harness runs `2026-11-22_1713_PP-5-part-parity-chutes-stock` and `2026-11-22_1715_PP-6-part-parity-chutes-modded`, design `docs/dev/design-part-ghost-parity.md` D.4); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-chute-canopy-aim`; FLOWN `2026-11-22_1809_PP-5-part-parity-chutes-stock` / `2026-11-22_1810_PP-6-part-parity-chutes-modded`; medium on ReStock, low on stock]

What: every air case of both lanes reads `fail` (report-only) on shape, and the structural diff names the canopy renderers alone: stock reaches its state for real (`ParachuteSemiDeployed` / `ParachuteDeployed` recorded, the ghost read-back `applied` on both routes), but stock re-aims the live canopy every physics tick (`ModuleParachute.FixedUpdate`: `LookRotation(-dragVectorDir, part.forward)` plus the Perlin wobble), while the ghost's canopy keeps the pose of the model. With the canopy measured inside its window (tilt + wobble 0.5 to 2.2 deg), the ghost's canopy is off by: stock `parachuteSingle` / `parachuteLarge` / `parachuteDrogue` about 179 deg (a roll about the canopy axis, 0 to 3 cm), stock `parachuteRadial` / `radialDrogue` about 90 deg (9 to 19 cm); on ReStock (modded-compat) the Mk16's canopy hangs UPSIDE DOWN below the part (179 deg, 25 m) and the clustered / radial canopies are turned (118 to 179 deg, 9 to 18 m). So the D.4 `canopy-airflow` cap never applies (it allows at most tilt + wobble + 1 deg). A watcher of a descending ghost sees the ReStock Mk16's canopy under the capsule.

Evidence: the sweeps and atlases in `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/p6-s7/sweeps/pp5` and `pp6` (the viewer site `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/p6-s7/index.html`); the reading flights `2026-11-22_1709_PP-5R` / `_1711_PP-6R` (local specs) read the same.

Fix: two ghost changes and one measure change.

1. The ghost aims an open canopy the way stock does (`GhostPlaybackLogic.CanopyAim.cs`, transcribed from decompiled `ModuleParachute.FixedUpdate`): `canopy.rotation = LookRotation((invertCanopy ? -1 : 1) * dragDir, up)`, `up` = the part's +Z, or for a symmetry group (snapshot `sym` count + 1, stock's `symmetryCount`) the direction from the part to the ghost root (stock: `vessel.CurrentCoM`), then the group's spread tilt `Clamp(spreadAngle * symmetryCount, 0, 45)` about the canopy's X (a third while semi), turned toward at `rotationSpeedDPS` (`RotateTowards`; snap on a stage change, a scrub or a gap over 1 s). `dragDir` is the ghost's own surface-relative velocity (`lastInterpolatedSurfaceVelocity`, stock's `rb.velocity + Krakensbane`), else straight down the body's gravity (velocity unknown or under 0.5 m/s), else the part's -Y. Armed by the semi / deployed appliers (aimed at once), stopped by cut / repack / destroyed / the loop re-stow, driven each frame from `ApplyPartStateForFrame` and `ApplyPartEvents` (KSC / preview ghosts). EVA chutes keep their fixed kerbal-relative pose (`ModuleEvaChute` does not aim by airflow). Not modelled: the Perlin wobble (+-5 deg noise) and the spread's ease over the deploy clip. No recorded data added.
2. The sampled semi / deployed canopy pose was read in the model's frame but written as the canopy's LOCAL pose, so a canopy under an offset parent (`model/chute/canopy`, `model/parachute/canopy`) sat 3 to 19 cm off; `MoveCanopySampleToParentFrame` re-expresses it in the canopy's parent frame at build.
3. The air context's `wobble` (`PartParityAirContext.MeasureCanopy`) is now the whole rotation between the canopy and stock's un-wobbled pose `LookRotation(aim, up)`: the noise also rolls the canopy about its axis, which the old forward-only angle missed, so a ghost aimed exactly showed up to 2 deg more than the cap allowed.

Proof: xUnit `CanopyAimTests` (aim, fallbacks, spread, up hint, step, read-back). Re-read with the fix (automation DLL sha256 prefix 2f1c4e0a, both installs): PP-5 cases=10 pass=0 warn=9 fail=1 (was fail=10), the canopy rotation difference 0.0 to 2.9 deg (was 89 to 180), canopy position difference 0 (was up to 0.19 m), every rotation within the measured tilt + wobble; PP-6 cases=10 fail=10, the rotation 0.8 to 2.9 deg (was 118 to 179; the Mk16 canopy now opens above the part) and within tilt + wobble on every case. The earlier build's re-read `2026-11-22_1747` / `_1750` read the same. Both PASS attempt 1, controls ok, complete, recompute 0 mismatches. The fails left are the cap's own limits, todo PARTPARITY-CANOPY-CAP-LEVER-ARM. Viewer: `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/chute-aim/index.html` (regression mode against p6-s7). Not flown: the airflow source and the rate-limited turn during real playback (the parity ghosts are static, so every aim there read the gravity fallback).

## ~~PARTPARITY-RESTOCK-SEMI-READBACK~~: the ghost read-back says a ReStock chute's semi canopy is not shown while the picture shows it [FILED 2026-11-22 from the same air flights; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-chute-canopy-aim`, FLOWN `2026-11-22_1810_PP-6-part-parity-chutes-modded`; low]

What: on modded-compat every `semi` case reads `ghostEvent = ghostStart = not-reached` (flag `state-not-modelled:*:not-reached`), while the atlas shows the ghost's semi canopy open like the real one (`parachutelarge--default--semi--air--a3de8fcb`). The read-back (`PartParityStateDriver.CanopyWord`) compares the canopy transform's `localScale` with the sampled semi scale; ReStock's chutes open by animating child bones, not that scale. The stock chutes read `applied`.

Fix: ReStock's canopy root keeps one scale at semi and full, so the deployed-scale test matched first. `CanopyWord` now also reads the animated canopy bones (`ParachuteGhostInfo.canopyBones`) against each stage's sampled pose and calls a stage only when the root scale and the bones both sit there (`PartParityStateDriver.ClassifyCanopyStage`, xUnit in `CanopyAimTests`). ## ~~PARTPARITY-CANOPY-CAP-LEVER-ARM~~: the D.4 canopy cap refuses an exactly aimed ghost canopy in two shapes [FILED 2026-11-22 from the GHOST-CHUTE-CANOPY-AIM re-read flights `2026-11-22_1809_PP-5-part-parity-chutes-stock` / `2026-11-22_1810_PP-6-part-parity-chutes-modded`; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `parity-instrument-fixes`; low (judge only, report-only lanes)]

What: with the ghost canopy aimed like stock's, every air case's canopy rotation difference equals the measured tilt + wobble (to 0.1 deg), yet 11 of 20 cases still read `fail`. (1) ReStock (all 10 PP-6 cases): the canopy renderers (`Canopy004`, `CanopyConnectorWire004`, ...) sit metres from the canopy transform's pivot, so the wobble's 0.6 to 3 deg rotation moves them 0.1 to 0.6 m in the part-relative records, and the cap needs `positionDeltaM <= 0.001`. (2) One stock case per PP-5 flight (`radialDrogue` full in `_1747`, `parachuteDrogue` full in `_1809`): the wobble was 0.49 / 0.57 deg and the ghost's rotation difference stayed under `PartParityStructure.RotationToleranceDeg` (0.5 deg), so the structure lists no `transformDiffers` entry and the cap could not engage.

Fix (design D.6, canopy cap): the air context writes each canopy renderer's distance from the canopy pivot into its structure entry (additive key `canopyPivotDistanceM`, `PartParityStructure.StampCanopyPivotDistances`), and the judge allows `positionDeltaM <= 0.001 + 2 d sin(t / 2)` with `t = min(|rotationDeltaDeg| + 0.5, bound)`: the chord the entry's own turn sweeps at its lever arm (a canopy moved without turning gets no arc). A route whose structure was measured with no transform difference at all is a sub-tolerance turn and caps when the measured `|tilt| + |wobble|` is at least 0.1 deg; a null structure (ghost not built) is never capped. Scale, mesh, material, visibility and a rotation beyond the bound still fail. C# tolerances, the key table and the key test are source-synced; Python cells red on the over-wide shapes (translation without a turn, a short arm, an unmeasured structure). The archived flights re-judge: PP-5 `_1809` 9 warn / 1 fail -> 10 warn; PP-1 / PP-2 stowed sweeps byte-identical.

Flown on this branch (`parity-instrument-fixes`, report-only lanes, every run PASS attempt 1, controls ok, complete): round 1 (automation DLL sha256 prefix 92662c43) PP-3 `2026-11-22_1946`, PP-4 `_1958`, PP-5 `_2010`, PP-6 `_2012`; round 2 on the final instrument (prefix 6fd81cd0) PP-3 `2026-11-22_2014`, PP-4 `_2026`, PP-5 `_2039`, PP-6 `_2041`. Viewer: `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/parity-instrument/index.html` (PP-1 `_0033` + PP-3 + PP-5 as `stock`, PP-2 `_1157_run2` + PP-4 + PP-6 as `modded`). PP-5 10 warn on both rounds; PP-6 10 fail (`_1810`) -> 10 warn on both rounds. In PP-6 every canopy entry's position difference is at or under the chord of its own rotation (`parachuteLarge` full: 0.080 m against 0.080 m at 13.8 m and 0.33 deg); the dropped-events control's 120 deg canopy still fails.

## ~~THRUST-REVERSER-NOT-RECORDED~~: a jet engine's thrust reverser is never recorded, so its ghost never shows it [FILED 2026-11-22 from the P6 state-rules enumeration (branch `part-parity-p6-s1`, design `docs/dev/design-part-ghost-parity.md` D.1); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `thrust-reverser-record`; low]

What: `JetEngine` (J-33 "Wheesley") and `turboFanSize2` (J-90 "Goliath") carry their thrust reverser as a standalone `ModuleAnimateGeneric` (`TF1ThrustReverser`, `TF2ThrustReverser`). Both parts also carry `ModuleAnimateHeat`, so `FlightRecorder.HasDedicatedAnimateHandler` is true and `PartStatePoller.PollAnimateGeneric` skips the whole part: a reverser the player deploys is never recorded and the ghost always shows it stowed. Found on both harness installs (stock-minimal and modded-compat); the P6 sweep lists the two modules as excluded `not-polled`, so the gap stays visible.

Fix: `ModuleAnimateHeat` left `FlightRecorder.HasDedicatedAnimateHandler`'s list. Decompiled, it is a `ModuleAnimationSetter` that drives only its own clip (`animName`, set from `ThermalAnim`: `TF1Heat` / `TF2Heat`) and owns no `ModuleAnimateGeneric`, and no part on either install shares a clip between the two (config scan), so the reverser is now polled by `PartStatePoller.PollAnimateGeneric` (both recorders) and seeded by `PartStateSeeder.SeedAnimateGeneric` through the one predicate, and replays through the existing `DeployableExtended` / `DeployableRetracted` path onto the part's standalone animate-generic ghost info (the ghost builder never skipped it; the heat info stays separate). The start route follows: `TryParseSnapshotPartBaseline` no longer counts `ModuleAnimateHeat` as a dedicated handler, so a snapshot with the reverser deployed spawns its ghost deployed. The sweep mirror (`PartParityStateRules.DedicatedHandlerModuleNames`) dropped it in step, so the reversers are `animate-generic` cases (D.1 12 / 17) and `not-polled` names no part. xUnit: `PartParityStateRulesTests` (the JetEngine case, the D.1 counts, the mirror cell, which reds when the recorder list alone re-adds the heat module), `SnapshotBaselineParserTests.StandaloneAnimateGeneric_BesideAnimateHeat_KeepsItsOpinion`, and the re-taken `part-state-poller-animate-generic` golden (the `genericOnAnimateHeat` part now emits `DeployableExtended` from both recorders). Live (2026-11-22, one automation DLL on both installs, sha256 prefix c3beb870): local `filter=` copies of PP-3 / PP-4 (specs kept in `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/thrust-reverser/specs/`), PP-3 `2026-11-22_1937` (JetEngine) and `_1939` (turboFanSize2), PP-4 `_1941` and `_1943`, all PASS attempt 1, partParity REPORT, controls ok, complete, recompute 10 / 0 mismatches, press ok: each deployed reverser case reached its state with the poll's `DeployableExtended` (midx 2 / 3), both ghost routes `applied`, start pose at target, verdict pass (6 of 6 cases pass). The background recorder's path is proven by the golden only (both recorders share `PollAnimateGeneric`).

## ~~GHOST-SCANNER-STATE-NO-INFO~~: a deployed orbital or surface scanner's ghost stays in its rest pose [FILED 2026-11-22 from PARTPARITY-STATE-SWEEP-FINDINGS-2026-11-22; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-deploy-fixes`; low]

What: `orbitalscanner--default--deployed--35b9ec6d` (stock: `ModuleAnimationGroup`, empty `deployAnimationName`, `activeAnimationName = miniscanner`), `orbitalscanner--size0--deployed--b6d5edab` and `surfacescanner--default--deployed--53e1f66f` (modded; the surface scanner a `ModuleAnimateGeneric`): the press reaches the target and the recorder's poll records `DeployableExtended`, but both ghost routes read `state-not-modelled:<route>:no-info` (the engine holds no deployable info for the module) and `start-pose-not-first-frame`; the real part shows its deployed / running pose, the ghost its rest pose (event-route shape blobs 2.7k to 30k px, up to 7 %).

Cause, two different shapes. (1) The M4435 (`OrbitalScanner`, both installs) has a `ModuleAnimationGroup` with no deploy clip and a running clip (`miniscanner`, ReStock `Spin`). Stock `CheckForActivity` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) plays the running clip while the group is deployed and any `IAnimatedModule` on the part reports active; a `BaseConverter` reports active only while it runs, but the scanner's `ModuleResourceScanner` / `ModuleGPS` report `isEnabled`, which the deploy sets, so the real scanner spins as soon as it is deployed. The ghost built the running loop (`ConverterLoopGhostInfo`) but only the converter edges ever started it, and a scanner has no converter. (2) ReStock's `SurfaceScanner` deploys with a `ModuleAnimateGeneric` clip `screenon` that moves no transform and only animates the screen colour; the deployable builder found no transform delta and built nothing, so the colour stayed at its rest value.

Fix: (1) the loop is marked deploy-driven at build (`GhostVisualBuilder.AnimationGroupLoopFollowsDeploy`: `alwaysActive`, or the part carries one of the stock `IAnimatedModule`s whose `ModuleIsActive` is plain `isEnabled`: ModuleResourceScanner, ModuleGPS, ModuleOrbitalSurveyor); DeployableExtended / Retracted start / stop it at the recorded event UT (`GhostPlaybackLogic.RecordDeployDrivenLoop`), the snapshot baseline's `isDeployed` starts it from spawn, and the converter edges keep driving only the converter loops (drills, ISRUs). (2) a colour-only standalone animate-generic deploy clip joins the part's `DeployableGhostInfo` as colour states (`DeployableColorState`, stowed = clip time 0, deployed = time 1, from the existing rest-state colour sampling), written at every deploy fraction. The sweep read-back (`PartParityStateDriver.ReadGhostInput`) counts the colours as a sampled pose and reads a deploy-driven loop as the deployed state. xUnit `GhostDeployFixesTests`. Not modelled: a scanner whose `IsSituationValid` refuses the enable spins on the ghost anyway; Breaking Ground ground parts (`ModuleGroundPart`: active only while its experiment is `Enabled`, which is not recorded) keep their idle loop stopped as before; on a part with several `ModuleAnimateGeneric`s any deploy event drives the deploy clip's colours (as it already drives its transforms); a colour-only part saved mid-travel spawns at the stowed colour; the running phase of a spinning part is not matched to the real one, so a still of it can still differ by phase (P7, design 9.2). The S7 in-game cell `ConverterLoopAdvancesWhileActiveAndStopsOnDeactivate` now skips a deploy-driven loop when it picks its part.

Proof (full lanes, against PP-3 `2026-11-22_1656` / PP-4 `2026-11-22_1718`): PP-4 `2026-11-22_1924` (modded-compat, automation DLL sha256 prefix ef5626b1, the build before the review narrowed the rule to the three module types, which changes nothing for these parts) PASS attempt 1: `surfacescanner--default--deployed` fail (colour blob 14006 px, `no-info` on both routes) -> warn (169 px, both routes `applied`, `deployColors=1`); `orbitalscanner--size0--deployed` both routes `no-info` -> `applied` (`driver=deploy`, `Converter loops driven: 1`), still fail on the picture because the ghost's spin phase is not the real one's (Scanner_Body 125 deg off on the event route, 92 deg on the start route). PP-3 `2026-11-22_2043` (stock-minimal, b6b7f08a, the final build) PASS attempt 1: `orbitalscanner--default--deployed` `no-info` -> `applied`, same phase residual. Viewer: `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/ghost-deploy-fixes/viewer-both/index.html` (regression mode).

## ~~GHOST-RESTOCK-COMMDISH-DEPLOY-POSE~~: ReStock's Communotron 88-88 ghost is deployed into the wrong shape [FILED 2026-11-22 from PARTPARITY-STATE-SWEEP-FINDINGS-2026-11-22; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-deploy-fixes`; low]

What: `commdish--default--deployed--632298e2` on modded-compat fails on shape on both routes (event-route shape blob 11203 px, 6.9 % on `side-a`): the real dish ends with its mast extended above the dish, the ghost with the body above the dish and the feed below it. The stock install's same case passes (PP-3), so it is the ReStock model's deploy the ghost poses wrongly. Flags `depth-mask-repaired:1` and `ghost-outside-real-bounds`; the only structural difference is the skipped ReStock `DepthMask` (by design).

Cause: the ReStock model (`restock-antenna-stack-4.mu`) is exported with a 100x scale baked into `Dish` (and `Case`), so its `Deploy` clip raises `Dish/center` by 0.0051 local units (0.0077 -> 0.0026), about 0.5 m on the part, and extends `Dish/Reflector center/Reflector` by 0.0038 (about 0.27 m). The pose sampler (`CollectTransformDeltas`) kept a transform only when its LOCAL move passed 0.01 units, so it kept the 24 arm rotations and dropped those moves: the ghost opened the dish at the foot of the body instead of lifting it above.

Fix: a position move also counts when it passes the same threshold measured in the model root's frame (`GhostVisualBuilder.IsSampledPoseDelta`, the local delta carried through the parent's matrix), so every transform the old test kept is still kept and a move under a scaled parent is added; one Verbose `kept N transform(s) whose local move is under the threshold` line per sampled clip that needs it. xUnit `GhostDeployFixesTests`.

Proof: PP-4 `2026-11-22_1924` (modded-compat, PASS attempt 1): `commdish--default--deployed` fail (shape blob 11837 px, IoU 0.23 on the side views) -> pass (shape 0, colour 5 px), the ghost's dish and reflector now above the body as on the real part; the wider test also adds transforms on ReStock's `miniLandingLeg` (`--bare--deployed` warn, shape blob 4072 -> 412 px) and `mk3CargoRamp` (pass, unchanged). PP-3 `2026-11-22_2043` (stock-minimal, PASS attempt 1): the wider test adds transforms only on `miniLandingLeg` and `mk3CargoRamp`, both cases unchanged (warn 393 px / pass); the stock `commdish` stays pass. Every verdict that moved the other way on either lane is a part whose sampling did not change: the sun-tracking panels (the same 1 deg pivot residual at a different sun angle) and one colour blob on PP-3 `liquidengineke-1--full--jettisoned` (58 -> 173 px).

## ~~GHOST-CABIN-LIGHT-NO-INFO~~: some cabin and bay lights have no ghost light info [FILED 2026-11-22 from PARTPARITY-STATE-SWEEP-FINDINGS-2026-11-22; CLOSED 2026-11-22, not a ghost defect (branch `ghost-deploy-fixes`), instrument follow-up PARTPARITY-STOCK-INVISIBLE-LIGHT-READBACK; low]

What: `kv1pod`, `kv2pod`, `kv3pod` (both installs), `size1to0servicemodule--notunnel` and `restock-service-module-125-625-1--notunnel` (cabin-light family, modded) and `telescopicladderbay--default--lit` (light family, modded): the toggle reaches `lit`, but both ghost routes read `state-not-modelled:<route>:no-info`. Every one is also `state-invisible`: switching the light on does not change the real picture under the capture rig (design D3 turns every scene light off), so these cases fail on the flags alone.

Finding (no code change): in every case stock itself shows nothing when the light is switched on, so the ghost is right to build no light, and the real picture not changing (`state-invisible`) is the same fact seen from the other side.

- KV pods (both installs): the pod's `ModuleAblator` names a second `ModuleColorChanger` as its char module and writes `_EmissiveColor` every frame after the cabin light module, so the window shows the char colour whatever the light says. The ghost builder transcribes that order (`ResolveColorChangerRendererSources`; `ColorChanger resolve 'kv1Pod' ... modules=2 built=1 cabinLight=1 ablationChar=1`), so only the char entry owns the window material.
- Service modules, `NoTunnel` variant (ReStock `Size1to0ServiceModule`, `restock-service-module-125-625-1`): the light module has no renderer filter, but the only materials with `_EmissiveColor` are on the crew tunnel and end caps, which the variant hides (`ColorChanger resolve ... built=0 cabinLight=1 renderersWritten=0` in PP-4 `2026-11-22_1718`).
- `telescopicLadderBay` (modded): KSPCommunityFixes' LadderToggleableLight adds `ModuleLight` with `lightName = Point light`, and ReStock's `restock-ladder-extending-2` model carries no `Light` at all, so stock's `FindModelComponents<Light>` finds none and the ghost's light builder (every `Light` under the model) finds none either.

The `no-info` read-back is the sweep calling a correctly absent info a gap: filed as PARTPARITY-STOCK-INVISIBLE-LIGHT-READBACK.

## PARTPARITY-STOCK-INVISIBLE-LIGHT-READBACK: the sweep flags a lit case `no-info` when stock itself shows no light [FILED 2026-11-22 from GHOST-CABIN-LIGHT-NO-INFO (branch `ghost-deploy-fixes`); OPEN; low; instrument]

What: the KV pods, the `NoTunnel` service modules and the modded `telescopicLadderBay` lit cases read `state-not-modelled:<route>:no-info` on both routes, but stock never draws their light (the ablator char owns the pod window, the variant hides every emissive material, the ladder bay has no `Light`), so the ghost is right to carry no light info. The flags turn a matching picture into a fail.

Fix: not started. Likely shape: the state rules classify such a case from the real side (`state-invisible` plus a part whose light module stock cannot show) as not applicable rather than not modelled, or the case list drops it (design D.1).

## ~~PARTPARITY-RADIATOR-TRACKING~~: deployable radiators track the sun but the sweep does not wait for them [FILED 2026-11-22 from PARTPARITY-STATE-SWEEP-FINDINGS-2026-11-22; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `parity-instrument-fixes`; low; instrument]

What: `foldingRadLarge` / `Med` / `Small` (`ModuleDeployableRadiator`, `isTracking` true by the `ModuleDeployablePart` default, `trackingSpeed = 0.1`) turn their `Pivot` after deploying, like a solar panel, but the sweep's sun-tracker rule read only `ModuleDeployableSolarPanel`, so a radiator was captured about 1.3 s after its done signal with the real pivot mid-slew.

Fix (design D.3): `HasSunTracker` is the ghost's rule (any tracking `ModuleDeployablePart` whose pivot resolves; 9 panels + 3 radiators per install). Each part gets its cap from its slowest tracker's own `trackingSpeed` (`25 s x 0.25 / trackingSpeed`, 62.5 s for a radiator, at most 90 s; stock's slew is `Lerp(rotation, aim, deltaTime * trackingSpeed)`), and the wave admission adds the wave's largest tracker cap. Two further holes the first flight showed: the still rule is per tracker (the turn its own slew makes in 0.5 s with 0.85 deg left: 0.1 deg at 0.25, 0.04 deg at 0.1), and the window angle is exact (`PreciseAngleDeg`), because Unity's `Quaternion.Angle` reads 0 below about 0.16 deg and let round 1's radiators read still 3 deg short of the aim (real 104.6 deg, event ghost 107.9).

Flown on this branch (`parity-instrument-fixes`, report-only lanes, every run PASS attempt 1, controls ok, complete): round 1 (automation DLL sha256 prefix 92662c43) PP-3 `2026-11-22_1946`, PP-4 `_1958`, PP-5 `_2010`, PP-6 `_2012`; round 2 on the final instrument (prefix 6fd81cd0) PP-3 `2026-11-22_2014`, PP-4 `_2026`, PP-5 `_2039`, PP-6 `_2041`. Viewer: `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/parity-instrument/index.html` (PP-1 `_0033` + PP-3 + PP-5 as `stock`, PP-2 `_1157_run2` + PP-4 + PP-6 as `modded`). Round 2: every radiator settles in 25 to 52 s within 0.85 deg of its aim (event ghost 0.1 to 0.8 deg past the real pivot, panels 0.1 to 0.7). Verdicts: PP-3 `foldingradlarge` fail (colour blobs up to 947 px, was shape blobs up to 4911 px), `foldingradmed` fail (colour 403 px), `foldingradsmall` warn; PP-4 large fail (287 px), med pass, small warn. The residual is the still rule's 0.85 deg, shared with the panels: todo PARTPARITY-SUN-TRACKER-RESIDUAL.

## ~~PARTPARITY-ANIMATION-GROUP-PRESS~~: two animation-group cases cannot be posed by the press [FILED 2026-11-22 from PARTPARITY-STATE-SWEEP-FINDINGS-2026-11-22; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `parity-instrument-fixes`; low; instrument]

What: (1) `isru--default--deployed--082cb595` (stock) was PP-3's one setup fault, `action-failed` / `refused` (`already deployed before the press`): the ISRU's `ModuleAnimationGroup` has `autoDeploy = true` and no deploy clip. (2) `radialdrill--default--deployed--19529948` (modded, ReStock) was captured `still-animating` half out: the classifier reads deployed the moment `DeployModule` runs, the 10.7 s clip outlasted the settle cap, and the state timeout read the part's longest clip at its parked snap speed (-1000), 2 s.

Fix (design D.1, D.3): an `autoDeploy` animation group is excluded `auto-deploy` (decompiled `ModuleAnimationGroup.OnLoad`: stock sets `isDeployed` and hides both events and the three actions, so the player never sees it stowed; mirrored in `partparity.STATE_EXCLUSION_REASONS`, stock fixture row carries `autoDeploy=true`). An animation group's done signal also waits for its own deploy clip (`DeployClipDone`: not playing or at its end), and its timeout reads that clip at speed 1.

Flown on this branch (`parity-instrument-fixes`, report-only lanes, every run PASS attempt 1, controls ok, complete): round 1 (automation DLL sha256 prefix 92662c43) PP-3 `2026-11-22_1946`, PP-4 `_1958`, PP-5 `_2010`, PP-6 `_2012`; round 2 on the final instrument (prefix 6fd81cd0) PP-3 `2026-11-22_2014`, PP-4 `_2026`, PP-5 `_2039`, PP-6 `_2041`. Viewer: `<umbrella>/logs/partparity/parity-instrument/index.html` (PP-1 `_0033` + PP-3 + PP-5 as `stock`, PP-2 `_1157_run2` + PP-4 + PP-6 as `modded`). The ISRU is an exclusion (PP-3 setup faults 1 -> 0). `radialdrill` reaches its state after 10.69 s and passes on modded (was fail) and stock; `minidrill` (modded, 6 s clip) warn -> pass.

## ~~PARTPARITY-STACKED-SHROUD-TOP-COLOR~~: stacked stowed shroud cases differ in colour on the top view [FILED 2026-11-22 from PARTPARITY-STATE-SWEEP-FINDINGS-2026-11-22; FIXED 2026-11-22 (the heat shields, instrument), branch `parity-instrument-fixes`; the LV-1 split to PARTPARITY-LV1-SHROUD-ZFIGHT; low]

What: the stacked stowed cases of the ReStock heat shields failed on colour over the whole top face (PP-4 `_1644`: 153k to 161k px), and which ones failed changed between runs; `liquidenginemini.v2--shroud--stowed--stacked--28013141` (stock) failed on its rim, also changing between runs.

Cause, heat shields (instrument): the real side. Stock `ModuleColorChanger.UpdateColor` writes its colour into the part's shared `Part.mpb` and applies it to its own renderer list only, while `Part.SetOpacity` and the part highlight push that same block to every renderer of the part (decompiled), so an excluded renderer shows the colour once one of those writes runs after the colour changer's, and not before. ReStock excludes the heat shield's internals and fairing from the ablation char; the real top face photographed at 0.85 of the ghost's (atlas pixels 174 / 205 = 0.849, the full-ablator `charMax`) whenever the leak happened. The ghost honours the exclusion (`renderersFiltered=2`) and is right.

Fix (design D.3, "Colour-changer leak on the real part"): `PartParityColorChangerLeakRepair` resets, before the real records are read, every real mesh renderer outside a colour changer's list whose property block holds exactly that module's current colour and whose material differs, back to its material's value; flag `colorchanger-leak-repaired:<n>` (report-only), one Info line naming the renderers.

## ~~PARTPARITY-LIGHT-LENS-FADE~~: a lit light case photographed the real lens still fading in [FILED 2026-11-22 from PP-3 `2026-11-22_1656`; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `parity-instrument-fixes`; low; instrument]

What: stock `ModuleLight.FixedUpdate` fades the lens in, `_EmissiveColor = Lerp(black, lightColor, currentTime / lightBrightenSpeed)` in game seconds, and every stock and ReStock light cfg sets `lightBrightenSpeed = 2.5`, while the state driver settled a light for 1 s. PP-3 `_1656`: the ghost / real lens emission ratio 1.87 on `spotlight1` (captured 1.34 s after the press), 2.35 on `spotlight2`, 1.0 on `domelight1` / `navlight1` (captured 5 to 7 s after); the six stock lit spot / strip light cases failed on colour.

Fix (design D.1, D.3): a light settles for its own `lightBrightenSpeed` + 0.5 s (at least 1 s, at most 5 s, `LightSettleFor`), measured in game time too; the quick wave bound reads the 5 s cap.

What: the still rule (design D.3) holds once a tracker is under 0.85 deg from its aim, where stock's exponential slew is still turning slowly; the event-route ghost reaches the aim. Round 2 measured the event ghost 0.1 to 0.8 deg past the real pivot on every panel and radiator, and a few big panels fail on that residual, some flipping run to run: PP-3 `solarpanelox10c` and `solarpanels3` fail in both rounds, `foldingradlarge` / `foldingradmed` fail in round 2 (colour blobs 186 to 947 px); PP-4 `largesolarpanel` pass -> fail and `solarpanelox10c` warn -> fail between round 1 and round 2, `foldingradlarge` fail.

Fix: not started. Either a smaller remaining angle (0.3 deg needs about 26 s for a panel and 65 s for a radiator, so the caps and the wave bound grow), or a judge cap for a sun tracker's pivot subtree turned within the measured `|targetDeg - eventDeg|`, the way the canopy cap works.

## PARTPARITY-ROTOR01-GRAY-EDGE-LINE: the stock EM-16 rotor's gray variant shows a one-pixel edge-shading row in some runs [FILED 2026-11-23 from the P5 mutation flight (branch `part-parity-p5-gate`); OPEN; low; instrument]

What: `rotor.01--gray--d4b107c3` (PP-1, stock-minimal) reads a colour blob of exactly 312 px on `side-a` in 2 of 9 archived PP-1 runs (`2026-11-21_2111`, `2026-11-23_0607`), 162 px on `side-b` in a third (`2026-11-21_2011`) and 0 to 2 px in the other six. On modded-compat the same part reads 329 px on `side-b` in 1 of 8 (`2026-11-22_0045`). Everything else matches in every run: IoU 1.0, colour p99 1.4 at most, no transform, material or mesh difference. In the `_0607` atlas the over-threshold pixels are one row (y = 30, x 75 to 403, 317 px; real (88,88,88), ghost (102,103,102) at its left end), so the likely cause is a raster tie on a model edge that the co-located real and ghost resolve differently from run to run; not proved. Against the 192 px colour tolerance a 312 px row reads `drift`, so a clean armed PP-1 would red on it in roughly 2 of 9 runs.

Found by the P5 mutation flight (`2026-11-23_0607`, PARSEK-FAIL): 27 of its 28 reds were the mutated decouplers, and this was the 28th. The three baseline runs had all missed it.

Fix: not started. Accepted on stock as noisy colour in `harness/partparity/accepted.toml`, its own entry because the owner's ruling (GHOST-PARITY-RESIDUALS-2026-11-22) covers the modded case only. No other rotor or spinning part sits near the line: of the 131 such cases on both installs, only the MechJeb part `mumech.mj2.ar202` (a stable 125 to 127 px) and `size0.rotorengine.02` (54 px) pass 16 px in any P5-era run. Owner to read it in the viewer.

A second row of this kind, PARTPARITY-TRUSSPIECE-BLANKETS-EDGE-LINE (2026-11-23): one image row along a horizontal model edge that flips between runs. They are not the same signal: here the alpha is 255 on both sides and the colour differs ((88,88,88) against (102,103,102)), there the colour is equal within 2 levels and the alpha differs (224 to 246 against 255), and the premultiplied metric reads both as colour. One kind of artifact by all appearance (a coverage tie on the edge's row), not proved. A third occurrence should get a general rule instead of another accepted entry.

## PARTPARITY-TRUSSPIECE-BLANKETS-EDGE-LINE: a modular truss's side view shows a one-pixel edge row on the ReStock install in one run [FILED 2026-11-23 from the armed PP-2 flight `2026-11-23_1846` (PARSEK-FAIL(part-parity), one red, branch `fx-fly`); OPEN; low; instrument]

Fix: not started. A row of this kind is the second (PARTPARITY-ROTOR01-GRAY-EDGE-LINE, whose row differs in colour at equal alpha). A third occurrence should get a general rule instead of another accepted entry.

## ~~GHOST-PARITY-RESIDUALS-2026-11-22~~: four report-only colour fails left after the part ghost parity flights [FILED 2026-11-22 from the final P3/P4 flights `2026-11-22_0033_PP-1-part-parity-stock` and `2026-11-22_0045_PP-2-part-parity-modded` (both PASS attempt 1, branch `part-parity-p4`, automation DLL sha256 prefix 0da811c9); CLOSED 2026-11-22 as accepted cosmetic differences (owner ruling 2026-11-22, after reading the viewer); low]

What: after the two ghost-fix rounds (PRs #2745, #2749) the sweeps read PP-1 792 cases (pass 766, warn 25, fail 1, error 0) and PP-2 1510 cases (pass 1392, warn 115, fail 3, error 0), controls ok, complete, recompute 0 mismatches. The four fails, each a colour blob over the 256 px line:

Evidence: the case atlases and sidecars (`<caseId>.png`, `<caseId>.part.json`) and `partparity-verdicts.json` in `harness/results/2026-11-22_0033_PP-1-part-parity-stock_partparity/pp1/` and `harness/results/2026-11-22_0045_PP-2-part-parity-modded_partparity/pp2/` of the `part-parity-p4` worktree (the results folder dies with the worktree); the sidecars and manifests are kept in `<umbrella>/automation/results-archive/<runId>/partparity/<label>/`, the run consoles in `<umbrella>/logs/console/2026-11-22/p4fix4-PP-1.log` / `p4fix4-PP-2.log`. ## ~~GHOST-HEAT-CLONE-PUSHES-NEARBY-VESSEL~~: building a ghost of a heat-animated part could push or break a real vessel near it [FILED 2026-11-21 from the part ghost parity sweep (harness run `2026-11-21_2011_PP-1-part-parity-stock`, branch `part-parity-p3`; the same break in the P2 flight `<umbrella>/logs/flights/pp1-ladder-evidence-2026-11-21/KSP.log` line 12432); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `ghost-heat-clone-destroy`; xUnit `GhostTempCloneDestroyGateTests` (mutation: reverting the fix reds it); FLOWN 2026-11-21: every PP-1 / PP-2 sweep from `2026-11-21_2111` on kept its host whole and read complete; medium (physics damage to a real vessel, first ghost build of a part type per session)]

What: the sweep's host Kerbal X lost its `Decoupler.2` and `dockingPort2` and dropped from pe 93 km to pe 63 km in the same frame (6 ms) that the ghost of a `Clydesdale` case was built, 160 m away; the P2 flight shows the identical break at the same case. `GhostVisualBuilder.SampleHeatAnimation3State` instantiates the part prefab's model, colliders included, to sample its heat animation, and freed it with a deferred `Object.Destroy`, so the clone lived into the next physics step with a full-size collider and pushed whatever real vessel overlapped it. The three sibling samplers in `GhostVisualBuilder.AnimationSampling.cs` already used `DestroyImmediate`. The heat sample is cached per part name, so it bites only the first ghost of each heat-animated part type.

Fix: `Object.DestroyImmediate(tempClone)`, like the siblings. `GhostTempCloneDestroyGateTests` scans `Source/Parsek/Ghost/` (line comments stripped) and reds on a deferred `Destroy(tempClone)` or on a `tempClone = Object.Instantiate(...)` count that differs from the `DestroyImmediate(tempClone)` count.

Proof: PP-1 `2026-11-21_2111` and every later PP-1 / PP-2 flight answered every step with the host in one piece and in orbit, through the final pair `2026-11-22_0033` / `_0045` (GHOST-PARITY-RESIDUALS-2026-11-22).

## ~~TEST-GAPS-BATCH4-REFLY-2026-11-23~~: Re-Fly quits, a separation inside a Re-Fly, KSC purchases before a Re-Fly, a Re-Fly resumed in a new process [FILED 2026-11-23 from the test-gap list, batch 4; DONE: ALL NINE LANES LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-23; branch `b4-refly`; one new seam verb (`ExitToMainMenu`) and one new `AnswerMergeDialog` arg (`exit=`), automation-only C#]

What: four Re-Fly gaps no lane drove. (1) Leaving a live Re-Fly by Quit without saving or by Quit to Main Menu (the second needs the flight Esc menu's Quit to Main Menu, which no seam verb drove, then a load back from the main menu). (2) A separation inside a Re-Fly: the nested, session-scoped rewind point it authors, kept by a merge, purged by a discard, dropped by an F9 to before the separation. RF-14's header named this as not driven. (3) Space Center purchases made between a separation and its Re-Fly. (4) A Re-Fly saved mid-session and resumed in a new game process.

Seam: `ExitToMainMenu` (FLIGHT, two-phase, 120 s budget) runs stock's Quit to Main Menu (`saveAndExit(MAINMENU)`: confirm-exit, save, load) and completes OK `scene=MAINMENU persisted=true` once the main menu has settled; it is REJECTED `dialog-required` when a merge modal would block the exit (a live Re-Fly, or auto-merge off), so a lane answers those with `AnswerMergeDialog exit=mainMenu`. `AnswerMergeDialog exit=quitWithoutSaving|mainMenu` (Re-Fly conclusion only) leaves through stock's no-save exit or the main menu instead of the default saving exit to the Space Center. hlib mirrors both (`ExitToMainMenuSourceSyncTests`, `AnswerMergeExitSourceSyncTests`); xUnit `TestCommandExitToMainMenuTests` and `TestCommandMergeAnswerTests`. ## REWOUND-RESCUE-KERBAL-NEVER-JOINS-ROSTER: after a rewind past a committed rescue, the rescued kerbal never becomes crew when the clock reaches the rescue [FILED 2026-11-23 by code reading (test-gap list batch 4, branch `b4-career`); no red test, no flight; medium (a kerbal the committed timeline rescued stays Unowned, stranded or unlisted, for good)]

What the design says: "Rescued kerbals exist from the recovery UT of the recording that rescued
them" (parsek-game-actions-and-resources-recorder-design.md, the kerbals section).

What the code does (main 0003b8107). A completed rescue flips the stranded kerbal from Unowned to
Crew (`ProtoCrewMember.type`), `GameStateRecorder.OnKerbalTypeChange` books KerbalRescued, and
the commit converter makes a KerbalRescue row. In the kerbals walk that row only adds the name to
`ledgerCreatedKerbals` (`KerbalsModule.ProcessAction`), a deletion guard. Nothing acts when the
clock reaches it: `KerbalsModule.PromoteReachedCommittedHires` promotes reached KerbalHire rows
(Applicant -> Crew), and no counterpart exists for KerbalRescue. So after a Rewind-to-Launch (or
any load) to before the rescue, the loaded save holds the kerbal as Unowned (aboard the stranded
vessel when the accept is before the load, or not at all), and when the clock passes the committed
rescue's recovery he stays that way: he never appears on the crew list.

Second gap seen on the way, also unproven: KerbalRescued is never forwarded to the ledger directly
(no `ShouldForwardDirectLedgerEvent` call in `OnKerbalTypeChange`), so a rescue flipped while no
recorder claims the event (filed untagged, e.g. a recovery from the Tracking Station) reaches no
ledger row at all.

Fix (not narrow, owner questions first): promote a reached KerbalRescue row's kerbal to Crew the
way reached hires are promoted, and decide what happens to the stranded copy (the Unowned kerbal
aboard the regenerated stranded vessel, todo CONTRACT-REBUILD-SKIPS-ACCEPT-WORLD-EFFECTS): remove
him from that vessel, or keep the vessel and treat it as the committed flight's ghost target. A
lane would be the full rescue rendezvous noted in TEST-GAPS-BATCH4-CAREER item 5.
