## ~~GHOST-POSE-DUPLICATE-PATHS~~: two same-named transforms collapse into one in the ghost's pose sampling [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-2` `2026-11-21_2317`, branch `part-parity-p4`; ReStock `mk2LanderCabin.v2` lander variant: one hatch missing at rest, the other slides through the cabin when the doors move; log `AnimateGeneric 'mk2LanderCabin.v2': sampled 5 animated transforms from 'Mk2Doors'`); confirmed by reading the sampler; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes-2`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFix2Tests` (PosePaths_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only, models with same-named sibling transforms)]

What: the model has two sibling transforms named `CommonHatchRound`. `SnapshotTransformStates` (AnimationSampling.cs) keyed poses by path, so the second hatch overwrote the first; `CollectTransformDeltas` then compared the first hatch against the second's pose and recorded a fake animated transform whose stowed pose is the other hatch's, and the ghost resolved that path to the first hatch (first match), placing it on top of the second. The heat sampler (`TryBuildHeatInfo`'s cold / medium / hot snapshots) had the same last-wins keying.

Fix: `MarkFirstPathOccurrences` (pure) marks the first transform of each path in hierarchy order, the one Unity's clip binding and `FindTransformByPath` resolve; `SnapshotTransformStates`, `CollectTransformDeltas` and the heat sampler skip every later duplicate (one Verbose count when any is skipped), so a repeated path is sampled as its first transform only. The ghost side still resolves a path through `FindTransformByPath` on the ghost hierarchy, whose clones are created in prefab order.

## ~~GHOST-LIGHT-MOVEMENT-TRANSFORM~~: a spot light's head is drawn turned around on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-2` `2026-11-21_2317`, branch `part-parity-p4`; ReStock `spotLight1` / `spotLight2` and their `.v2`: the lamp head faces the other way on the ghost); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes-2`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFix2Tests` (LightMovement_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only, adjustable lights)]

What: stock `ModuleLight.OnStart` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) clamps the persisted `rotationAngle` / `pitchAngle` to the module's limits and calls `ModifyLightVector`, which sets the movement transform's `localRotation = Euler(rotateAxis, rotationAngle) * Euler(pitchAxis, pitchAngle)` (identity at 0 / 0), or the separate rotate / pitch transforms when there is no combined one. ReStock's lamps name `SpotLightBase` / `FloodR` (`canPitch`, `pitchAxisName = X`), whose .mu rest pose is turned 180 degrees from that, and `BuildLightGhostInfo` never applied the stock rotation.

Fix: `ApplyLightMovementTransforms` (PartInfoBuilders.cs), called at the top of `BuildLightGhostInfo` before the no-Light return: the persisted `movementTransformName` and angles come from the snapshot module (else the prefab module), the other names, axes and limits from the prefab module; `ResolveLightMovementTransforms` (pure, generic over the lookup) transcribes stock's combined / equal-names / separate lookup, `ClampLightAngle` the limits and `ResolveLightAngleVector` `GetAngleVector` (first letter X / Y / Z, a '-' second letter negates). The ghost clones get the stock local rotations once at build, with one Verbose line per light part. A light rotated in flight is not replayed (no event carries it).

## ~~GHOST-RESTOCK-LINKED-MESH~~: ReStock struts and fuel lines are never stretched or aimed on their ghosts [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-2` `2026-11-21_2317`, branch `part-parity-p4`; ReStock `fuelLine` / `strutConnector`: the line keeps its prefab length and direction; the modded KSP.log has zero `Compound part` fixup lines where the stock log has them); confirmed by the ReStock config and a decompile of `Restock.dll`; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes-2`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFix2Tests` (LinkedMesh_*); NOT FLOWN; medium (visual only, every ReStock strut and fuel line)]

What: ReStock deletes `CModuleLinkedMesh` and adds `ModuleRestockLinkedMesh` (a `CModuleLinkedMesh` subclass; lineObjName `line` / `strut`, targetAnchorName `pipe_target_anchor` / `strut_target_anchor`). `GhostVisualBuilder.TryParseCompoundPartData` looked for a MODULE named exactly `CModuleLinkedMesh`, so it returned false and `TryFixupCompoundPartVisuals` did nothing: no stretch, no aim, and the GHOST-LINKED-MESH-NO-TARGET hide never ran. ReStock's subclass also rescales the line material's textures in `UpdateStretch` (stretch = line z scale / part scaleFactor on `stretchAxis`, offset (1 - stretch) / 2, for each `stretchTextures` property of the first material of each line renderer).

Fix: the fixup finds the module by type (`prefab.FindModuleImplementing<CModuleLinkedMesh>()`) and passes its `moduleName` to a `TryParseCompoundPartData` overload, which reads the transform names from that MODULE node (the old signature keeps the stock name). For `ModuleRestockLinkedMesh` the parser also reads `stretchAxis` / `stretchTextures` (`ParseReStockStretch`, pure) and the fixup applies `ComputeReStockTextureStretch` (pure) to a clone of each line renderer's first material, one Verbose line per part.

## ~~GHOST-LOOKAT-CONSTRAINT~~: gimbal and door pistons keep the prefab roll on their ghosts [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2306` / `PP-2` `2026-11-21_2317`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `liquidEngineMainsail.v2`, `liquidEngine2.v2`, KE-1, RE-I2, `Skipper.v2`, `radialEngineMini.v2`, ReStock valiant / corgi, `ServiceBay.250.v2`: piston shading differs, the rod rolled about its own axis); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes-2`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFix2Tests` (LookAt_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only)]

What: stock `FXModuleLookAtConstraint.Track` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) runs `mover.LookAt(target, part.transform.up)` every (Late)Update for each CONSTRAINLOOKFX pair (`FindModelTransforms(rotatorsName)` movers, the first `FindModelTransform(targetName)` target). The ghost had no code for the module, so every mover kept the .mu rest rotation, which differs in roll from what LookAt produces.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.BuildLookAtConstraints` (new `GhostVisualBuilder.LookAtConstraints.cs`, end of `AddPartVisuals`): `ParseLookAtConstraintNames` (pure) reads the pairs, the builder maps the movers and the target to their ghost clones (mirroring a target chain no renderer created), uses the ghost part root's up, aims them once, and hands the list to the part's `GimbalGhostInfo` and `DeployableGhostInfo`. `GhostPlaybackLogic.ApplyLookAtConstraints` re-aims after `ApplyDeployableFraction` (events and in-flight transitions only) and after the synthesized gimbal drive and loop-reset neutral restore, the gimbal case only when the deflection differs from the one last aimed at (`ShouldReaimLookAtConstraints`, pure), so a steady ghost writes nothing per frame. One Verbose summary per part. Every part with the module is covered (engines, service bay, airbrake, claws, gear and wheels), aiming at the ghost's own pose; suspension pose itself is unchanged.

## ~~GHOST-ANIMATION-REST-STATE~~: a part whose animation only changes colours shows the lit asset on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2306` / `PP-2` `2026-11-21_2317`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `ionengine--default`: real ring black, ghost cyan; ReStock `surfacescanner--default`: real screen off, ghost green, log `AnimateGeneric 'SurfaceScanner': animation 'screenon' produced no transform deltas`); confirmed by decompile and the .mu bindings (`colorAnimation` animates `_Color.r/g/b`, ReStock `screenon` `_EmissiveColor.*`); FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes-2`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFix2Tests` (AnimationRest_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only)]

What: stock `FXModuleAnimateThrottle` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) samples its clip at the engine level, 0 with the engine off, and `ModuleAnimateGeneric.OnStart` sets the clip to the persisted `animTime`. The ghost only ever read TRANSFORM deltas from part clips (deployable and heat pose sampling), so a clip that animates only material colours or active states never reached it, and the heat fallback clears only `_EmissiveColor` / `_EmissionColor` / `_Emissive`: the ghost kept the asset's baked colour.

Fix: `ApplyAnimationRestStates` (new `GhostVisualBuilder.AnimationRestState.cs`), called once per part at build after the heat, light and colour-changer infos. `CollectAnimationRestCandidates` (pure) lists the FXModuleAnimateThrottle clip at 0 and each ModuleAnimateGeneric clip at its snapshot `animTime` (`ResolveAnimateGenericRestTime`, clamped). Each clip is sampled on a temporary prefab clone (cached per part, clip and rest time): a clip that moves any transform between its ends is skipped whole, so the existing pose sampling stays the only pose authority and nothing here writes a transform; otherwise every Color shader property that differs between the ends (`IsAnimatedColor`, read from the property block and the material) is written at its rest value into a ghost material clone (reused when another ghost info owns the material, skipped when a colour changer or light lens / flare drives that property), and every active state the rest sample changes is applied. Values are written as material colours, never as a property block, so later heat / light / colour-changer writes still show. For the FXModuleAnimateThrottle clip that is also the part's heat animation, each animated colour joins the heat info with cold / medium / hot = the clip at 0 / 0.5 / 1, so a running ion engine's ghost still lights up. One Verbose summary per part; the sample cache is a `process` static cleared with `ClearAnimateHeatCache`.

## ~~GHOST-COLORCHANGER-GAPS~~: ReStock engines glow at rest, colour changers ignore their renderer filters, and KV pod windows show the asset colour on their ghosts [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2306` / `PP-2` `2026-11-21_2317`, branch `part-parity-p4`; atlases LV-T91, LV-TX87, RE-J10, `restock-engine-schnauzer`, `restock-engine-cherenkov`, `radialLiquidEngine1-2`, `mite`, `shrimp`, `restock-srb-mallet-1`: real nozzle black, ghost orange with a white-hot core; `restock-heatshield-1875-1` top plate; `kv1pod` / `kv2pod` / `kv3pod`: real window grey-white, ghost blue); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes-2`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFix2Tests` (ColorChanger_*); NOT FLOWN; medium (visual only, every ReStock engine and the KV pods)]

What: `GhostVisualBuilder.BuildColorChangerInfos` accepted only two module shapes (an in-flight `_EmissiveColor` toggle and a `_BurnColor` char) and logged every other ModuleColorChanger as `unrecognisedPattern`, painted every renderer of the part, and cloned materials per module. Stock `ModuleColorChanger` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled): with `useRate` on (the default) `Update` writes the curves at `currentRateState` every frame, which `Start` sets to `animState ? 1 : 0`; `Start` narrows its renderers by `useMaterialsList` / `materialsNames` (substring of a material name) and `OnLoad`'s singular `includedRenderer` / `excludedRenderer` keys (exact renderer names; excluded wins, the plural spelling some ReStock configs use is never read); every write goes through the PART's one shared `part.mpb`, applied whole to the module's renderers. ReStock replaces FXModuleAnimateThrottle with two such modules (heatColor on `_EmissiveColor`, throttleColor on `_TintColor` or `_EmissiveColor`), so the real engine draws its curves at t=0 (black) while the ghost kept the asset's baked glow. `ModuleAblator.Update` drives the module its `charModuleName` names whatever the property; on the KV pods that is `shieldChar` on `_EmissiveColor`, which lands after the cabin light module on the same block (the KV atlas shows the char colour), and the per-module clone left the first module's material off the renderer.

Fix: `ClassifyColorChangerPattern` (pure): an ablator-driven module is the char (via `TryResolveAblationCharScalars`, any property), an in-flight `_EmissiveColor` toggle the cabin light, any other `useRate` module a rest-state writer at `animState ? 1 : 0` (`ResolveColorChangerAnimState` from the snapshot, else the config), and `useRate` off with no ablator is never written. `EvaluateColorChangerColor` adds `alphaOnly`. `ParseColorChangerRendererFilter` / `ColorChangerKeepsRenderer` transcribe the filters, `ResolveColorChangerFrameOrder` puts the ablator-driven modules last, and `ResolveColorChangerRendererSources` computes what each renderer shows from the shared block (a renderer takes the block as it stood at the last writer that includes it), so a cabin light overridden by the char on the same property gets no material and its light events do nothing, as on the real pod. The builder clones each drawn material once per part, hands each (material, property) to the module that owns it and writes the rest colours at build time only; `ApplyColorChangerCharState` now drives only the char (`ColorChangerGhostInfo.isAblationChar`). One Verbose summary per part counts the patterns and the renderers written and filtered.

## ~~GHOST-HEATSHIELD-BLACK~~: every heat shield ghost renders fully charred (black) from its first frame [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111` / `PP-2` `2026-11-21_2123`, branch `part-parity-p4`; atlases `heatshield0/1/1p5/2/3`, `restock-heatshield-1875-1`, `restock-pod-sphere-1/2/3`: real tan, ghost black); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (AblationChar_*, ReentryGlow_*); NOT FLOWN; high (visual only, on every craft with a heat shield)]

What: `GhostVisualBuilder.BuildColorChangerInfos` read the ablation-char ModuleColorChanger (`shieldChar`, `_BurnColor`, curves 0 -> 1, alpha 0.8) as "off = curves at t=0 (unburnt)" and wrote that colour at build time. Stock `ModuleAblator.UpdateColor` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) calls `charModule.SetScalar(charMin + (charMax - charMin) * fraction)` every physics frame, fraction = remaining ablator times the persisted `nominalAmountRecip` (capped at 1), defaults `charMax = 0.85`, `charMin = 0.1`. So t=0 is past fully charred (black `_BurnColor`), and an unburnt shield sits at t=0.85. Regression from commit 4c13c13da (GS6-GHOST-HAS-NO-COLORCHANGER-STATE), which first applied the colour.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.TryResolveAblationCharScalars` (pure) finds the ModuleAblator that drives this colour changer (`useChar` on, `charModuleName` == the colour changer's `moduleID`, default `colorChanger`; a non-empty `ablativeResource`, else stock never calls SetScalar) and returns the snapshot's current char scalar (`nominalAmountRecip` from the snapshot module, else `1 / maxAmount`; no RESOURCE node = unburnt) and the charred end `charMin`. The ghost's off colour is the curves at the current scalar, its on colour the curves at `charMin`, so `ApplyColorChangerCharState`'s off -> on lerp during reentry darkens toward stock's charred colour. A `_BurnColor` module no ablator drives keeps stock's Start colour (curves at t=0) and does not change during reentry.

Reentry follow-up (review of the same branch): the lazy reentry FX build (`CollectReentryGlowMaterials`, first atmospheric frame above about Mach 1.2, so every ascent too) re-cloned every material of a part without a HeatGhostInfo, leaving the colour-changer states (this char, and every cabin light since GS6) and the light lens / flare states writing to materials no renderer draws, so the shield never darkened. The collector now reuses a material a ghost info already holds (`GhostPlaybackLogic.CollectGhostOwnedMaterials`, decision `GhostVisualBuilder.DecideReentryGlowMaterial`, pure): no clone, not added to the reentry info's destroy list, and the emissive property its owner drives is left to the owner. Reuse was chosen over remapping each info through an old -> new map: it keeps one material per slot and needs no knowledge of each info's list shape. xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (ReentryGlow_*).

## ~~GHOST-VARIANT-BUMPMAP-CONVERTED~~: a variant's `_BumpMap` is loaded as a converted normal map and corrupts the shared texture [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111`, branch `part-parity-p4`; Size3 tanks, `rocketNoseCone.v2` / `.v3` Orange: ghost shading differs); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `VariantTextureTests` (ResolveVariantMaterialCommand_*, TryParseHtmlHexColor_Forms); NOT FLOWN; medium (visual, and it damaged the live part's texture for the session)]

What: `GhostVisualBuilder.ApplyVariantTextureRules` loaded a variant TEXTURE value `_BumpMap = <url>` through `GameDatabase.GetTexture(url, asNormalMap: true)`. For a readable texture not already flagged a normal map, stock's `TextureInfo.normalMap` getter (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) runs `BitmapToUnityNormalMap` and OVERWRITES the entry's `texture` (and flags it), so the ghost got a converted map and every later reader, the real part included, got it too. Stock `PartMaterialInfo.PartMaterialCommand` takes `GetTextureInfo(url).texture` raw. The ghost also classified a command by its KEY (a fixed key list, `*URL` suffix rewrites, comma colours) where stock classifies by the VALUE.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.ResolveVariantMaterialCommand` (pure) transcribes stock's command: a value starting with '#' that parses as an html colour (managed `TryParseHtmlHexColor`, #RGB / #RGBA / #RRGGBB / #RRGGBBAA) is a colour; else a value that parses as a float (Float | AllowThousands, the "en" rules KSP pins) is a float; else a texture url. Only mainTextureURL / color / backTextureURL / backColor are renamed (`_MainTex` / `_Color` / `_BackTex` / `_BackColor`); every other key is the shader property verbatim. The applier loads textures raw through `GetTextureInfo(url).texture` and, like stock, sets the property even when the lookup is null (one rate-limited Verbose line). The key classifier, `TextureUrlToShaderProperty` and `TryParseKspColor` (comma colours stock never reads) are deleted with their tests; those tests pinned the defect.

## ~~GHOST-VARIANT-RESKINS-FLAG~~: a variant's TEXTURE rules re-skin the part's flag and auto-truss materials on the ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `roverbody.v2--gold` / `--silver` `materialDiffers` on `.../probeRoverBody_v2/Flag`: real `KSP/Alpha/Cutoff`, ghost `KSP/Bumped Specular (Mapped)` with the gold diffuse); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests.VariantRules_SkipFlagAndAutoTrussMaterials`; NOT FLOWN; low (visual only, variant parts with a flag decal)]

What: stock `ModulePartVariants.OnAwake` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) builds the variant material list from the part's renderers but leaves out every material whose lowercased name contains "flag" or "auto truss", so a variant TEXTURE rule with no `materialName` (the RoveMate's) never touches the flag (`RoveMate_Flag`). `GhostVisualBuilder.ApplyVariantTextureRules` applied the rule to every material slot.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.IsVariantExemptMaterial` (pure, same two substrings, case-insensitive) and the applier skips those slots, logging one rate-limited Verbose count per part.

## ~~GHOST-FLAG-ALL-MESHES~~: a flag part's ghost draws every FlagDecalBackground mesh at once [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `flagpartflat`, `flagpartsize0/1/1p5/2/3/4`: e.g. `flagpartsize1--white` 12 renderers paired, `renderedDiffers=11`, all on the ghost); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (FlagMeshes_*); NOT FLOWN; medium (visual only, every flag part)]

What: stock `FlagDecalBackground.EnableCurrentFlagMesh` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) keeps active only the MESH whose index equals the persisted `flagSize`, whose `variantNames` contain the selected variant and whose orientation matches `displayingPortrait`, and SetActive(false)s the rest. The flag prefabs hold no active renderer, so `ShouldFilterInactiveVariantRenderers` took the include-all fallback and the ghost cloned every flag mesh.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.ResolveFlagDecalHiddenMeshNames` (pure) transcribes `OnLoad` + `EnableCurrentFlagMesh`: a MESH needs name, displayName and meshName; its index is that of the first earlier MESH with the same `name`, else one past the highest so far (distinct names in order of first appearance); orientation defaults to LANDSCAPE; `flagSize` defaults to 0 and `displayingPortrait` to true (false when the module has no PORTRAIT mesh, as the prefab load forces); meshes are applied in order, last state wins. A null selected variant drops the variant test (stock would hide every mesh; no flag part lacks variants). `ResolveStockHiddenTransformNames` (PartVisualDecisions.cs) gathers these names per part, logs one Verbose count, and `AddPartVisuals` leaves the renderers on or under them off the ghost through the busted-wheel name-or-ancestor filter.

## ~~GHOST-HINGE-PISTON-ARM~~: a hinge ghost draws the piston arm stock hides in flight [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `hinge.03`, `hinge.03.s`, `hinge.04` in both variants: `renderedDiffers` on `Bar1`, `Bar2`, `TopPlateKnuckle`, `BasePlateKnuckle`, drawn on the ghost only); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (HingePistons_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only, hinges)]

What: stock `ModuleRoboticServoHinge.OnStart` and both inventory-mode hooks (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) call `TogglePistons(false)`, which SetActive(false)s each child named in the private `[SerializeField] pistonTransforms` (default `Bar1,Bar2,TopPlateKnuckle,BasePlateKnuckle`; not a KSPField, so no config changes it). Nothing re-enables them in flight. The hinge prefab shows no active renderer, so the ghost took the include-all variant fallback and cloned the arm.

Fix: `GhostVisualBuilder.ResolveStockHiddenTransformNames` adds the hinge's piston names for a part whose config has a ModuleRoboticServoHinge: read from the prefab module's own field by reflection (cached; a failed read Warns and uses the stock default `DefaultHingePistonTransforms`), split like `TogglePistons` (`ParseHingePistonTransformNames`, pure), one Verbose line per part. The renderers on or under those transforms stay off the ghost. The two new reflection-cache statics carry a `process` lifetime in `scripts/arch/lifetimes.toml`.

## ~~GHOST-INFLATABLE-SPAWNS-INFLATED~~: a packed inflatable is drawn inflated on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111` / `PP-2` `2026-11-21_2123`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `InflatableHeatShield` (stock), `InflatableAirlock` and `restock-airlock-1` (ReStock): real packed, ghost inflated); confirmed by decompile and the sweep logs; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests.AnimateGeneric_StowedAndDeployedPoses_AreTheEndsTheRecorderClassifies`; NOT FLOWN; medium (visual only, inflatables)]

What: a part whose deploy clip is a standalone `ModuleAnimateGeneric` was sampled through `SampleLadderStates`, which scores the two clip ends and calls the one closer to the model's rest pose "stowed". These models are authored inflated, so the scoring picked clip time 1 as stowed (`Ladder 'InflatableHeatShield': sampled 8 animated transforms from 'InflatableHS' (stowed=time1)`, the same for ReStock's `InflatableAirlock` / `restock-airlock-1` 'Deploy'). Stock `ModuleAnimateGeneric.OnStart` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) sets `normalizedTime = animTime` (persisted, default 0), and the recorder and the snapshot baseline read animTime near 0 as retracted and near 1 as deployed, so the ghost spawned at the wrong end and the extend / retract events animated it backwards. The module has no invert flag (`revClampDirection` only reverses a deploy-limit slider).

Fix: the standalone animate-generic branch of `TryBuildDeployableInfo` samples through `SampleStandaloneAnimateGenericStates` at fixed `AnimateGenericStowedNormalizedTime = 0` / `AnimateGenericDeployedNormalizedTime = 1` (own cache key, one Verbose line). Scope check from both sweep logs: 23 stock and 26 modded scored samples read `stowed=time0` and are unchanged by this (the fixed path samples the same two poses); the only `stowed=time1` lines were the three parts above. The other families sharing `SampleLadderStates` (animation group, robot-arm scanner) keep the scoring; the stock `InflatableAirlock` (clip 'AirlockDeploy') already scored time 0.

## ~~GHOST-STRUCTURAL-NODE-FAIRINGS-ONLY~~: the stock ModuleStructuralNode rule ran only on procedural fairings [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111` / `PP-2` `2026-11-21_2123`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `memlander` `renderedDiffers` on `Adapter`, drawn on the ghost only, node `bottom2` empty); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (StructureNodes_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only; the one stock non-fairing part with the module is the Making History `Size1_5_Lander`)]

What: stock `ModuleStructuralNode` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) runs `CheckDisplay` on any part: its `rootObject` shows only when spawned manually or when an attach node in `attachNodeNames` holds a part, inverted by `reverseVisibility`. `GhostVisualBuilder.BuildFairingStructureNodes` applies that rule, but it was called only from `BuildFairingVisual`, which returns early without a snapshot ModuleProceduralFairing node, so the MEM lander's `Adapter` (attachNodeNames `bottom2`) was always drawn.

Fix: `AddPartVisuals` also calls `BuildFairingStructureNodes` when `ShouldBuildNonFairingStructureNodes` (pure) says the snapshot carries no ModuleProceduralFairing and the part config declares a ModuleStructuralNode. The rule, the recorder's display stamp and the one Verbose summary line are the fairing path's own.

## ~~GHOST-LIGHT-LENS-GLOWS-OFF~~: a light's lens keeps its lit emissive on the ghost while the light is off [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `spotlight1--default` (stock `spotLight1`): real lens dark, ghost lens lit; every other stock and ReStock light atlas reads the same on both rows); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (LightLens_*, LightFlare_*, LightOnColor_*, LightLensWrite_*, ReentryGlow_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only)]

What: stock `ModuleLight.OnStart` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) writes `_EmissiveColor` on its lens renderer (`lightMeshRendererName`, else `part.GetPartRenderers()[0]`, the first renderer under "model") and `_TintColor` on its flare renderer at once when the light is off, and its FixedUpdate fades them to the light colour / white when on and back to black when off. The ghost cloned only the Unity `Light` components, so the lens kept the prefab material's emissive. The pre-filing diagnosis (sample the `LightAnimation` clip; spotLight1/2 `.v2` and ReStock affected) did not hold: stock only `Stop()`s that clip, and the `.v2` and ReStock atlases already match (their lens glow is the texture, which a black emissive leaves as is).

Fix: `BuildLightGhostInfo` (`AttachLightLensAndFlare`) clones the first material of the ghost's lens renderer (the named one, else the first part renderer, as stock) and of its flare renderer (`flareRendererName`, default `Flare`; the TransparentFX-layer fallback is not transcribed), each only when the material has the property, and starts them off. `WriteUnityLightState` (every light event, the per-frame light driver `UpdateBlinkingLights`, which calls it for every light each frame, and the loop-cycle reset) then writes `ResolveLightLensEmissive` (black off, `ResolveLightOnColor` from the snapshot's `lightR/G/B` on) and `ResolveLightFlareTint` (black / white), settled rather than faded, like the ghost's `Light` components. The material writes run only when the on / off state differs from the last one written (`ShouldWriteLightLensAndFlare`, fields on `LightGhostInfo`); the lazy reentry FX build clears that record (`InvalidateLightLensAndFlareWrites`) and reuses the lens / flare materials instead of re-cloning them (see GHOST-HEATSHIELD-BLACK), so a light switched on after the first fast atmospheric frame still lights the drawn lens. One Verbose line per light part names what was bound.

## ~~GHOST-JETTISON-STALE-ACTIVE-NAME~~: a stale persisted `activejettisonName` leaves a variant's shroud unmanaged on the ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-2` `2026-11-21_2123`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `liquidenginere-i2--shroud_alternate` and `restock-engine-caravel-1--shroud_alternate`: `renderedDiffers` on `SkiffBoattail/Shroud2x3/Shroud2x3_Orange`, real hidden, ghost drawn; log `Jettison 'Shroud1p5x3_2' found on prefab but not in cloneMap` and the seeded `ShroudJettisoned` reading `no-family-state`); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (Jettison_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only, variant engines whose shroud list spans variants)]

What: `SelectJettisonNames` narrows a ModuleJettison's list to the snapshot's persisted `activejettisonName`. On these parts it still names `Shroud1p5x3_2`, a shroud of another variant, which the ghost never clones, so the module resolved no transform: the empty-bottom-node hide and the shroud events had nothing to act on. Stock `ModuleJettison` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) re-resolves on every variant apply (`onVariantApplied` -> `CheckAttachNode` -> `FetchActiveMeshTransform(jettisonName)`): the first listed transform that is active wins and becomes the active name, here `Shroud2x3`.

Fix: `SelectJettisonNamesForGhost` (pure, `EnginePlates.cs`) keeps the persisted name when it has a ghost clone, else uses the first listed name that does ("has a ghost clone" standing for "active under the selected variant"), else none; with no persisted name every listed name stays a candidate, as before. `ResolveJettisonTransforms` passes a cloneMap probe and logs one Verbose line when it remaps.

## ~~GHOST-LINKED-MESH-NO-TARGET~~: an unconnected strut or fuel line draws its line and target end on the ghost [FILED 2026-11-22 from the part ghost parity sweep (`PP-1` `2026-11-21_2111`, branch `part-parity-p4`; `fuelline` `renderedDiffers` on `obj_line_pivot`, `obj_targetAnchor-Pivot`, `obj_targetCap-Pivot`; `strutconnector` on `Mesh`, `obj_strut_pivot`; all drawn on the ghost only); confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-22, branch `ghost-part-parity-fixes`; xUnit `GhostPartParityFixTests` (LinkedMesh_*); NOT FLOWN; low (visual only; a strut or line left unconnected)]

What: stock `CModuleLinkedMesh.OnStart` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) SetActive(false)s the line and the target anchor (the end cap is its child) and only `OnTargetSet` shows them; `CompoundPart.OnSave` always writes PARTDATA with `tpersID` 0 for no target. `GhostVisualBuilder.TryFixupCompoundPartVisuals` never checked for a missing target, so it left the prefab line and anchor showing (and `RefreshCompoundPartVisibility` skips a target pid of 0 by design).

Fix: `IsUnconnectedLinkedMesh` (pure, `tpersID == 0`); for such a part the fixup deactivates the cloned line and target anchor and logs one Verbose line, leaving the start cap as stock does.

## ~~GHOST-LADDER-SPAWNS-DEPLOYED~~: a stowed retractable ladder is drawn extended on its ghost [FILED 2026-11-21 from the part ghost parity sweep (harness run `2026-11-21_1645` on stock-minimal, branch `part-parity-p2`, control `ctl-ghost-missing-mesh`; evidence in `<umbrella>/logs/flights/pp1-ladder-evidence-2026-11-21/`), owner confirms every ladder ghost in play; confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `ghost-ladder-stowed`; xUnit `RetractableLadderGhostPoseTests`; in-game `LadderGhost` (never run); NOT FLOWN; medium (visual only, on every craft with a ladder)]

What: the one-part `telescopicLadder` spawned in orbit shows only the retracted cover (box 0.571x0.224x0.630), and its ghost built from that vessel's own snapshot shows the bay and the ladder fully out (box 0.651x1.535x0.630; side-b coverage 11613 px real vs 29500 px ghost). Stock `RetractableLadder` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) holds its `ladderRetractAnimationName` clip at `normalizedTime = 1` in `st_retracted` and `0` in `st_extended` (extending plays it at speed -1, retracting at +1), and the model's rest pose is the extended ladder. `GhostVisualBuilder.SampleLadderStates` scores the two clip ends and calls the one closer to the rest pose "stowed", so for this module it picked time 0, the extended pose (`Ladder 'telescopicLadder': sampled 13 animated transforms from 'Retract' (stowed=time0)`). The spawn baseline (`PopulateDeployableInfos`) then stowed every ladder to that pose, which is extended. The seeder (`PartStateSeeder.SeedLadders`) only seeds an already-deployed ladder, so a stowed one never got an event to fix it.

Fix (build-time, so every existing recording heals). The `RetractableLadder` branch of `TryBuildDeployableInfo` now samples through `SampleRetractableLadderStates`, at stock's fixed rest-state times (`RetractableLadderRetractedNormalizedTime = 1` stowed, `RetractableLadderExtendedNormalizedTime = 0` deployed, no scoring; its own cache key, one Verbose line naming the endpoints). The other families that share `SampleLadderStates` (animation group, standalone animate-generic, robot-arm scanner, the Breaking Ground deployed-science parts) keep the scoring. The snapshot baseline now reads stock's persisted `RetractableLadder.StateName` (`isPersistant`; an inventory store forces `Retracted`): `Extended` -> `ladderExtended = true`, `Retracted` -> false, `Extending` / `Retracting` / unreadable -> no opinion, still suppressing the standalone animate-generic read; the resolver ranks it after explicit deploy state and gear and before the cargo bay. So a ghost built from a snapshot with the ladder out (a split tip, a continuation, a part parity capture: no seed event) spawns out too. Mirror direction: a ladder extended at the recording start still gets its `DeployableExtended` seed and shows extended (deployed pose = clip time 0, the extended pose), and recorded extend / retract events animate between the two corrected poses; the loop-cycle reset re-stows and re-applies the snapshot baseline as before.

Proof owed: the in-game cell `LadderGhost` (`RetractableLadderGhostSpawnsInTheSnapshotState`) builds `telescopicLadder` and `telescopicLadderBay` ghosts from a `Retracted` and an `Extended` snapshot through the real spawn pipeline and asserts the retracted mesh box diagonal is under 0.8 of the extended one. Not run yet; the part parity lane `PP-1-part-parity-stock` (PR #2741, unmerged) would read the control's iou.

## ~~GHOST-SHROUD-EMPTY-BOTTOM-NODE~~: the ghost draws an engine shroud the real craft hides because nothing is attached below the engine [FILED 2026-11-21 from the part ghost parity P0 capture spike (`PPS-0a` `2026-11-21_1242`, `PPS-0b` `2026-11-21_1244`, throwaway branch `part-parity-spike`), confirmed by decompile; FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `ghost-shroud-empty-bottom`; xUnit `GhostShroudEmptyBottomNodeTests`; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21 on the spike lanes (fix merged locally into `part-parity-spike`, never pushed): `PPS-0a` `2026-11-21_1327` PASS, LV-T45 iou 1.0000 xor=0 in all four views, and `PPS-0b` `2026-11-21_1329` PASS, ReStock Size1 LV-T45 iou 0.975-0.997 with equal coverage (xor 4-30 px of about 1200, edge aliasing at the spike's 10 m framing); every other case unchanged; medium (visual only, but on the commonest rocket shape: the bottom engine of a stack)]

What: a one-part LV-T45 (stock, and ReStock Size1) shows the bare engine on the real side and a solid shroud on its ghost (`pps-liquidengine2-side-a-real.png` / `-ghost.png`, side-view iou 0.40-0.54). Stock `ModuleJettison.SetupJettisonState` (KSP 1.12.5, decompiled) deactivates the jettison transform when `FindAttachNode(bottomNodeName).attachedPart == null` and `ignoreNodes` is off, without setting `isJettisoned`. `GhostVisualBuilder` (`PartInfoBuilders.cs`, the jettison resolver) forces every jettison transform active and leaves hiding to `ShroudJettisoned` events, and `PartStateSeeder.SeedJettisons` seeds only `isJettisoned = True`, so no event hides it. Any recorded vessel whose bottom engine has nothing below plays back with a shroud.

Fix (build-time, from the snapshot; chosen over a recording-start seed because it also fixes every existing recording and continuation recordings, which carry no seeds, #290). `GhostVisualBuilder.ResolveJettisonSpawnHideReason` (`PartVisualDecisions.cs`, pure) transcribes stock's flight start per ModuleJettison: `OnStart` folds `shroudHideOverride` into `isJettisoned`; then with `ignoreNodes` off an empty bottom node hides (`BottomNodeEmpty`), else a jettisoned (`Jettisoned`) or hide-override (`HideOverride`) shroud hides, else it shows. "Empty" is the snapshot's `attN = <bottomNodeName>, -1` row (`IsAttachNodeEmptyInSnapshot`); no row is no evidence and keeps the shroud. Stock reads only the node's `attachedPart`, so a surface-attached child does not count, and `ignoreNodes` parts (the Making History / ReStockPlus service modules) keep the node check off. `ResolveJettisonTransforms` collects each hiding module's ghost transforms into the new `JettisonGhostInfo.spawnHiddenTransforms` and logs one `ModuleJettison[i] '...': starts hidden|shown (reason=... bottomNode=... bottomEmpty=... ignoreNodes=...)` line per module (rate-limited); the #290 whole-part rule (any module `isJettisoned = True` hides every jettison transform) is unchanged and lands in the same list. The build hides the list (`GhostPlaybackLogic.ApplyJettisonSpawnBaseline`), and the loop-cycle reset (`ReapplySpawnTimeModuleBaselinesForLoopCycle` step 3) now re-hides it after re-attaching every panel, so cycle 2 onward starts from the spawn look too (before, it re-showed a #290 shroud as well). Mirror direction: an engine with a part on its bottom node keeps the shroud (FGV-1 config 6), and engine plates follow the same stock rule (their `ModuleJettison` reads `bottom`, no `ignoreNodes`).

Live proof. Spike runs before the fix (`2026-11-21_1242` / `_1244`): LV-T45 side views iou 0.54 / 0.44 (stock) and 0.46 / 0.40 (ReStock), top and bottom 0.99 / 0.68. After (`2026-11-21_1327` / `_1329`, automation DLL sha256 c387f9a8 from local branch `shroud-spike-proof` = spike + this fix): stock 1.0000 in all four views with xor=0; ReStock 0.9966 / 0.9934 / 0.9967 / 0.9752 with covered pixels equal or within 4, the residue being edge pixels on an engine about 35 px across (the spike frames the real part's 10 m renderer box, a spike framing artifact). Each log carries `ModuleJettison[1] '...': starts hidden (reason=BottomNodeEmpty bottomNode='bottom' bottomEmpty=True ignoreNodes=False transforms=1)`. All 24 stock and 40 modded views of the other cases read the same as before.

Known divergence, accepted: a part whose bottom-node neighbour leaves by a joint break (crash breakup), not a decouple, keeps its shroud live until the vessel next loads (stock's setup runs once, and only a decouple calls `Jettison`), while its debris ghost, built from a split-time snapshot with the node empty, starts without it.

## ~~OPTIMIZER-SPLIT-RULES-V3~~: new flights also split where a burn changes the orbit kind (circularization, orbit, transfer, capture, deorbit / descent), for new flights only (owner rulings Q-P1, the case table and "Yes, deorbit row" of 2026-11-20; decision 2026-11-21: no recorder or format change) [FILED 2026-11-20 as step 2 of `docs/handoff/recording-split-review/atmosphere-pass-analysis.md` section 8. BUILT 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp11-burn-cuts`; xUnit; NOT FLOWN; OPEN: the lane re-pins and flights below]

**Cause:** under version 2 a burn in space never starts a row, so a Mun flight's one space row held the circularization, the parking orbit, the transfer, the capture and the Mun orbit, and a deorbit burn and its coast sat in the orbit row; the rows did not read like a mission profile and an orbit row did not loop cleanly.

**Fix:** split rule version 3 (`RecordingOptimizer.SplitRuleVersionCurrent = 3`, every new commit; versions 1 and 2 keep their rules, mixed versions never merge). Design `docs/dev/done/plans/optimizer-persistence-split.md` section 14.1, code `RecordingOptimizer.BurnCuts.cs`.
- A burn (physics-frame `ExoPropulsive` run on one body, engine-off gaps up to 10 s merged, on-rails time or an SOI change ends it) is judged on the orbit kind (falling / in orbit / leaving) of the coast before and after it. A burn that arrives in orbit ends the row before it (cut at the burn end: circularization, capture, the raise out of aerobraking); one that leaves an orbit opens the next row (cut at the burn start: transfer, deorbit, direct descent); falling -> leaving (direct ascent) cuts at the burn end (injection row); leaving -> falling at an atmosphere body (capture into an aerobraking orbit) cuts at the burn end. The deorbit row is cut on every body (descent role at an airless body); ascents still end at the atmosphere exit; aerocapture keeps ruling B1; an SOI change is never a cut.
- The kind comes only from recorded data: non-predicted on-rails checkpoint elements and the terminal orbit (`ClassifyOrbitKind`), the recording's own later SOI change walked back over correction burns (a semi-major-axis step of at most 25 %; when the coast after a burn has no elements, the burn is a correction when the orbit before it already reaches the target: the moon's orbit band, or leaving for the parent), an SOI crossed from the parent, an atmosphere / ground entry or an approach run that lands, and an atmosphere / ground exit (an approach-band exit only for a burn that starts right there: orbit can be reached inside the band; also read from the chain piece before the recording, `ResolveBurnStartContext`). Point velocities are never read. A burn without evidence on both sides is not cut (counted `burnsUnjudged=`). Body facts: the live `CelestialBody`, headless the stock table.
- Guards: no kind cut that makes a row under 45 s next to another cut (`SuppressedBurnShortRow`); EVA kerbals and debris get none; a transfer between two children of one body stays one row (`SuppressedInterplanetaryTransfer`, see Phase 0): no kind cut for a burn around the parent between two of its children, a departure / injection after which the vessel goes through the parent to a sibling, or any arrival-side kind cut (insertion, injection, capture, capture into the atmosphere, direct descent) at a body reached from a sibling through the parent with no landing or splashdown since (an atmosphere dip or a low pass through a moon's approach band does not end the transfer; an arrival whose low point is under the floor reads falling, so a capture from it is an insertion and a correction lifting it an injection). The guard walks the whole chain line (`ResolveBurnLineContext`), so an earlier cut can never make a later suppressed cut appear. A row holding such a transfer is a `transfer` row.
- Roles (new): circularization, orbit, transfer, injection, deorbit, descent, set on both halves; a head is renamed only when it is unclassified (`space`). `capture` is not produced: the case table gives the capture burn to the transfer row and the aerocapture stays an aerobraking row (B1). `CanAutoMerge` refuses any version-3 join the version-3 rules would cut again (`WouldSplitRulesCutJoin` carries the second piece's terminal orbit and judges a join that starts in space with and without an atmosphere exit before it).
- Phase 0 (`OptimizerBurnCutsPhase0Tests`, every committed fixture save, the re-aim classifier and loiter cuts per resulting recording): with departure / capture cuts on interplanetary transfers, 16 of the 21 fixture trees whose transfer re-aims under version 2 (Kerbin to Dres, Duna, Eeloo, Eve, Jool, Moho, the Duna park and route fixtures) lost the re-aim or its parking-orbit loiter cut (todo REAIM-CLASSIFIER-FRAGILE-TO-MEMBER-SPLITS: parking orbit and coast + arrival land in two recordings). Those transfers are therefore kept whole; with the guard all 21 keep the same verdict and loiter cuts. Table: `logs/console/2026-11-21/rsr-wp11-phase0-table.txt` (umbrella).
- Logs: `Burn kind change: ... Before -> After (Kind) cut|<reason>` (once per state), `Split candidate (OrbitInsertionBurnEnd|CaptureBurnEnd|CaptureToAtmosphereBurnEnd|InjectionBurnEnd|DepartureBurnStart|DeorbitBurnStart|DirectDescentBurnStart)`, the split summary's `rules=v3 burns= burnsUnjudged= burnKindKept= burnShortRowKept= transferWholeKept=`, `Split rules: stamped version 3`.
- Accepted: a cut needs on-rails elements (or an atmosphere / ground boundary, an SOI change, the terminal orbit) next to the burn, so a flight flown with no time warp around a burn keeps that burn inside its row. A correction with no elements after it whose orbit before it does not yet reach the target (a second departure burn after a phasing orbit) is taken as the departure. The row label (`HoldsInterplanetaryTransfer`, read at the cut) sees the piece alone, so a row whose transfer is held only by evidence in another chain piece is labelled `orbit` rather than `transfer`; the cut decisions read the whole line, and the different label can at most keep two such rows from merging (an extra row, never a re-cut). A stock-named body in a planet pack whose live registry cannot be read falls back to stock values.

**Lanes:** flown lanes commit version 3, fixture-hosted recordings keep their stored version. Lanes whose spec pins split candidates / split counts and that fly a new flight, to re-pin from their first version-3 flight: B4 (deorbit row before the reentry), B7, B11, B12, B13, B14, B15, B16, B17, B18, B19, B20, B21, B22, B33, B36 (its new flight), GS-8, L5, QL-2, QL-4b, RF-13H, RF-9, V3C (circularization / orbit rows at Kerbin; Mun / Minmus transfer, orbit and descent rows on B11-B14; interplanetary transfers stay one row). RE-PINNED 2026-11-23 from their first version-3 flights on main 08445c153 (branch `lane-repins-1023`): B5 11 and B6 11 (circularization + orbit rows; both missing from this list), B7 10 (circularization row, departure kept whole); and the same day (branch `lane-repins2-1023`) PWR-1 / PWR-2 / PWR-3 9 (circularization row, the orbit coast its own row; `2026-11-23_1322` / `_1323` / `_1321`, `committed=7->9`; all three missing from this list); GS-8 flew and took no version-3 cut (`2026-11-23_0840`, a suborbital flight, count 10 unchanged). RE-PINNED 2026-11-24 from their first version-3 flights (branch `lane-repins3-1124`; all six missing from this list): CS-5 16 and KSS-1 13 (circularization + orbit rows), CS-6 25 (those plus the Mun orbit and return transfer rows), CS-6c 37 (circularization + orbit + the Mun orbit row; its Mun capture has no rails time after it and is not cut), B34 3 and B35 3 (Jool orbit / transfer / moon orbit); runs `2026-11-24_0033`, `_0029`, `_0113`, `2026-11-23_2349`, `2026-11-24_0304`, `_0313`. Flown on version 3 with their pins unchanged: CS-4 7 (`2026-11-24_0137`, no rails time between its burns, both unjudged; missing from this list too), CS-7 52 (`2026-11-23_2306`, window 49-55; missing too), B33 3 (`2026-11-24_0246`, window 1-3). Fixture-hosted, unchanged unless a lane commits new flights: RF-13R, V12, W1. The 29 lanes test-gaps batch 3 adds or edits (PR #2735, flown on builds without version 3) were checked against their last green flight logs (2026-11-21): no recording flown in any of them has a physics-frame `ExoPropulsive` section (zero `TrackSection started: env=ExoPropulsive`), so version 3 builds an empty burn map and cuts, roles and merges stay as flown; none pins a split token; no re-flight owed for version 3.

**Tests:** `OptimizerBurnCutsTests` (every case of the table, staging gaps, the Mun transfer ellipse, the mid-course correction, the powered flyby, starting / ending mid-burn, the terminal orbit, the short-row and interplanetary guards, EVA / debris, the version-1 / version-2 pins, the merge refusals and the floor-exit join; each shape run twice through the real pass; 21 of them red with the burn check disabled; review follow-up: a correction with no elements after it, a no-warp departure, a low-periapsis arrival with and without a correction, the guard across chain pieces and the approach-band exit, the five red before the fix; re-review: a departing piece that starts on the pad reads its line, a low Mun assist through its approach band is no touchdown), `OptimizerBurnCutsPhase0Tests` (red with the interplanetary guard disabled; plus the low-periapsis arrival shapes), `OptimizerRepeatPassSweepTests.EveryFixtureSave_SecondPassChangesNothing_VersionThree`. Ghost replay across the cuts: GHOST-REPLAY-ACROSS-V3-CUTS-LANE below.

## ~~GHOST-REPLAY-ACROSS-V3-CUTS-LANE~~: a lane that replays a ghost straight through the four version-3 cuts of a committed Mun flight [FILED 2026-11-21 as the live check of OPTIMIZER-SPLIT-RULES-V3. AUTHORED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-lane-repins`; harness and docs only; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-22 (run `2026-11-22_0509`: all four cuts hand off camera-live; the first flight's only red was a seam-endpoint forbid the spec should not carry, todo SEAM-ENDPOINT-LENS-FORBID-ON-PHASE-LOCKED-MOON-LOOPS)]

**Why:** a v3 cut turns one recording into a chain, so a replaying ghost must pass from one piece to the next at the cut UT with no gap. No lane did: injected presets and older fixtures carry no `splitRuleVersion` (version 1), and the rewind-and-replay lanes fly suborbital ascents.

**Lane:** `GS-13-mun-v3-chain-loop-replay` (nightly, never flown) on the new fixture `mun-orbit-recorded-v3`, harvested `--keep-parsek` from B11 run `2026-11-21_1612` (12 recordings: a five-piece Kerbal X chain cut at 213.08, 300.77, 1872.79 and 21593.12 recorded UT, plus seven debris). The mission loop replays cycle 0 from its predicted relaunch (13 Kerbin sidereal days after the span start, 280178.5; V6M's measured rule) and crosses each cut at 1x; each cut must print `Chain-loop unit owner=N camera-live member #A->#B at loopUT=<cut>`, which prints only when both pieces are live. The map tracer is on with `icon-jump` / `line-blink` forbidden. Rewind-to-Launch is not used: a committed fixture cannot carry the `parsek_rw_*` launch quicksave.

**Not covered:** a watch-mode follow across the cuts (the save's only vessel is parked over the Mun, so the ghost is on another body and EnterWatchMode refuses) and the ghost mesh (beyond render range throughout). Both need a watcher near the launch, i.e. a lane that flies, commits and rewinds its own v3 flight.

**First flight:** confirm `relaunchUt=` against the prediction, re-pin the UTs if it differs, then tighten the 1x windows and run `flight_efficiency.py`.

## ~~RESTOCK-GHOST-SKIRT-AND-CHUTE~~: under ReStock, ghost LV-T45 boosters showed a skirt and a second shroud, and a deployed Mk16-XL ghost parachute stayed small [FILED 2026-11-19 by V from a CKAN smoke test of Parsek 1.0.2 on his Steam install (ReStock + ReStockPlus, Waterfall + WaterfallRestock, logs in `<umbrella>/logs/smoke-ckan-2026-11-19/`); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `restock-ghost-visuals`; xUnit `VariantFxFilterTests` + `CanopyBonePoseTests`; in-game `ReStockCompat` members `LvT45GhostHidesMeshesUnderDisabledVariantSections` and `Mk16XlGhostCanopyBonesReachTheDeployedPose`; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21 by MC-2 run `2026-11-21_1130_MC-2-restock-compat` (PASS attempt 1, `total=11 passed=10 failed=0 skipped=1`; LV-T45 ghost `Frame=1 Frame_Boat=0 ShroudT45_CompactWhite=0`; Mk16-XL 22 rig bones resolved, 31 moved bones at the deployed pose, worst error 0.0000 m); low (visual only)]

Skirt. ReStock's LV-T45 default variant `Size1` (`ReStock/PatchesLegacy/Engines/restock-engines-liquid-125.cfg`) sets `Frame_Boat = true` under `LV_T45_Boattail = false` and `ShroudT45_CompactWhite = true` under `ShroudT45_Compact = false`. Stock applies each rule as `SetActive`, so a disabled section hides its enabled children; the ghost's `GhostVisualBuilder.IsAncestorChainEnabledByVariantRule` let the NEAREST rule win and drew both meshes (log: 10 MeshRenderers cloned per engine where the live part shows 8). The jettisoned `fairing` shroud itself was hidden correctly. Fix: any disabling rule in the ancestor chain disables the transform. The same walk filters engine and RCS FX transforms, which now follow the same rule.

Chute. ReStock's Mk16-XL canopy (`canopyName = B_ParachuteLargeRotator`) is a bone rig: the deploy clips move 21 bones below the canopy root, and the ghost posed only the root, so the skinned canopy stayed folded. Fix: `SampleCanopyStates` also samples every bone below the canopy that either clip moves away from its rest pose (child-index path, local pose at the end of each clip); `TryBuildParachuteInfo` maps them onto the ghost through cloneMap (`ParachuteGhostInfo.canopyBones`, one `canopy rig sampled= resolved= unresolved=` Verbose line per part); the semi-deployed, deployed, repack and loop-reset paths pose them with the root. Canopies whose clips move nothing below the root (stock) get no bone list and keep the root-only pose. EVA chutes keep their fixed overhead override.

Plumes (not a bug, owner 2026-11-21: no Waterfall on ghosts). Live parts draw Waterfall plumes; the ghost draws ReStock's own particle FX recovered from ReStock's patch files, as `docs/dev/mod-compatibility-notes.md` describes.

## ~~OPTIMIZER-PASS-NOT-A-FIXED-POINT~~: one merge phase then one split phase per pass, so some chains settled only over later loads [FILED 2026-11-21 by the whole-batch review of the split / trim / merge fixes (finding B7), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp10-batch-fixes`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; low (rows and their ids changed again after the next load)]

**Cause:** `CommittedListOptimizer.RunOptimizationPass` ran the merge phase once, then the split phase. A split can leave a new piece next to one it may join (the air half of a cut beside the chain's next air piece); that join waited for the next pass, a later load, which gave the rows new ids again.

**Fix:** `CommittedListOptimizer.RunMergeSplitToFixedPoint` repeats the merge phase, the split phase and the row role re-read (ROW-ROLE-STALE-OR-MISSING) until a round changes nothing, at most `MaxMergeSplitRounds` = 16 rounds: Warn `Optimization pass: merge/split did not settle after N round(s) (merges= splits=), the next pass continues` when hit, Verbose `settled after N round(s)` otherwise. The trim, spawn-stamp move, loop sync, name pass and flush still run once after it. Each phase keeps its own per-round summary lines.

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitRulesV2Tests.SplitThenJoinableNeighbour_SettlesInOnePass` (version 1 red before the fix: the second pass merged; version 2 is the stability mirror), and every shape cell of that class runs the pass twice.

## ~~ROW-ROLE-STALE-OR-MISSING~~: a row's role was stamped only at a cut, so a resumed reentry row kept "reentry" after climbing back to orbit and uncut rows had none [FILED 2026-11-21 by the whole-batch review of the split / trim / merge fixes (finding B6), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp10-batch-fixes`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; low (a wrong or mixed label in the Recordings table and the map). OPEN (later, foundation F4): one role registry (role -> phase, loopable, label), roles total along the vessel line, loopability on roles]

**Cause:** `Recording.SegmentRole` was written only by a version-2 split (`CommittedListOptimizer.AssignSplitRoles`) and the RULE 3 fold. A resumed reentry row that climbs back to orbit is never cut (its own pass entry and a braking exit are not cut), so it kept "reentry"; a version-2 row no cut touched had no role, so its label read the phase ("exo") beside rows labelled by role ("space").

**Fix:** `CommittedListOptimizer.ReReadRowRoles`, run by every optimization pass after the split pass (the pass runs after every commit and on every cold load): for each version-2 row that is not EVA, newer-rule or held (route source, live copy), the role is `RecordingOptimizer.ResolveHeadRoleAfterCut` of its content: an unset role becomes the start role, a pass role is re-read, any other role stays. Verbose `Row role re-read: '<id>' <old> -> <new>` (at most 20 per pass) and Info `Optimization pass: re-read N row role(s) from their content`. Loopability (`Recording.IsLoopableRecording`) stays on `SegmentPhase`. Accepted: a commit whose pass is skipped (a live Re-Fly or merge journal) gets its roles on the next pass.

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitRulesV2Tests.ResumedReentryRow_ClimbsBackToOrbit_RoleReReadAsAerobraking`, `UnsplitVersionTwoRow_GetsItsStartRole_VersionOneRowStaysUnset`, `RoleReRead_DoesNotChangeLoopability` (all red before the fix; each runs the pass twice, the second changing nothing).

## ~~CHAIN-NEXT-PIECE-EXACT-INDEX~~: seven chain readers still stopped at a hole in a chain's indices [FILED 2026-11-21 by the whole-batch review of the split / trim / merge fixes (finding B5), by code reading; CHAIN-INDEX-HOLE-RESTORES-EARLIER-PIECE fixed one reader only. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp10-batch-fixes`; xUnit; no lane; low (a hole: a piece removed from a chain)]

**Cause:** every "next piece of this chain" reader looked for exactly `ChainIndex + 1`: `RecordingTree.HasNextChainSegment`, `GhostChainWalker.TraceLineagePids`, `ParsekFlightPlaybackHost.FindNextChainRecording`, `MissionCrossTreeDock.FindChainSuccessor`, `SplitParentLinks.UniqueChainSuccessor` and the three chain cases of `GhostPlaybackLogic.WatchMode.cs` (`ResolveChainNextSlotIndex`, `FindNextWatchTarget`, `TryGetPendingWatchActivationUT`). Past a hole the chain looked ended: the watch camera, the chain tip walk, the lineage pid trace, the cross-tree journey and the parent-link repair all stopped early.

**Fix:** one pure helper in the module that owns chain queries, `RecordingChainQueries.NextChainIndexAfter(rec, list | tree dictionary)`: the lowest `ChainIndex` above rec's among the recordings of the same chain id (ordinal) and branch, `NoNextChainIndex` (int.MinValue, matches no recording) when none. Each reader takes its next index from it and keeps its own match loop (first match, the duplicate warning, the uniqueness check). No new module edge (Recording is below every caller's module). Mirror direction: `RecordingChainQueries.PreviousChainIndexBefore` (the highest non-negative lower index on the same chain and branch, `NoPreviousChainIndex` when none) serves the backward readers `RecordingChainQueries.GetChainPredecessorIndex`, `GhostMapPresence.TryFindChainPredecessor`, `RouteHarvestAnalysis.FindChainPredecessor`, the chain predecessor index of `MissionStructureListBuilder.BuildContext` and `RecordingTreeSplitter.TryFindChainPredecessor`. Kept on the exact index on purpose: the ledger's two chain-gap readers (`LedgerOrchestrator.AdjustStartUtForChainGap`, `ResolveStandaloneCommitWindowStartUt`), because widening a commit window back across a missing piece sweeps that piece's untagged science into the next one (pinned by `LedgerOrchestratorTests.ResolveStandaloneCommitWindowStartUt_PredecessorIndexMismatch_LeavesSubsetAtOwnStart`); and the Re-Fly splitter's TIP probes, which look for the piece the split itself made at exactly the next index; and `RecordingOptimizer.CanAutoMerge`, which joins consecutive pieces only.

**Tests:** `ChainIndexHoleReaderTests` (both helpers, then one cell per reader in each direction over a chain indexed 0 and 2; every reader cell red before the fix). Two existing cells pinned the exact backward index with no stated hazard and now expect the step over the hole: `Bug614GhostMapAncestorChainTests.TryFindChainPredecessor_StepsOverAHoleInTheIndices`, `ChainTests.GetChainPredecessorIndex_GapInChainIndex_StepsOverTheHole`.

## ~~FOLDED-PIECE-ROW-SETTINGS-SPREAD~~: a folded split piece's hide, ghost-off or loop setting spread over the whole re-flown flight [FILED 2026-11-21 by the whole-batch review of the split / trim / merge fixes (finding B4), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp10-batch-fixes`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; low-medium (a loop or hide set on one row of a flight flown again covered the whole flight, then every row a later split made)]

**Cause:** the RULE 3 fold of a covered split piece (`TreeCommitService.CarryTipOwnedStateOnFold` -> `CarryUnsetPlayerSettings`, `TreeCommitService.LiveFlownCopy.cs`) carried every player setting the survivor left at its default from the piece onto the survivor. Those per-row settings covered only the piece's span; on the survivor they covered the whole flight, and `RecordingOptimizer.CopyPlayerRowSettings` then copied them onto every row the next splits cut from it.

**Fix:** a loop on the piece, when the survivor has no loop of its own, is carried as a loop RANGE over exactly the span it covered (owner RULE 1, "always keep them"; `CarryLoopAsRange`): the piece's own `LoopStartUT` / `LoopEndUT`, each falling back to the piece's `StartUT` / `EndUT`, in absolute UTs, with its interval, unit and anchor. Info `CommitTree: fold of '<piece>' into '<survivor>' carried its loop as a range [a,b] - the span it covered`. The range holds the survivor whole in the split pass (`HasPlayerLoopRange`, intended), so no re-cut row copies the loop. `Hidden` and `PlaybackEnabled` off have no range field, so they are not carried; the survivor keeps its own, logged once per fold: Info `CommitTree: fold of '<piece>' into '<survivor>' kept the survivor's own row settings, dropped=[Hidden,PlaybackEnabled] - they covered only the folded piece`. Groups are still carried where the survivor has none. Accepted: a hide or ghost-off set on that piece is lost with the piece.

**Tests:** `LiveFlownCommittedTreeTests.CarryTipOwnedStateOnFold_LoopOnTheFoldedPieceOnly_BecomesARangeOverThePiece` (red before the fix: the range over the piece's span, the piece's own range winning; mirror: a loop the survivor has itself stays and nothing is dropped). Two existing expectations changed because they pinned the spread: `CommitPendingTree_FlownAgainAfterAReCut_...` (the tail's loop lands on the head as a range over the tail's span [100, 200]) and `CarryTipOwnedStateOnFold_TipStateWins_...` (the tip's hide no longer lands on the head).

## ~~SPLIT-RULES-NO-FORWARD-GATE~~: an older build would cut, join and trim rows a newer build split under rules it does not know [FILED 2026-11-21 by the whole-batch review of the split / trim / merge fixes (finding B3), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp10-batch-fixes`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; latent until a split rule version 3 ships (must land in a build before it)]

**Cause:** `RecordingOptimizer.UsesCurrentSplitRules` reads `SplitRuleVersion >= SplitRuleVersionCurrent`, so a row stamped 3 by a newer build would be judged by the version-2 rules here: cut again, glued back to its neighbours and tail-trimmed, against the save-format policy (data newer than the build is held, never coerced).

**Fix:** `RecordingOptimizer.IsSplitRuleVersionNewerThanBuild` (version above the build's current one). Such a recording is held verbatim: `FindSplitCandidatesForOptimizer` skips it before the checkpoint normalization (Verbose `held N recording(s) whole: split rules newer than this build`), `SplitRulesKeepApart` makes `CanAutoMerge` refuse it (Verbose `... newer than this build (v2), held verbatim`), `DescribeTrimHold` holds it from the boring-tail trim (`newer-split-rules`, counted in the trim skip summary) and `SplitPieceFoldRefusal` keeps it beside a re-flown live recording. The codec already writes the number back unchanged.

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitRulesV2Tests.NewerSplitRuleVersion_IsNeverSplit_AndRoundTrips`, `NewerSplitRuleVersion_IsNeverMergedOrFolded` (both red before the fix; the second's mirror merges the same pair at version 2).

## ~~UNION-COMMIT-STALE-INCOMING-TREE~~: after a committed vessel was flown again, the ledger and the leaf spawn read the dropped live copy [FILED 2026-11-21 by the whole-batch review of the split / trim / merge fixes (finding B2), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp10-batch-fixes`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; medium (science and milestones past the cut of a re-flown row never reach the ledger; a leaf whose ending moved to the new tail is not spawned)]

**Cause:** the RULE 3 union (`TreeCommitService.TryUnionFlownAgainCopy`, and the active Re-Fly union) folds the incoming copy INTO the existing committed tree object and reassigns only `CommitTree`'s local `tree`. The callers kept the incoming copy: `MergeDialog.MergeCommit`, `ParsekFlightMergeFlow.CommitTreeFlight` and the two outside-flight auto-commits in `ParsekScenario.AutoCommit.cs` passed it to `LedgerOrchestrator.NotifyLedgerTreeCommitted` (and the in-flight commit to `SpawnTreeLeaves`) after the optimizer pass, whose split tails exist only in the committed tree.

**Fix:** `TreeCommitService.ResolveCommittedTreeAfterCommit(tree, context)` returns the committed tree with the same id (else the caller's tree), with one Info `ResolveCommittedTreeAfterCommit (<context>): tree id='...' was unioned into the committed tree; using it` when they differ. The merge dialog rebinds `tree` right after the commit (mark applied, parent-chain tip adoption, ledger notify, committed listeners, route prompt all read it); the in-flight commit reads it for the ledger notify, the leaf spawn and the supply-route prompt (`RouteRunPrompt.NotifyTreeCommitted`, which classified the stale copy); the safety-net and ghost-only auto-commits for the ledger notify.

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitCommitSingleWalkTests.FlownAgainUnionMergeCommit_FilesTheTailMilestone` (a milestone past the cut files a row tagged to the tail id), `MergeFlowDecisionTests.CommitTreeFlight_FlownAgainUnion_SpawnsLeavesFromTheCommittedTree`, `ResolveCommittedTreeAfterCommit_FirstCommit_ReturnsTheSameTree`; the first two red with the callers on the incoming tree. The source order gate `InFlightCommitOptimizationTests.CommitTreeFlight_RunsOptimizationBetweenCommitAndLeafSpawn` pins the resolve before the notify, the spawn and the route prompt (red with the prompt on the live copy).

## ~~RESCUE-REGEN-COUNTS-PROTOVESSELS~~: the rebuilt rescue's stranded-vessel regeneration reported `added=0`, so the repair read as failed and the same-scene double-spawn guard could not see the new vessel [FILED 2026-11-20 from the first flights of RSQ-1 / RSQ-2 (branch `test-gaps-batch3`); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-batch1`; xUnit `ContractAcceptWorldIndexTests` (red first on the stubbed indexer: 6 of 8); LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21: RSQ-1 `2026-11-21_1140` and RSQ-2 `2026-11-21_1142` read `added=1 [... live]`, `repaired=1` and `regenerated=1` (TEST-GAPS-BATCH3-FLIGHTS-2026-11-21); medium (the regeneration's own result was misread, and a second rebuild or drain in the same scene would have regenerated the vessel again)]

Evidence: RSQ-1 `2026-11-20_2308_RSQ-1-rescue-rebuilt-at-space-center` and RSQ-2 `2026-11-20_2311_RSQ-2-rescue-rebuilt-in-flight-deferred` (runner runs `b3-flights-1` / `b3-flights-2` / `b3-flights-3` on V's PC, Debug automation DLL sha256 prefix 5b46a1c1 from `test-gaps-batch3` e59ceeebc; logs in `automation/results-archive/<runId>/KSP.log.gz`). RSQ-1 at the Space Center crossing: `PatchContracts: accept-side world effect not run on rebuild: contractId='e8ba5ea6-...' ... worldMissing=True repair=RegenerateStrandedAsset skip=none (...; vessels=3 scene=SPACECENTER)`, then `PatchContracts: regenerated stranded asset for rebuilt contract 'e8ba5ea6-...' through RecoverAsset.GenerateOrbitalRecovery: added=0 [] (orbit kerbal='Rayvan Kerman'; partID 4161328136 -> 268551258)` and `1 rebuilt contract(s) name world objects ...; repaired=0`. RSQ-2 at the Space Center drain: the same `added=0 []` line, `Rescue accept deferral removed: ... (drain evaluated: outcome=Regenerate regenerated=False); pending=0` and `drained ... evaluated=1 regenerated=0`. The partID swap proves stock's generator ran.

Correction to the filing: RSQ-1's save taken right after the crossing (`rsq1-01-after-crossing.sfs` in the run's `_save` snapshot) DOES hold the vessel: its FLIGHTSTATE has `name = Rayvan's Shipwreck` (line 13238) with Rayvan aboard. A FLIGHTSTATE `VESSEL` names itself with `name =`; the filing grepped `vesselName =`, which only the contract and recording nodes use. The vessel was in the world from the regeneration on.

Cause (decompiled KSP 1.12.5, `logs/decompile/2026-10-26_full/`). `RecoverAsset.GenerateOrbitalRecovery` / `GenerateLandRecovery` end in `HighLogic.CurrentGame.AddVessel(node)`. `Game.AddVessel` is `new ProtoVessel(node, this)`, `protoVessel.Load(flightState)`, `GameEvents.onNewVesselCreated.Fire(protoVessel.vesselRef)`; `ProtoVessel.Load(st, null)` builds the `Vessel`, runs `StartFromBackup(this, st)` (which only sets `protoVessel` and the orbit driver) and ends with `FlightGlobals.AddVessel(vesselRef)` and `onVesselCreate`. Nothing appends to `flightState.protoVessels` (the only appenders are `ContractSystem`'s pre-built-ship spawn and `MissionSystem`, both outside the FLIGHT scene, and `FlightState`'s own constructors). That list is rebuilt from `FlightGlobals.Vessels` by `new FlightState()` inside `Game.Updated()` whenever `HighLogic.LoadedSceneHasPlanetarium` (FLIGHT, TRACKSTATION, SPACECENTER), i.e. at every save there ("Flight State Captured", the line right after `cmd=SaveGame start` in both logs). So the vessel is live at once and saved with the game at the next save, as after stock's own accept; Parsek need not add it to `flightState.protoVessels`, and does not (stock's accept at Mission Control does not either). But `KspStatePatcher.RegenerateRebuiltStrandedAsset` counted `flightState.protoVessels` before and after the call (always 0), and `BuildContractAcceptWorldIndex`, the double-spawn guard's world, read only that list, so until the next save a second rebuild or drain in the same scene would have read the target missing and regenerated it again.

Fix. `GameActions/ContractAcceptWorldIndex.cs` (pure `ContractAcceptWorldIndexer`, `WorldVesselFact`): `Build` indexes the union of the saved and the live vessels (a vessel in both counted once by its id; flight id 0, the part Parsek's ghost map vessels carry, ignored), `SelectAdded` diffs both lists by object before and after the generator (one entry per vessel, live first), `Describe` names each added vessel (`'name' pid=N crew=(a; b) parts=K live`, no square bracket inside the logged list). `KspStatePatcher.ContractAcceptEffects.cs` reads `FlightGlobals.Vessels` in the `[NoInlining]` `ReadLiveWorldVesselFactsCore` (a loaded vessel by its live parts, an unloaded one by its ProtoVessel, dead vessels skipped as stock's save does; a failed read logs a Warn and indexes flightState alone), builds both the index and the witness from it, logs `PatchContracts: accept-side world index: vessels=N saved=N live=N liveOnly=N deadSkipped=N parts=N crewAboard=N` (Verbose) and adds `; flightStateGrew=N, stock's next save captures it` inside the regeneration line's parentheses. The `added=N [...]`, `vessels=N scene=S)` and `regenerated=` tokens RSQ-1 / RSQ-2 pin are unchanged in form; on this fix they must read `added=1 ['Rayvan's Shipwreck' pid=... crew=(Rayvan Kerman) parts=1 live]`, `repaired=1`, `regenerated=True` and `regenerated=1`. The drain still takes an evaluated id off the list whatever it decided (by design); the false `regenerated=False` was the witness, now fixed. Tests: `ContractAcceptWorldIndexTests` (9 cases: the live-only vessel indexed, one vessel in both lists counted once, a ghost map vessel adds nothing, the witness counts the live-only vessel RSQ-1 / RSQ-2 missed, a second rebuild in the same scene plans `TargetPresent` / no repair where the flightState-only index planned a second regeneration).


## ~~REVERT-LEAVES-REWIND-POINT-FILE~~: a stock revert dropped the reverted flight's rewind point but left its quicksave file [FILED 2026-11-21 from STR-3's report-only reading (owner ruling V 2026-11-21: delete it at once), branch `test-gaps-batch3`; FIXED 2026-11-21, xUnit `InSessionStagedListsCarryTests`; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21: STR-3 `2026-11-21_1134` (`Rewind point file deleted on revert`), its rewind block armed; low (disk only: the file was unlisted and never offered)]

Evidence: STR-3 `2026-11-20_2256_STR-3-revert-takes-back-strategy-share` (PASS, rewind block report-only) read
`rewindPointFiles=1 unlistedRewindPointFiles=1` in the produced save. The revert's in-session step B dropped
the staging's point (`In-session RP owner partition decisions: <rp>:FollowSave:dropped-memory-only`) and every
later save wrote `rewindPoints=0`, but the file `Parsek/RewindPoints/<rp>.sfs` stayed: `ParsekFileCollector`,
the only code that deletes it, skipped the in-session load as `rate-limited` and the batch's cold loads as
`zero-known-ids`.

Fix: step B now reports the ids of the memory-only points it drops (`MergeRewindPointsByOwner`'s new
`droppedMemoryOnlyIds`); the revert-cleanup phase of the same OnLoad calls
`ParsekScenario.DeleteRevertedFlightRewindPointFiles(refinedLoadKind)`, whose pure selector

id the installed list holds, and `ParsekFileCollector.DeleteRewindPointFilesDroppedByRevert` deletes each file
under the collector's own rule: a file stays while any save in the folder or memory names the point (a mid-flight
F5 after the staging, so the OQ-3 "F9 back into a mid-flight quicksave" case keeps working; Info
`Rewind point file kept on revert: rp=... reason=named-by-save-or-memory`), and an unreadable referrer keeps every
file. Deleted: Info `[FileCollector] Rewind point file deleted on revert: rp=<rp> path=Parsek/RewindPoints/<rp>.sfs`.
Every other in-session load (F9 is cold; Discard Re-fly, InSessionOther) keeps OQ-3's "files untouched"; the
deletion stays inside `ParsekFileCollector` (the `parsek-file-deletes` gate's owner). Red first: the delete and
the kept-by-quicksave cells failed against a no-op stub. `LoadReconcilePolicy`'s RewindPoints decision text,
design-load-restores-the-save.md 4.5 and the OnLoad step / token goldens follow.

Owed: re-fly STR-3 (stock-minimal); it now requires the deletion line after the revert mark and its report-only
