## ~~SURVIVOR-DESTROYED-AT-SCENE-EXIT~~: a crash's living probe survivor was finalized Destroyed at the scene exit [FILED 2026-11-20 from SURV-2's first flight (report-only structure block), branch `test-gaps-batch3`; FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-survivor`, xUnit `IdentityLossClassifierTests`; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21: SURV-2 `2026-11-21_1141` (`partSource=Proto ... lost=False`, `terminal=Orbiting hasSnapshot=True`), both blocks armed; high (the surviving vessel's recording ended Destroyed with its spawn snapshot dropped, so its end-of-flight spawn was lost)]

Evidence (flight): SURV-2 `2026-11-20_2313_SURV-2-recorded-half-destroyed-survivor-recorded` (PASS, its structure block report-only; runner runs `b3-flights-1` / `b3-flights-2` / `b3-flights-3` on V's PC, Debug automation DLL sha256 prefix 5b46a1c1 from `test-gaps-batch3` e59ceeebc). The crash went as designed: `ProcessBreakupEvent: controlled child created: pid=1433524667, name='Kerbal X Probe', recId=4522b6db..., alive=True, bgRecorder=True`, `not all leaves terminal - other vessels still alive`, and the background finalizer cache kept reading `terminal=Orbiting` through `reason=background_commit_on_rails`. Then the scene-exit finalize: `FinalizeTreeRecordings: recorded controllable identity lost for '4522b6db736b4880b1b39f268abe4cbc' pid=1433524667 recordedControllers=1 sceneExit=True - classifying as Destroyed at UT=432.13`, `MarkDestroyedAtTerminal: ... source=FinalizeTreeRecordings.identityLost`, and the merge reads `leaf='4522b6db...' vessel='Kerbal X Probe' terminal=Destroyed hasSnapshot=False canPersist=False`. The probe was alive and orbiting (the live vessel with its probe core), so the identity check misread it.

Log read in short: `Kerbal X Probe Unloaded` (stock line, UT ~423) came before the scene exit, so the
identity check ran on an unloaded vessel.

Cause: a regression of the BREAKUP-REMNANT-ENDING-DEPENDS-ON-DISTANCE fix (a3bb6e94e, merged), which
runs `IdentityLossClassifier.IsRecordedIdentityLost` on every live leaf at finalization. The live
adapter read `v.parts` and `ParsekFlight.IsTrackableVessel(v)`, which see only LOADED parts. An
unloaded vessel (on rails beyond the physics range) has an empty live part list, so trackability
read false and the predicate's "no parts survive at all" branch sealed the living probe Destroyed.
The background go-on-rails seam, the adapter's first caller, always runs while the vessel is still
loaded, so it never hit this; #2724 and the open rsr branches do not touch the adapter.

Fix: the adapter picks its part source (`IdentityLossClassifier.SelectPartSource`): a vessel in
`Vessel.State.DEAD` (killed on rails, e.g. in atmosphere; `FindVesselByPid` does not filter it)
reads as no survivor; a LOADED vessel reads only its live parts, as before (zero live parts means its
parts all just died with the Destroy pending, and its protoVessel is a stale snapshot still listing
the controller, so it is never consulted); an unloaded one reads its proto part snapshots
(`CollectProtoPartIdentity`: part pids, and a command module for trackability, resolved per part
through its prefab's `FindModuleImplementing<ModuleCommand>` so a mod's subclass counts as on the
loaded path, with the exact `ModuleCommand` name match as the fallback when no prefab resolves:
pure `ProtoPartCarriesCommand`, live core `ResolvePrefabImplementsCommand`); an unloaded vessel with
no proto part is not sealed (no evidence of loss). The pure composite
`ShouldClassifyRecordedIdentityLostFromSources` feeds the unchanged predicate; one `[Recording]`
Verbose line (`dead= loaded= partSource= liveParts= protoParts=`) names the source whenever it is not
a non-empty live part list. Mirrors: an unloaded wreck that kept no controller still reads Destroyed
(the distance-independent ending holds), debris and controller-less recordings still opt out (also
when dead), a survivor destroyed later never reaches this check (no live vessel, the destroyed flag
wins), and a loaded vessel is read exactly as before. The red cell
`UnloadedSurvivor_ProtoPartsCarryTheRecordedController_IsNotLost` fails with the source pinned to the
live parts (mutation run 2026-11-21: 8 of the new cells red, 45 green). Review follow-up (same day):
the first cut read the proto of a loaded vessel with zero live parts, which turned a just-destroyed
vessel into a survivor (red cell `LoadedVesselWithNoLiveParts_StaleProtoListsController_IsLost`), and
read neither the DEAD state nor a modded command subclass on the proto side (mutation: 7 cells red).

Owed: re-fly SURV-2; its report-only structure block should read the probe `Orbiting` with a
snapshot and the merge line `terminal=Orbiting hasSnapshot=True` (or the proto source line
`partSource=Proto ... lost=False`). Arming the block stays an owner decision.

## ~~BG-SOI-SEAM-WORLD-GAP~~: a background probe's on-rails Mun -> Kerbin seam resolves 9.1 km apart on its two sides [FILED 2026-11-20 from SOI-3's first flight, branch `test-gaps-batch3`; SETTLED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-bgsoi-gap`: NOT a product defect, the in-game cell measured wrong; cell fixed, xUnit pins the recorded seam; SOI-3 RE-FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-21 `2026-11-21_1138` (`gap=0.0m`)]

Evidence: SOI-3 `2026-11-20_2310_SOI-3-bg-probe-mun-exit-on-rails` (runner runs `b3-flights-1` / `b3-flights-2` / `b3-flights-3` on V's PC, Debug automation DLL sha256 prefix 5b46a1c1 from `test-gaps-batch3` e59ceeebc). `BgSoiCrossingPlaybackInGameTests.BackgroundProbeSeamWorldPositionsAreContinuous` measured `bg probe seam Mun->Kerbin ut=1317.090 gap=9127.7m (tolerance 5000m)`, evaluating the Mun side at seam - 0.5 s and the Kerbin side at seam + 0.5 s through `TrajectoryMath.EvaluateOrbitSegmentTruePositionAtUT`.

Cause: the cell compared two DIFFERENT instants in the world frame, and `getTruePositionAtUT` anchors on the Sun, so the 1 s spread is the probe's heliocentric travel. Evaluated headless from the produced save's segments (recording `9a3188810727437db35873666be0c061`, elements verbatim) with stock's Mun and Kerbin ephemerides through `TwoBodyOrbit` (stored frame, no Zup read): the probe's heliocentric speed at the seam is 9127.7 m/s (Kerbin's 9284.5 m/s orbital speed combined with the probe's 609.8 m/s Kerbin-relative velocity), and the cell-style spread reproduces 9127.8 m. The recorder is right: the Kerbin segment's epoch (UT 1316.656) is the true crossing (the Mun-side position sits on the Mun's SOI radius, 2,429,559 m, there), the SOI event fired 0.434 s later, and at the seam UT the two sides agree to 0.57 m in position and 0.008 m/s in velocity. The original tolerance comment ("about 0.7 km, the probe's own travel") was the Kerbin-relative travel (610 m) and missed the Sun-anchored frame.

Fix (test only): the cell evaluates both sides at the seam UT itself (the instant playback hands the ghost from one segment to the other; a one-segment list is closed at both ends) in one synchronous pass, and logs `kerbinEpoch=`, `seamMinusKerbinEpoch=` and `munSideFromMun=`. Tolerance 5 km -> 1 km, derived in the cell's comment: the same-UT residual is the patched-conic divergence 0.5 * da * L^2 (da below 0.025 m/s^2 at the Mun SOI edge, L the event's lateness behind the crossing; millimetres at SOI-3's 0.43 s, 1 km allows about 280 s of warp lag), while a wrong-body side (~12,000 km), a frame rotation above ~0.005 deg and an evaluation more than ~0.11 s off the seam all stay above it. xUnit `BgSoiSeamWorldGapTests` (3 cases) pins the three readings above from the recorded elements.

Mirror check: S1.8's `SoiCrossingPlaybackInGameTests.SoiSeamWorldPositionsAreContinuous` uses the same 0.5 s either side and its pinned readings (10,146.3 m at Kerbin -> Sun, 7,284.0 m at Sun -> Duna) are the same artifact (about 1 s of heliocentric travel just after Kerbin escape and at Duna arrival), not the "capture jitter" its comment names; its 25 km tolerance therefore guards only the 50-90 thousand km class. Taken: S18-SEAM-CELL-ONE-SECOND-SPREAD (branch `test-gaps-s18-seam`) moved that cell to the same seam-UT evaluation with a 1 km tolerance and owes S1.8's re-flight.

Owed: SOI-3's re-flight on a DLL from this branch; expected `bg probe seam Mun->Kerbin ut=1317.090 gap=<1 m (tolerance 1000m, both sides at the seam UT) kerbinEpoch=1316.656 seamMinusKerbinEpoch=0.434s munSideFromMun=2429672m` (the seam UT moves if the warp lands the event on another frame).

## ~~CONTRACT-REBUILD-SKIPS-ACCEPT-WORLD-EFFECTS~~: after a rewind to before a rescue accept, the rebuilt rescue contract has no stranded vessel and can only fail [FILED 2026-11-18 from the test-gap analysis, by decompile and code reading; DETECTION 2026-11-18, branch `tkh1m4-rescuecontract`: a pure classifier and guard plus one Info line per rebuilt contract, no world change; FIXED 2026-11-20 (rescue and tourism), branch `test-gaps-rescuecontract`: the rebuild regenerates the stranded vessel through RecoverAsset's own stock generator and converts the tourists, xUnit only; FOLLOW-UP 2026-11-20, branch `test-gaps-batch1` (owner rulings): a rescue rebuilt in Flight or an editor is regenerated at the next Space Center or Tracking Station visit, tourism skips a committed resolution, a half-present compound rescue is never regenerated, xUnit only; FIX 2026-11-21, same branch: the regeneration's witness and the double-spawn world index read the live vessels too (RESCUE-REGEN-COUNTS-PROTOVESSELS), xUnit only; the PC lanes RSQ-1 / RSQ-2 / RSQ-3 / RSQ-4 LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21 (TEST-GAPS-BATCH3-FLIGHTS-2026-11-21); FIXED 2026-11-21 (prebuilt ship, experimental part; item 4), branch `test-gaps-contract-templates`, measured from the decompile, xUnit only; every stock template surveyed, nothing else left; lanes CT-2 and CT-3 LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-22 (`2026-11-22_1132` / `_1135`, PASS attempt 1 each; CT-3 on the derived fixture `cs-career-mun4-vessel-repair` is the prebuilt-ship spawn's live proof), branch `test-gaps-lane-pins`; CLOSED; high (an Active contract that cannot be completed charges its failure penalty at the deadline)]

**What happens.** The player accepts a rescue contract (`Contracts.Templates.RecoverAsset`) at UT
T, rewinds to before T, and the clock reaches T again. `KspStatePatcher.PatchContractsCore`
rebuilds the committed accept from its snapshot (`Activator.CreateInstance` + `Contract.Load`),
which sets the state field directly and never runs `SetState(Active)`. Stock's accept order is
`AwardAdvance`, `OnAccepted`, `onAccepted.Fire` (decompiled `Contract.SetState`), and
`RecoverAsset.OnAccepted` is what adds the stranded vessel to the game (`GenerateOrbitalRecovery`
/ `GenerateLandRecovery` -> `Game.AddVessel`; `GenerateKerbalInPart` / `GenerateLonePart` also set
`partID`). The snapshot is taken at `onAccepted`, so it already holds what `OnAccepted` wrote into
the contract (the kerbal in `AcquireCrew` / `RecoverKerbal`, the part id), but the vessel was
spawned at T, after the rewind save, so the rewind world has none. The kerbal himself is created
Unowned / Assigned at OFFER time (`RecoverAsset.Generate`), so he is in the rewind save's roster
when the offer predates it (cs-career-mun4: Rayvan Kerman, Unowned) and absent when it does not.
The Offered copy the rebuild replaces is removed with `Unregister` only (no `Cleanup`), so the
kerbal is not expunged. Result: an Active rescue naming a kerbal no vessel holds.

**Other templates** (every stock `OnAccepted` override, decompiled): `TourismContract` turns each
tourist (created Unowned / Assigned at offer) into a Tourist and Available, so after the rebuild
the tourists stay Unowned and cannot be seated; `OrbitalConstructionContract`,
`RoverConstructionContract` and `VesselRepairContract` call `ContractSystem.SpawnPreBuiltShip`
(the snapshot carries the spawned vessel's id, never `waitingForVslSpawn`: see item 4); `PartTest` makes the part experimental
(`ResearchAndDevelopment.AddExperimentalPart`). `BaseContract`, `SatelliteContract`,
`StationContract` and `GrandTour` only stamp a launch id into a parameter the snapshot carries.
Nothing else in Parsek re-creates any of these (grep `RecoverAsset`, `OnAccepted`,
`GenerateOrbitalRecovery`, `recoveryKerbal`, `SpawnPreBuiltShip`, `AddExperimentalPart`: no hit
outside this entry's code). A rewind or Re-Fly to a point AFTER T is unaffected: its save holds
the vessel and the Active contract.

**Shipped (detection only).** `GameActions/ContractAcceptWorldEffects.cs` (pure): `Classify` names
the template's accept-side effect; `ReadRecoverAssetTarget` reads the snapshot's own
`recoveryType` / `recoveryLocation` / `kerbalName` / `partID`; `DecideStrandedAsset` is the guard a
regeneration must pass, first match wins: `NotReadable`, `TargetPresent` (the kerbal aboard some
vessel, the part in some vessel; also what keeps a regeneration from running twice, since the
vessel it adds is live at once and saved with the game at the next save), `CommittedResolution` (the committed timeline completes,
fails or cancels the contract at any UT), `KerbalReserved` (`KerbalsModule.ShouldBlockDismissal`: managed or
named by a committed flight; or either side of the crew swap map), `KerbalNotInRoster`, `KerbalNotUnowned`
(the kerbal is no longer the offer's Unowned stranded kerbal), `Regenerate`. `KspStatePatcher.ContractAcceptEffects.cs` builds the world facts
from `flightState.protoVessels` and `FlightGlobals.Vessels` (`ContractAcceptWorldIndexer`, see
RESCUE-REGEN-COUNTS-PROTOVESSELS) once per patch, only when a rebuilt contract has an effect, and logs
`PatchContracts: accept-side world effect not run on rebuild: contractId=... effect=StrandedAsset
outcome=Regenerate worldMissing=True (...)`, plus one summary line naming this id. Tests:
`ContractAcceptWorldEffectsTests` (28 cases; 11 red with `Classify` stubbed to the rebuild's current
"no effect" answer, e.g. `Assert.Equal() Failure` Expected `StrandedAsset`, Actual `None`).

**Fix (built 2026-11-20, rescue and tourism).** Owner rules: never reduce earned value, no paradox,
earliest outcome wins. Nothing here touches funds, science, reputation or a ledger row. The pure
`ContractAcceptWorldEffects.Plan` now also names the repair (`ContractAcceptRepair`) and, when a
missing effect is left alone, a grep-stable `skip=` reason; `KspStatePatcher.ContractAcceptEffects.cs`
applies it right after the rebuilt contract's `Register`, only for a contract the rebuild just
re-Activated (a contract the loaded save already holds Active survives the patch and never reaches
this; its vessel is in that save).
1. RecoverAsset, on `Regenerate` only and only in SPACECENTER or TRACKSTATION
   (`IsRegenerationScene`; stock's own accept runs at Mission Control, every vessel packed; FLIGHT
   and the editors defer it, item 1a): reflect and call the private
   `GenerateLandRecovery` (surface) or `GenerateOrbitalRecovery` on the rebuilt contract (decompile
   in `logs/decompile/rescuecontract-2026-11-20/`), under `SuppressionGuard.Crew()`. Not
   `OnAccepted`: the snapshot already carries its parameter half. The private `partID` is read
   before and after; when the generator re-drew it for a part recovery (`NeedsPartListRepair`),
   `AcquirePart` / `RecoverPart` swap the old id for the new one (the live contract only: the
   accept snapshot keeps the old id). Double-spawn guards: the world check reads
   `flightState.protoVessels` and `FlightGlobals.Vessels` target by target (a vessel `Game.AddVessel`
   made this scene is only in the live list until the next save). `TargetPresent` when every named target is in the
   world (the kerbal aboard any vessel, the part in any vessel); `PartiallyPresent` (review finding
   2026-11-20) when a compound rescue has one target in the world and not the other, because stock's
   generators make both together: with the kerbal aboard, `GenerateKerbalInPart` -> `SeatKerbal`
   would seat the same `ProtoCrewMember` in a second vessel, and with the part present a second copy
   of its vessel would be added. That is also the case a later rebuild of a regenerated compound
   rescue meets (the kerbal aboard, the snapshot's stale part id in no vessel), so it is skipped,
   never regenerated; the rebuilt contract then names that stale part id (residual gap, see
   below). The index is rebuilt after a spawn, and a regenerated contract is Active in the live
   list so later patches skip it. The orbit is stock's (`ChooseOrbit`; low orbits are random), so the vessel
   sits elsewhere than in the first timeline (no committed flight depends on it: `KerbalReserved` /
   `CommittedResolution` skip that case). Lines: `PatchContracts: regenerated stranded asset for
   rebuilt contract '<id>' through RecoverAsset.<generator>: added=N [...]` (N counted on both
   vessel lists, each added vessel with its pid, crew and part count) and, on a part swap,
   `rebuilt rescue '<id>' part lists now name partID=...`.
1a. Deferral (owner ruling 2026-11-20). A `Regenerate` decision in FLIGHT or an editor plans
   `ContractAcceptRepair.DeferStrandedAsset` (the line still reads `skip=scene=<scene>`) and lists
   the contract in `RescueAcceptDeferrals` (`GameActions/RescueAcceptDeferrals.cs`: `Rescue accept
   deferral listed: contractId='<id>' (rebuild scene=FLIGHT)`). The list is saved in the PARSEK node
   (`RESCUE_ACCEPT_DEFERRALS { contractId = <guid> }`, an additive child, no format bump) and each
   load takes the loaded save's copy (`LoadStateCategory.RescueAcceptDeferrals`: Save on Cold,
   Re-Fly start, the three in-session kinds, and a plain rewind and a Discard Re-fly, whose
   persistent.sfs splice keeps the landed file's own list (RESCUE-DEFERRAL-LOST-ON-REWIND-LOAD);
   a scene change reads the copy OnSave just wrote). A
   non-empty list subscribes `KspStatePatcher.DrainRescueAcceptDeferrals` to stock's
   `onContractsLoaded` (stock fires it once a scene's contracts are loaded, and the contract patch
   fires it at its end). The drain, per listed id (`DecideDeferredRescueDrainStep`, first match):
   keep while the scene is not SPACECENTER / TRACKSTATION, while `ParsekScenario.OnLoad` or a
   deferred contract patch is still running, or while the ledger's contracts module is absent; drop
   when stock holds no Active RecoverAsset with the id or the ledger no longer holds it accepted by
   now; else save the LIVE contract and re-run `Plan` with the rebuild's own guards (present, half
   present, committed resolution, reserved kerbal, roster), regenerate on `Regenerate`, and take the
   id off the list whatever the outcome, so it is never regenerated twice. A later rebuild of the
   same contract that decides anything but a deferral also takes it off. Lines: `Rescue accept
   deferral evaluated: contractId='<id>' outcome=... repair=...`, the regeneration lines of item 1,
   `Rescue accept deferral removed: ...` and `Rescue accept deferrals drained (onContractsLoaded,
   scene=SPACECENTER): evaluated=N regenerated=N dropped=N kept=N pending=N`. Why a persisted list
   and not a scan of every Active rescue: only the rebuild adds an id, so a contract the player
   accepted live (stock spawned its vessel) is never on it, and a later loss of that vessel (the
   player terminated it from the Tracking Station, where no part dies in physics, so the part
   parameters may never fail) is
   never read as a missing accept effect; a scan could not tell the two apart.
2. `KerbalNotInRoster`: left alone (re-creating a named Unowned kerbal is a roster write stock never
   makes; its offer draws a fresh random name). Owner ruling 2026-11-20: accept the gap, never recreate
   him. `KerbalNotUnowned` is also left alone (stock's generator would seat a crew kerbal in a
   second spot).
3. Tourism, any scene: each listed tourist whose `TouristConversion` is `Convert` (in the roster,
   Unowned, not reserved) gets `TourismContract.OnAccepted`'s three lines (type Tourist,
   `SetExperienceTrait(touristTrait)`, Available) under `SuppressionGuard.Crew()`, one Info line per
   tourist. `AlreadyTourist`, `Reserved` (a committed flight or the crew bookkeeping holds him),
   `NotUnowned` and `NotInRoster` are never touched and are named in `skip=`. A missing tourist is
   not recreated. Owner ruling 2026-11-20: when the committed timeline completes, fails or cancels
   the contract (the same `CommittedResolution` fact the rescue side reads), nobody is converted and
   the line reads `skip=CommittedResolution`.
4. Prebuilt ship and experimental part (FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-contract-templates`).
   Measured from the decompile (`logs/decompile/2026-10-26_full/`, KSP 1.12.5):
   - Construction / repair (`OrbitalConstructionContract`, `RoverConstructionContract`,
     `VesselRepairContract`). `OnAccepted` builds a `VesselSituation` from the contract's own
     saved values (body, the orbit regenerated from the mission seed, the rover / repair start
     lat / lon, the vessel name), sets `waitingForVslSpawn` and calls
     `ContractSystem.SpawnPreBuiltShip`; nothing else. `SpawnPreBuiltShip` is
     `StartCoroutine(ConstructShip(...))` and `ConstructShip` has no `yield return`, so the craft
     is assembled (`ShipConstruction.AssembleForLaunch`), added (non-FLIGHT branch:
     `protoVessels.Add` + `ProtoVessel.Load`) and announced (`onContractPreBuiltVesselSpawned`)
     inside the accept, and the contract's handler (subscribed in `OnRegister`) stores the vessel's
     persistent id (`constructionVslId` / `roverVslId` / `repairVslId`) before `onAccepted` fires.
     So the accept snapshot names the first timeline's vessel id. `waitingForVslSpawn` is NEVER
     saved or loaded (OnSave / OnLoad do not name it), so the premise of the old question is wrong:
     a rebuilt contract has it false and never spawns on its own. Its `OnLoad` looks the id up and
     falls back to a vessel of the saved (or seed-derived) name; after a rewind to before the accept
     neither exists, so the Active contract names a vessel nobody can reach and fails at its
     deadline (`OnVesselDestroy` never fires for it).
   - Part test (`PartTest`). `OnAccepted` sets `PartIsExperimental = !purchased || experimental`
     and, when set, calls `ResearchAndDevelopment.AddExperimentalPart` (a per-part COUNT in R&D's
     `ExpParts` node; `RemoveExperimentalPart`, run by `OnFinished` and on purchase, decrements and
     is a no-op when the part is absent). The snapshot carries `exp = True` when the accept added
     one. R&D is not ledger state: the rewind save's `ExpParts` lacks the count, so after the
     rebuild the player cannot build with the part (`PartModelPurchased` / `PartTechAvailable` read
     the count). Parsek's committed-outcome retirement removes a contract without `OnFinished`, so
     a count added for a contract the committed timeline resolves would never be taken back.
   Fix, the rescue pattern (pure `ContractAcceptWorldEffects.Plan`, a guard, logging):
   - `PrebuiltShipDecision` (first match): `NotReadable` (no craft definition), `NoSpawnRecorded`
     (vessel id 0: the first accept built nothing), `TargetPresent` (a vessel with the id, or with
     the saved name, in `flightState.protoVessels` or `FlightGlobals.Vessels`; the index now holds
     every vessel's persistent id and name), `CommittedResolution`, `VesselRecordedByCommittedFlight`
     (an ERS recording's `VesselPersistentId` is the contract's vessel id,
     `CommittedFutureIndexCache.CommittedFlightRecordsVessel`; a `ConstructShip` pid is drawn with
     `GetUniquepersistentId`, not craft-baked), `Regenerate`. The guard reads the LIVE rebuilt
     contract's save (stock's OnLoad has already re-pointed the id at a same-named vessel). On
     `Regenerate` in SPACECENTER only (`IsPrebuiltShipSpawnScene`; stock's own accept runs at
     Mission Control, the Tracking Station path is unproven) the shell invokes the contract's own
     `OnAccepted` by reflection (`repair=SpawnPrebuiltShip`): the same situation, so the same orbit
     or site and name as the first timeline, a new persistent id, which the contract's handler
     stores. Any other scene plans `DeferPrebuiltShip` (`skip=scene=<scene>`) and lists the id in
     `RescueAcceptDeferrals` (same node, ids only; the drain dispatches by the live contract's type
     and keeps a construction id until the Space Center, `DecideDeferredRescueDrainStep(effect, ...)`).
     Lines: `PatchContracts: spawned prebuilt ship for rebuilt contract '<id>' through
     <Type>.OnAccepted: added=N [...] (craft='<url>'; vesselPid a -> b)`, `Rescue accept deferral
     evaluated: contractId='<id>' type='<Type>' outcome=... repair=...`, and the Warn lines
     `prebuilt ship not spawned for '<id>'` / `<Type>.OnAccepted threw`. Double-spawn guards: the
     spawned craft is live at once and the contract names it (TargetPresent by id); a later rebuild
     from the old snapshot finds it by name (stock's OnLoad, and the index); a drained id leaves the
     list whatever it decides. When the re-run `OnAccepted` adds no vessel (`ConstructShip` returns
     early on a missing craft file or launch site, or it throws), the shell clears the contract's
     protected `waitingForVslSpawn` (`ContractAcceptWorldEffects.ClearPrebuiltSpawnWait`, Warn
     `prebuilt ship not spawned ... waitingForVslSpawn outcome=cleared`), because a flag left set
     makes the contract adopt the next prebuilt craft any other contract spawns.
   - `ExperimentalPartDecision` (first match): `NotReadable`, `NotExperimentalAtAccept`
     (`exp = False`), `RnDNotReadable` (R&D not loaded or its private `experimentalPartsStock` map
     unreadable), `Present` (R&D's count >= 1 + the other Active PartTests of the same part with
     `PartIsExperimental`, matched by `PartName` as stock's `OnPartResearched` does; also the
     double-add guard, since stock counts and never dedups), `PartPurchased` (stock's accept in this
     world would add nothing), `CommittedResolution`, `Add`. On `Add`, any scene: one
     `ResearchAndDevelopment.AddExperimentalPart`, `PatchContracts: experimental part '<part>' of
     rebuilt contract '<id>' added to R&D the way PartTest.OnAccepted does: count a -> b`. A
     contract the patch later retires on its committed outcome keeps the count only if no committed
     outcome existed when it was rebuilt (that case reads `CommittedResolution`).
   Tests: `ContractAcceptWorldEffectsTests` 90 cases, `ContractAcceptWorldIndexTests` 10. Red before

   saved node, guid re-keyed, offer extended, `roverCraftDef` written install-relative, which
   `PreBuiltCraft.CraftByURL` resolves from the last `GameData`; craft `Repair Contract Sat 9`, Kerbin

   ... through VesselRepairContract.OnAccepted: added=1` line, no second spawn after a Cold reload

   Survey of every stock contract template (2026-11-21, decompile; `Contract.SetState(Active)` runs
   `Register`, `ContractSystem.AdjustWeight` (generation weights only), `AwardAdvance` (the
   ledger's), `OnAccepted`, `onAccepted.Fire`; the only stock `onAccepted` subscribers are UI lists):
   | Template | OnAccepted world effect | Decision |
   | --- | --- | --- |
   | `RecoverAsset` | stranded vessel (`Game.AddVessel`) | regenerated (items 1-1a) |
   | `TourismContract` | tourists Unowned -> Tourist, Available | converted (item 3) |
   | `OrbitalConstructionContract`, `RoverConstructionContract`, `VesselRepairContract` | craft via `SpawnPreBuiltShip` | re-spawned / deferred (item 4) |

Tests: `ContractAcceptWorldEffectsTests` (45 cases). Red before the fix with the repair assignments

**Residual gaps (not fixed).** A compound rescue regenerated once and then rebuilt again from its
accept snapshot names the snapshot's stale part id (the snapshot is never rewritten), so its part
parameter cannot complete; reaching that needs a second rebuild of a contract whose regenerated
vessel survived, which a rewind to before the accept does not produce (that world lacks both
targets and regenerates afresh). The rescue a rewind save or rewind point had deferred is closed by
~~RESCUE-DEFERRAL-LOST-ON-REWIND-LOAD~~. A re-spawned construction / repair craft has a new
persistent id while the accept snapshot keeps the first one; a later rebuild of the same contract
finds the craft by name (stock's own OnLoad fallback and the index's name set), so a player rename
of that craft would let a second rebuild spawn a second one (needs a rename, a survival of the craft
and a second rebuild). Experimental counts are stock R&D state outside the ledger: a contract the
patch takes off the active list in-session without stock's `OnFinished` (the accepted-later
removal) leaves its count behind, as it already did for a live accept; the Present guard keeps a
rebuild from adding on top of such a count.

## ~~RESCUE-DEFERRAL-LOST-ON-REWIND-LOAD~~: a rescue the landed save already holds Active with its stranded vessel missing is not regenerated after a plain rewind or Discard Re-fly [FILED 2026-11-20 from the batch-1 re-review of the CONTRACT-REBUILD-SKIPS-ACCEPT-WORLD-EFFECTS follow-up; FIXED 2026-11-21 on branch `test-gaps-rescue-rewind` (xUnit; lanes RSQ-3 / RSQ-4 LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21, `2026-11-21_1145` / `_1148`); low (needs a rescue rebuilt in Flight before a rewind save or rewind point was written, then a rewind or Discard Re-fly to that save)]

**What happened.** `RESCUE_ACCEPT_DEFERRALS` describes the world of the `.sfs` that carries it. A plain rewind's OnLoad
node is persistent.sfs carrying the session's PARSEK node, and a Discard Re-fly's is the session's node carried around
the rewind point's world, so both loads clear the list (`LoadReconcilePolicy.DecideRescueAcceptDeferrals`). When the
rewind save (written at launch) or the rewind point (written at a separation) already holds the rescue Active with its
vessel missing, its own node listed the id, but that copy is never read; the landed Space Center's contract patch
skips the contract as existing, so the vessel is never regenerated and the contract can only fail at its deadline.
A missed regeneration, never a duplicate.

**Fix direction.** Read the deferral list from the landed save's own PARSEK node on these two loads (the rewind save /
rewind point file), or re-derive pending ids at the landed Space Center for rescues whose accept snapshot the ledger
holds and whose target is absent, with the same guards. Owner rulings 2026-11-20 also leave the related
`KerbalNotInRoster` case as an accepted gap (the kerbal is never recreated).

**Fix (2026-11-21).** The first direction. Both loads already write the landed file to persistent.sfs
through one splice, `RevertInterceptor.SpliceLiveParsekScenarioNode` (plain rewind:
`RewindLauncher.WriteRewindGameAsPersistent`; Discard Re-fly: `WriteRewindPointGameAsPersistent`), which
carries the session's PARSEK node but keeps the landed file's own `STOCK_POOL_REFERENCE` and ledger
held-through UT. It now keeps the landed file's own `RESCUE_ACCEPT_DEFERRALS` the same way (none when it
had none, so a session-only deferral describing the abandoned world is dropped), logging
`persistent.sfs splice kept the landed save's own RESCUE_ACCEPT_DEFERRALS: landed=N session=M` on the
`RewindSave` tag. The OnLoad node then carries the landed world's list, so the PlainRewind and DiscardReFly
cells of `LoadReconcilePolicy.DecideRescueAcceptDeferrals` are now `Save` (no OnLoad body change; the
token golden is untouched). No double spawn: the drain re-plans each id against the landed world (target
present or half present, committed resolution, reserved kerbal, ledger accepted by the landed clock),
drops it when stock or the ledger no longer holds it Active, and an id the landed Space Center's patch
rebuilds leaves the list there. A failed splice or write lands on the session's last persistent.sfs, whose
own node carries that world's list. Tests: `RescueAcceptDeferralsTests` (policy cells,
`LoadPolicy_RewindAndDiscardCells_NameTheSplice`, `Splice_KeepsTheLandedSavesOwnList_NotTheSessions`,
`Splice_LandedSaveWithoutAList_DropsTheSessions`, `Splice_Refused_LeavesTheLandedListUntouched`), red on
the pre-fix code (6 cells). Lane: `RSQ-3-rescue-deferral-kept-across-rewind` (authored 2026-11-21 on
`test-gaps-batch3`, never flown; stock-tree, cs-career-mun4, RSQ-2's prefix): the deferral is listed in Flight,
a recording started then writes its rewind save with it, the session's own Space Center visit drains its copy
and persistent is saved empty, and a Rewind-to-Launch onto that recording must show `landed=1 session=0`,
`Rescue accept deferrals installed (load PlainRewind): pending=1 (was 0)`, the `Rescue accept deferral
evaluated: ... outcome=Regenerate` line, `regenerated stranded asset ... added=1` and `drained
(onContractsLoaded, scene=SPACECENTER): evaluated=1 regenerated=1`, then a Cold reload adding nothing. The
Discard Re-fly path has its own lane, `RSQ-4-rescue-deferral-kept-across-discard-refly` (authored 2026-11-21 on
`test-gaps-batch3`, never flown; stock-tree, cs-career-mun4, the same prefix on RW-5's two-command `CS Flea Probe`):
after the deferral is listed in Flight, G is recorded and decoupled on the pad so its rewind point is written with the
list, committed in flight and its slot stashed, the Re-Fly is invoked from that flight (`installed (load ReFlyStart):
pending=1`), and Discard Re-fly must show `landed=1` on the splice line (`session=` regexed: the Re-Fly holds the rewind
point's copy too, so the splice line alone does not discriminate), `Rescue accept deferrals installed (load
DiscardReFly): pending=1` (the pre-fix cell logged `cleared (load DiscardReFly (Clear))`), the landed Space Center's
`evaluated ... outcome=Regenerate`, `added=1` and `drained ... evaluated=1 regenerated=1`, exactly one regeneration in
the whole run, and a Cold reload adding nothing. Both flights owed (PC).

## ~~SAVE-FREEZE-ON-MISSING-SIDECAR~~: one recording whose sidecar cannot be written froze its whole tree in every later save [FILED 2026-11-18 by code reading (test-gap pass, branch `test-gaps-savefreeze`); CONFIRMED 2026-11-20 by two red xUnit cells on the pre-fix code. FIXED 2026-11-20, same branch; xUnit; ST-4 re-pinned by code read and RE-FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-20 (`2026-11-20_2317`); high (silent loss of every later change to the tree; the sidecars of recordings the save no longer named were left as orphans on disk)]

What happened. `ParsekScenario.SaveTreeRecordings` (`Controllers/ParsekScenario.Save.cs`) writes a
committed tree only when every recording's sidecars are current. When one is not (a `.prec`
missing or unreadable at load, so `SidecarLoadFailed` stays set, or a sidecar write that fails),
the save-must-not-delete fix of QUICKLOAD-OVER-COMMITTED-RESTORE-OVERLAP-DELETES-TREE-ON-SAVE
carried the tree's last-known-good RECORDING_TREE node forward from the on-disk persistent.sfs,
reconciled to recordings the live tree still had (`TryCarryForwardCommittedTreeNodeFromLoadedSave`).
The skip condition is sticky, so that old node was written on every save until the fault cleared:
a recording added to the tree since (a Re-Fly fork, a switch continuation segment, a new branch)
was missing from every save, every edit to a healthy member (a rename, a group move, a terminal
state) was replaced by its old value, and the branch-point topology stayed the old one. The two
red cells on the pre-fix production files: a recording added after the disk save was absent from
the written tree (`Assert.Contains() Failure`), and a healthy member renamed in memory was written
with its disk name (`Expected: Renamed In Memory, Actual: Old Name On Disk`).

Fix. The tree is always written from memory. For each recording whose files could not be written,
`SpliceLastKnownGoodRecordingNodes` (`Controllers/ParsekScenario.CommittedTreeCarry.cs`) replaces
only the keys that name its sidecar files (`CarriedSidecarIdentityKeys`: `sidecarEpoch`,
`precHash`, `vesselHash`, `ghostHash`, `ghostSnapshotMode`, `pointCount`) with the values of its
node in the on-disk save; a key the disk node lacks is removed, and a recording the disk save does
not hold keeps memory's node. The rest of that recording's node stays memory's on purpose: its
`childBranchPointId` must agree with memory's BRANCH_POINT nodes, or a recording a branch was
added under reloads as a leaf. Nothing is added from disk, so a recording the player deleted is
never resurrected, and the reconcile / root-refusal / branch-point prune of the old carry are
gone with it. A tree with no on-disk node is now written from memory instead of dropped at Error.
Logs: one Warn per affected tree (`OnSave: tree '<name>' id=<id> written from memory with N
unwritable recording(s) [ids]: recordings= splicedFromDisk= unwritableWithoutDiskNode= source=
diskTreeNode=`, ids capped at 10) and one Info summary per save.

Load side (mirror). The spliced node loads as the same tree: the recording with the missing
`.prec` hydrates as `trajectory-missing` with no points, which `DropFailedSidecarHydrationRecordings`
keeps (`IsSyntheticFixtureSidecarMarker`), and keeps its branch-point link; the next save takes the
same path. Not changed here: a root whose sidecar is unreadable (not missing) still drops its
whole tree at load, which is the load-side policy, not this save path.

Tests: `UnserializableTreeCarryForwardTests`
(`SaveTreeRecordings_UnwritableMember_DoesNotFreezeTheRestOfTheTree` is the red cell, plus the
load-back mirror, the key-set pin against the codec and the splice units). ST-4 pins the reworded
Warn line; re-flown green 2026-11-20 (`2026-11-20_2317_ST-4-safe-write-crash-after-temp`).

## ~~GHOST-SERVO-CHILDREN-STATIC~~: parts mounted on a Breaking Ground servo stay frozen on the ghost while the servo moves [FILED 2026-11-20 by code reading (test-gap pass). FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `test-gaps-servoghost`; xUnit + mutation; in-game cell `ServoFollowers` PASSED in game 2026-11-20; lane SRV-1 AUTHORED 2026-11-20 (branch `test-gaps-b3-servo-lane`, stock-tree), FIRST FLIGHT 2026-11-20 RED (no hinge motion recorded: RECORDER-SERVO-ANGLE-PAW-ONLY; a pad rig's ghost hidden by the launch-site rule), REDESIGNED 2026-11-21 on `srv-hinge-rover`, RE-FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-21 `2026-11-21_1151`; low (visual only: a hinge arm, a rotor's blades or a piston's payload does not move on the replay)]

What the code did: the ghost builder parents every part (`ghost_part_<pid>`) directly to the ghost's
part container at its snapshot pose (`GhostVisualBuilder.AddPartVisuals`), and the robotic
appliers (`GhostPlaybackLogic.ApplyRoboticPose`, the rotor step in `UpdateActiveRobotics`) write
only the servo's own moving transform inside the servo part's clone. Nothing beyond the servo part
is under that transform, so every part attached to a hinge, rotation servo, piston or rotor kept
its snapshot pose while the servo's own mesh turned.

Fix: a build-time follower plan and a per-servo-write re-pose, no re-parenting (pid lookups,
visibility walks and the camera pivot all assume the flat hierarchy).
- `ServoFollowerPlanner` (pure, `Ghost/ServoFollowerPlanner.cs`) decides which parts ride which
  servo from the snapshot's `parent` / `attN` / `srfN` lines and the prefab's `servoAttachNodes` /
  `servoSrfMeshNames`, mirroring stock `BaseServo.SetChildParentTransform`: a part follows the
  NEAREST servo on whose moving side its branch hangs, so a base-side part does not move and a
  servo on a servo composes through its carrier. A servo whose parent hangs off its moving node
  (stock's "rotate base" case) is reported and carries nothing.
- At build, `GhostPlaybackLogic.BindServoFollowers` puts each servo at the moving-transform pose
  stock saved in the same OnSave that refreshed the attached parts' positions
  (`servoTransformPosition` / `servoTransformRotation`, decompiled `BaseServo.OnSave` ->
  `ApplyCoordsUpdate`), stores each follower's pose in its servo's frame, then restores the
  baseline pose and re-poses the followers.
- Per frame: `PropagateServoFollowers` runs only where a servo transform is written and the servo
  has followers: O(followers), no allocation; a ghost without a servo pays one null check per
  robotic write. Logs: `Servo follower plan for ...` and `Servo followers bound: ...` once per
  build (rate-limited per ghost), and `Servo followers re-posed in playback: servoPid= module=
  followers= value= (first since bind)` once per servo per build, on the first playback re-pose
  (`ConsumeFirstFollowerRepose`; the bind re-arms it after its own baseline re-pose), so a log can
  tell "the servo moved and its followers were carried" from "the servo moved alone".
- Recorder side (mirror check): nothing new to record. Servo motion is already recorded per module
  ordinal, the snapshot already carries the attach lines and stock's moving-transform pose, and the
  moving-side node and mesh names come from the prefab.

Proof: `ServoFollowerPlannerTests` (which parts follow, nested, base side, inverted, malformed)
and `ServoFollowerPoseTests` (the pose math, nested composition, scale). Red against the pre-fix
behaviour by mutation (planner yields nothing, follower pose ignores the servo): 9 of 21 cells red.

Lane (2026-11-20, branch `test-gaps-b3-servo-lane`; REDESIGNED 2026-11-21, see the last
paragraph): `SRV-1-hinge-followers-ghost` (operator, stock-tree by owner approval 2026-11-20) on
the derived fixture `srv-hinge-pad`
(`harness/tools/build_srv_hinge_pad.py`: fresh-sandbox plus `SRV1 Hinge Rig`, an OKTO2 on an
FL-T100 with a G-11 Hinge `hinge.01` whose moving (top) node carries a Z-200 `batteryBankMini`,
and `SRV1 Watcher`). The rig records on the pad from UT 100 while the new seam buttons
`PartAction button=servomax|servomin` (the hinge's own `MaximumAngleAction` / `MinimumAngleAction`
KSPAction, what an action group fires; xUnit `TestCommandPartActionTests`, hlib
`PartActionSourceSyncTests`) swing it +90 then -90, commits, is Rewound-to-Launch and replays
beside the watcher; the plan / bind / re-pose lines are pinned (followers=1, geometryPosed=1),
then the `ServoFollowers` cell runs in the same FLIGHT scene (interim batch pin). Requires
Breaking Ground (`GameData/SquadExpansion/Serenity`) on the install.

OPEN:
- Live proof: SRV-1's re-flight on `srv-hinge-rover` (owed; see the last paragraph). The batch
  split is pinned whole from the first flight (`passed=1 skipped=0`) and the lane left
  `INTERIM_PIN_IDS`. The rotor lane SRV-2 was AUTHORED 2026-11-21 (branch `test-gaps-rotor`)
  on a sibling fixture `srv-rotor-rover`, with new `PartAction button=rotoron|rotoroff`
  (BaseServo's non-toggle `MotorOnAction` / `MotorOffAction`); never flown, see
  RECORDER-ROTOR-RPM-PAW-ONLY.
- Known limits, not measured: a servo with an inverted mount keeps its base side still; a strut or
  fuel line spanning the servo keeps its snapshot endpoints; a servo locked in flight after moving
  with no save in between may have saved its children at an older pose (stock skips the
  coordinate refresh in OnSave for a locked servo).

SRV-1's first flight 2026-11-20 (`2026-11-20_2314_SRV-1-hinge-followers-ghost`, runner runs `b3-flights-1` / `b3-flights-2` / `b3-flights-3` on V's PC, Debug automation DLL sha256 prefix 5b46a1c1 from `test-gaps-batch3` e59ceeebc): PARSEK-FAIL(expectation) attempt 1, with no Parsek defect shown. The `ServoFollowers` cell passed on its synthetic rig (`carried its moving-side part through 45`), but the flight itself recorded nothing to replay: both `PartAction servomax` / `servomin` set the target (`state='servo:target=90.00'` / `-90.00`) and the recorder tracked the hinge (`Robotics: tracking 'hinge.01' ... source=currentAngle`), yet 0 part events were recorded (no `RoboticMotionStarted` / `RoboticPositionSample`), and the committed pad rig's ghost is hidden by the launch-site rule (`LaunchSiteGhost: Ghost hidden: vessel 'SRV1 Hinge Rig' ... never left the launch site`), so no `Servo follower plan for 'SRV1 Hinge Rig'` was ever logged. Two lane problems: the derived craft (`build_srv_hinge_pad.py`) writes no MODULE nodes, so the hinge runs on prefab defaults (KSPCF `ModuleIndexingMismatch`) and was not seen to move (read the hinge's state next flight: locked, motor disengaged, or unpowered); and a rig that never leaves the pad has its ghost hidden by design. Redesign: give the craft its hinge MODULE (unlocked, motor engaged) and fly the rig off the pad (a hop), or replay away from the launch-site circle.

## ~~S18-SEAM-CELL-ONE-SECOND-SPREAD~~: S1.8's seam cell measured 1 s of heliocentric travel, not a seam gap [FOUND 2026-11-21 from the BG-SOI-SEAM-WORLD-GAP mirror check (branch `test-gaps-bgsoi-gap`, SOI-3's sibling cell); CELL FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-s18-seam`, test only; S1.8 RE-FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-21 `2026-11-21_1144` (both seams `gap=0.0m`); low (a gate too loose to catch anything under ~25 km, no product effect)]

`SoiCrossingPlaybackInGameTests.SoiSeamWorldPositionsAreContinuous` evaluated the before side at
seam - 0.5 s and the after side at seam + 0.5 s through `TrajectoryMath.EvaluateOrbitSegmentTruePositionAtUT`,
whose world frame `getTruePositionAtUT` anchors on the Sun. Its pinned readings (flight 3,
2026-08-06: 10,146.3 m Kerbin -> Sun, 7,284.0 m Sun -> Duna) are exactly the probe's heliocentric
speeds there (10,146.3 m/s and 7,284.0 m/s), not "capture jitter", and its 25 km tolerance only
guarded the 50-90 thousand km class. The same mistake as SOI-3's cell (BG-SOI-SEAM-WORLD-GAP, on
the `test-gaps-batch3` line).

Measured headless from the corpus elements (`LoopedInterplanetaryFixture`, the flown duna-direct
segments) through `TwoBodyOrbit` in the stored frame: each after segment's epoch is the true
crossing (the non-Sun side sits on Kerbin's SOI radius, 84,159,286 m, and Duna's, 47,921,949 m,
there), the handoff fired 0.015 s / 0.048 s later, and at the seam UT the two sides agree to 0.1 mm
in position and 1e-5 m/s in velocity. The 1 s spread reproduces 10,146.3 m and 7,284.0 m to 0.01 m.
That needs the body constants the game holds, not the rounded cfg ones: the stock prefab keeps the
orbit elements as floats (mean anomaly 3.14f, Duna's eccentricity 0.051f and inclination 0.06f) and
mu_Sun is 1.1723327948324905e18; the rounded values put 1.3 km / 2.1 km of along-track ephemeris
drift into the comparison (97 m / 159 m with float elements but the rounded mu_Sun). The in-game
cell resolves against the live bodies, so none of that reaches it. (SOI-3's headless 0.57 m Mun ->
Kerbin residual is the same float effect: the Mun's mean anomaly 1.7f vs 1.7 is 4.8e-8 rad, 0.57 m
at its 12,000 km orbit.)

Fix (test only): the cell evaluates both sides at the seam UT in one synchronous pass and logs
`afterEpoch=`, `seamMinusAfterEpoch=`, `localBody=`, `localSideFromBody=` and `localSoi=`. Tolerance
25 km -> 1 km, derived in the cell's comment (patched-conic divergence 0.5 * da * L^2 with da below
1e-3 m/s^2 at either SOI edge; 1 km allows about 1,400 s of handoff lag and still catches a
wrong-body side, a rotation of one side's body-relative vector above ~0.0007 deg, and an evaluation
more than ~0.1 s off the seam). xUnit `SoiSeamWorldGapTests` (7 cases) pins the crossing, the
same-UT agreement, the 1 s readings and the wrong-body class. The S1.8 spec's two seam tokens now
require the new tail, so a stale DLL reds them. Comments in `GhostRenderTrace` (loop-seam teleport
floor) and `SeamEndpointOracle` that took the 10 / 7 km readings as the healthy population now call
them an upper bound; neither threshold moves.

Owed: S1.8's re-flight on a DLL from this branch (stock-minimal, daily). Expected lines:
`seam Kerbin->Sun ut=4742953.221 gap=0.0m (tolerance 1000m, both sides at the seam UT) afterEpoch=4742953.206 seamMinusAfterEpoch=0.015s localBody=Kerbin localSideFromBody=84159300m localSoi=84159286m`
and `seam Sun->Duna ut=9128108.755 gap=0.0m (...) afterEpoch=9128108.707 seamMinusAfterEpoch=0.048s localBody=Duna localSideFromBody=47921878m localSoi=47921949m`,
then `BATCH_COMPLETE v1 total=3 passed=3 failed=0 skipped=0`. After it, tighten the spec's `gap=` windows.

## ~~FLIGHT-CLOCK-CROSSING-COMMITTED-ROWS~~: in flight a committed row the clock reached took effect only at the next recalculation [FILED 2026-11-21 from the PADX lanes (TEST-GAPS-B3-PAD-AND-JUMP-LANES on `test-gaps-batch3`; owner decision: the flight scene needs the cursor); FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-flight-ksc-clock`; xUnit; PADX-2 re-pinned and re-flown green `2026-11-21_1135`, its recording-time lane PADX-3 green `2026-11-21_1138`; medium (a committed pad crash, purchase or contract outcome landed at the next warp exit, commit or spend instead of at its UT)]

The Space Center and Tracking Station run `CareerLedgerClockCursor`: one cached next-row lookup per
frame, and one clock-advance recalculation (`RecalculateAndPatchForClockAdvance`) when the clock
reaches the next ledger row. FLIGHT had only the milestone cursor (`CommittedMilestoneClockCursor`,
add-only world-firsts), so at 1x the reached rows waited; in warp they applied at the warp exit.

Fix:
- `ParsekFlight` owns a third cursor, `flightLedgerClock` (reason `flight-clock`), advanced in
  `Update` beside the milestone cursor, after the teardown early-out and only while no rewind UT
  adjustment is pending. The first frame seeds (the scene load walked at that clock). A time jump,
  a commit or a load that already walked costs at most one redundant walk (the committed-future
  snapshot then reaches no crossing), as at the Space Center after a purchase. The recalculation
  is wrapped (`ParsekFlight.RecalculateLedgerAtFlightClockCrossing`: one Info line
  `Flight clock reached a committed ledger row: reason=flight-clock` per crossing; a failure is a
  Warn that never breaks `Update`). F9, revert, rewind and Re-Fly loads rebuild the scene, so the
  cursor reseeds at the loaded clock.
- Row kinds: every kind the Space Center cursor applies (funds, science, reputation, facility
  levels and buildings, contracts, tech, hires, strategies, dismissals), because the flight warp
  exit already runs the same walk in FLIGHT; the cursor only moves it to the row's UT.
- While a flight records, or its tree is uncommitted or pending, that walk's KSP patch stays
  deferred (#466: the pools hold the flight's uncommitted effects) and the live building patch
  skips (the flight owns collapses the ledger has not received). The one exception is the
  buildings: the cursor's after-recalculate hook
  (`FacilityStatePatcher.PatchCrossedBuildingRowsWhileTreeLives`) applies the FacilityDestruction /
  FacilityRepair rows of the crossing window only (`ComputeBuildingStatesCrossed`, rows in
  `(previous cutoff, now]`), so a pad the committed timeline knocks down falls at its UT even under
  a recording. A full fold would repair a building the live flight knocked down after an earlier
  committed repair; a window never reaches back past the previous crossing, so it agrees with the
  fold the commit's patch makes later. Rows tagged to the active Re-Fly's suppressed subtree are
  left out (the flight being re-flown stays in the ledger until the merge). Skipped inside OnLoad,
  from a ledger held from a newer version, on a clock that is not ready, and for an empty window.
- Double apply: the patch's Demolish / Repair run under `SuppressionGuard.ResourcesAndReplay`, so
  stock's collapse event is not captured as the live flight's; a crash the live flight itself
  causes is captured once and becomes its row at commit, which the next crossing finds already
  matching the building.
- xUnit `FlightLedgerClockCursorTests` (window, fold, mode, headless live step, ParsekFlight wiring
  gate), `KscBuildingLivePatchWiringTests` (two pinned `PatchDestructionState` feeds).

Lanes (2026-11-21, `test-gaps-batch3`, all owed a flight): PADX-2's header now describes the
fall inside the warp and each crossing window requires `Flight clock reached a committed ledger
row: reason=flight-clock`, then `PatchDestructionState: demolished`, then `Warp exit ledger
recalculation started`; QL-14's header no longer says the rows wait for the return and it requires
the flight cursor line between the rewind and the return; the new `PADX-3-pad-row-crossed-while-recording`
(stock-minimal) crosses PADX-1's committed pad collapse at 1x while a second flight RECORDS (the
hook's Apply path): `PatchCrossedBuildingRows: flight clock crossed 1 committed building row(s) ...
while the ledger patch is deferred (live recorder active)`, the demolish, and no
`Game state: BuildingDestroyed` after the rewind (no second row on that flight's commit).

L12 (2026-11-23, branch `lane-repins2-1023`): its cell `ReachedCommittedOutcomeBlocksDeadlineExpiryAndFail`
filed the committed completion one second behind the clock, inside the cursor's window, so
`2026-11-23_1548` refused stock's expiry once and then completed the contract at the crossing
(`Flight clock reached a committed ledger row: reason=flight-clock`, `filed ended contract 07c8e34d
... as Completed ... silently`, funds 536558.0 and reputation 2.000 unchanged): the rule above, read by
the cell as stock ending the contract. The row now sits one second after the contract's accept, behind
the scene load and so behind the window; both halves of the fail block (todo
CONTRACT-FAIL-AFTER-REACHED-COMMITTED-OUTCOME) stay proven on an Active contract and no spec token moved.
xUnit `RowFiledBehindTheSeed_IsNoCrossing_RowInsideTheWindowIs` pins both sides. Re-flight owed.

## ~~OPTIMIZER-SPLIT-RULES-V2~~: the 2026-11 split rules: atmosphere passes, one row across an SOI change, a touch-and-go as a graze, for new flights only (owner rulings Q5, Q7 with A1 / B1, Q8, Q9) [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (design questions 1-3 and 14), ruled by the owner 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-20 (`docs/handoff/recording-split-review/atmosphere-pass-analysis.md`, step 1 of section 8). BUILT 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; NOT FLOWN; step 2 (cuts where the orbit changes kind, the deorbit row) is OPTIMIZER-SPLIT-RULES-V3]

**Cause:** the 2-minute graze clock, not what a pass did, decided how atmosphere passes split (a skip reentry had no row of its own, ten deep aerobraking passes made 21 rows, a short aerocapture was invisible); an engine running at an SOI change or the atmosphere line decided whether a leg was its own row; every touch-and-go cost two rows; and a rule change re-cut every old flight on the next load (ruling Q5: "freeze old recordings").

**Fix:** design `docs/dev/done/plans/optimizer-persistence-split.md` section 14, code `RecordingOptimizer.SplitRules.cs`.
- Version gate: `Recording.SplitRuleVersion` (key `splitRuleVersion`, written only above 1; absent = 1). Stamped with the current version (2, then 3 from OPTIMIZER-SPLIT-RULES-V3; a version-2 recording keeps the version-2 rules) when a recording enters the committed list (tree commit append, Re-Fly provisional) or when an in-flight tree is saved; a recording that has a version keeps it. Both halves of a split carry it; `CanAutoMerge` refuses mixed versions. Version 1 runs the old predicate body unchanged.
- Row role: `Recording.SegmentRole` (key `segmentRole`), stamped on both halves of a version-2 split (ascent, space, aerobraking, reentry, approach, surface, atmosphere). At every cut the first half's pass role is read again from its own content (`ResolveHeadRoleAfterCut`: a grown reentry row whose first pass now ends back in space becomes an aerobraking row). `CanAutoMerge` refuses different roles AND, for two version-2 rows, any join the version-2 split predicate would cut again (`WouldSplitRulesCutJoin`, Verbose `the split rules would cut the join again`), so the merge pass (which runs before the split pass) and the split pass can never undo each other on every load. The existing row label (`RecordingSegmentLabels.GetSegmentPhaseLabel`) reads the role in place of the phase ("Kerbin reentry"); no new UI; the table's phase sort reads `GetSegmentPhaseSortLabel` (the phase), so the table order does not move.
- Atmosphere passes (Q7 / A1 / B1): a pass entered from space that ends on the ground or in the air is cut at its first entry (reentry row; skip dips inside it); one that ends back in space is cut at its first accepted touch of the row (aerobraking row; later passes and the exit stay inside it). The engine at the crossing no longer matters for such a pass; ascents and the airless approach band keep the old rules. Debris follows these rules; EVA kerbals keep version 1.
- The first touch of an aerobraking row resets at a body change: a braking pass at another body (a Duna aerocapture after a Kerbin aerobrake, one row across the SOI change per Q9) opens its own aerobraking row.
- Q9: any SOI change between two space sections stays one row. Q8: a Surface run under 30 s between air or approach runs is never cut and reads as air, except inside a launch-site start's leading run, where rule 5b already keeps a bounce off the pad with the ascent (the two rules must agree on where that run ends).
- Logs: `Split candidate (FinalDescentEntry|BrakingPassEntry)`, `Split roles: ...`, `Split rules: stamped version N ...`, the split summary's appended `passKept= touchdownKept= rules=v2`, `CanAutoMerge: rejecting ... split rules vA/vB roles ...`.
- Accepted: a Re-Fly attempt committed later is version 2 beside version-1 pieces of the same tree. The split recorder's fallback commit (`TreeCommitService.CommitRecordingDirect`) stamps too. The RULE 3 fold of a covered split piece into a re-flown live recording (`CommittedListOptimizer.ReabsorbSplitPieceIntoLiveCopy`) refuses a piece cut under another rule version than the live recording (`SplitPieceFoldRefusal`, the piece kept beside it like the other refusals) and re-reads the survivor's pass role from its content after the fold (`ReReadSurvivorRoleAfterFold`, Info `role re-read after the fold: A -> B`); the next pass re-cuts it and the merge guard never re-joins the cut. `ForceSplitRuleVersionForTesting` judges a fixture by version 2 (Phase 0). Tests: `OptimizerSplitRulesIntegrationTests` (the fold refusal, the fold role re-read, the direct-commit stamp; the last two red with the fix disabled).

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitRulesV2Tests` (every shape of the analysis section 3 with its version-1 pin where it differs, debris, EVA, Q8, Q9, the gate, the codec, the merge refusals, the stamps, a version-1 boundary-by-boundary pin), each shape run twice through the real pass with the second pass changing nothing; every existing optimizer cell is unchanged (the version-1 pin). `OptimizerRepeatPassSweepTests` loads every committed fixture save headlessly (74 with track sections, harness and xUnit fixtures) and runs the pass twice under version 1 and forced version 2: the second pass changes nothing.

## ~~OPTIMIZER-SPLIT-IN-ONE-PASS~~: a big mission needed several loads to finish splitting (owner ruling Q19, "finish in one go") [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (design question 15), ruled by the owner 2026-11-18. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; no lane]

**Cause:** the split loop of `CommittedListOptimizer.RunOptimizationPass` stopped after 50 splits (and the merge loop after 50 merges), leaving the rest for the next cold load or commit.

**Fix:** both loops run until no candidate remains. The split loop is bounded by the committed list's section count plus its recording count (`ComputeSplitSafetyBound`, at least 50; every cut consumes a boundary), the merge loop by the list size; hitting a bound Warns `Optimization pass: hit split|merge safety bound (N), some candidates may remain`. Applies to every rule version (it changes when a cut happens, not where).

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitRulesV2Tests.OnePass_SplitsAMissionPastTheOldFiftySplitCap` (79 cuts in one pass), `SplitSafetyBound_CountsSectionsAndRecordings`.

## ~~CHAIN-INDEX-HOLE-RESTORES-EARLIER-PIECE~~: a hole in a chain's indices made an earlier piece look like the chain's end to the committed-tree restore [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding L11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; no lane; low (a resume of a committed vessel could record onto an earlier piece)]

**Cause:** `ParsekFlight.HasNextChainSegmentInTree` (the "a later piece exists" check of `IsCommittedSpawnedRecordingRestorable`) looked for exactly `ChainIndex + 1`, so when that piece was gone (a hole in the indices) an earlier piece passed as the chain's last one.

**Fix:** the check accepts any later piece of the same chain and branch (`ChainIndex > rec.ChainIndex`).

**Tests:** `CommittedRestoreChainTipTests.ChainIndexHole_HeadIsNotRestorable` (red before the fix).

## ~~TRIM-IGNORES-SUPERSEDE-AND-REFLY~~: the boring-tail trim cut superseded recordings and the recordings of a live Re-Fly [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding L7), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; no lane; low (a superseded or in-merge recording lost its tail behind the merge's back)]

**Cause:** the split pass skips superseded recordings and defers the live Re-Fly provisional, and the merge pass refuses both and the recordings the live session names, but `CommittedListOptimizer.TrimBoringTailsForOptimization` held only supply route sources.

**Fix:** `DescribeTrimHold` adds two skip categories to the trim pass: `superseded` (a supersede row names the recording) and `active-refly` (the live Re-Fly's provisional, or a recording the live session or merge journal names, `CommittedListOptimizer.CollectLiveReFlyMergeHeldIds`). They are counted in the existing `TrimBoringTail skipped N recording(s)` summary.

**Tests:** `CommittedListOptimizerUnitTests.TrimHolds_SupersededAndLiveReFlyRecordings` (red before the fix).

## ~~SPLIT-LEAVES-END-FIELDS-ON-HEAD~~: an optimizer split left the end situation, dock partner and route windows on the first half [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding L6), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; no lane; low (the timeline's spawn wording for the real end fell back to generic text)]

**Cause:** `RecordingOptimizer.TransferTerminalFieldsToSecondHalf` moved the terminal state, snapshot and terminal orbit to the second half but left `VesselSituation`, `DockTargetVesselPid`, `TransferTargetVesselPid` / `TransferKind` and `RouteConnectionWindows` on the first half.

**Fix:** `MoveEndOfFlightFieldsToSecondHalf` moves them with the terminal; a route connection window that closed (undocked) before the cut stays on the first half, every other window moves (Verbose `Split: end-of-flight fields moved onto the second half (... windowsMoved=N windowsKept=M)`). The Re-Fly cut (`SplitAtUT`) goes through the same step, so TIP carries them. `SceneExitSituation` was not in the finding and is unchanged.

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitPlayerSettingsTests.Split_MovesEndOfFlightFieldsToTheSecondHalf` (red before the fix).

## ~~LOOP-SYNC-PARENT-LINK-WRONG~~: a debris piece's loop-sync parent link pointed at the wrong recording [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (findings L4 and L5), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; no lane; low (a looping debris ghost follows another recording's loop clock)]

**Cause:** (L4) `Recording.LoopSyncParentIdx` is a committed-list position the engine reads as an index into its trajectory list, but nothing shifted it on a mid-list removal or insertion between optimization passes, so after a discard or an insert it named whatever recording slid into that slot. (L5) `CommittedListOptimizer.PopulateLoopSyncParentIndices` picked the first non-debris recording of the tree whose range covered the debris's start, ignoring the debris's own parent (`ParentAnchorRecordingId`), so a sibling stage listed first won.

**Fix:** (L4) the two committed-list primitives `RecordingStore.RemoveCommittedAt` / `InsertCommittedAt` shift every link through `ShiftLoopSyncParentIndices` (a link to the removed recording is dropped; Verbose `Loop sync parent links after removal|insertion at index N: shifted=.. dropped=..`). (L5) `FindLoopSyncParentIndex` prefers the parent anchor when it covers the debris's start, then the piece of the anchor's chain that does (an optimizer split moved the birth onto a later piece), and falls back to the covering rule; the summary line gains `byParentAnchor=N`.

**Tests:** `OptimizerLoopSyncParentTests` (removal shifts and drops, insertion shifts, the anchor wins over an earlier covering sibling, the anchor's chain piece is found, no anchor keeps the covering rule); four red before the fix.

## ~~LAUNCH-HEAD-LABELLED-SURFACE~~: every launch's first row was labelled "surface" [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding M10), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; no lane; low (a wrong label in the Recordings table and the map)]

**Cause:** since the launch-site rule (step 5b, owner ruling 2026-10-07) keeps the pad or runway time with the ascent, a split's first half starts on the pad, and `SplitAtSection` took its `SegmentPhase` from section 0, so the ascent row read "Kerbin surface".

**Fix:** `RecordingOptimizer.ResolveHeadPhaseSection` labels a launch-site start's first half by the section where it leaves the site (`FindLaunchSiteDepartureSection`); any other first half keeps section 0. Verbose `Split: head <id> labelled by its launch-site departure section N (...)`. Rows split earlier keep their label.

**Tests:** `OptimizerLaunchSiteLeadingRunTests.PadLaunch_Split_HeadIsLabelledByItsAscentNotThePad` (red before the fix) and `NonLaunchSurfaceStart_Split_HeadKeepsTheSurfaceLabel`.

## ~~SPLIT-DROPS-PLAYER-ROW-SETTINGS~~: an optimizer split dropped the player's hide / disable / loop settings on the new piece [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding H6), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp5-optimizer`; xUnit; no lane; high (a hidden flight's second half reappears; a loop replays only the first half)]

**Cause:** the merge pass refuses recordings with player settings (`CanAutoMerge`: loop, `PlaybackEnabled`, `Hidden`), but the split pass checked none and `SplitAtSection` / `CopySplitIdentityFields` copied none of them, so a recording the player hid, disabled or looped while its split was postponed (a live Re-Fly, a supply route hold) came apart on the next cold load with the new piece visible, enabled and not looping. The tail trim also cut looped recordings.

**Fix:** owner RULE 1 ("always keep them"). `SplitAtSection` copies `Hidden`, `PlaybackEnabled` and the whole-recording loop (`LoopPlayback`, period, unit, anchor) onto the second half through `RecordingOptimizer.CopyPlayerRowSettings` (the seal and the groups already travelled). Both halves of a whole-recording loop share the period, so each cycle still runs head then tail. A loop RANGE (`LoopStartUT` / `LoopEndUT`) names UTs of the whole flight and cannot be divided, so `FindSplitCandidatesForOptimizer` keeps such a recording whole (Verbose `kept N recording(s) whole: the player set a loop range on them`), and `TrimBoringTailInternal` skips a recording with a loop or a loop range (category `loop-settings`).

**Tests:** `OptimizerSplitPlayerSettingsTests` (split keeps hidden / disabled / loop / seal / groups on both halves through the real pass; a loop range is neither split nor trimmed; the trim skips a looped recording), all three red before the fix.

## ~~BG-SEPARATION-CLOSES-PARENT-RECORDING~~: a background vessel's staging closed its recording and started a second one [FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp8-bg-shape`; xUnit `BackgroundSeparationShapeTests`; low (two recordings-table rows for one vessel; no data lost)]

Cause: a decouple or a broken-off part of a BACKGROUND vessel went through
`BackgroundRecorder.HandleBackgroundVesselSplit`'s closing path: `CloseParentRecording` ended the
parent recording at the split, a parent continuation recording (same pid) carried the vessel on,
the pieces were anchored to the continuation, and each deferred scan (one per frame) made its own
branch point. The focused vessel's decouple or breakup keeps one recording that runs past the
split (`ParsekFlight.WireBreakupIntoTree`) and groups the pieces of a 0.5 s window into one
branch point, so the same staging gave two different tree shapes depending on focus.

Fix: owner ruling Q15 (2026-11-18), "One shape for both". `BackgroundRecorder.SeparationWindows.cs`
keeps one `CrashCoalescer` per background parent pid (the class moved from `Rewind/` to
`Recording/`, its own module, so the background recorder adds no backward module edge). The
deferred scan feeds each new vessel (snapshot and pose captured at the scan) into the window;
`ProcessPendingSplitChecks` ticks it; the emitted JointBreak branch point is wired with
`WireBreakupIntoTree` onto the parent recording, which keeps its BackgroundMap entry and keeps
sampling, gets its VesselSnapshot refreshed, and keeps the structural-event point the joint break
wrote. Children go through `ParsekFlight.CreateBreakupChildRecording` anchored to the parent
recording (a controlled piece gone before the window closed gets none, a debris piece gone gets
the destroyed one-point row, as focused), live ones join the background recorder with the debris
limit keyed on the branch point UT, and a split with two or more controllable vessels authors a
rewind point whose parent slot is the parent recording itself. An undock keeps the closing shape
(it is the focused undock shape), emitting a window the parent still holds first. Windows are
emitted early (never drop one) from `FlushPendingSplits` (save, scene exit, revert, every
recorder start), `FinalizeAllForCommit`, `Shutdown` (with a Warn), and when the parent stops
being a background vessel: `OnVesselRemovedFromBackground` (promotion, switch, debris end, member
reconcile), go-on-rails (before the identity-loss check), `OnBackgroundVesselWillDestroy` and
`RetireDestroyedBackgroundEntry`. A piece still held by a window that acts on its own (separates
again, undocks or is decoupled, or the player switches to it) emits its window first
(`EmitSeparationWindowHoldingChild`, from `OnBackgroundPartJointBreak`, `OnBackgroundPartUndock`,
`OnBackgroundPartDeCouple` and `OnVesselSwitchComplete`) so it is a background member with its
own recording when it does, and an undock of it is still classed UNDOCK. A piece is held by one
window only: two background parents splitting in one physics step both see each other's new
vessel (a held piece is not in the BackgroundMap yet), so the new-vessel scan and the window feed
skip a piece an open window holds (one recording per vessel). `DebrisParentStateGate` and the
Re-Fly HEAD/TIP splitter already handle this shape (the focused breakup writes it).

The vessel-line rule (`RecordingTree.ChildBranchLeavesVesselLineOpen`) read a recording whose
`ExplicitEndUT` is at or before the branch UT as closed at the split. A background parent's end
equals the branch UT from the joint break's structural point until its next ordinary sample (2 s
close in, 3 s / 8 s for a steady parent at Medium / Low density), so an F5 in that span saved a
parent that F9's `RebuildBackgroundMap` then dropped (never sampled again, no terminal). The
branch point now says it: `BranchPoint.ParentContinues`, stamped by every
`ParsekFlight.WireBreakupIntoTree` caller (focused and background), skips the end-UT rule. It is
an additive optional key `parentContinues = True` on the BRANCH_POINT node (absent reads false,
today's reading for older saves and for the background undock's close; no format bump), carried
by both branch-point clones and `ScenarioWriter.SeparationBranch(parentContinues:)`.

Tests: `BackgroundSeparationShapeTests` (shape with the parent's end at the branch UT, the map
rebuild and the `parentContinues` round trip, the unstamped closed-at-split reading, the focused
stamp, coalescing and BROKE_OFF combine, dead controlled piece, one recording for a piece two
parents saw, flush / Shutdown / retire emission, recording change, missing parent, the held-piece
emit, and source gates on every emission site; the stamp, the one-holder and the held-piece cells
were red before their fixes, the earlier gate cells and the retire cell were mutation checked).
The `BackgroundSplitTests` continuation / bug #285 simulation cells now pass the
`UNDOCK` cause: they pinned the decouple continuation shape the ruling replaces, and the undock
path is the one that still builds it.

## ~~REFLY-ROUTE-SOURCE-REFUSED~~: Re-Fly was offered on a flight a supply route is built from [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (design question 13: the optimizer holds route sources, the Re-Fly splitter had no such hold); ruled by the owner 2026-11-18 (Q17 "Refuse Re-Fly"). FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp6-live-flight`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; medium (a merge would cut or supersede the route's source and pause the route for good)]

**Cause:** the Re-Fly gate (`RewindInvoker.CanInvoke`) did not know about supply routes. Route candidates come only from fully sealed trees, but a slot of such a tree can open later, and nothing then stopped a Re-Fly whose merge splits the closure root and supersedes the slot's subtree, moving or hiding recordings the route's `SourceRefs` name (route reads `SourceChanged` / `MissingSourceRecording`).

**Fix (Q17):** `RewindInvoker.SlotFlightIsRouteSource` (pure): the slot's origin recording's committed tree holds a recording id from `Logistics.RouteStore.CollectSourceRecordingIds()` (committed and dormant routes); with no slot, any slot of the rewind point. `EvaluateCanInvoke` refuses with `RouteSourceReFlyReason` ("A supply route is built from this flight - delete the route to re-fly it") after the session checks and before the value gate. Both Fly buttons (the Unfinished Flights row and the timeline row) read it through `RecordingsTableUI.CanInvokeRewindPointSlot`, grey the button and show the reason as its existing tooltip; `StartInvoke` re-reads the same gate on the confirm click, so the mark and the click-block share one predicate (stock-control annotation rule; no new UI). Seal stays available. Verbose `[Rewind] CanInvoke: refused rp=<id> slot=<n|all> tree=<id> routeSourceRec=<id> reason=route-source` (rate-limited per slot), plus the existing `CanInvoke: disabled ... reason=...` change line. Design `docs/parsek-rewind-to-separation-design.md` section 2.12 (after Rule 1).

**Tests:** `RouteSourceReFlyGateTests` (a route on the slot's flight refuses the slot, the rewind-point-only overload and the table's slot gate with the tooltip reason, and logs the tree and source; a route on another flight does not refuse; the pure predicate table). The refusal cell red with the check disabled.

## ~~LIVE-FLOWN-TREE-RECUT-DROPS-NEW-LEG~~: a committed vessel flown again lost its new leg to an optimizer re-cut and the duplicate skip [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding H7), by code reading; ruled by the owner 2026-11-18 (RULE 3 "My live flight wins"). FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp6-live-flight`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; high (the player's flight is dropped from the timeline)]

**Cause:** flying a committed vessel again makes the live tree a copy of the committed tree (same tree id, another object; `TryTakeCommittedTreeForSpawnedVesselRestore`'s copy-on-write clone, a Re-Fly tree, or either one in a quicksave). The cold load restores that copy into the pending slot (Limbo, or a finalized pending tree) BEFORE the load's optimizer pass, and the pass then split, merged or trimmed the committed tree under it. The committed tree now held recording ids the copy lacked, so at commit `TreeCommitService.ShouldReplaceCommittedTree` refused (`incoming-missing-existing-ids`) and, with no Re-Fly marker, `CommitTreeCore` took the duplicate skip: since #2722 (MERGE-DUPLICATE-SKIP-TOASTS-MERGED) the pending tree is dropped honestly, but the new leg was still lost.

**Definitions (code: `TreeCommitService.LiveFlownCopy.cs`, `IsCommittedTreeFlownAgain`).** A pending tree is **a committed vessel flown again** when its id names a committed tree, it is a different object, and it carries flight the committed tree does not have, first match wins: (1) a branch point id the committed tree lacks; (2) a recording both hold whose recorded data (points, track sections with samples, non-predicted orbit segments) runs past everything the committed tree holds for that recording's chain (an optimizer split moves the committed copy's end onto a later chain piece, so a re-cut alone is not new flight); (3) a recording only the copy holds whose recorded data runs past every committed recording of the tree. Predicted tails never count. A copy with none of these is a **true duplicate** and still takes the duplicate skip (the commit returns false, the pending tree is dropped, as #2722 made it). A **live copy exists** for a committed tree while the pending tree or the saved pending tree an active-tree restore parks beside it has its id and is not the committed object, or the committed-tree restore attempt is armed for it. The flight scene's own active tree is not read: after an in-flight commit it is still the copy object while the committed tree is the union result, and the commit's own pass must run.

**Fix (RULE 3):** (a) `CommittedListOptimizer.RunOptimizationPass` adds every recording of a committed tree with a live copy to its held set (`TreeCommitService.HoldLiveCopiesForOptimizer`, one call in the pass that hands it the committed trees, both pending slots and the restore attempt id, so the helper reads no store: the set the route-source hold already uses, so the merge, split and trim phases all skip them; the per-phase "held for route source" Verbose lines count them too). Info `Optimization pass: tree '<id>' held whole while its live copy is flown (recordings=N pendingCopy=<b> savedPendingCopy=<b> restoreAttempt=<b>) - no split, merge or trim until the live flight is committed or discarded`. (b) `CommitTreeCore`, after the Re-Fly union and before the duplicate skip: a committed vessel flown again is unioned into the committed tree (`TryUnionLiveCopyIntoCommitted`, the Re-Fly union's core: incoming-only recordings and branch points added, shared recordings take the live instance with the player's settings kept (MERGE-REVERTS-PLAYER-SETTINGS), committed-only recordings kept, the live active recording id wins; `TryUnionFlownAgainCopy`). Committed-only recordings that are split pieces the live recording covers are re-absorbed instead of kept (`FindCoveredCommittedOnlySplitPieces`: a committed-only recording on the committed chain of a shared recording whose span lies inside the live recording's span, start to latest recorded data). An optimizer split while the copy lived keeps the original id as HEAD and moves the ending, snapshots, VesselDestroyed and MergeState to a new-id tail; kept beside the copy's whole recording that tail replayed twice and stayed the chain tip with the old ending. `CommittedListOptimizer.ReabsorbSplitPieceIntoLiveCopy` runs the optimizer merge's own steps on it: ledger rows, events and pending science retagged to the surviving id, an awaiting stock payout moved, Relative section anchors and parent anchors re-pointed (`RepointAnchorsAfterOptimizationMerge`), the tree drops it and its branch points and children name the survivor (`UpdateTreeStateAfterOptimizationMerge`), and it leaves the committed list through `RemoveCommittedAt` (index notifications fire); its sidecars are left to the orphan collector.
