Before the piece goes, what it owned as the chain tip (where later writes land) is carried onto the committed copy of the survivor's id, which the replace step then hands to the live recording (`TreeCommitService.CarryTipOwnedStateOnFold`): its `MergeState` outright (slot state is read from the tip, so a Seal or Stash taken there wins), the spawn claim and spawn counters and the crew death respawn stamp where the head has none, and the groups where the head has none (the piece's own hide, ghost-off and loop settings stay with it, FOLDED-PIECE-ROW-SETTINGS-SPREAD). A piece a supersede row names (either side) or a supply route sources from is never folded (`CommittedListOptimizer.SplitPieceFoldRefusal`, Info `CommitTree: kept split piece '<id>' beside '<id>' although the live recording covers it: <reason>`). `CommitTree`'s own `VesselNameStore.ApplyAll("commit-tree")` runs right after the fold. The survivor keeps the committed HEAD's player settings (RULE 1), a live recording without a chain id takes the committed copy's, and the touched chains are re-indexed over the tree. Committed-only recordings the live span does not cover stay. Info `CommitTree: re-absorbed split piece '<id>' into '<id>' (...)` per piece and `CommitTree: committed vessel flown again - unioned the live copy of tree id=... (strictGateReason=..., evidence=..., addedRecordings=N addedBranchPoints=N reabsorbedSplitPieces=N keptCommittedOnlyRecordings=N activeRecordingIdSwapped=<b> restoreAttemptArmed=<b>)`; the duplicate skip's Verbose line now ends `flownAgain=false evidence=<why>`. `ParsekFlight.TryGetLatestRecordedUT` forwards to the shared `TreeCommitService.TryGetLatestRecordedDataUT`, which now also owns the section test. The helpers live on a `TreeCommitService` partial so they add no type to the architecture knot. Design `docs/parsek-flight-recorder-design.md` (the committed-tree clone branch).

**Residue:** a committed-tree restore attempt left armed after a true-duplicate skip (an unflown copy dropped) keeps that tree held from the optimizer until the attempt is cleared (a cold load, a commit or discard of the tree, the next arm). Not cleared on the skip path because the clear there would need a choice between the discard purge and a bare clear of the clone's held events; a duplicate carries no new flight, so the hold only postpones optimizer cuts for the session.

**Tests:** `LiveFlownCommittedTreeTests` (a flown-again copy after a re-cut commits with the new leg and re-absorbs the covered split tail: no other piece of the chain overlaps the live recording, the stale tail is gone so the chain tip carries the new ending, its ledger row, branch point and parent anchor name the survivor, the survivor keeps the committed player settings and takes the tip's seal, spawn claim and a loop only the tip had; a piece a supersede row or a route names is kept; the tip-state carry table; a committed-only piece the live span does not cover stays; the covered-piece finder table; an unflown copy of a re-cut tree is still a duplicate; the three evidence kinds, predicted tails, not-a-copy; the optimizer leaves a tree with a pending live copy whole and still merges it without one; the live-copy id collection). The commit cell red with the union disabled, the optimizer cell red with the hold line removed. Review follow-up (2026-11-21): the first version kept the covered tail beside the copy and its test pinned that (`..._KeepsTheNewLegAndTheCommittedOnlyPiece`); the reworked cell was red against a finder that returned nothing. Second review follow-up (same day): the fold dropped what only the tail carried (a Seal on the tip, the spawn stamp); the extended cell and the guard cells were red before the tip carry and the fold refusal.

## ~~MERGE-REVERTS-PLAYER-SETTINGS~~: a merge of a live copy reverted the seal, stash, hide, ghost, loop and group settings the player made meanwhile [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding H5), by code reading; ruled by the owner 2026-11-18 (RULE 1 "Always keep them"). FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `rsr-wp6-live-flight`; xUnit; no lane; high (a sealed slot whose rewind point the seal deleted came back open with no rewind point, blocking routes)]

**Cause:** a live tree that copies a committed tree (a Re-Fly tree, a resumed committed vessel, a quicksave of either) is a clone taken before the player's later clicks. At commit `TreeCommitService.UnionRecordingsInto` (the Re-Fly union and the merge journal's `TreeMerge` union) and `MergeTreeRecordingsIntoCommitted` (every replace commit) swapped the committed recording for the clone's copy, carrying only runtime fields (`PreserveLiveRuntimeFieldsOnReplace`), so `MergeState` (Seal / Stash), `Hidden`, `PlaybackEnabled`, the loop fields and `RecordingGroups` went back to the clone's values. Seal and Stash stay enabled during a Re-Fly.

**Fix (RULE 1):** the committed side wins for the fields the player owns. `TreeCommitService.PreservePlayerOwnedFieldsOnReplace` copies onto the incoming copy, before it replaces the committed one: `MergeState`, `Hidden`, `PlaybackEnabled`, `LoopPlayback`, `LoopIntervalSeconds`, `LoopTimeUnit`, `LoopStartUT`, `LoopEndUT`, `LoopAnchorVesselId`, `LoopAnchorBodyName` and `RecordingGroups` (a copy of the list). It runs in both swap sites, so the Re-Fly union, the journal's `TreeMerge` union and every replace commit keep them. Exception: the re-flown slot's own recordings (the live marker's `ActiveReFlyRecordingId`, `OriginChildRecordingId`, `SupersedeTargetId`, `ReFlownSlotRecordingIds`) take the incoming `MergeState`, which the Re-Fly commit owns; their other settings are kept too. Logs: Verbose `... kept the player's settings of the committed copy rec=<id> fields=[...] mergeStateFromIncoming=<bool>` per recording, Info `CommitTree: tree '<id>' kept the player's settings (seal, hide, ghost, loop, groups) on N replaced committed recording(s)`. The split side of RULE 1 (both halves of an optimizer split) is a separate package. Design `docs/parsek-rewind-to-separation-design.md` section 2 (slot state paragraph).

**Tests:** `TreeCommitPlayerFieldsTests` (a Re-Fly union keeps another slot's seal and settings while the re-flown origin keeps the incoming merge state; a strict replace keeps them; the `UnionRecordingsInto` journal path keeps them; the pure carry, its count and list copy; the marker id set). The behaviour cells were red before the fix.

## REFLY-GHOST-ONLY-AUTOCOMMIT-NO-SUPERSEDE: a ghost-only auto-commit outside flight during a Re-Fly writes no supersede rows [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding L13), by code reading. NOT A BUG (by design), decided 2026-11-20 from the code and `docs/dev/done/plans/silent-full-fidelity-autocommit.md` section 4.2; comment added at the site, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`]

`ParsekScenario.AutoCommitPendingTreeOutsideFlight` routes an active Re-Fly to the ghost-only commit (`ClassifyAutoCommitFidelity` reason `re-fly-active`) on purpose: a full commit would run `MergeDialog.TryCommitReFlySupersede`, the irreversible supersede the plan forbids doing without the player's click. The ghost-only commit leaves the attempt `NotCommitted` (`ApplyRewindProvisionalMergeStates` only touches `Immutable` recordings). While the session marker validates, the session and its Discard stay alive; once it does not, `LoadTimeSweep` ends the session and discards the attempt as a zombie, keeping the old flight. That is the dialog-less equivalent of Discard, which is the safe default the plan chose. Nothing to fix; the comment at the ghost-only branch now says so.

## ~~MERGE-DUPLICATE-SKIP-TOASTS-MERGED~~: a duplicate-commit skip dropped the pending flight while toasting "Merged" [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding M13), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; medium (a merge reported that never happened). The commit side of owner RULE 3 ("my live flight wins") is LIVE-FLOWN-TREE-RECUT-DROPS-NEW-LEG: a copy that carries new flight is unioned in, not skipped; this entry only makes the skip of a true duplicate honest. Approach changed after review the same day: the skipped tree is dropped, not kept pending]

**Cause:** `TreeCommitService.CommitTreeCore` returns early when a different tree object with the same id is committed and the incoming tree is not a richer topology (`ShouldReplaceCommittedTree`), but `CommitPendingTree` still emptied the pending slot and `MergeDialog.MergeCommit` went on to notify the ledger, run the Re-Fly supersede and toast "Merged".

**Fix:** `CommitTree` / `CommitPendingTree` return whether the tree reached the timeline (a reference-equal tree already committed counts as committed). A skipped tree is dropped from the pending slot as before (Warn `CommitPendingTree: tree id=... was skipped as a duplicate of the committed tree - nothing committed, pending slot cleared`): kept pending, every route would skip it again (the dialog, `AutoCommitPendingTreeOutsideFlight`, `SafetyNetAutoCommitPending` on every OnSave), the dialog would come back on each flight entry with a Merge that does nothing, and `RewindLauncher` would refuse Rewind and Fast-forward ("Merge or discard pending tree first") with nothing to discard it. `MergeCommit` stops before the ledger notify, the Re-Fly supersede and the toasts (Warn `... commit skipped as a duplicate of the committed tree; nothing merged, pending tree dropped, no success toast`); when the player clicked Merge it shows one plain message, "Nothing new to merge: this flight is already in the timeline", and a silent auto-commit shows none. The outside-flight seam `CommitPendingTreeAsApplied` returns false so the safety net and the ghost-only auto-commit skip their notify and toast (a call with no pending tree still marks the tree applied, as before).

**Tests:** `MergeDialogResourcesAppliedTests.MergeCommit_DuplicateSkip_NoMergedToast_PendingDropped_RewindNotHeld` (a committed tree plus an unchanged pending clone, through the dialog click and a silent call: slot cleared, no "Merged", the plain message only on the click) and `ScenarioAutoCommitResourcesAppliedTests.AutoCommit_DuplicateSkip_ReturnsFalse_NothingMarked_PendingDropped`, both red on the keep-pending version; the source gate `CommitPendingTreeAsApplied_CommitsBeforeMarkingApplied` follows the new `bool` signature.

## ~~REFLY-INTERRUPTED-MERGE-TOASTS-MERGED~~: an interrupted Re-Fly merge toasted "Merged" and offered the route prompt [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (part of finding H4), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; low (a wrong message)]

**Cause:** `MergeDialog.MergeCommit` ran its success tail (route prompt, "Merged - N vessel(s) ..." toast) whatever `TryCommitReFlySupersede` returned, so an `Interrupted` result showed "Merge interrupted - will finish on next load" and then "Merged".

**Fix:** on `Interrupted` the commit still fires `OnTreeCommitted` (the tree is committed; ghost chains must re-evaluate) but skips the route prompt and the success toast. Warn `User chose: Tree Merge (...) - Re-Fly supersede interrupted; route prompt and the merged toast suppressed`.

**Tests:** `MergeDialogResourcesAppliedTests.MergeCommit_InterruptedReFlyPath_NoMergedToast_CommittedListenersStillRun` (red under a mutation that drops the early return).

## ~~REFLY-MERGE-FINISHER-NEVER-CONVERGES~~: a Re-Fly merge that fails the same way every time blocked every later load of the save [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding H4), by code reading; ruled by the owner 2026-11-18 (RULE 4). FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; high (the load aborts before the sweep, the reaper and the file collector; the journal never clears and Discard stays refused)]

**Cause:** `RecordingTreeSplitter` rolls back and rethrows, `MergeJournalOrchestrator.RunFinisher` rethrew, and `ParsekScenario.OnLoad` rethrows, so a merge step that throws deterministically (bad split data, or `SupersedeCommit.ClassifyMergeStateOrThrow` when an Orbiting provisional's slot never resolves) threw on every load and the journal never cleared.

**Fix (RULE 4, "Both, in that order"):** `RunFinisher` never throws. Each attempt starts from the state the load read (`RestoreFinisherEntryState` puts back the supersede rows, tombstones, the marker and its supersede target, the phase and the provisional's merge fields after a failed attempt; the split is transactional itself). Stage 1 is the ordinary retry. When it fails before Finalize, stage 2 runs in the same load: the whole old recording is hidden instead of cut (the split is skipped; a split an earlier attempt completed gets its closure root pointed back at HEAD, `RecordingTreeSplitter.TryResolveHeadOfCompletedSplit`), re-running from `TreeMerge`. When that fails too, the merge is given up: the rows and tombstones this merge wrote are removed (`RemoveSessionRows`: rows naming the provisional created at or after the journal start, so an older merge's rows survive), the journal is cleared and the marker kept, so Discard is unlocked and the old flight plays as it was (the attempt then goes the way every dropped attempt goes: the player's Discard purges it and its session rewind points, or the sweep's nested-session cleanup does once the marker no longer validates); the ledger is recalculated at once (`Give-up recalc ... reason=merge-journal-finisher-gave-up`), because the load's own recalc ran before the finisher with the removed tombstones still in place. A failure after Finalize is a completed merge (the merge state is already final): the session's rewind points are promoted and reaped as the Durable1Done step does (`TagRpsForReap` + the reaper, so the quicksaves of slots the merge left open are not left session-provisional for the sweep to delete), then the marker and the journal are cleared and the ledger recalculated (`reason=merge-journal-finisher-gave-up-after-finalize`). The escalation state is local to the one `RunFinisher` call (never on `MergeJournal`, never saved): the journal is cleared in the load that started it. A game killed between stage 1 and stage 2 leaves the journal as the load read it (the finisher writes nothing to disk), so the next load starts at stage 1 again, one more retry before the fallback. Logs `[MergeJournal] Finisher stage=<retry|whole-recording-fallback>`, `Finisher escalating`, `Finisher gave up ... Discard unlocked` / `... session rewind points promoted like a completed merge`, one screen message "Re-Fly merge could not be finished - the old flight is kept". `MergeDialog.MergeDiscard`'s doc no longer says the journal finisher rolls back. Design `docs/parsek-rewind-to-separation-design.md` section 6.12.

**Tests:** `MergeJournalFinisherFallbackTests` (a deterministic Finalize failure gives up with the old flight kept and older rows untouched; a split failing every time hides the whole old recording; the fallback after a completed split supersedes HEAD too; the escalation fields are not saved; `RemoveSessionRows`). The two convergence cells red under a mutation that restores the rethrow. Review follow-up (same day): the give-up cell now also pins the recalc, and `Finisher_GivesUpAfterFinalize_KeepsTheSessionRewindPointsLikeACompletedMerge` pins the rewind point promotion; both red before the follow-up.

## ~~CUT-INSIDE-TIME-JUMP-OR-TELEPORT~~: optimizer splits and Re-Fly cuts never land inside a cheat teleport or time jump (owner ruling Q18) [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review, ruled by the owner 2026-11-18 ("move the cut to the nearest point outside it"). FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane]

**Cause:** a cut inside a stretch where the vessel did not move continuously (a time jump, or a teleport between the last sample and the boundary seam the recorder writes after it) interpolates between two unrelated states: `RecordingOptimizer.SplitAtUT` synthesizes a boundary point there, and an optimizer split there gives each half a bound inside the jump.

**Fix:** `RecordingDiscontinuities` (pure) collects the windows from `TimeJump` segment events (`preUT` / `postUT`) and from `isBoundarySeam` sections (last sample before the seam to the seam), and moves a cut out of them. Re-Fly: `RecordingTreeSplitter.ResolveDiscontinuitySafeCutUT` cuts at the window's start, the last recorded point before it, so HEAD still ends at or before the rewind (the chain-head carve-out reads `HEAD.EndUT <= rewindUT`); the windows are read over the vessel's chain neighbours so a re-entry after the split resolves the same cut, and the span check, the existing-tip checks, the cut and the post-split retags all use it. Info `[Splitter] Re-Fly cut moved out of <kind>[a,b]: ... rewindUT=<ut> cutUT=<ut>`. Optimizer: `RecordingOptimizer.TryPlaceSplitOutsideDiscontinuity` moves a split whose boundary lies inside a window to the section boundary at its nearer edge (the other edge next), and refuses the split when no usable boundary sits there; Verbose `Split moved out of ...` / `Split refused: ... lies inside ...`, counted as `discontinuityKept=` on the split summary. A same-body cheat teleport's own boundary is a seam the optimizer never splits; a cross-body cheat teleport writes no marker, so it is not detected.

**Tests:** `RecordingDiscontinuitiesTests` (collection, edge choice, the producer's details format, optimizer move / refuse / stay) and `RecordingTreeSplitterTests.SplitOriginAtRewindUT_RewindInsideATimeJump_CutsAtTheJumpStart_AndReentryIsIdempotent`; the splitter and optimizer cells red under mutations that skip the move.

## ~~REFLY-CUT-ORPHANS-RELATIVE-ANCHORS~~: Relative-frame recordings anchored to a Re-Fly-cut origin after the rewind point anchored to HEAD, which ends at the rewind [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding L12), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; low (a ghost retires early for lack of an anchor)]

**Cause:** `RecordingTreeSplitter` keeps the origin's id on HEAD (which now ends at the cut) and gives TIP a fresh id. It rewrote `TrackSection.anchorRecordingId` only on TIP's own sections and on reparented debris, so any other recording with a Relative section anchored to the origin after the cut resolved against HEAD, which no longer covers that time.

**Fix:** step 2.8c, `RecordingTreeSplitter.RewriteOtherRecordingAnchorsToTip`: every other committed recording's Relative section anchored to the origin that starts at or after the cut points at TIP (on the split's rollback ledger, `FilesDirty` set). A section straddling the cut cannot be cut there and stays on HEAD, counted. The session's own attempt recordings (the provisional and every recording stamped with the session) are left alone. Verbose `Step8: anchor rewrites - ... otherSections=<n> otherStraddlersKeptOnHead=<n>`.

A split that throws undoes these re-points with the rest of its rollback ledger. A split that completed is not undone by a later RULE 4 give-up, so when HEAD and TIP are joined again (the given-up merge left no supersede row, and the session ends), the re-pointed sections would name TIP's vanished id: the optimizer's merge pass now moves every other recording's reference to an absorbed recording onto the merge target (`CommittedListOptimizer.RepointAnchorsAfterOptimizationMerge`: Relative section anchors and `ParentAnchorRecordingId`; Info `Optimization: anchors re-pointed <absorbed> -> <target> (sections=N parentAnchors=N)`), which also covers any other optimizer merge of a recording something anchors to.

**Tests:** `RecordingTreeSplitterTests.SplitOriginAtRewindUT_OtherRecordingsRelativeSectionsAfterTheCut_FollowTip` (red under a mutation that skips the walk); `OptimizerMergeAnchorRetagTests.OptimizerMerge_RepointsOtherRecordingsAnchorsFromTheAbsorbedIdToTheTarget` (red before the merge-pass re-point).

## ~~REFLY-MERGE-OPTIMIZER-PASS-AFTER-MERGE~~: the optimizer pass right after a Re-Fly merge (owner ruling Q6) [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review, ruled by the owner 2026-11-18 ("Yes, right after merge"). FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane]

**Cause:** the merge dialog's optimizer pass runs before the supersede step while the Re-Fly marker is live, and `CommittedListOptimizer.RunOptimizationSplitPass` defers the active provisional while a marker is live, so the new attempt stayed one recording until the next commit or cold load.

**Fix:** `MergeJournalOrchestrator.RunPostMergeOptimizationPass` runs one `CommittedListOptimizer.RunOptimizationPass` as soon as the journal and the marker are cleared: on the live merge before Durable Save #3 (so that save holds the split), and at the end of the load-time finisher. It never runs while a journal or a marker is live, and a throw is logged and the merge stands. Info `[MergeJournal] Post-merge optimization pass ran sess=<sid> route=<merge|finisher>`.

**Tests:** `MergeJournalPostMergeOptimizationTests` (live merge, finisher, a throwing pass); all red under a mutation that skips the pass. `MergeJournalOrchestratorTests.CrashAtBegin_Finisher_KeepsOptimizerSplitTailOfTheFork` gives its optimizer-split tail a different phase from its head, the shape a real split leaves (with one phase the new pass rightly joins them).

**In-game fixtures (2026-11-23, branch `lane-repins2-1023`):** R7c `2026-11-23_1529` red on four `[ERROR][RecordingStore] SaveRecordingFiles failed ... Non-null string expected in binary string table` lines (`FlushDirtyFiles: saved 0, failed 2`, twice). The two cells that author their own recordings and drive the real `RunMerge` (`IncompleteBallisticRuntimeTests.ReFlyFromSpannedRecording...`, `ReFlyRecoveryBundleRuntimeTest`) built every point and section frame with no `bodyName`; until this pass nothing flushed HEAD and TIP, now it does. Their points carry the body, their teardown reaps the sidecars the pass writes (`InGameTestSidecarReaper`; the DiskOnly batch restores persistent.sfs only, and R7c counts the `.prec` files), and `MergeFixtureSidecarFlushTests` writes both fixtures' HEAD, TIP and fork through the production writer and runs them through the real `RunMerge` and pass. No other in-game cell reaches a flush with such a point (the remaining body-less ones, `FindWaypointIndexBrackets` and `WatchAutoFollowFollowsSupersedeFork`, never save), and no production path can author one: every recorder, densifier, descent, split, trim and merge producer names the body, the text reader defaults it and the binary reader refuses a file without it.

## ~~REFLY-FALLBACK-SEALS-SUBORBITAL~~: the slot-less merge fallback sealed a sub-orbital Re-Fly that the normal path keeps open [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding M11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; low (reached only when the slot lookup fails)]

**Cause:** when `SupersedeCommit` cannot resolve the Re-Fly's slot it falls back to `TerminalKindClassifier` and flipped every outcome but a crash to `Immutable`. The tip's `MergeState` is the slot's open / closed bit (design section 6.24), and the slot-aware path keeps a `SubOrbital` ending open (`CommittedProvisional`, section 4.9: a sub-orbital arc is still in flight), so the fallback sealed a slot the main path leaves open. `Orbiting` never reaches the fallback (`RequiresSlotAwareMergeClassification` refuses to fall back for it).

**Fix:** `SupersedeCommit.FallbackMergeStateForTerminal`: `Destroyed` and `SubOrbital` keep the slot open (`CommittedProvisional`); every other terminal, and a recording with no terminal, commits `Immutable`.

**Tests:** `SupersedeCommitTests.FallbackMergeStateForTerminal_AgreesWithTheSlotAwareVerdict` (theory); `SubOrbitalStableLeaf_SlotLookupFailure_DoesNotThrow_FallsBackToInFlight` now expects `CommittedProvisional` (its old `Immutable` pinned the bug). Red under a mutation that restores the old mapping.

## ~~REFLY-HEAD-TIP-REGLUED-BEFORE-MERGE-ROWS~~: the optimizer could join a Re-Fly merge's HEAD and TIP back together before the merge finished [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding M8), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; medium (the old flight stays whole beside the new attempt: a duplicate ghost and untombstoned ledger rows)]

**Cause:** the cold `ParsekScenario.OnLoad` runs the committed-list optimizer (phase `optimization`) before the merge journal finisher (phase `merge-journal`). Between the merge's `split` save and Durable Save #1 the supersede rows that keep `CanAutoMerge` off HEAD + TIP do not exist yet, so a HEAD and TIP with no ghosting-trigger event were offered as a merge candidate and glued back.

**Fix:** `CanAutoMerge` refuses a pair naming a recording a live Re-Fly session names (the ids come from `CommittedListOptimizer.CollectLiveReFlyMergeHeldIds`, which the merge pass hands to `FindMergeCandidates` / `CanAutoMerge`: the Recording-module optimizer must not name Rewind types, a backward layer pair the architecture ratchet holds): the marker's supersede target (TIP once the split ran) and its origin (HEAD), and while a merge journal is active also the provisional. The marker and journal load in the OnLoad prologue, before the optimizer. Without a journal the provisional stays mergeable (a live commit pass may merge the attempt and `MergeDialog.ResolveOptimizedRecordingSurvivor` follows it), as does an in-place continuation whose provisional is the origin. Verbose `CanAutoMerge: rejecting merge of '<a>' + '<b>' - <marker supersede target|marker origin|merge journal provisional> sess=... journal=... (Re-Fly merge not finished)`.

**Tests:** `RecordingOptimizerTests.CanAutoMerge_JournalActive_RejectsHeadPlusTipBeforeTheRowsExist` (red under a mutation that disables the check).

## ~~OPTIMIZER-MERGE-INTO-DESTROYED-DELETES-RECORDING~~: the optimizer deleted a recording it "merged" into a destroyed one [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (finding M9), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp2-refly-merge`; xUnit + mutation; no lane; low reachability, high impact (a recording, its ledger tags and its sidecars deleted)]

**Cause:** `RecordingOptimizer.MergeInto` skips a merge into a target with `VesselDestroyed` (a destroyed recording is sealed at its terminal UT) but returned the absorbed id as if it had merged, so `CommittedListOptimizer.RunOptimizationMergePass` retagged the absorbed recording's ledger rows, removed it from the committed list and deleted its sidecars. Reachable because a split moved the terminal state onto the second half but left `VesselDestroyed` on the first, so a split crashed flight had a head reading destroyed with no terminal, and `CanAutoMerge` offered it as a merge target.

**Fix:** `MergeInto` returns null on that skip (Warn `MergeInto: refused - target is already destroyed ... nothing merged, nothing removed`) and the merge pass stops without touching either recording (Warn `Optimization: merge of ... refused - nothing removed`); `CanAutoMerge` refuses a destroyed target up front; the split moves `VesselDestroyed` with the terminal onto the second half (Verbose `Split: VesselDestroyed moved with the terminal onto the second half`).

**Tests:** `RecordingOptimizerSplitAtUTTests.SplitAtUT_CrashedFlight_VesselDestroyedMovesWithTheTerminal`, `MergeInto_DestroyedTarget_RefusesAndCanAutoMergeRefusesUpFront`; `IdentityLossClassifierTests.RecordingOptimizer_MergeInto_SkipsDestroyedTarget` now expects null (its old expectation pinned the bug). All three red under a mutation that restores the old code.

## ~~SPAWN-ESCAPE-TRAJECTORY-NEVER-SPAWNS~~: a probe left on an escape trajectory ended SubOrbital and never became real [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (design question 4), owner ruling Q10 "spawn on its path". FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp7-spawn-ends`; xUnit (`EscapeTrajectorySpawnTests`); no lane flies it yet; medium (a vessel the player left flying vanished at the end of its replay)]

What the player saw: commit a flight with a probe on its way out of Kerbin (or the Mun), rewind,
and watch the replay end: the probe's ghost disappears and no vessel is left on the path.

Cause. KSP reports such a vessel ESCAPING (`Vessel.updateSituation`, decompiled 1.12.5: outside
the atmosphere, `eccentricity >= 1` or `ApR >= sphereOfInfluence`, whatever the periapsis), and
`RecordingTree.DetermineTerminalState` folds ESCAPING into `TerminalState.SubOrbital`, which
`GhostPlaybackLogic.IsSpawnableTerminal` never admits (the #45 rule written for FLYING). The
terminal orbit was captured (`ParsekFlight.CaptureTerminalOrbit` covers ESCAPING), but
`VesselSpawner.HasRecordedTerminalOrbit` and the orbit seeds required `semiMajorAxis > 0`, so a
hyperbolic orbit could not have been spawned anyway, and nothing carried an orbit across a sphere
of influence change.

Why no new `TerminalState` member (decided from the code). A dedicated `Escaping` member would be
the cleaner label, but about 25 consumers switch on the terminal state, and the Re-Fly ones in
`Rewind/` (`UnfinishedFlightClassifier`: an Orbiting / SubOrbital non-focus slot is an Unfinished
Flight; `ReFlyAutoSealPreview`: Orbiting seals the focus slot) would silently change meaning for
escaping vessels; `Orbiting` is wrong too (it means a stable bound orbit to the Re-Fly seal, the
timeline "Ends orbiting X" text and route endpoints). A new member also could not reach recordings
already committed. So the terminal state stays `SubOrbital` (in flight, unconcluded, labelled
"Sub-orbital" as before) and only the spawn changes.

Fix. `Recording.IsEscapeTrajectoryTerminal` / `EscapeTrajectoryTerminal.IsEscapeTerminal`: a
`SubOrbital` terminal with a propagatable recorded terminal orbit and escape evidence (an open
conic, or the snapshot's ESCAPING situation for a closed conic whose apoapsis is beyond the sphere)
is admitted by `TryRejectSpawnForTerminalAndSituation` and deferred to the flight scene at the Space
Center like an Orbiting one. It takes the orbit spawn route (`ShouldUseRecordedTerminalOrbitSpawnState`,
`ShouldRouteThroughSpawnAtPosition`), seeded from the terminal orbit itself and carried from its
epoch to the spawn UT by `EscapeTrajectoryTerminal.ResolveAtUT` (the scene-exit finalizer's
two-body `BallisticExtrapolator` over the live bodies: sphere-of-influence exits and encounters);
`VesselSpawner.ResolveEscapeSpawnBody` gives the end-of-recording, chain-tip and Ready-reference
spawns the body the vessel is in at the spawn UT. A path that ends in an atmosphere or on a surface
before the spawn UT, or cannot be followed, is refused (`Cannot spawn terminal orbit safely ...
terminal-orbit-resolution-failed`, with the `escape path refused` line naming the reason). The
terminal-orbit safety check runs on the spawn-UT orbit; for a conic that leaves the sphere and is
past periapsis the periapsis it judges is the current altitude (`ResolveEscapeEffectivePeriapsisAltitude`),
so a direct-ascent escape whose periapsis is inside the planet spawns, and the same conic flown
inbound is refused. `ComputeSpawnMeanAnomaly` propagates a hyperbolic mean anomaly without wrapping.
A spawned escape vessel that dies is abandoned like a terminal-orbit vessel (BUG-C path). Log lines:
`Escape-trajectory terminal admitted for spawn`, `Escape spawn body resolved through patched conics`,
`escape terminal orbit for rec=...`, `Escape spawn safety: ... judgedPeriapsis=`.

Tests: `EscapeTrajectorySpawnTests` (evidence truth table, the spawn decision and KSC deferral
(red on the old code), the spawn routes, the hyperbolic mean anomaly, the effective periapsis and
the safety verdicts, `ResolveAtUT` in-sphere / after the sphere exit / diving into the atmosphere /
unknown body).

Review follow-ups (2026-11-20, same branch):
- Chain tips. A chain tip that spawns on its recorded terminal orbit (Orbiting, or an escape)
  and whose orbit cannot be resolved at the spawn UT fell back to the snapshot / last trajectory
  point with no orbit override, so a refused escape path would have materialized mid-coast
  (#45). Both chain-tip spawns (`VesselGhoster.SpawnAtChainTip`, `TrySpawnBlockedChain`) now
  refuse through `StopChainTipForUnresolvedTerminalOrbit`, which stamps the end-of-recording
  path's `terminal-orbit-resolution-failed` CannotSpawnSafely and releases the collision block
  (`Chain tip spawn refused: recorded terminal orbit unresolved`). This also changes an Orbiting
  tip whose orbit cannot be built: refused like the end-of-recording spawn, not placed at its
  last point. To keep that refusal from catching good tips, the chain-tip, blocked-tip ghost and
  Ready-reference spawns now pick the body as the end-of-recording spawn does
  (`VesselSpawner.ResolveSpawnBodyName` / `ResolveSpawnBody`): an orbit-route spawn reads the
  recording's preferred endpoint body before its last trajectory point, which can sit in another
  sphere (a burn at the Mun, then a rails coast out to a Kerbin orbit adds no point).

- Consumers. `GhostPlaybackLogic.HasSpawnableTerminal(Recording)` (a spawnable terminal or an
  escape) is now the one "does this end in a vessel" test for the breakup-continuous effective
  leaf (`TryRejectSpawnForTreeShape`, `IsFinalSpawnSegment`, `TimelineBuilder.IsBreakupContinuousSpawnLeaf`),
  the stable-leaf snapshot refreshes (`ParsekFlight.Finalization`, `ShouldRefreshActiveEffectiveLeafSnapshot`),
  the ghost CommNet continuation hold and the chain-tip route cargo scan; the lazy snapshot
  re-hydration also reads a SubOrbital with a propagatable terminal orbit
  (`Recording.IsEscapeTrajectoryTerminalCandidate`, since the closed-conic evidence is in the
  snapshot); the auto-merge scene-exit release keeps an escape's snapshot
  (`ShouldKeepVesselSnapshotForSpawnAtEnd`). Left Orbiting-only, noted: the terminal map-presence
  retention (`ParsekPlaybackPolicy.ShouldRetainMapPresenceForTerminalRealSpawn`, whose map orbit
  code assumes a closed conic in one sphere) and the optimizer's tail trim (`RecordingOptimizer`,
  owned by another package; it refuses to trim a non-spawnable terminal, the safe side).

- Patch-start epoch. A terminal orbit captured on rails carries the epoch of its patch start,
  the last sphere-of-influence crossing, where the state sits on the boundary and the
  extrapolator's immediate exit / entry tests are numerical noise (a Moon flyby could be carried
  on the parent conic, or an escape bounced to the transition cap). `ResolveAtUT` now starts at the
  recording's end UT when that is later than the epoch, and a start still at the epoch does not
  take an immediate crossing of the boundary it sits on (`Extrapolate`'s new initial
  suppressions, `EscapeTrajectoryTerminal.ResolveBoundarySuppressions`).

Residue: (a) the label still reads Sub-orbital for an escaping vessel; (b) live-proven by no lane
(recommended: a probe committed on a Kerbin escape, rewound, the end spawn read in flight before and
after the sphere exit); (c) the extrapolator samples encounters at 3600 s, so a very short moon pass
between the end and a much later spawn UT can be missed (the scene-exit finalizer shares the limit).

## ~~SPAWN-RESTING-ON-ROCK~~: a vessel that ends sitting on an asteroid or comet spawned on its own orbit, not on the rock [FILED 2026-11-18 by the recording split / trim / merge review (design question 5), owner ruling Q11 "on the rock". FIXED 2026-11-21 by option B (owner ruling 2026-11-21, "Yes, both"), branch `rsr-wp9-orbit-spawn-clear`; xUnit `OrbitSpawnClearanceTests`; in-game `OrbitSpawnClearance`; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-22 by `OSC-1-orbit-spawn-clearance-lko` run `2026-11-22_1141` (4 of 4); low-medium (a lander parked on a rock reappeared inside it, beside it, or blocked)]

Cause. "Landed on" a rock is not a KSP state: `Part.LandedCollisionChecks` (decompiled) sets
`GroundContact` / `Vessel.Landed` only for terrain colliders, so a vessel resting on a rock ends
ORBITING (or SUB_ORBITAL / ESCAPING) and spawns from its own terminal orbit. The ordinary overlap
check skips SpaceObject vessels (`SpawnCollisionDetector.ClassifyLoadedVesselHit`), so a loaded rock
never blocked the spawn, and an unloaded one has no colliders: the lander could appear inside the
rock. Klaw-attached is different and was already right: a grab couples the rock part into the
grabbing vessel, which records and spawns as one vessel with the rock (owner rulings 2026-11-15,
ROCK-SPAWN-BOUNDS-TOO-SMALL). The Klaw is the supported way to stay attached to a rock.

Fix (ruling: no new save data, no recording change, every use logged). Every recorded-terminal-
orbit spawn site with a collision check (end-of-recording, both chain-tip sites) first looks for a
rock at the propagated spawn point: a loaded part with `ModuleAsteroid` / `ModuleComet` (or a rock
part name) whose colliders the spawn box reaches, or an unloaded SpaceObject whose size-class
sphere (`RockHalfExtentForClass`, from the saved `prefabBaseURL` or `DISCOVERY size`) is that close
(`SpawnCollisionDetector.TryFindRockBlocker`). Found: the spawn is pushed straight out from the
rock's centre in 0.5 m steps until its bounds clear the rock's colliders by 1 m (unloaded: the
size-class radius plus the bounds radius plus 1 m), and takes the rock's orbital velocity through a
co-moving orbit built at the spawn UT (`ResolveRockPushOut`, `OrbitSpawnClearance.TryBuildCoMovingOrbit`),
so it moves with the rock and drifts slowly like stock. The terminal-orbit spawn safety check is re-run
on that orbit. A pushed spot another loaded vessel blocks takes the blocked retry; that final
check leaves out the rock part itself, since a rock held by another vessel's Klaw is a part of that
Ship / Probe vessel and would otherwise block every push-out at the 5 m padding (the holding
vessel's other parts still block). Logged:
`[SpawnCollision] Rock push-out: ...` and `Orbit spawn clearance: ... outcome=RockPushedOut`. Landed
spawns are unchanged (the ordinary check still skips rocks). Not done (option A, not ordered): no
rock identity or relative pose is recorded, so a rock that drifted after a rewind is not followed;
the spawn reacts only to a rock that is at the spawn point.

Tests: xUnit `OrbitSpawnClearanceTests` (push-out search, direction, clearance distance, wiring of
the rock check before the phase search); in-game `OrbitSpawnClearance` cell
`OrbitSpawnInsideARock_IsPushedOutAndCoMovesWithTheRock` (spawns a PotatoRoid, isolated only).
Residue: no lane flies it (recommended: a lander resting on a loaded asteroid, rewound, end spawn in
flight beside the rock).

## ~~SPAWN-ORBITAL-WALKBACK-NOT-WHERE-IT-SPAWNS~~: the end-spawn collision walkback for an orbit spawn tested positions the vessel is not placed at [FILED 2026-11-20 from the WP7 review (asteroid / comet second opinion), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-21 by option (b) (owner ruling 2026-11-21, "Yes, both"), branch `rsr-wp9-orbit-spawn-clear`; EX-2 re-flown green on the widened preset `2026-11-22_1139`; xUnit `OrbitSpawnClearanceTests`; in-game `OrbitSpawnClearance`; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-22 by `OSC-1-orbit-spawn-clearance-lko` run `2026-11-22_1141` (4 of 4); low-medium (an orbit spawn blocked by a loaded vessel could still appear inside it, or be abandoned)]

Cause. When an end-of-recording orbit spawn (an Orbiting terminal with a recorded terminal orbit,
or an escape path) overlapped a loaded vessel, `VesselSpawner.CheckSpawnCollisions` walked back
along the recorded trajectory, reading each body-fixed point at the spawn UT (so a candidate turned
with the planet), and the spawn then went through `SpawnAtPosition` with the orbit override, which
places a non-landed ProtoVessel by its ORBIT node: a "cleared" walk still spawned inside the
blocker, and an exhausted walk abandoned a spawn whose blocker could have moved. The chain-tip
walkback (`VesselGhoster.TryWalkbackSpawn`) had the same shape and spawned an orbital tip at an old
body-fixed point with a reseeded orbit.

Fix. An orbit-route spawn that overlaps a loaded vessel moves a little ahead or behind along its OWN
orbit: same elements, the spawn epoch's mean anomaly shifted by the time the along-track offset
takes (`OrbitSpawnClearance.TryBuildPhaseShiftedOrbit`). The bounded search tries +4, -4, +6, -6 m
... growing by 1.5 per pair to 1000 m (30 candidates) and takes the first whose bounds overlap no
loaded vessel and no rock (`SpawnCollisionDetector.SearchClearOrbitPhase`); the terminal-orbit spawn
safety check is re-run on the shifted orbit. No clear spot within 1000 m takes today's blocked
outcome for a spawn that cannot walk back: retry next frame, abandon after 150 blocked frames
(`VesselSpawner.BlockOrbitRouteSpawn`); a chain tip stays blocked and retries every second at its
orbit propagated to that second (`TrySpawnBlockedOrbitChainTip`, no ghost-extender position, no
walkback). Never spawned overlapping. The duplicate-blocker recovery (#112) still runs first.
Landed, splashed, EVA-endpoint and breakup spawns keep the walkback. The Space Center and Tracking
Station spawns have no collision check (nothing is loaded there) and are unchanged. Logged:
`CheckSpawnCollisions: orbit phase shift moved the spawn of #N ...`, `Orbit spawn clearance: ...`,
`Orbit phase search: ...`, `Chain tip orbit spawn moved: ...`.

Tests: xUnit `OrbitSpawnClearanceTests` (schedule, mean-anomaly shift and wrap, searches, the
blocked retry and abandon, wiring gates at all three sites, red on the old sources); in-game
`OrbitSpawnClearance` cell `OrbitSpawnOnTheActiveVessel_MovesAlongItsOwnOrbitToAClearSpot`.
Residue: no lane flies it (recommended: an orbit spawn next to a parked station).
`EX-2-single-point-held-ghost` reached its D18 hold through this path (its `single-point-hold`
orbit spawn blocked by the co-orbiting probe): the phase search would now clear at about 230 m and
spawn it, so EX-2 takes its own preset `single-point-hold-wide` (the same shape with the outriggers at
1300 m instead of 150 m, so every phase candidate still covers the probe) and the lane is re-pinned to the orbit route's no-clear-spot block, with the same hold,
retries and timeout; re-flight owed. The non-orbit single-point branch EX-2 used to read is now the
in-game cell `SinglePointSpawnWithNoTerminalOrbit_KeepsTheSinglePointRetry` (a non-orbit single point
cannot be held in LKO, and no committed fixture has a ground host outside the KSC circles).
`SPW-11-rsc-warp-orbital-held-target` keeps `single-point-hold` and its 150 m box (live-proven
2026-11-20 with the target spawned; the phase search still clears and spawns there).
`SPW-5-physics-warp-end-spawn-near-active` would read a phase shift if its probe ever blocked, which
its LeafPlacement verdict may report as `phase`.

## ~~DEBRIS-LIFETIME-LOST-ON-PROMOTION~~: a debris piece the player switched to lost its 60 s limit [FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp4-background-debris`; xUnit `DebrisLifetimeTests`; medium (a promoted booster recorded until it crashed; GS-11 measured it)]

Cause: the debris time limit lived only in `BackgroundRecorder.debrisTTLExpiry`. A promotion to the
active recorder cancels that entry (D5-PROMOTED-DEBRIS-TTL-NOT-CANCELLED: the background recorder no
longer owns the piece), and the active recorder had no limit, so the booster recorded to impact
(GS-11 `points=271 terminal=Destroyed`). Switching away again did not re-arm it, a Fly / Switch-To
continuation segment of the piece recorded as a plain, non-debris segment with no limit, and a
post-switch watch armed while the piece was tracked started a fresh recording once its limit ended
it (draft review question 7). Owner ruling Q13 (2026-11-18): "Always the 60 s limit".

Fix: the limit is read from the tree by the pure `BackgroundRecorder.TryResolveDebrisExpiryUT` (separation
branch point UT + 60 s, walking up through `VesselSwitchContinuation` points). The active recorder
honours it: `ParsekFlight.CheckActiveDebrisLifetime` (pure gate `EvaluateActiveDebrisLifetimeEnd`,
deferred while a split, an unprocessed split check, dock merge, restore or hand-off is in progress)
hands the piece back to the background recorder the way a vessel switch does, flushing the coalescer
window and unprocessed decouple captures first (`FlushPendingSplits`) and ends it there
(`BackgroundRecorder.EndDebrisRecordingForLifetime`, a background time-limit end); the vessel stays
focused, unrecorded. `OnVesselBackgrounded` re-arms the same limit for a debris piece with none
(`Debris lifetime re-armed from the tree`, Info for a hand-back, Verbose for a recording created this
frame; a background split child sets its own deadline before the hand-off). `SwitchSegmentBuilder.InheritDebrisIdentityFromParent`
keeps `IsDebris`, `ParentAnchorRecordingId` and `Generation` on a continuation of a debris piece whose limit still
runs (a piece past its limit, from an older flight, continues as a plain segment, as before).
`CheckDebrisTTL` returns the pids it ended and the flight host disarms a post-switch watch armed on
one (`reason=debris-recording-ended`). Promotion already kept `IsDebris` and
`ParentAnchorRecordingId` (same `Recording` object); only the limit was lost.

Tests: `DebrisLifetimeTests` (lifetime resolution, the active gate, the hand-back re-arm and end, the
continuation inheritance, `CheckDebrisTTL`'s ended pids). Red before the fix, by disabling the two
new call sites: `HandBackToBackground_RearmsTheSeparationLifetime`,
`SwitchContinuation_OfLiveDebris_StaysDebris`; the active gate and resolver are new code. The live
hand-back (`TransitionToBackground` -> flush -> `OnVesselBackgrounded` -> end) is not headless-testable;
lane GS-11 flies it (expected to change: the promoted booster now ends at its limit, not at impact).

## ~~EVA-MARKS-SHIP-AS-SPINOFF-GENERATION~~: an EVA gave the ship the spinoff generation and the kerbal the ship's [FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp4-background-debris`; xUnit `BackgroundSplitTests`; low (no player-visible effect left after BG-BREAKUP-GENERATION-CAP)]

Cause: `ParsekFlight.BuildSplitBranchData` gives the ACTIVE child the parent's generation and the
background child one more. On an EVA KSP hands focus to the kerbal, so the kerbal kept the
generation and the ship was marked as the spinoff; with the old cascade cap a landed ship that
tipped over after an EVA recorded no breakup (draft review question 9).

Fix: on an EVA branch whose kerbal is the active child, the ship (background child) keeps the
parent's generation and the kerbal gets one more, as when the kerbal is the background child.
BG-BREAKUP-GENERATION-CAP already lets the ship record its breakups (its recording is not debris),
so this corrects the stored generation only. Merge note: a five-line edit inside the EVA block of
`BuildSplitBranchData` in `ParsekFlight.SplitBranching.cs`.

Tests: `BackgroundSplitTests.BuildSplitBranchData_EvaFromActiveShip_ShipKeepsGeneration_KerbalIsSpinoff`
(red before the fix), `BuildSplitBranchData_EvaKerbalInBackground_ShipKeepsGeneration`.

## ~~BG-BREAKUP-GENERATION-CAP~~: a background vessel never recorded its own breakup after its first split [FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp4-background-debris`; xUnit `BackgroundSplitTests`; medium (a second separation of a probe or crewed vessel left its pieces unrecorded)]

Cause: `BackgroundRecorder.HandleBackgroundVesselSplit` skipped every split whose parent recording
was at `Generation >= MaxRecordingGeneration` (1), so a probe or crewed vessel that had come off
the launched vessel (generation 1) never recorded its own later separations while in the
background (draft review question 9; the cap was undocumented).

Fix: owner ruling Q14 (2026-11-18), "Yes, for controllable ones". `ShouldSkipForCascadeCap` takes
whether the parent is controllable (`IsCascadeCapControllableParent`: a recording that is not
debris, or a live parent that `ParsekFlight.ShouldRecordAsOwnBranch` accepts) and caps plain debris
only. A lifted cap logs `Cascade depth cap lifted for a controllable parent`; the cap line gains
`parentIsDebris` and `liveParentOwnBranch`. The flight-recorder design doc now states the rule.

Tests: `BackgroundSplitTests.ShouldSkipForCascadeCap_ControllableParent_NeverSkips` (red before the
fix), `IsCascadeCapControllableParent_PlainDebrisOnlyIsCapped`; the existing cap cells pass
`parentControllable: false` and keep their expectations.

## ~~DEBRIS-ENDS-WHEN-PARENT-GOES-ON-RAILS~~: time warp ended every parent-anchored debris recording [FIXED 2026-11-20, branch `rsr-wp4-background-debris`; xUnit `DebrisLifetimeTests`; medium (a booster's fall was cut off whenever the player warped)]

Cause: `BackgroundRecorder.CheckDebrisTTL` ended a parent-anchored debris recording when its parent
vessel was packed or unloaded (`ParentOnRailsOrDestroyed`, plan Decision section 10). Time warp
packs every loaded vessel, so warping right after staging ended every dropped stage's recording at
once (draft review question 6). Owner ruling Q12 (2026-11-18): keep to the time limit.

Fix: the per-entry verdict is the pure `BackgroundRecorder.ClassifyDebrisTtlEntry`. A parent that
is on rails (packed or unloaded) no longer ends the debris; only a parent vessel that is gone does
(`ParentVesselDestroyed`, log `Debris TTL: parent vessel gone, ending recording`). The debris keeps
its 60 s limit and its other ends (vessel gone, left the physics bubble, parent recording missing
or no longer written). While on rails it records through the existing background on-rails state
(orbit checkpoints); no section is added to that state. A kept entry logs, rate-limited,
`Debris TTL: parent on rails, debris keeps recording to its time limit`.

Tests: `DebrisLifetimeTests` (the verdict table; `ParentPackedByTimeWarp_DebrisKeepsRecording` and
`ParentUnloaded_DebrisKeepsRecording` red before the fix).

Reading the decompile (2026-11-21) moved the first problem from the lane to the product: the hinge's prefab defaults are already free (`servoIsLocked` false, `servoIsMotorized` / `servoMotorIsEngaged` true), but the field the recorder sampled, `currentAngle`, is refreshed only by `UpdatePAWUI`, so the recorder could not see ANY hinge move with its part menu closed (RECORDER-SERVO-ANGLE-PAW-ONLY, below). SRV-1 REDESIGNED 2026-11-21 (same branch) on the new derived fixture `srv-hinge-rover` (`harness/tools/build_srv_hinge_rover.py`, drift test `harness/lib/test_srv_hinge_rover.py`): MINE-6's `miner-rover-watched` pair with the rover renamed `SRV1 Hinge Rover` and a G-11 Hinge stacked on its front adapter's top node (the `miner-rover-depot` port precedent) carrying a Z-200 on the hinge's moving node, both turned 90 deg about the stack axis so the battery swings sideways; the hinge's `ModuleRoboticServoHinge` node written unlocked, motorized and engaged at 90 deg/s (no `servoTransform*` / `jointParentRotation` keys: `BaseServo.OnLoad` applies them only when present). The rover is LANDED 820 m from the runway threshold, so the launch-site rule cannot hide it, and after Rewind-to-Launch strips it a reload lands FLIGHT on `Miner Watcher` 120 m north (MINE-6's measured shape). The lane records from UT 30, swings the hinge at 33 and 38, commits in FLIGHT at 43, rewinds, reloads and replays at 1x to 48, then runs the cell. The re-flight must show `Robotics: tracking 'hinge.01' ... source=servoTransformAngle`, RoboticMotionStarted / PositionSample / Stopped in the swing-out window and Started in the swing-back window, then `Servo follower plan for 'SRV1 Hinge Rover': servos=1 followers=1 invertedServos=0`, `Servo followers bound: followers=1 ... geometryPosed=1 ...`, a robotic `apply ... applied=[1-9]` and `Servo followers re-posed in playback: ... module=ModuleRoboticServoHinge followers=1 ... (first since bind)`. The old fixture `srv-hinge-pad`, its builder and drift test are no longer flown by any spec and stay until their deletion is approved.

## ~~RECORDER-SERVO-ANGLE-PAW-ONLY~~: a hinge or rotation servo recorded no motion unless its part menu was open [FILED 2026-11-21 from SRV-1's first flight and the decompile. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-b3-servo-lane`; xUnit `ReflectionClassifierCoreTests` (3 red before the fix); LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21: SRV-1 `2026-11-21_1151`; medium (most player hinge and rotation servo moves replayed frozen)]

Cause: the robotic position probe (`FlightRecorder.TryClassifyRoboticPositionFromFieldValues`,
shared by the active and background recorders) read the angular servos' `currentAngle` KSPField
first. Decompiled KSP 1.12.5: `ModuleRoboticServoHinge` / `ModuleRoboticRotationServo` write
`currentAngle` only in `UpdatePAWUI`, which `BaseServo` calls from `OnStart`, `OnPartMenuOpen`
and `Update` while `partActionMenuOpen`. With the part menu closed the field holds its start
value, so `CheckRoboticTransition` never saw a delta: SRV-1's first flight tracked the hinge
(`source=currentAngle`) through two full swings and recorded zero robotic events. The piston is
not affected (`UpdateCurrentExtension` runs in `OnFixedUpdate`).

Fix: a live stage ahead of the field plan for the hinge and the rotation servo. The reader
gained `IModuleFieldValues.TryGetServoTransformAngleDegrees`; its live half
(`TryReadServoTransformAngle`, NoInlining) rebuilds stock's protected
`BaseServo.currentTransformAngle()` from the public `MovingObject()` and `mainAxis`, and the pure
`TrySelectServoMainAxisAngle` picks the axis and wraps above 180 the same way. The new stage
(`TryClassifyLiveServoAngleFromFieldValues`) adds the hinge's `modelInitialAngle` (the
rotation servo adds nothing), so the value is what `currentAngle` shows with the menu open: the
same convention as `targetAngle` and the ghost's snapshot baseline. The tracking line reads
`source=servoTransformAngle`. A servo with no moving object yet falls back to the old plan. No
save-format change (the event values keep their meaning).

Follow-ups from the review (2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-robotics-debounce`): a servo moving
slower than about 6 deg/s flooded the event stream with Started / Stopped pairs
(RECORDER-ROBOTIC-MOTION-DEBOUNCE, below), and the ghost posed every recorded hinge angle without
taking the hinge's `modelInitialAngle` back off, so hinge_03 / hinge_03_s / hinge_04 replay 90 deg
off (GHOST-HINGE-POSE-MODEL-INITIAL-ANGLE, below). Both fixed.

The rotor has the same shape (its `currentRPM` is refreshed only in `UpdatePAWUI`): fixed
separately, RECORDER-ROTOR-RPM-PAW-ONLY below.

## ~~RECORDER-ROTOR-RPM-PAW-ONLY~~: a rotor recorded no spin unless its part menu was open, and a steady spin read as stopped [FILED 2026-11-21 from the decompile (RECORDER-SERVO-ANGLE-PAW-ONLY's follow-up). FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-rotor`; xUnit `ReflectionClassifierCoreTests` (2 red before the RPM read, 7 red under a mutation of the spin signal); LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-21: SRV-2 `2026-11-21_1227`, its third flight after a seam fix (`rotoron` raises the torque limit stock zeroes in FLIGHT) and a lane fix (`rotorbrake`), TEST-GAPS-BATCH3-FLIGHTS-2026-11-21; medium (a Breaking Ground rotor's blades replayed still)]

Cause 1 (the read): the robotic position probe sampled a rotor through its plan
`currentRPM` / `rpm` / `rpmLimit`. Decompiled KSP 1.12.5: `ModuleRoboticServoRotor` assigns
`currentRPM = transformRateOfMotion` only in `UpdatePAWUI`, and only when the 0.3 s
`refreshRPMReadouts` flag (set in `OnFixedUpdate`) is up; `UpdatePAWUI` runs from `OnStart`,
`OnPartMenuOpen` and `Update` while the part menu is open. `currentRPM` is not persistent, so with
the menu closed it reads 0 for the whole flight and no spin is ever recorded. The live value is
`BaseServo.transformRateOfMotion` (an `internal float`, no KSPField), refreshed every physics frame
by `BaseServo.FixedUpdate` -> `CalculateAverageRateOfMovement` (20-frame average of
`GetFrameDisplacement() / fixedDeltaTime`; on the rotor that is `|delta angle| * 60 / 360` per
frame, i.e. unsigned RPM, exactly what `currentRPM` copies).

Cause 2 (the moving signal): no servo carries a moving-flag KSPField (`servoIsMoving` and the
other names in `RoboticMovingFieldNames` do not exist on `BaseServo`; `IsMoving()` is a method),
so `CheckRoboticTransition` inferred motion from the VALUE changing. For a rotor the value is a
speed: once the RPM held steady the machine emitted `RoboticMotionStopped`, and the ghost's
`RotorRpm` mode (`GhostPlaybackLogic.ApplyRoboticEvent`) plays a Stopped event as "stop
spinning", so even a menu-open recording spun the ghost only while the rotor spun up or down.

Fix: a live stage ahead of the rotor's field plan. `IModuleFieldValues.TryGetServoRateOfMotionRpm`,
live half `TryReadServoRateOfMotion` (NoInlining; the `FieldInfo` lives in the nested
`ServoRateOfMotionReflection` holder, resolved on the first rotor read; a missing or non-float
field logs `Servo rate of motion unreadable` rate-limited Verbose and falls back to the plan), pure
stage `TryClassifyLiveRotorRpmFromFieldValues` (rotor only; a non-finite reading falls back). The
recorded value is the same RPM `currentRPM` holds with the menu open, so the ghost's spin rate is
unchanged. The pure `ResolveRoboticMovingSignal`, used by both the active and the background
recorder, makes a rotor sampled through a measured RPM (`servoRateOfMotion` or `currentRPM`)
moving while it spins above 0.5 RPM (stock's `IsMoving()` threshold); every other module keeps
its module flag or the inference, and a rotor read through `rpmLimit` (a setting) stays inferred.
A steady spin now records Started, samples while the RPM changes, and Stopped only once it spins
down. Follow-up 2026-11-21 (review, branch `test-gaps-robotics-debounce`, with
RECORDER-ROBOTIC-MOTION-DEBOUNCE): the spin signal was OR'd with the value inference, so a
spin-down whose last sample sat between 0.125 and 0.5 RPM never emitted Stopped and the ghost kept
creeping round until the recording ended; for the rotor-rpm source the signal now decides alone
(Stopped the frame the RPM falls to 0.5). And the fixed 0.5 RPM sample deadband turned a hovering
rotor's normal wobble into a 4 Hz sample stream; the rotor-rpm deadband is now
max(0.5 RPM, 2% of the RPM). The tracking line reads `Robotics: tracking 'rotor...' ...
module=ModuleRoboticServoRotor source=servoRateOfMotion deadband=max(0.500,2%rpm) sampleHz=4.0
moving=rotor-rpm stopHold=0.25s stop=signal`. No save-format change (the event values keep their
meaning). Not changed: the recorded RPM is unsigned, as `currentRPM` is, so the ghost spins in its
snapshot's direction.

OPEN:
- Live proof: lane `SRV-2-rotor-spin-ghost` AUTHORED 2026-11-21 (branch `test-gaps-rotor`,
  stock-tree), NEVER FLOWN; owed: its first flight. Host: the new derived fixture
  `srv-rotor-rover` (`harness/tools/build_srv_rotor_rover.py`, a sibling of SRV-1's
  `srv-hinge-rover`: an EM-16 `rotor.01` carrying a Z-200 on the rover's front, motor OFF at
  rpmLimit 30). Seam: `PartAction button=rotoron|rotoroff` press BaseServo's own
  `MotorOnAction` / `MotorOffAction` KSPAction on a `ModuleRoboticServoRotor` (refusal
  `partaction-rotor-not-found`; `state=` reads `rotor:engaged=0|1 rpmLimit=<F2>`). Ghost: a new
  one-shot Verbose `Rotor spin applied in playback: pid= module= rpm= deltaDeg= followers=
  (first since build)` (`GhostPlaybackLogic.ConsumeFirstRotorSpin` / `FormatRotorSpinLine`,
  `ServoFollowerPoseTests`), since no playback line showed a rotor turning. The lane pins the
  tracking line `source=servoRateOfMotion deadband=max(0.500,2%rpm) sampleHz=4.0
  moving=rotor-rpm stopHold=0.25s stop=signal` (the shape after the merge of
  RECORDER-ROBOTIC-MOTION-DEBOUNCE), no rotor event before the
  engage, exactly one `RoboticMotionStarted` and no `RoboticMotionStopped` before the spin-down
  mark, a Stopped after it, then the replay's follower plan / bind (servos=1 followers=1), a
  robotic apply, the first rotor spin and the rotor's first follower re-pose. The ServoFollowers
  in-game cell skips rotors (it poses a servo), so SRV-2 runs no batch.

## ~~RECORDER-ROBOTIC-MOTION-DEBOUNCE~~: a slow servo flooded the recording with Started / Stopped pairs, and a rotor could end a spin-down still "moving" [FILED 2026-11-21 from the review of RECORDER-SERVO-ANGLE-PAW-ONLY / RECORDER-ROTOR-RPM-PAW-ONLY. FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-robotics-debounce`; xUnit `RoboticMotionDebounceTests` (21 red before the fix; mutating the rotor's signal-decides, the start deadband or the stop hold reds 9 / 4 / 3 cells); live proof owed: SRV-1's re-flight for the hinge (its spec now pins `stopHold=0.25s stop=debounced` and one Started / Stopped pair per swing) and SRV-2's first flight for the rotor (`deadband=max(0.500,2%rpm) ... stop=signal`); medium (event volume on every Breaking Ground servo, and a spin-down that never stopped on the replay)]

Cause: `FlightRecorder.CheckRoboticTransition` (shared by both recorders) inferred motion from ONE
frame's change against the last EMITTED value, at a quarter of the deadband (0.125 deg). A servo
moving slower than about 6.25 deg/s changes by less than that per 0.02 s physics frame, so it read
stopped, then moving again two frames later: a RoboticMotionStarted / RoboticMotionStopped pair
every 2-3 frames (about 33 events a second at 5 deg/s), and about a dozen extra pairs in the
settle tail of every ordinary swing as stock's drive eases in. For the rotor the inference was
OR'd with the spin signal (RECORDER-ROTOR-RPM-PAW-ONLY), so a spin-down whose last sample sat
between 0.125 and 0.5 RPM kept reading moving at 0 RPM and the ghost's RotorRpm mode crept round
until the recording ended. And the rotor's sample deadband was the angular 0.5, applied to an RPM
near 460: a steady hover's wobble of more than 0.5 RPM emitted a sample at the 4 Hz cap forever.

Fix (`FlightRecorder.PartEvents.cs`): one poll, `EvaluateRoboticPoll`, used by the active and the
background recorder alike (the BG recorder now also logs the tracking line, with `(bg vessel N)`,
and an unsampleable module once). A pose servo is debounced by a per-key `RoboticMotionWindow`
(new instance dictionaries `roboticMotionWindows`, no static): at rest it starts only on a module
flag or a change of a whole deadband from its rest value (`RoboticStartDeadbandFraction`); while
moving, a change of a quarter deadband from the window reference (or a true flag) is evidence and
restarts the window, and it stops only once a whole stop hold (one 0.25 s sample interval) passes
without evidence; the Stopped event carries the settled value. A window whose key lost its
`lastRoboticPosition` entry (rails transition, departed part, reset) re-seeds on the next poll, so
those clear paths need no change. For the rotor-rpm source the spin signal decides alone, and the
sample deadband is `ResolveRoboticSampleDeadband` = max(0.5 RPM, 2% of the RPM): at hundreds of RPM
the blades turn several revolutions per rendered frame and a 2% rate difference is not visible.
The tracking line gained `stopHold=0.25s stop=debounced|signal` and, for the rotor,
`deadband=max(0.500,2%rpm)` (the `source=` / `moving=` tokens are unchanged). Measured in the
xUnit loop: 10 s at 5 deg/s gives 1 Started, at most 41 samples, 1 Stopped (it was hundreds of
events); sub-deadband creep is silent; the worst stop-start rhythm (0.45 deg/s) stays within 2
events a second; a noisy 460 RPM hover gives at most 4 samples a minute; every spin-down profile
of a sweep ends Stopped. `GearSuspensionRoboticGateTests`' root-cause cell now pins that the core
alone no longer storms on suspension jitter (the suspension gate stays). No save-format change.

## ~~GHOST-HINGE-POSE-MODEL-INITIAL-ANGLE~~: a hinge_03 / hinge_03_s / hinge_04 ghost posed 90 deg off [FILED 2026-11-21 from the review of RECORDER-SERVO-ANGLE-PAW-ONLY (code reading + decompile). FIXED 2026-11-21, branch `test-gaps-robotics-debounce`; xUnit `RoboticPoseAngleOffsetTests` (4 red before the fix); live proof 2026-11-21: SRV-3 `2026-11-21_1154` (an offset Alligator hinge and a mirrored G-11 pair, ServoMirroredPose 1/0/0); medium (visual only: the G-11 Hinge's larger siblings replay bent at the wrong angle)]

Cause (pre-existing): every recorded hinge angle is in stock's DISPLAYED convention. The live read
and the part menu's `currentAngle` are `currentTransformAngle() + modelInitialAngle`
(`ModuleRoboticServoHinge.UpdatePAWUI`), and the snapshot baseline reads the commanded
`targetAngle`. Decompiled KSP 1.12.5, stock poses the moving transform at
`AngleAxis(JointTargetAngle, mainAxis)` with `JointTargetAngle = targetAngle - modelInitialAngle`
(`OnVisualizeServo`, `SetTargetRotation(..., setRotation: true)`), so the model's rest pose IS the
displayed `modelInitialAngle` (hinge_03.cfg: `targetAngle = 90`, `modelInitialAngle = 90`). No
ghost code read `modelInitialAngle`: `ApplyRoboticPose` turned `stowedRot` (the prefab rest) by the
displayed value, so the three `modelInitialAngle = 90` hinges posed 90 deg off, at rest and through
every swing, and with no snapshot baseline spawned at the displayed 0 (fully closed) instead of the
rest.

Fix: the ghost builder reads the prefab hinge's `modelInitialAngle`
(`GhostVisualBuilder.ResolveRoboticPoseAngleOffsetDegrees`, hinge only, a missing or non-finite
field is 0; one rate-limited `Servo pose offset for '<part>' ... modelInitialAngle=90.0 taken off
every recorded angle` Verbose line when non-zero) into `RoboticGhostInfo.poseAngleOffsetDegrees`,
`ApplyRoboticPose` turns by `ComputeRoboticPoseAngleDegrees(value, offset)` = value - offset, and a
servo with no snapshot baseline spawns at `ResolveRoboticDefaultSpawnValue` (the offset for a
Rotational servo), which poses the prefab rest. Every offset-0 servo (hinge_01 / hinge_01_s /
hinge_02, every rotation servo) poses exactly as before, so their existing recordings replay
identically. The in-game `ServoFollowers` cell now returns its servo to the spawn pose through
the servo's own `spawnValue` rather than a literal 0 (the same for an offset-0 servo, the rest for
an offset hinge). No save-format change.
