## ~~SEAL-LEAVES-SPLIT-CHAIN-HEAD-PROVISIONAL~~: sealing an Unfinished Flight whose recording was split kept its tree "not finished" forever, so no supply route could be made from it [FILED 2026-11-17 from AST-3's red, run `2026-11-17_1636_AST-3-klaw-mine-route` (PARSEK-FAIL(expectation)), by log and code reading plus a headless repro. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `item31-seal-split-chain`, PR #2714; xUnit + mutation; NO REGRESSION 2026-11-17: all 36 seal / route lanes PASS on the fix (run `item31-proof`), but no flight reached the split-then-seal shape, so the fix itself is proven headless only; OPEN: a lane for that shape, todo SEAL-SPLIT-CHAIN-LANE-OWED; medium (route creation blocked for that tree for good, no data loss)]

What happened. The "AST Depot" re-entered and was destroyed after its undock, so its slot under
the undock's Rewind Point committed as an open Unfinished Flight (CommittedProvisional). At the
tree commit the optimizer split its recording at the ExoBallistic -> Atmospheric boundary
(`Split candidate (PersistedPhaseChange): rec=fae42b9b... splitUT=1291.94`, then `Split:
MergeState=CommittedProvisional carried with terminal=Destroyed onto the second half`): chain
`c98f39e5` = head `fae42b9b` (UT 1030.39-1291.94) + tip `8e79fc01` (1291.94-1469.54, Destroyed).
`SealSlot mode=Tree` then logged `Sealed slot=0 rec=fae42b9b... tip=8e79fc01...
mergeState=CommittedProvisional->Immutable` and `Sealed slot=1 rec=990818d4...` (the Miner), and
ended `sealslot incomplete ... total=8 sealed=2 failed=0 remaining=1
firstReason=member-not-slot-tip`; the route-create gate refused `sealed=False ...
refusal=TreeNotSealed`. The produced save holds `fae42b9b` at CommittedProvisional.

Cause. Every slot seal flips ONE recording, the slot's effective chain+supersede tip: the
player's Seal button (`UnfinishedFlightSealHandler.TrySeal`), the missing-quicksave and
value-sealed load sweeps (`LoadTimeSweep`) and the seam (which calls `TrySeal`). Two producers
leave a non-tip chain member CommittedProvisional: the commit promotion demotes a qualifying head
AND its chain tip separately (`TreeCommitService.ApplyRewindProvisionalMergeStates`), and the
split COPIES the state onto the new tip and keeps the head's copy
(`RecordingOptimizer.TransferTerminalFieldsToSecondHalf`; `MergeDialog.MergeCommit` promotes,
then runs the optimizer pass). No writer ever demotes that head. Re-Fly open / closed reads only
the tip, but `RouteCandidateFinder.IsTreeFullySealed` read every member's RAW MergeState, and it
gates route candidates, the near-miss list ("Not finished yet", N "still re-flyable") and the
seam's create gate. The seal also reaps the Rewind Point once its last slot closes, after which
the head resolves no slot (`TrySeal` -> `noMatchingRP`), so nothing could ever close it. The
player reached this without the seam: any sealed tree with a Rewind Point slot whose recording is
a chain (a commit-time phase-change split, or a chain born in flight).

Fix (reader side). `EffectiveState.ResolveMemberSealState` (new,
`Rewind/EffectiveState.MemberSealState.cs`) reads a member through the walk every slot consumer
uses (`EffectiveTipRecordingId` with the tree as context and the loaded scenario's supersede
rows): the recording it resolves to decides. A NotCommitted member never reads sealed; a member
that resolves to itself, or to a recording that cannot be found, reads its own state; an
Immutable member whose walk ends on an open tip reads open. `IsTreeFullySealed`,
`CountReflyableFlights` and the seam (`TestCommandSealSlot.RecordingIdsNeedingSeal` /
`IsMemberSealed`, and the applier's re-read and remaining count) all use it; `IsTreeFullySealed`
logs one rate-limited Verbose line per tree when it reads sealed only through tips, built only
when verbose logging is on (the Logistics window polls it about once a second).

Re-flyable count. The near-miss hover reads "not finished yet (N flights can still be re-flown)".
It counted every non-Immutable RECORDING, so an open split chain (head + tip) read 2 even before
this fix, and the through-tip read would have made a whole superseded subtree pointing at one
open fork count each of its recordings. `RouteCandidateFinder.CountReflyableFlights` (was
`CountReflyableRecordings`) now counts DISTINCT deciding recordings (the open tip a member
resolves to, from `ResolveMemberSealState`'s `out` overload; a NotCommitted member counts as its
own), so N is the number of flights the player can re-fly. Only the number changes; the wording
and the tooltip budget are untouched.

Re-Fly leftovers, settled by xUnit (`TreeSealedThroughTipTests`): an old recording superseded by
a concluded fork reads sealed (was open), by an open fork reads open (unchanged); the splitter's
HEAD kept visible walks HEAD -> chain -> TIP -> supersede -> fork and reads the fork (was open
whatever the fork); a provisional retired empty leaves no row, so its origin reads its own open
state (unchanged). Must-stay-open cases: an open split chain, a NotCommitted head with a sealed
tip, a NotCommitted tip, a Stash-reopened slot (head included, which before read sealed on its
own), a tip in another committed tree that is open, and a dangling supersede row on an open
member. The walk is deterministic, so every slot tip resolves to itself and an open slot always
reads open.

Other raw "sealed" reads, from a grep of every `MergeState.Immutable` / `CommittedProvisional`
read in `Source/Parsek`: the seal, stash, reaper, load sweeps, disk-usage and list-handles reads
already read the slot's tip; the classifier's qualify checks, the promotion loop, the optimizer
carry and the codec are not seal gates. One per-member read is reached by the head leftover and
left as is: `AnchorDetector.IsSealedRecordingAnchor` ranks a sealed recording first among
equally valid relative-frame anchor candidates. It is the first tie-break among eligible candidates, not a
gate (a head of a closed slot stays eligible and only loses to an otherwise-equal sealed
candidate, both valid anchors), and reading through the tip there would add a new backward
Recording -> Rewind dependency.

Proof. `CollapseSealMergeStateRegressionTests.SealOfOptimizerSplitSlot_LeavesTreeFullySealed`
drives the real `CommitTree` -> `RunOptimizationPass` -> `TrySeal` and asserts the tree reads
sealed and the create gate moves past `TreeNotSealed` (red on the old reader at its final
assertion); `TestCommandLogisticsVerbSeamTests.CreateGate_SealedSplitChain_ReadsSealed` pins the
gate and its open mirror. Mutation: reverting `IsTreeFullySealed`, `CountReflyableFlights`,
`IsMemberSealed`, the NotCommitted guard or the committed-store tip lookup each reds at least one
named test. The applier's re-read is Unity-only and has no xUnit cell. Review follow-up
(PR #2714): the two 1 Hz Logistics derivations read the loaded scenario's rows, pinned by
`TreeSealedThroughTipTests.DeriveCandidates_ReadsTheLoadedScenarioRows`,
`DeriveNearMisses_ReadsTheLoadedScenarioRows` and `DeriveNearMisses_ReflyableCount_...`;
passing empty rows in `DeriveCandidates`, in `DeriveNearMisses`, or to the near-miss count each
reds one of them, and dropping the tip as the deciding id reds six flight-count cells. Walk
boundary cells (Undock, foreign Board, own EVA, a different ChainBranch, the same ChainId in
another tree, a NotCommitted in-place fork, a switch continuation) pin where the read must stop.

Flights. Run `item31-proof` (V's PC, parallel runner, 3 slots, 2026-11-17 22:45Z to 23:07Z,
automation DLL sha256 prefix 58c54586 built from 5887933a7) flew every committed lane that seals
in tree mode or creates a route, 36 lanes, and all 36 PASS on attempt 1: 36 `sealslot complete`
lines, 0 `sealslot incomplete`, 0 `routecommand create gate` lines with `sealed=False`. That is a
no-regression result only: the 36 logs hold 0 "read through their slot's closed effective tip"
lines, so no lane exercised the new through-tip read. `AST-3-klaw-mine-route` `2026-11-17_2245`
PASS with the Depot left in orbit (0 vessel-destroyed lines): `sealslot complete mode=tree ...
total=7 sealed=1 remaining=0` and the create gate `sealed=True eligible=True status=Eligible
refusal=None`; its red `2026-11-17_1636` (the one this entry was filed from) flew the PR #2687
build, before the fix.

Still open. The fix is proven only headless (the real `CommitTree` -> `RunOptimizationPass` ->
`TrySeal` cell above); no flight has reached a split chain that is sealed and then made a route.
A deterministic lane for that shape is owed: todo SEAL-SPLIT-CHAIN-LANE-OWED. AST-3 is not that
lane: its flight variance is a lane-robustness matter for the mission, not a Parsek defect. Two of
its three recent flights (`2026-11-15_2130`, `2026-11-17_2245`) kept the Depot in orbit; the
`2026-11-17_1636` flight docked 106 s longer (449 s against 343 s) and both vessels re-entered,
which split the Depot's recording and reached this defect by chance.

OPEN residue, left unfixed by decision: `AnchorDetector.IsSealedRecordingAnchor` still reads a
member's own MergeState, so the CommittedProvisional head of a sealed split chain ranks below an
otherwise-equal Immutable anchor candidate. Reason it stays: it is a tie-break among candidates
that are all valid anchors, not a gate, and reading through the tip there needs a new backward
Recording -> Rewind type dependency the layer ratchet forbids. Reopen it if a flight shows a
relative-frame anchor choice that a sealed split head should have won.

OPEN residue, left unguarded by decision: a supersede cycle through a recording outside the tree
(rows X -> Z and Z -> X, Z Immutable) makes an open X read sealed. `EffectiveTipRecordingId`'s
cycle guard stops on Z (and warns), and every slot consumer reads that same Z, so the Unfinished
Flights list already shows the slot closed and the route gate agrees with it. A guard only in
`ResolveMemberSealState` would make the gate disagree with the slot list and leave the tree
unsealed with no slot left to seal. No writer produces the shape (each Re-Fly row points at a
fresh fork id, and the load sweep drops self rows), so it needs hand-edited rows; pinned as
`SupersedeCycleThroughAnOutsideRecording_ReadsWhatTheSlotWalkReads`. A fix belongs in the walk
or the row loader, for every consumer at once.

## ~~BG-ON-RAILS-SOI-LANE-OWED~~: no flight has shown a background vessel crossing an SOI boundary on rails [FILED 2026-11-20 from test gap batch 3 (`logs/test-gaps-doc-2026-11-18.md`), branch `test-gaps-b3-bg-soi`; xUnit green, lane SOI-3 FLOWN 2026-11-20 and red on BG-SOI-SEAM-WORLD-GAP (a cell defect, fixed 2026-11-21; RE-FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-21 `2026-11-21_1138`); low]

SOI-2 flew only the LOADED background SOI change. The on-rails route of
`BackgroundRecorder.OnBackgroundVesselSOIChanged` closes the old body's open OrbitSegment at the
event UT (an OrbitalCheckpoint section through `OrbitSegmentCheckpointBridge`) and opens one on the
new body from the vessel's re-based orbit. Read from the code and driven end to end headless by
`BackgroundOnRailsSoiCrossingTests` (9 cases, green): the Mun section ends and the Kerbin section
starts at the same UT, the flat OrbitSegment cache carries exactly one Mun -> Kerbin seam, and
`TrajectoryMath.FindOrbitSegment` (playback) and `FindOrbitSegmentForMapDisplay` (the map line)
answer the Mun before the seam and Kerbin from the seam to the recording's end. No defect found;
the vessel-free close half was already covered by `BackgroundRailsEventRouteTests`.

Finding while authoring: SOI-1's host cannot produce the subject. `mun-park-kerbalx` has one
command part, so anything it decouples is debris, and `CheckDebrisTTL` ends a parent-anchored debris
recording when its parent packs (`ParentOnRailsOrDestroyed`), when it unloads, or after 60 s. Any
rails warp packs the parent, so a recorded DEBRIS piece never crosses an SOI on rails; only a
controlled child (or a vessel switched away from) does. By design, not a defect.

Owed: the first flight of `SOI-3-bg-probe-mun-exit-on-rails` (operator, stock-minimal, seam only)
on the new by-construction fixture `mun-escape-probe-stack` (`gs2-orbital-stack`'s Kerbal X stack
on a Mun escape hyperbola, SOI exit at about UT 1316.9; `harness/tools/build_mun_escape_probe_stack.py`).
It decouples the probe core, rails-warps to UT 1500, commits and runs the new FLIGHT category
`BgSoiCrossingPlayback` (3 cells: one seam with touching checkpoint sections and a Kerbin terminal,
seam continuity within 1 km at the seam UT on live bodies, playback and map segment on Kerbin outside
the Mun's SOI after the seam). Provision with a DLL from this branch first (the category is new C#). After a
green reading run: pin the batch split whole, leave `INTERIM_PIN_IDS`, tighten the count.

Flown 2026-11-20 (`2026-11-20_2310_SOI-3-bg-probe-mun-exit-on-rails`, runner runs `b3-flights-1` / `b3-flights-2` / `b3-flights-3` on V's PC, Debug automation DLL sha256 prefix 5b46a1c1 from `test-gaps-batch3` e59ceeebc): PARSEK-FAIL(results) attempt 1. The crossing recorded as designed (one seam at UT 1317.090; two of the three cells passed), but the continuity cell measured a 9.1 km gap: filed as BG-SOI-SEAM-WORLD-GAP (top of this file), settled 2026-11-21 as the cell comparing two instants 1 s apart in the Sun-anchored world frame (the probe's 9127.7 m/s heliocentric speed); the cell now evaluates both sides at the seam UT within 1 km. Owed: the re-flight.

(the docked pair re-entered), so no lane reaches it on purpose.

optimizer pass splits its recording (an atmosphere edge on a suborbital hop is the cheapest), is
kept open as an Unfinished Flight, then sealed (`SealSlot` in tree mode), then made a route
(`RouteCommand action=create`). Pins: `sealslot complete mode=tree`, the through-tip line
`IsTreeFullySealed: tree=... reads sealed with 1 member(s) not Immutable themselves` (a
rate-limited Verbose line, so confirm the lane's verbose setting before pinning it), and the
create gate `sealed=True`. Reuse a host that already flies a boundary crossing before adding a
flight (`harness/README.md` -> "Authoring a fast lane").

Flown 2026-11-23: `_2110` red (FirstLaunch and two record rows of the sandbox hop sealed the pod's slot,
`recordingAction:MilestoneAchievement`, design section 2.12: a counted row seals even at zero value), so an
unrecorded Jumping Flea hop now reaches them first; `_2201` / `_2204` INVALID on a practice hop that left a
stand behind (fixed), `_2229` PASS attempt 1 with the through-tip line and `sealed=True`.

Authored 2026-11-23: `SSC-1-sealed-split-chain-route-gate` on `rover-route-recorded`, IR-3's CS
Flea Probe pad decouple (a Rewind Point), RW-11's hop, a 30 s landed dwell and the pod exploded:
the slot commits open and the landing is a SurfaceInvolved split (the air run is over 120 s). The
create is expected REJECTED as `candidate-ineligible`, with the gate line pinned at `sealed=True`;
verbose logging is on for the through-tip line.

## ~~COLD-LOAD-INTO-FLIGHT-DROPS-DUE-SPAWN~~: loading a save into FLIGHT after a recording's end, before its vessel spawned, drops the vessel for good [FILED 2026-11-17 by code reading during the end-spawn lane program (todo END-SPAWN-LANES-2026-11-17); no flight yet; SPW-8 and SPW-9 are pre-registered to red on it; high (a vessel the player was owed never appears, silently apart from one log line); FIXED 2026-11-17 under the id COLD-LOAD-DROPS-OWED-SPAWN (the same defect, found twice the same day); SPW-8 and SPW-9 read green on their first flights 2026-11-17 (runs `2026-11-17_2320` / `_2322`, runner run `spawn-flight-2026-11-18`), the fix's live proof]

What happens. Every Cold load (a save-file load: the Load menu, and stock F9, which classifies Cold
`coldReason=save-file` in `LoadReconcilePolicy`) runs the phase `crew-auto-unreserve`
(`ParsekScenario.OnLoadPhaseAutoUnreserveCrewPastEndUT`). Outside the Space Center it takes every
non-loop recording whose EndUT is already past and whose vessel never spawned, unreserves its crew,
NULLS its vessel snapshot and marks it spawned (`Auto-unreserved crew for recording #N (<name>) -
EndUT passed without spawn`). Nothing spawns it afterwards: the flight scene sees a spawned recording
with no snapshot.

Two ordinary ways to get there:
- a spawn still owed when the player quicksaves: a terminal-orbit spawn held until its next safe UT
  (SS-1's Low Perigee Probe), a collision-held spawn, a spawn deferred by warp; F9 then drops it
  (lane SPW-8);
- a save written at the Space Center after an Orbiting or Docked end: the KSC never spawns those
  (#171, `GhostPlaybackLogic.ShouldSpawnAtKscEnd` defers them to the flight scene), so the save holds
  the recording unspawned past its end, and loading it into FLIGHT drops it (lane SPW-9).

The phase predates the deferral paths: it was written when a past-end unspawned recording meant a
spawn that could no longer happen. The comment above the call names only the Space Center exemption
(bug #99), and it ignores `PlaybackScopeTracker` and every deferral state.

Fix: not designed. The shape the lanes gate: a Cold load into FLIGHT (or the Tracking Station)
leaves a past-end unspawned recording owed, and the scene's own end-spawn path makes it once
(recorded terminal orbit for Orbiting ends). Whether the crew unreserve should still run for a
recording that will spawn is part of the design question.

## ~~SPAWN-TS-STACK-NO-DE-OVERLAP~~: two landed deliveries that end on one spot while the player is in the Tracking Station are spawned inside each other [FILED 2026-11-17 by the end-of-recording spawn audit (END-SPAWN-SCENE-LANES-2026-11-17), by code reading; lane `TSS-3-two-deliveries-same-spot-ts` authored to red on it, NEVER FLOWN. ~~done~~ 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix3`; NOT YET FLOWN (TSS-3 is its regression lane)]

What the code does. The Space Center end spawn nudges a Landed / Splashed spawn clear of every
existing same-body landed vessel, proto vessels included (`ParsekKSC.cs`, the `#duplicate-stack`
block: `VesselSpawner.GatherExistingLandedVesselPositions` ->
`SpawnCollisionDetector.ComputeDeOverlappedLandedSpawn`, 15 m minimum, logged `De-overlap for #N`).
That block is the only caller of `ComputeDeOverlappedLandedSpawn`. The Tracking Station handoff
(`GhostMapPresence.TryRunTrackingStationSpawnHandoffs`) spawns through `VesselSpawner`'s
end-of-recording path, whose collision check (`SpawnCollisionDetector.CheckOverlapAgainstLoadedVessels`,
a `Physics.OverlapBox`) sees only LOADED vessels, and the Tracking Station has none. The comment on
`GatherExistingLandedVesselPositions` names exactly this case ("At KSC / Tracking Station nothing is
loaded"), but only the Space Center calls it.

What the player sees (derived, not measured). Two flights of the same craft to the same base, both
ending while the player sits in the Tracking Station (or warps there across both ends), are
created at the same spot; loading that spot into physics puts two vessels inside each other
(they push apart or explode). The same holds for a delivery landing on a vessel already standing
there.

Lane. `TSS-3-two-deliveries-same-spot-ts` (injected preset `spawn-stack`: two committed Landed
probes ending 20 s apart on one KSC grass point) crosses both ends at 100,000x in the Tracking
Station and pins `Spawning vessel: ... nearest vessel=<D>m` with D >= 10 for both, then loads FLIGHT
on the spot and forbids `Spawn-death detected`. Red today on the second probe's nearest-vessel
distance (~0 m expected). The same gap held for an end spawn far from the player in flight
(defect F of the 2026-11-17 placement audit): the vessels there are unloaded too.

Fix (2026-11-17). The shared end-of-recording spawn (`VesselSpawner.SpawnOrRecoverIfTooClose`,
called by the Tracking Station handoff and by every flight end spawn) now runs the Space Center's
de-overlap before its collision check (`ApplyEndOfRecordingLandedDeOverlap`, gated by the pure
`ShouldDeOverlapEndOfRecordingSpawn`: non-EVA, Landed or Splashed, not on the recorded terminal
orbit). It gathers with `GatherExistingLandedVesselPositions(..., includeLoadedVessels: false)`:
loaded vessels stay with the bounding-box check and the trajectory walkback as before, so a spawn
next to the player behaves as it did, and the unloaded rest (every vessel in the Tracking Station,
the far ones in flight, including a delivery spawned earlier in the same handoff pass) is kept
15 m clear. The tree-sibling and earlier-tree exemptions are the gather's, so a placed-part
cluster is not pulled apart. A nudged spawn re-runs its floor at the new spot
(`ReFloorNudgedSurfaceSpawnAltitude`: Landed `ClampAltitudeForLanded`, Splashed the recorded-depth
rule); the Space Center de-overlap now does the same.
Logged `[Spawner] De-overlap for #N "<name>": nudged <M>m (site=end-of-recording, ...)` (Verbose
`clear` otherwise), worded like the Space Center line so the EVA-6 / EVA-9 / EVA-10 forbidden
nudge patterns cover both sites. TSS-3 re-pinned: no longer an expected red, its `nearest vessel`
pins kept, plus the de-overlap line. Tests: `TipSpawnPlacementTests` (`EndOfRecordingDeOverlap_*`,
`Wiring_EndOfRecordingSpawn_DeOverlapsAgainstUnloadedLandedVesselsBeforeTheCollisionCheck`).

## ~~TIP-SPAWN-PLACEMENT~~: where an end-of-recording vessel is placed: four confirmed defects in the walkback, the splashed clamp, the over-water test and the chain tip [FILED 2026-11-17 from the tip-spawn verification pass (items G, H, S1, S2; headless proofs on scratch branch `scratch/spawnverify` 39102b11, never pushed), by code reading and failing xUnit cells. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix2`; xUnit (`TipSpawnPlacementTests`); no lane flies any of the four paths; medium (a vessel placed far off its path, under water, or as an empty capsule)]

- **G, walkback read Relative offsets as lat/lon.** `TryWalkbackForEndOfRecordingSpawn` handed the
  flat `rec.Points` list to `WalkbackAlongTrajectorySubdivided` with no frame dispatch and no
  body check, so a lander that approached a base inside a RELATIVE section walked into
  anchor-local metres read as degrees (proof: a candidate 885 m off the path). Fix:
  `SpawnCollisionDetector.ResolveWalkbackPointsOnBody` keeps only the contiguous run ending at
  the last point that places on the spawn body, substituting a Relative point's body-fixed
  shadow (`FlatPointFrameDispatch`) and stopping at a Relative point with no shadow or at a point
  on another body. The end-of-recording collision path walks that run (fewer than two points
  falls to the existing single-point retry path), and the chain-tip walkback
  (`VesselGhoster.TryWalkbackSpawn`) uses the same run. The Orbiting-end variant (walkback
  coordinates mixed with a propagated orbit) was only plausible and is not addressed.
- **S1, the Splashed spawn altitude differed by path.** The walkback clamp only lowered a
  positive altitude to 0 while the endpoint floored every Splashed spawn to sea level (#313).
  First fix (`wip/spawnfix2`): one helper used by both, flooring to 0. **Owner ruling 2026-11-17
  reverses #313:** a Splashed end spawns at its RECORDED depth (a submarine that ended 50 m down
  appears 50 m down, where its ghost held it, instead of popping to the surface with a ~50 m jump
  at the ghost-to-vessel handoff). #313 floored an EVA kerbal recorded at -0.2 m so he would not
  appear under water; he now spawns where he was recorded and swims up. The one real hazard kept
  solved: a spot shallower than the recorded depth (a walkback sub-step, a de-overlap nudge, a
  terrain change). Fix (`wip/spawnfix3`): `VesselSpawner.ResolveSplashedSpawnAltitude(alt,
  seaFloor, ...)` keeps a depth <= 0, sends a positive altitude to 0, and raises a depth below
  `TerrainAltitude(lat, lon, true) + UndergroundSafetyFloorMeters` (2 m) to that floor, never above
  0 (unknown floor, e.g. headless: no floor). Used by `ResolveSpawnPosition` (so the Space Center
  end spawn too; sea floor read headless-safe by `TryReadSeaFloorAltitude`), the collision
  walkback, both de-overlaps (`ReFloorNudgedSurfaceSpawnAltitude`, which the Space Center
  de-overlap now also runs, Landed included) and every non-orbital chain-tip spawn
  (`VesselGhoster.ResolveChainTipSurfaceSpawnAltitude`, sea floor under the tip). The chain tip's
  underground terrain correction no longer runs for Splashed (`TerrainCorrector.ShouldCorrectTerrain`
  returns false for it, its only caller being that site): it reads `TerrainAltitude(lat, lon)`, which
  clamps a sea floor to 0, so it rewrote a resolved -50 m tip to +2 m before `RespawnVessel`. Logged
  `Clamped altitude for SPLASHED spawn #N (...): X -> Y (above-sea-level|below-sea-floor, ...)` or
  `Splashed spawn #N (...) keeps its recorded depth alt=...` (rate-limited). Not flown: no lane has
  a submerged end; a submarine lane (scratch `submarine.md` design) would pin the depth line and
  the `LeafPlacement height:` reading.
- **S2, a sea spawn was written LANDED.** `SpawnAtPosition` read `body.TerrainAltitude(lat, lon)`,
  whose stock default `allowNegative = false` clamps a sea floor to 0 (decompiled IL), so
  `overWater` was always false and `DetermineSituation` wrote `sit=LANDED` for a Splashed EVA,
  breakup or position-routed spawn at alt <= 0. Fix: `VesselSpawner.IsSpawnOverWater` reads
  `TerrainAltitude(lat, lon, true)`.
- **H, chain tip skipped two end-of-recording rules.** (1) No all-crew-dead abandon (#170):
  `SpawnChainTipWithResolvedState` now runs `VesselSpawner.TryAbandonChainTipForDeadCrew` before
  spawning, settling the tip VesselSpawned + SpawnAbandoned with the no-living-crew note (EVA tip
  exempt), the same outcome as an invalid-materialization abandon on this path: the chain stays
  ghost-only. The same guard runs on the chain tip's snapshot-respawn fallbacks (no tip point,
  unresolved position or body) and, through `VesselSpawner.TryAbandonEndOfRecordingSpawnForDeadCrew`,
  on the end-of-recording fallbacks (no trajectory, unresolved endpoint body), which also lacked
  it. A deliberate settle (`VesselGhoster.IsChainTipSettledWithoutVessel`) now logs as an Info
  abandon instead of the `spawn failed` Error / Warn lines. (2) An orbital tip was collision-checked at its snapshot position while it spawns
  at its terminal orbit propagated to the spawn UT: `SpawnAtChainTip` now resolves that state
  first and checks there. The other three H claims (per-kerbal crew, the attempts cap, the EVA
  exempt pid) were refuted.

## ~~SPAWNED-VESSEL-TERMINATED-RESPAWNS~~: an end vessel the player terminates or deletes in the Tracking Station is spawned again [FILED 2026-11-17 from the tip-spawn defect verification (headless probes, branch `spawnverify`, scratch cells in 39102b11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix1`; xUnit; no lane gates it yet; medium (a vessel the player threw away comes back)]

Cause. `ParsekScenario.OnVesselTerminated` (fired by stock only from
`SpaceTracking.OnVesselDeleteConfirm`, i.e. TS Terminate / Delete) stamped only the pending tree.
The committed recording kept `VesselSpawned` and its pid, so the next flight's
`RunSpawnDeathChecks` found the pid missing, counted a spawn death and reset the recording for a
respawn. The 3-cycle cap did not bound it: `SpawnDeathCount` was not saved and every in-session
load zeroed it.

Fix. A termination writes a `VesselTerminated` ledger row (new `GameActionType` 42, additive, same
keys as `VesselRecovered`; `LedgerOrchestrator.OnRealVesselTerminated`), mirroring the owner-ruled
recovery row: same owner selection, skipped under crew-event suppression, pid 0 or an active
Re-Fly, deduplicated, retired by a Re-Fly supersede, no impact on any resource. It is not recovery
evidence. `RunSpawnDeathChecks` clears the spawn claim with no respawn when the row exists
(`TryClearTerminatedSpawnClaim`), and `TryRejectSpawnForTerminalAndSituation` rejects the spawn.
`SpawnDeathCount` is now saved (`spawnDeathCount`, written when above 0, restored on in-session
loads by `RestorePersistedSpawnDeathCount`), and a recording that already reached the cap stays
abandoned with no further increment. A genuine spawn death (not the player) still retries within
the cap. The row also ends the crew holds of the terminated vessel: `KerbalsModule`'s walk adds
a closure at the row's UT for each kerbal its owner recording still carries (Aboard / Unknown),
scoped like a recovery (`CollectTerminationClosures`, `RecoveryClosesHold`), and the crew
reservation walk now reads the row. It is never a recovery (no `KerbalRecovered` row, no reward);
stock's own Missing -> respawn handling takes the kerbal from there, a rewind before the row holds
him again, and a supersede that tombstones the row reopens the hold. Without it the vessel, which
no longer respawned for a later recovery, left its crew reserved forever. Tests:
`VesselTerminatedRowTests`; in `KerbalRecoveryReservationCloseTests`
`TerminatedCrewedVessel_EndsTheOpenEndedHold_WithoutARecovery`,
`TerminationClosure_RewindReReserves_AndATombstonedRowReopensTheHold`,
`CollectTerminationClosures_OnlyTheOwnersAboardCrew_NeverARecovery`; the in-session restore of
the count is gated by `LoadReconcileWiringGateTests.InSessionLoadRestoresTheSpawnDeathCountAfterTheReset`.

## ~~SPAWN-FAILED-NO-GHOST-NEVER-RETRIED~~: a completion with no ghost whose end spawn fails is not retried in that scene [FILED 2026-11-17 from the tip-spawn defect verification (headless probes, branch `spawnverify`, scratch cells in 39102b11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix1`; xUnit; no lane gates it yet; low (the vessel appears late, on the next scene change)]

Cause. `ParsekPlaybackPolicy.HandlePlaybackCompleted` held a failed spawn for retry only when a
ghost was active (`heldGhosts`); `FlushDeferredSpawns` logged "flushed without materializing" and
dropped it, and the engine's completion is one-shot. Real trigger: an Orbiting end deferred from
the Space Center to flight, entered past its end, held by `TerminalOrbitSpawnSafety` or pending
placement.

Fix. A separate id-keyed retry set `ghostlessSpawnRetries` (kept out of `heldGhosts` so the
engine's `IsGhostHeld` and ghost release are untouched) is armed from both places and driven by
`RetryGhostlessSpawns` at the start of `RetryHeldGhostSpawns`, with the held-ghost timeout and
decision (`DecideHeldGhostAction`); under warp it hands the spawn to the deferred queue. Logs
"Spawn retry armed with no ghost" / "succeeded" / "gave up". Tests in `DeferredSpawnTests`
(`NoGhostCompletion_*`, `WarpFlush_FailedSpawnWithNoHeldGhost_ArmsTheRetry`).

## ~~SPAWN-ABANDON-SURVIVES-LOAD~~: an in-session load or a Re-Fly strip keeps the spawn abandon state while clearing the spawn claim [FILED 2026-11-17 from the tip-spawn defect verification (headless probes, branch `spawnverify`, scratch cells in 39102b11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix1`; xUnit; no lane gates it yet; low]

Cause. `ResetTreeRecordingMutableStateForLoad` and `ReconcileSpawnStateAfterStrip` cleared
`VesselSpawned`, the pid, `SpawnAttempts` and `SpawnDeathCount` but left `SpawnAbandoned`,
`WalkbackExhausted`, `CollisionBlockCount` and `DuplicateBlockerRecovered`; only
`RewindLauncher.ClearSpawnState` cleared them. The recording was eligible again with a stale
abandon: a failed retry was marked spawned with pid 0 and no failure log, and a successful one was
never death-checked.

Fix. One `Recording.ClearTransientSpawnState` clears the whole family and all three resets call
it (the load reset also clears `TerminalOrbitSpawnSafety`), so an in-session load starts the
recording like a cold load. The persisted terminal-orbit abandon and the persisted spawn-death
count are put back after the reset as before. Tests in `SpawnStateReconciliationTests`
(`InSessionLoadReset_ClearsTheAbandonFamily_LikeAColdLoad`,
`ReFlyStripReconcile_ClearsTheAbandonFamily`).

## ~~COLD-LOAD-DROPS-OWED-SPAWN~~: a cold load into flight marks in-scope recordings that still owe their end spawn as spawned [FILED 2026-11-17 from the tip-spawn defect verification (headless probes, branch `spawnverify`, scratch cells in 39102b11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix1`; xUnit; no lane gates it yet; low (the vessel appears on the next scene change, its crew free meanwhile)]

Cause. `ParsekScenario.OnLoadPhaseAutoUnreserveCrewPastEndUT` unreserves the crew, drops the
snapshot and stamps `VesselSpawned` for every non-loop recording past its end outside the Space
Center, without consulting `PlaybackScopeTracker`, so warp-deferred, held and KSC-deferred orbit
spawns were dropped too.

Fix. A recording in replay scope (`PlaybackScopeTracker.IsInReplayScope`, installed from the save
before this step) is skipped, with a Verbose line per recording and one Info summary. The plain
historical case is unchanged. Test:
`ParsekScenarioOnLoadPhaseTests.AutoUnreserve_ColdLoadIntoFlight_KeepsInScopeRecordingThatOwesItsSpawn`.

## ~~REFLY-LIFTS-HISTORICAL-GATE-FOR-ALL~~: an active Re-Fly lifts the historical-never-replayed gate for every recording, not only the session's tree [FILED 2026-11-17 from the tip-spawn defect verification (headless probes, branch `spawnverify`, scratch cells in 39102b11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix1`; xUnit; no lane gates it yet; low]

Cause. Flight, Tracking Station, Space Center and the TS map lifecycle passed "Re-Fly active" into
`GhostPlaybackLogic.ResolveHistoricalNeverReplayed`, which then answered false for every
recording, so an unrelated historical recording with pid 0 could spawn during a Re-Fly.

Fix. The exemption is scoped to the session's tree: `IsInReFlySessionTree(marker, rec)` (marker
tree id equal to the recording's; a marker with no tree id keeps the old whole-world answer).
Tests in `LoopFirstRunSpawnTests` (`ReFlyActive_UnrelatedTreeRecording_KeepsHistoricalGate`,
`IsInReFlySessionTree_NoMarker_StandaloneRecording_AndTreelessMarker`).

## ~~TIMEJUMP-CROSSED-CHAIN-TIPS-DEAD~~: `TimeJumpManager.SpawnCrossedChainTips` was unreachable and bypassed the end-spawn gate [FILED 2026-11-17 from the tip-spawn defect verification (headless probes, branch `spawnverify`, scratch cells in 39102b11), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `wip/spawnfix1`; xUnit; no lane gates it yet; cleanup]

Every `ExecuteJump` caller passed no chains, so the step never ran; wired up, it would have
spawned past `ShouldSpawnAtRecordingEnd`. Deleted with `FindCrossedChainTips`,
`VesselGhoster.IsChainTipSettledAsKscRetirement` and their tests; `ExecuteJump(targetUT)` takes the
target only, and end spawns after a jump come from the playback loop. The
`facts_pins.toml` uncalled pin is gone with it.

## ~~RESTORE-ATTEMPT-CUTOFF-AHEAD-OF-CLOCK~~: a resumed recording whose end is a predicted terminal ahead of the clock gives its restore attempt a history cutoff in the future, so everything the resumed flight earns reads as committed history [FILED 2026-11-16 from the v1.0.2 release check, lane RF-11-both-slots-in-sequence, run `2026-11-16_2341` (release build) failing against the pass `2026-11-11_0134` (pre-#2622). FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `item30-restore-cutoff`, PR #2687; xUnit + mutation; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-17: RF-11 `2026-11-17_1712` and `2026-11-17_1730` PASS attempt 1, SE-1 `2026-11-17_1714` and `_1729` PASS, RC-7 `2026-11-17_1728` PASS; high (a Re-Fly slot the player kept open seals itself at the next load, and value from a discarded flight stays in the ledger). OPEN: residue (d) and the killed run note below]

What the player sees: re-fly a slot, merge with "Commit, don't seal" while the vessel still
flies (its tip ends in a predicted crash), then load the save. The vessel is resumed, stock
re-awards its altitude / speed / distance records in the load frame, and after the next Re-Fly
start and load the slot the player kept open is sealed by the load sweep, with the awards of a
flight the rewind abandoned still booked.

Cause. A committed-tree restore attempt (`CommittedTreeRestoreAttempt`, armed by
`ParsekFlight.TryTakeCommittedTreeForSpawnedVesselRestore`) gave every recording of the tree an
event cutoff equal to its `EndUT` (`BuildCommittedTreeRestoreEventCutoffs`): an event at or before
it is committed history, one after it is the attempt's own. Right when the end is in the past
(SE-1); wrong when the RESUMED recording's end is a predicted terminal ahead of the live clock.
The arm gate (`IsCommittedRecordingAheadOfLiveClock`) refuses only recorded data past the clock,
so a recording whose end is extrapolation (the merged provisional `rec_558d1318`, points=0,
`terminal=Destroyed terminalUT=429.426`) is resumed at UT 131.9 with a cutoff of 429.43. Every
award of the resumed flight is then below the cutoff: the coalescer skips the stored seed (131.6)
and its own new seeds too (`TryCoalesceWorldRecordReward: ... skipped N restore-attempt history
event(s) at or before cutoff=429.42601042389236`, five lines at LoadGame 0008 and the same five
for the slot-1 provisional `rec_5cfdf180`, cutoff 429.478, at LoadGame 0014), so five standalone
events (RecordsAltitude thresholds 3 and 4, RecordsSpeed 3 and 4, RecordsDistance 3, all
`ut=131.9`) are written to the file as history (`ShouldSuppressCommittedTreeRestoreAttemptEventPersistence`
false), the Re-Fly start's rollback discard (`RewindInvoker.DiscardRestoreAttemptOfAbandonedFlight`)
purges only past the cutoff (no `same-id game-state event tail` line in the log), and the next
tree commit files them as ledger rows of the merged provisional
(`BuildTreeCommitRowsPreview: ... rows=5`, `NotifyLedgerTreeCommitted`, window [StartUT, EndUT]),
which the RetireSet gate reads as sealing rows. Before #2622 (RESTORE-ATTEMPT-RECORD-FOLDS-INTO-HISTORY)
the awards folded into the stored seed (`Coalesced world-record milestone 'RecordsAltitude' ...
seedUT=131.6`, zero standalone events), which hid the wrong cutoff for world records. The wider
point: ANY event type the resumed flight emitted before the predicted end got the history
treatment (kept on the file, survived a rollback discard, filed at the next commit), not only
world records.

Fix: the arm takes the resumed recording id and the live UT
(`ArmCommittedTreeRestoreAttempt(tree, reason, resumedRecordingId, resumeUT)`), and only that
recording's cutoff changes (`ComputeResumedRecordingEventCutoff`): when its end lies after the
resume instant, the cutoff is the largest double below the resume UT, so an award stamped in the
resume frame itself (stock's load-frame awards carry the same `Planetarium.GetUniversalTime()`
the arm read) is the attempt's own. Every other recording keeps its end (a sibling can hold
recorded data past the clock, and a clamp would purge it on a discard), and an end at or before
the resume instant keeps the end (SE-1 unchanged). The cutoff is never lowered below a stored
event of the resumed recording stamped strictly after the resume instant (GameStateStore and
milestone events; such an event is history the store already holds). Every cutoff reader (the
coalescer's event and ledger-row loops, the milestone enrichment, the persistence filter, the tail
purge and the live re-home) reads the clamped value through the one map; the #2622 guards are
unchanged. Durability: `ATTEMPT_EVENTS` carries two optional keys, `attemptResumedRecordingId` and
`attemptResumeUT` (round-trip "R"; additive, absent keys mean every cutoff at its end, as before);
the cold re-arm (`ParsekScenario.TryRearmSaveAttemptForRestoredTree`) passes them back, and the
in-place shape (no active tree in the save, the flight re-arms at the load's clock) moves the
resume instant back to the saved one (`CommittedTreeRestoreAttempt.AdoptSavedResumeInstant`, from
`ResolveHeldSaveAttemptEventsOnArm`) so the held events between the two instants are restored, not
dropped. An in-session load keeps memory's attempt and its clamp. The arm line now prints
`resumed=... resumeUT=... endUT=... resumedCutoff=... rule=... storedEventsAtResume=N`. Tests:
`RestoreAttemptCutoffAheadOfClockTests` (red on the old code: two standalone events where one is
expected; a resume-frame award, the sibling, SE-1 mirror, non-finite clock, the raise, the
milestone raise, the round trip, the adopt, and the discard / commit ledger-row cells), plus two
cold-load cells in `ColdLoadRestoreAttemptRearmTests`. Mutation: a cutoff AT the resume UT reds
nine cells.

Left as is, not built:
  (a) A stored event of the resumed recording stamped EXACTLY at the resume UT cannot be told from
      a resume-frame award by its UT; it reads as the attempt's (kept off the file, purged by a
      rollback discard). Counted on the arm line (`storedEventsAtResume=N`); not seen in RF-11.
  (b) The other recordings of the tree keep their end cutoffs even when that end is a predicted
      terminal ahead of the clock; an event tagged to one of them during the attempt reads as
      history. Not reached by RF-11 (awards tag the active recording).
  (c) The purge summary `...: purged N same-id game-state event tail(s) ...` stays a Warn (the RC-7
      lane pins its text). The log validator's only WRN rule (`WRN-001`) flags a redundant
      `WARNING:` / `WARN:` prefix, which it does not have, so this now reachable designed case is
      not flagged.
  (d) OPEN (review follow-up): when the clock is BEHIND a stored event of the resumed recording
      (load UT 131.5, stored seed 131.6) the raise keeps the cutoff at that event, so an award in
      the gap between the clock and the event still reads as history and the RF-11 effect
      remains for that gap. The cleaner fix is for the arm gate to refuse such a resume:
      `ParsekFlight.IsCommittedRecordingAheadOfLiveClock` checks recorded data only, so a points=0
      provisional with stored events past the clock slips past it.
  (e) Downgrade: a save written by this build and loaded by 1.0.2 has the two new keys ignored, so
      the old defect returns there; no data is lost.
  OPEN: the KILLED run `2026-11-16_2307` (same lane, same build) froze at the first
  AnswerMergeDialog; unexplained and separate from this defect.

Wiring, admission. `VesselSwitchTreeTests` drives `TryTakeCommittedTreeForSpawnedVesselRestore`
with `liveUT` (red with the call site's recording id nulled, and with its `liveUT` replaced by
NaN). The RF-11 provisional (terminal Destroyed) was resumed because it was the tree's ACTIVE
recording: `IsCommittedSpawnedRecordingRestorable` refuses a Destroyed / Recovered / Docked /
Boarded terminal only for a non-active (background) member, so a background tip needs a live
terminal such as Orbiting. Same take path either way (`ResumeActiveRecording` vs
`PromoteFromBackground`); both shapes are cells. A held save without the resume facts logs
`Held ATTEMPT_EVENTS name no resume instant: ... reason=...` and keeps the flight's own instant.
The arm line's new resume fields broke RC-7's exact arm-line pin (`2026-11-17_1707`
PARSEK-FAIL(expectation)), so RC-7 is re-pinned to them with `rule=end (not ahead of the clock)`.

Live proof, on V's PC with the parallel runner. Run `item30-proof` (automation DLL sha256
c4b9d2d4..., built from faa900183): RF-11 `2026-11-17_1712` PASS (78 s), SE-1 `2026-11-17_1714`
PASS. Run `item30-proof2` (sha256 00f09f15..., from 82da7beb6): RC-7 `2026-11-17_1728` PASS
(143 s, `rule=end (not ahead of the clock)`, endUT = resumedCutoff = 367.15...,
`storedEventsAtResume=0`), SE-1 `2026-11-17_1729` PASS, RF-11 `2026-11-17_1730` PASS. RF-11 on
both fix runs: both arm lines `rule=resume instant (end ahead of the clock)`, resumedCutoff 131.9
against endUT 429.43; 3 standalone world-record events in each of the LoadGame 0008 and 0014
windows (5 before the fix); `refly-start: ... purged 3 same-id game-state event tail(s)`; the
RetireSet gate reads slot 0 `sealingRows=0` on all three lines; no `Value-sealed slot concluded`
line; both `sealslot complete` lines `alreadySealed=False`. SE-1 ledger rows: 13 at load, 13
before the discard, 15 after it, still 15 at every later save. Windows xUnit at 82da7beb6, Debug
and Release: 35812 total, 35627 passed, 0 failed, 185 skipped. The same `item30-proof` run's
AST-3 red (`2026-11-17_1636`, `firstReason=member-not-slot-tip`) is not evidence either way; it
is todo SEAL-LEAVES-SPLIT-CHAIN-HEAD-PROVISIONAL.

## ~~KSC-END-SPAWN-SKIPS-OFF-KERBIN~~: the Space Center never spawns the end vessel of a recording that starts off Kerbin, and logs nothing [FILED 2026-11-17 from LAY-1's first flight, run `2026-11-17_1417_LAY-1-laythe-reentry-splashdown` (Debug DLL from main 65ac33ee8; diagnostics on branch `forge-logs-2026-11-17-next-tests`, folder `logs-carrier/next-tests-2026-11-17/<runId>/`), by log and code reading. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch `kscspawn`; xUnit; LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-17: LAY-1 `2026-11-17_1740` PASS attempt 1 and the nine confirmation lanes below green in the same run (`spawn-reflight-2026-11-17`, Debug DLL from main e9353aa5); medium (the vessel appears late, on the next Tracking Station or flight visit, not never)]

What happened. LAY-1 landed the crewed Duna Rocket's pod on Laythe and committed it
(`CommitTreeFlight terminal: rec=ba455ab6a039477ab19b9b362b1d4240 terminalState=Splashed
terminalOrbitBody=Laythe`), rewound to launch (`Stripped 1 vessel(s) from save (1 by name
[Duna Rocket] ...)`), visited the Tracking Station before the recording's start, loaded the Space
Center and warped past the end (`warptout complete reachedUT=28820999.795564618 ut=28821000`).
No vessel appeared: `LeafPlacement summary: scene=SPACECENTER compared=0 ok=0 bad=0 absent=0
duplicate=0 unsupported=0 bodies=[]` (no committed recording carried a spawn pid at all), and the
log holds no `KSCSpawn` line of any kind between the Space Center load and the batch. The Space
Center's walk read `ParsekKSC initialized, 7 committed recordings, 0 eligible for KSC ghost
playback` / `ineligible(Destroyed=5, <null>=1, Splashed=1)`.

Cause. `ParsekKSC.Update` (`Controllers/ParsekKSC.cs`, the "Structural reject" branch) calls
`IsKscStructurallyEligible`, which is false when `rec.Points[0].bodyName != "Kerbin"`, and then
`continue`s before every Space Center spawn path: the non-looping end spawn
(`UpdateSingleGhostKsc` -> `TrySpawnAtRecordingEnd`, including its "never created, past end"
branch), the playback-disabled past-end detour (bug #433) and the loop first-run spawn
(`TryLoopFirstRunSpawnKsc`). The predicate is a RENDER gate (the Space Center can only draw a
ghost at Kerbin) used as a spawn gate, and the skip writes nothing. The spawn decision itself has
no body rule: `GhostPlaybackLogic.ShouldSpawnAtKscEnd` defers Orbiting / Docked terminals to the
flight scene by design (#171, logged `orbital vessel deferred to flight scene`) and otherwise
answers like flight, and the Tracking Station's handoff
(`GhostMapPresence.TryRunTrackingStationSpawnHandoffs` -> `ShouldSpawnAtTrackingStationEnd`) is
body-agnostic. The fix-433 plan (`docs/dev/done/plans/fix-433-playback-enabled-visual-only.md`,
"Risks") kept non-Kerbin out of the spawn detour on the premise that every structural cause
describes a recording with no valid trajectory; that holds for `Points.Count < 2`, not for an
off-Kerbin start.

What the player sees. Land anywhere off Kerbin (or play such a recording forward after a rewind),
return to the Space Center and time-warp past the landing: the vessel is not created. A save made
at the Space Center lacks it, and its crew stays reserved (`Reservation extended: 'Valentina
Kerman' endUT->Infinity`). It is created on the next Tracking Station visit (the body-agnostic
handoff) or flight scene; LAY-1 did neither after the warp, so that late spawn is inferred from
code, not measured. No green lane contradicts this: FAR-1 (Ike) and FAR-2 (Duna) read
`compared>=1` at the Space Center on vessels their saves already held, not on a Space Center end
spawn.

Fix direction. Split the structural predicate into a render half and a spawn half: a recording
with at least two points whose only reject is the off-Kerbin first point still runs the past-end
spawn path (gated like the #433 detour: `currentUT > rec.EndUT && !historicalNeverReplayed`, plus
the loop first-run spawn), and every skip logs once per recording (Verbose, `KSCSpawn`). The
Landed / Splashed placement then goes through `SpawnAtKscEnd`, which already works from
`protoVessels` in any scene. Not fixed here, because it changes the Space Center's behaviour for
every far-body recording: before landing it, read the far-body lanes that sit at the Space Center
past an off-Kerbin end (FAR-1's DD1, which the fixture already holds, must be adopted, not
duplicated; V20K's Jool -> Kerbin recording stays deferred by #171; the moon loop lanes), add
xUnit cells over the split predicate (`IsKscStructurallyEligible` is `internal static`) and
re-fly them with LAY-1.

Fix: `ParsekKSC.ClassifyKscStructuralRoute` splits the old `IsKscStructurallyEligible` into
a draw half and a spawn half: `Render` (two or more points, first point on Kerbin; the old
predicate, now `IsKscDrawEligible`), `SpawnOnly` (two or more points, first point off Kerbin;
the spawn half is every route but `Skip`) and `Skip` (null or fewer than two points: no ghost, no spawn, the #433
premise kept for the case it fits). A `SpawnOnly` recording is never drawn (ghosts and overlap
ghosts torn down, `ShouldShowInKSC` and the init `eligible` count unchanged) and goes through
`RunKscSpawnOnlyDispatch`, which makes the calls the render branches would make past the end;
the per-recording choice is the pure `DecideKscStructuralDispatch` (route plus
`DecideKscSpawnOnlyAction`) the Update loop calls: a loop-driven recording (its own LoopPlayback or a Mission
loop-unit member) through `TryLoopFirstRunSpawnKsc`, any other once past its end unless
historical (BUG-B) through `TrySpawnAtRecordingEnd`, the #433 detour's rule. No new spawn rule:
every refusal (chain mid-segment, non-leaf, debris, branch > 0, superseded / retired (checked
before the split), already spawned, Destroyed / Recovered terminals, the per-scene attempt
latch) stays in `ShouldSpawnAtKscEnd` / `ShouldSpawnAtRecordingEnd`, which have no body rule,
and the #171 Orbiting / Docked deferral keeps every far-body orbit to the flight scene.
The ghost-chain hold-back (review of b19930a2): the Tracking Station
(`ShouldSpawnAtTrackingStationEnd` -> `ShouldSuppressSpawnForChain`) and flight
(`ComposeFlightFinalNeedsSpawn`) hold back the spawn of an intermediate ghost chain link (a
vessel a later committed tree docks to or boards: the chain tip continues it), but the Space
Center never did, for Kerbin recordings either, so such a leaf spawned there with a fresh pid
and the tip spawned again later (`ChainTipStaleVessel` probes only the claimed pids): a
duplicate the split would have widened to off-Kerbin leaves. `ShouldSpawnAtKscEnd(rec, ut,
chains)` now applies `ShouldSuppressSpawnForChain` after the spawn decision (reason
`KscSpawnSkipIntermediateGhostChainLink`), for every route; `TrySpawnAtRecordingEnd` passes
`GhostChainWalker.ComputeAllGhostChains(CommittedTrees, ut)`, built at most once per Update pass
