## V22T-TS-ADOPTION-BRANCH-UNFLOWN: no committed lane flies the Tracking Station's adoption of an already-live vessel [FILED 2026-11-16 from V22T's red on the 1.0.2 release flight; V22T RE-PINNED AND RE-FLOWN GREEN, branch `item29-v22t-repin`. OPEN: the coverage gap]

What happened. `V22T-kerbin-splashdown-ts-arrival` red PARSEK-FAIL(expectation) on the v1.0.2
release build (2026-11-16 23:12Z) on one required token, `Tracking-station handoff skipped
duplicate spawn for #N "Kerbal X" ... real vessel pid=P already exists`. The product is right:
since LOAD-SPLIT-SPAWN-STAMP-ON-HEAD (2026-11-14) `RecordingOptimizer.MoveChainSpawnStampsToTip`
moves the spawn stamp of `kerbin-splashdown-recorded`'s split head (`28b6e543...`, pid
2708531065) onto the terminal tip at load (`Chain spawn stamp moved to the tip: ... spawnedPid=
2708531065 vessel='Kerbal X'`), so the Tracking Station's eligibility screen
(`ShouldSpawnAtTrackingStationEnd` -> `GhostPlaybackLogic.ShouldSpawnAtRecordingEnd`, "already
spawned") skips the tip silently and `RunTrackingStationSpawnHandoffForEligibleIndex` never runs
for it. The run printed no `Tracking-station handoff spawned` / `resolved` line and its save holds
one real Kerbal X (pid 2708531065, LANDED). The old line was a side effect of the stamp sitting on
the head.

Done. V22T now requires the stamp-move line (head id and pid literal, the chain and tip ids as
regex) and forbids `Tracking-station handoff spawned #N "Kerbal X" pid=`, so it still gates the
player promise (no second Kerbal X in the Tracking Station). Its D13 `pid-dedup` claim is dropped,
because the cell is the handoff's ADOPTION branch (`alreadyMaterialized` in
`RunTrackingStationSpawnHandoffForEligibleIndex`: `RealVesselExistsForRecording` finds the
recording's launch live, stamps `VesselSpawned` / `SpawnedVesselPersistentId`, removes the ghost
presence) and V22T no longer reaches it. Coverage 250 of 251 -> 249 of 251. Re-flown PASS
`2026-11-16_2343_V22T-kerbin-splashdown-ts-arrival` (attempt 1, 74 s, v1.0.2 release DLL sha256
431dd6c5...): the stamp-move line once, zero `Tracking-station handoff spawned`, recordings 9.

Still open. No committed lane flies the adoption branch. Its predicate is unit-tested
(`TrackingStationSpawnTests.ShouldSkipTrackingStationDuplicateSpawn_*`); the branch body (the
stamp, the ghost-presence removal, the map-focus restore, the Info line) is not. A lane for it
needs, in the Tracking Station: a committed recording that is the terminal tip of its chain (or
not a chain piece), past its end UT, NOT stamped (`VesselSpawned` false, `SpawnedVesselPersistentId`
0, and no earlier piece of the same launch carrying a stamp the load-time move would hand it),
whose `VesselPersistentId` names a real vessel live in the save with the same launch guid
(`VesselLaunchIdentity.LiveVesselIsRecordedLaunch`), and not superseded or retired. Then require
the `skipped duplicate spawn` line and forbid `Tracking-station handoff spawned` for that vessel,
and re-claim D13 `pid-dedup` off it. A save-edited twin of an existing fixture (clear the stamp on
a single-piece landed recording whose vessel is in FLIGHTSTATE) is the likely cheapest host. Read
first whether a save load can deliver such a recording at all: LOAD-SPLIT-SPAWN-STAMP-ON-HEAD
records that `ParsekScenario.OnLoadPhaseAutoUnreserveCrewPastEndUT` set `VesselSpawned` (with no
pid) on an unstamped recording past its end, which would make the Tracking Station skip it as
already spawned before the adoption branch. If no load path reaches the branch, say so here and
rule on the cell (retire it, or move the claim to an in-game test that drives the branch).

## AIR1-GLIDE-SLOPE-STEEPER-THAN-PLANNED: AIR-1's approach glides at about 8.6 deg, not the planned 6 [FILED 2026-11-16 from AIR-1's first green flight, run `2026-11-16_2218` (diagnostics on branch `forge-logs-2026-11-16-air1d`). OPEN; low, harness only, cosmetic for the lane]

The Mallard's final glide toward the touchdown point came out at about 8.6 deg instead of the
`glideSlopeDeg = 6` the mission flies, crossing the aim point at 120 m and splashing down
about 1.4 km past it (touchedDown `missMeters` 1376). The lane passed: the splashdown is in open
water either way and nothing gates the slope. Worth a look only if a later lane needs a precise
touchdown point (a runway landing): the pitch loop's glide target or the throttle on the final.

A log reader's note from the same flight, not a defect: while the Mallard was airborne the
active recorder's finalizer cache logged `[FinalizerCache] Refresh accepted: ... terminal=Destroyed
terminalUT=...` (and `status=Fresh terminal=Destroyed` in the refresh summary) on its periodic
refreshes. That is the ballistic extrapolator's FORECAST of where an unpowered plane would end
if the recording stopped at that moment, not the recording's terminal: the committed recording
finalized `terminal=Splashed`, and the produced save holds `Splashed 1`, `Destroyed 0`.

## ~~EVA-SWITCH-STOP-DROPS-OPEN-SECTION~~: an EVA leg that ends by boarding loses its last track section [FILED 2026-11-16 from the D5 residual review (vessel-switch stop distance, branch `fix-residuals-contract-d5`), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-16, branch fix-board-merge-open-section; xUnit; no lane gates it yet; medium (the ghost of a kerbal's walk or jetpack flight to the hatch is wrong after a save)]

What was wrong. `FlightRecorder.HandleVesselSwitchDuringRecording` (the ChainToVessel decision:
an EVA recording whose active vessel is now a non-EVA vessel) was the one stop that never closed
the open TrackSection. StopRecording, StopRecordingForChainBoundary and ForceStop close it in
`FinalizeRecordingState`, TransitionToBackground closes it itself. `BuildCaptureRecording` deep
copies only the CLOSED sections, while the flat Points carry every sample of the open one, so
`FlushStoppedRecorderIntoMergeParent` -> `AppendCapturedDataToRecording` (confirmed board) and
`FinalizeTreeRecordings` -> `FlushRecorderToTreeRecording` (unconfirmed board, or a plain switch
from an EVA kerbal to a vessel, which is the same ChainToVessel decision) both handed the EVA leg
a flat tail no section covers. Nothing later adds it back: the stopped recorder is dropped on the
board merge, and `FlushRecorderIntoActiveTreeForSerialization`'s section checkpoint only runs for
the recorder the tree still holds. The codec then writes the uncovered tail as flat points
(`AppendSafeFlatFallbackTailOutsideFrameSections` / the plain flat path) and, after a load,
`FlatPointFrameDispatch.Classify` reads a point no section holds as body-fixed: a Relative open
section (a kerbal walking to a hatch near the vessel, the common case) replays its anchor-local
metres as degrees of latitude and longitude, and an EVA that never closed a section saves with
no section at all. An Absolute open section keeps real lat/lon but no section, environment or
frame metadata for the end of the leg. No analyzer invariant checks flat points outside every
section, so nothing reported it. The committed fixture `cs-career-mun4` (from CS-6c) shows both
Mun-orbit EVA legs ending about 1.8 s before their stamped board UT (`debce1a4...` last frame
157914.246, `explicitEndUT` 157916.006), consistent with this but not proven by it.

Fix: the switch stop calls `FlightRecorder.CloseOpenTrackSectionForVesselSwitchStop(UT)` before
`BuildCaptureRecording`, so the capture (and the recorder lists the unconfirmed path flushes) holds
the leg's last section. Only the section is closed: no terminal events, RELATIVE state untouched,
the confirmed and unconfirmed paths otherwise as before. One Info line `Vessel-switch stop: closed
the open TrackSection before the capture (...)`, or a Verbose `no open TrackSection to close`.
With the D5 residual's `openSectionForDistance` (branch `fix-residuals-contract-d5`) the open
section is now already closed when the capture is built, so the switch stop no longer passes that
argument and the distance walks the closed list, which holds the section. Tests: `VesselSwitchStopOpenSectionTests`
(three witnesses of the unfixed shape through a codec round trip, open Relative / open Absolute /
whole EVA in one section; the fix for each; the no-open-section no-op; and a source-order gate
that the close precedes `BuildCaptureRecording` in the switch stop). Lane that would prove it:
EVA-2-orbital-board or EVA-1-pad-flag with a report-only check that the EVA leg's last section
ends at its board UT and no flat point lies outside a section.

## ~~RECORDER-GEAR-SUSPENSION-AS-ROBOTICS~~: a plane rolling on its landing gear records the suspension as robotics motion, about 22 start / stop events a second [FILED 2026-11-16 from AIR-1's first flight, runs `2026-11-16_1955` and `_1956_a2` (diagnostics on branch `forge-logs-2026-11-16-air1`, `diag/<runId>/KSP.log.parsek-lines.txt`), by log and code reading. FIXED 2026-11-16, branch `gear-suspension-fix`, landed on `claude/project-thread-vpr29t`; xUnit; GS-6 re-pinned (two suspension-fed applier tokens out, the skip line in) and re-flown green 2026-11-16 `2026-11-16_2130`; low (recording size and log volume, plus a wrong ghost gear pose on replay)]

What the log shows: while the stock Mallard rolled on the Runway, the active recorder wrote
`Part event: RoboticMotionStarted` / `RoboticMotionStopped` for its three gear parts
(`GearMedium` x2, `SmallGearBay`), every one on `midx=0 module=ModuleWheelSuspension
source=suspensionPos deadband=0.003 ... moving=inferred` (the `Robotics: tracking` lines).
Counted from the Parsek lines: run `_1955` 484 events in 22.1 s (21:56:01.892 .. 21:56:24.004:
GearMedium 207 started + 207 stopped, SmallGearBay 35 + 35), run `_1956_a2` 466 in 22.2 s
(204 + 204, 29 + 29); about 22 a second, and zero `RoboticPositionSample` events. A Started is
often followed by its Stopped on the next physics frame (`21:56:01.892` / `.895`), with values
around 1.34 .. 1.51 (the `suspensionPos` magnitude). Each event is also one Verbose KSP.log line.

Why: `FlightRecorder.CheckRoboticState` (and the background twin in
`BackgroundRecorder.PartEventPolling.cs`) polls every module `IsRoboticModuleName` accepts, which
includes the wheel modules; only the DERIVED wheel visuals (`ModuleWheelMotor*` spin and
`ModuleWheelSteering`, `IsDerivedWheelVisualModuleName`) skip emission, so
`ModuleWheelSuspension` still emits. Its position is the magnitude of the `suspensionPos` vector
(`TryClassifyWheelRoboticPositionFromFieldValues`) with a 0.0025 deadband, and stock has no
moving flag for it, so `CheckRoboticTransition` infers motion: moving when the value differs from
the LAST EMITTED value by at least max(deadband * 0.25, 0.0001) = 0.6 mm. Each Started / Stopped
stores the current value as the new reference, so gear suspension jittering by about a millimetre
on a rolling plane crosses that threshold on one frame and not on the next: a Started, then a
Stopped one frame later, then a Started again. The 0.25 * deadband motion test is the noise
gate, and it sits below the suspension's own jitter. A rover's `ModuleWheelSuspension` goes
through the same code (not counted here: no rover lane log was read for this entry).

Against the recording design principle (record threshold crossings, debounce noise, nothing
that is not visible at playback speed): millimetre suspension travel on a runway is not visible
on a ghost, and the pairs carry no state a ghost needs. Likely fix, in order of preference:
(1) treat `ModuleWheelSuspension` like the derived wheel visuals: keep it in
`cachedRoboticModules` (so `moduleIndex` numbering stays in lockstep with the ghost builder) but
skip its emission in both recorders, and let playback leave the suspension at rest or derive it
(legacy recordings keep their events; playback stays tolerant); or (2) if suspension travel is
wanted, debounce it: a Started only after the value has moved a full deadband (not 0.25 of it)
from a HELD reference, a Stopped only after it stayed within the deadband for a dwell (say
0.5 s), and a coarser suspension deadband (centimetres, not 2.5 mm). Either way: an xUnit cell
over `CheckRoboticTransition` fed a 1 mm frame-to-frame jitter must emit no events, and the next
AIR-1 flight's KSP.log should show zero `RoboticMotion*` lines for the gear parts.

Playback, read while fixing: the events were NOT harmless. The ghost builder gives
`ModuleWheelSuspension` a `Linear` robotic info on the `suspensionTransformName` transform, and
`GhostPlaybackLogic.ApplyRobotic*` posed it at `stowedPos + up * value`. Decompiled,
`suspensionPos` is `suspensionTransform.localPosition` (sentinel `-Vector3.one` before the first
update), so `value` is the length of an absolute position (1.34 .. 1.51 on the GearMedium, 1.73
for the sentinel), not a travel: every replayed Started lifted the ghost's wheel by about its own
position length. So a debounce (option 2) would have kept a wrong pose, and option (1) is the fix.

Fix: option (1), recorder and playback. `FlightRecorder.IsWheelSuspensionModuleName` joins the
derived wheel visuals in the shared emission gate `IsRoboticEmissionSkippedModuleName`, applied by
both recorders through one `ShouldEmitRoboticEvents` head (one `Robotics: wheel suspension not
recorded for ...` Verbose line per module key, `[Recorder]` or `[BgRecorder] ... (bg vessel N)`;
the derived-visual line keeps its wording). The module stays in `CacheRoboticModules` /
`TryBuildRoboticInfos`, so the robotic module index keeps its lockstep. Playback:
`ApplyRoboticEvent` returns the new outcome `IgnoredRecordedSignal` (`reason=ignored-recorded-signal`
on the applier line) for a suspension info, so legacy recordings keep their events on disk but the
ghost gear stays at its rest pose. Breaking Ground hinges, pistons, rotation servos and rotors go
through the unchanged path. Tests: `GearSuspensionRoboticGateTests` (an AIR-1-shaped 1 mm jitter
over 22 s emits zero events in both recorders' loop and logs the skip once; the ungated core emits
over 200; a hinge sweep still records Started / samples / Stopped; playback ignores a legacy
suspension event and still applies a hinge event). The synthetic `Part Showcase - Wheel Dynamics
Gear Fixed` row drives moduleIndex 0 (the suspension) and now holds still at playback. HARNESS:
`GS-6-part-event-applier-sweep` required `apply family=RoboticMotionStarted|Stopped surface=robotic
... applied=[1-9]`, which only its landing legs' `ModuleWheelSuspension` fed: the `Kerbal X Sweep`
craft carries no Breaking Ground servo (stock-minimal does link SquadExpansion; H32 flies
`hinge.01`), so those two tokens could no longer match. GS-6 was re-pinned in the same change:
both tokens deleted and the regression guard `\[Recorder\] Robotics: wheel suspension not recorded
for 'landingLeg1'` added as a required token (38 required). GS-6 RE-FLOWN 2026-11-16:
`2026-11-16_2130_GS-6-part-event-applier-sweep` PASS attempt 1 (543 s, automation DLL sha256
81a33bc9, main after #2653), expectations 0 mismatches, armed rewind save-structure, ghostLifecycle
8/8 balanced, logValidate / analyzer / anomaly sweep green; the guard matched (three skip lines, one
per `landingLeg1`, zero `RoboticMotion` lines). One report-only stock NullReferenceException in
`FlightCamera.Startup`. AIR-1's third flight (runs `2026-11-16_2126` and `_2128_a2`, diagnostics on
branch `forge-logs-2026-11-16-air1c`) read the same on the Mallard: zero `RoboticMotion` lines for
its gear and the three expected skip lines (`SmallGearBay`, `GearMedium` x2) on each attempt.
The background recorder formats its `(bg vessel N)` suffix only inside the once-per-key log
branch (`ShouldEmitRoboticEvents` takes the vessel pid), so the per-frame poll allocates nothing.

## ~~MISSION-LOOP-LAUNCH-BODY-PREFERS-LATER-APPROACH~~: a looped mission that starts in orbit is timed around a later moon it passes low over [CLOSED 2026-11-16: V43M flew green on its first flight with the fix, `2026-11-16_1803_V43M-vall-tylo-player-loop` PASS attempt 1 (46 s, automation DLL built from 866ac123, sha256 prefix 8dfcbc5e; every verifier green), KSP.log reading launch moon Vall, constraints=3, `Solve: dominant=Tylo method=dominant-intercept residual=2.18 withinTol=yes` and `PhaseLock APPLIED ... P=211926.36 ... zeroDrift=yes scheduleWithinTol=yes`. FILED 2026-11-16 from V43M's first flight `2026-11-16_1726_V43M-vall-tylo-player-loop` (PC, parallel run `moon-loops-2026-11-16d`, DLL unchanged since PR #2638, PARSEK-FAIL(expectation) attempt 1, 58 s; diagnostics on branch `forge-logs-2026-11-16d`, folder `diag/2026-11-16_1726_V43M-vall-tylo-player-loop/`). FIXED 2026-11-16, branch `claude/project-thread-vpr29t`; xUnit; V43M re-pinned, awaiting PC flight; low (the loop still phase-locks, on the wrong launch moon)]

The `vall-tylo-recorded` tree 91205f57 is one vessel's chain: the root ef182ffd starts IN ORBIT
around Vall (a 2.6 s Absolute coast, then Vall, Jool and Tylo orbit checkpoints from UT
28,896,852.5), the second segment 6a000db2 is one 5.4 s Approach section at Tylo (~87 km, UT
29,178,745.6 - 29,178,751.0) and the tip a0ba73e4 is Tylo coast and burn sections. V43M expected
`ExtractConstraints: moon-rooted frame launchMoon=Vall ...` and `launchBody=Vall ... constraints=2
[Orbital(Tylo) same-parent ...; Orbital(Vall) same-parent ...`. KSP logged
`launchMoon=Tylo planet=Jool` and `launchBody=Tylo ut0=28896849.902240183 support=Supported
constraints=3 [Rotation(Tylo) P=211926.358 off=281895.72; Orbital(Vall) same-parent P=105962.09
off=2.62; Orbital(Tylo) same-parent P=211926.358 off=2.62]`; the lock itself read `PhaseLock
APPLIED ... P=211926.358 method=dominant-intercept ... fixedCadenceWithinTol=yes`.
Cause: `MissionPeriodicity.ExtractConstraints` sets `launchBody = earliestSurfaceBody ??
earliestOrbitBody`, so ANY surface-class section (Atmospheric, Surface*, and Approach, which
`IsRotationConstrainingEnvironment` counts) out-ranks the orbit fallback whatever its time. A
mission that starts in orbit and later dips into Approach over another body is read as launched
from that body: here Tylo became the launch moon, Vall a sibling SOI entry, and the launch moon's
phase was pinned at the Vall orbit start instead of the Vall SOI exit.
Fix: the launch body is the body of the EARLIEST included segment
(`MissionPeriodicity.ResolveLaunchBody`): the earliest surface-class start and the earliest orbit
start are compared and the earlier one names it, a tie going to the surface (an ascent and its
orbit can share a UT). A surface launch starts with its ascent, so no surface-launch answer moves
(every existing extraction pin is unchanged). When the two bodies differ the extractor logs
`ExtractConstraints: launch body <B> from the earliest segment (first orbit <B> off=..., first
surface <C> off=...)`. On this tree it now reads launch moon Vall and `constraints=3
[Rotation(Tylo) P=211926.358 off=281895.72; Orbital(Tylo) same-parent P=211926.358 off=261721.52;
Orbital(Vall) same-parent P=105962.089 off=10191.44]`: Rotation(Tylo) stays under rule 2 (the
Approach arc is body-fixed and Tylo has an inertial orbit in the set) and, Tylo being tidally
locked, shares Orbital(Tylo)'s period; Vall is pinned at its SOI exit. Solve still reads
`dominant-intercept` at P = P_Tylo within tolerance, and the zero-drift schedule anchors on
Orbital(Vall). Pinned by `MissionPeriodicityTests.ResolveLaunchBody_TruthTable`,
`Extract_VallOrbitStartThenTyloApproach_LaunchBodyStaysVall` (the fixture's shape at its real UTs)
and `Build_VallOrbitStartThenTyloApproach_LocksOnTyloWithVallInTolerance`; all three red with the
old rule. V43M now requires the launch-body line, `launchMoon=Vall` and the three-constraint
summary, and forbids `launchMoon=Tylo`.
Closed 2026-11-16: V43M flew green on the fix (`2026-11-16_1803`, PASS attempt 1, 46 s, DLL 8dfcbc5e),
logging `ExtractConstraints: launch body Vall from the earliest segment (first orbit Vall off=2.62,
first surface Tylo off=281895.72)`, `launchMoon=Vall planet=Jool`, `launchBody=Vall ... constraints=3
[Rotation(Tylo) ...; Orbital(Tylo) same-parent ...; Orbital(Vall) same-parent ...]`, `Solve:
dominant=Tylo method=dominant-intercept residual=2.18 withinTol=yes` and `PhaseLock APPLIED ...
P=211926.36 ... fixedCadenceResidual=2.18 withinTol=yes zeroDrift=yes scheduleWithinTol=yes
scheduleWorstResidual=39.24`, the xUnit prediction.

## ~~MISSION-LOOP-LAUNCH-BODY-PHYSICS-COAST-UNCOUNTED~~: a loop that starts in orbit off rails can still be timed around a later moon it passes low over [FILED 2026-11-16 from the review of PR #2640. FIXED 2026-11-16, branch fix-loop-launch-body-exo; xUnit; no lane covers it; low (needs a mission that never warps before its first Approach)]

`MissionPeriodicity.ExtractConstraints`' orbit side of the launch-body comparison counts only
`OrbitSegments` and `OrbitalCheckpoint` checkpoints, never physics-frame Absolute `ExoBallistic` /
`ExoPropulsive` sections. A mission that starts in orbit, stays off rails (no time warp) and whose
first surface-class section is an Approach over another body before any on-rails segment still
names the Approach body as its launch body. V43M escaped this only because its root goes on rails
2.6 s in.
Fix: `ExtractConstraints` also scans each member's physics-frame (Absolute) `ExoBallistic` /
`ExoPropulsive` sections inside the trimmed window (`ScanOffRailsExoSectionsWithinWindow`) and
keeps the single earliest start and its body. The six-argument `ResolveLaunchBody` takes the
earlier of that and the earliest OrbitSegment as the orbit side (a tie keeps the OrbitSegment),
then compares it with the earliest surface-class segment as before (surface wins a tie). The Exo
sections never enter the per-body orbit dictionary, so the SOI rules and rule 2's hand-off are
unchanged. Relative and OrbitalCheckpoint sections are skipped. When the off-rails start names a
body the first OrbitSegment does not, the launch-body line gains `, first off-rails coast <B>
off=...` (an absent side prints `<none>`); V43M's line is unchanged (its coast and first
checkpoint are both Vall). A scan of every committed fixture's `.prec.txt` (whole save, untrimmed)
finds no launch body that moves. Pinned by `MissionPeriodicityTests.ResolveLaunchBody_WithOffRailsCoast_TruthTable`,
`Extract_OffRailsVallStartThenTyloApproach_LaunchBodyIsVall`,
`Extract_OffRailsVallStartBeforeOnRailsJoolAndTylo_IsMoonRootedAtVall` (both red with the Exo
feed removed) and the mirror `Extract_TyloApproachBeforeOffRailsVallCoast_LaunchBodyStaysTylo`.

## ~~ROUTE-HELD-ROCK-HARVEST-UNCOUNTED~~: Ore drilled from a Klaw-held rock was not counted as harvest, so the route was refused [FILED 2026-11-15 from the AST-3 flight `2026-11-15_2035_AST-3-klaw-mine-route` (PR #2633; results branch `ast-flights-2026-11-15`, folder `ast-klaw-2026-11-15d`). FIXED 2026-11-15, same PR; xUnit; AST-3 re-flown green 2026-11-15 (folder ast-klaw-2026-11-15e); medium (a rock-mining route could never be made)]

What the player saw: launch a miner, grab a rock with the Klaw, drill it, release it, dock at a
station and move the Ore across. Creating a route from that flight was refused: `RouteAnalysis
rejected: undocked-start origin (harvest-refined) ... reason=delivered-exceeds-harvested
resource=Ore delivered=0.7994 harvested=0`, although the hold leg carried the harvest window.

Cause: the harvest gain check anchors its backward walk at the arrival leg and never crossed an
Undock / Dock branch point, so the anchor was the leg after the release. The drilled Ore was
already aboard at that leg's start (zero gain), and the hold leg's harvest window sat before the
anchor and was excluded, so the harvested total was 0 and the undocked-start gate refused.

Fix: `RouteHarvestAnalysis.FindGainAnchorIndex` crosses the grab and the release of a structural
grapple hold (`IsStructuralGrappleSeam`): an Undock out of a leg, and then that leg's own Dock,
whose run manifest scope is the window scope plus exactly the endpoint parts of one of its own
Grapple connection windows whose endpoint has no resource storage at either corner (a rock;
a derelict or colony with tanks keeps the old anchor, or its own converters' output would read
as transport harvest), with the bare transport on the other side. Both seams are crossed or
neither: a transport that arrives still holding the object keeps its anchor on the hold, and a
grab from a larger vessel keeps the post-release anchor. In AST-3 the anchor becomes the launch
leg and the drill window counts. A docking-port hold, or a hold that also carries other parts,
still stops the walk. Tests: `RouteHarvestAnalysisComputeTests` (six anchor-walk cells) and
`RouteHarvestAnalysisTests.CheckTransportGains_OreDrilledOnAHeldRock_CountsAsHarvest`.

## ~~REFLY-ATTEMPT-STALE-END-UT~~: a flown Re-Fly attempt can be saved with its end UT at its start [FILED 2026-11-15 from the AST-4 reading run `2026-11-15_1941_AST-4-klaw-refly` (PR #2633, fcceccd; results branch `ast-flights-2026-11-15`, folder `ast-klaw-2026-11-15b`). FIXED 2026-11-16, branch `fix-refly-stale-end-ut`; xUnit; low (saved metadata; one latent leaf misread)]

What was seen (report-only, the lane passed): in the produced save the Re-Fly attempt recording
reads `explicitEndUT = 358.01` (its start UT) and `pointCount = 1`, while its `.prec` sidecar
holds an orbit segment from UT 358.0 to 1097.5 plus one point at 1097.5. The log carries the
observation-only `outcome=unbound-refly-provisional reason=refly-provisional-has-no-trajectory-at-save`
at the invoke's save. Open question: is the end UT written once at that early save and never
refreshed after the attempt flies, and does anything (playback end, spawn, Missions duration)
read the stale value?
Cause. The sidecar is right and `pointCount = 1` is right (it counts flat points; the one point
at 1097.53 is the only one, the coast is an orbit segment). The stale field is `explicitEndUT`,
and it is not Re-Fly specific: the quickload-resume trim (`ParsekScenario.TrimRecordingPastUT`)
stamps the cutoff as the explicit end of the open recording it resumes (log: `Quickload resume
prep: activeRec='rec_d494...' cutoffUT=358.01 preTrimEndUT=0.00`, after the invoke's own save),
and nothing lifted it as the recorder flew on: neither active flush
(`FlushRecorderToTreeRecording`, `FlushRecorderIntoActiveTreeForSerialization`) touches
`ExplicitEndUT` (the background recorder does), and finalization only fills an unset one. Every
later save wrote 358.01. The `unbound-refly-provisional` Warn is unrelated: it fires on the
invoke's save, 40 ms before `RestoreActiveTreeFromPending` binds the recorder.

What read it. `Recording.EndUT` takes the later of the explicit end and the trajectory bounds, so
playback end, ghost retire, spawn timing, Missions and merge-dialog duration and the ledger
(`Committed recording 'rec_d494...' ... endUT=1100.0`) all read the real end; the player saw
nothing in this run. The raw-field readers did not: `RecordingTree.ChildBranchLeavesVesselLineOpen`
reads an explicit end at or before a Breakup / JointBreak / Launch branch as "closed at the
split", so a resumed flight that shed debris after the resume and flew on was not its vessel's
line end (spawnable-leaf, background-map and destruction-gate queries, Missions terminal rows),
and `ParsekFlightMergeFlow.TryGetFinalTrackSection` picked the section at the cutoff instead of
the last one (endpoint segment-phase fallback). Without a hydrated trajectory `EndUT` would also
fall back to the cutoff.

Fix: `ParsekFlight.LiftStampedExplicitEndToTrajectoryEnd`, called by both active flushes after
they append, lifts an explicit end that is set, not terminal-stamped and not parent-anchored
debris up to the recorded trajectory end (Verbose `Explicit end lifted to the recorded data:`).
`EndUT` never moves (it already took the later value); an unset end stays unset. Tests:
`ResumedRecordingExplicitEndTests` (the AST-4 shape through the trim, the real stop flush, the
codec write, the final-section lookup, the breakup line-end case and the four guards). Live proof
if wanted: AST-4 again, whose produced save should read `explicitEndUT = 1100.03...` on the
attempt and whose KSP.log should carry `Explicit end lifted to the recorded data: rec=rec_...
context=FlushRecorderIntoActiveTreeForSerialization oldExplicitEndUT=358.01`.

## ~~ROCK-GHOST-PREFAB-MESH~~: a grabbed asteroid or comet replays as the part prefab's small placeholder lump [FILED 2026-11-15 from the H42 flight log of 2026-10-12. FIXED 2026-11-15, branch `ast-ghost-visual`; xUnit + in-game `ClawCouple`; H42 and H41 re-flown green 2026-11-15; low (visual only)]

What the player sees: a 40 m asteroid on a ghost ship's claw, a released asteroid's own replay and
the hold ghost of a claimed rock after a rewind (`ClaimedVesselHoldGhost`, built from the despawn
snapshot) all showed the PotatoRoid prefab's default lump at scale 1; a comet likewise, with no
tail. The H42 log read `Part 'PotatoRoid' pid=102222: modelRoot='model' modelScale=(1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
... 1 MeshRenderers` and `potatoRoidMesh=yes`: the ghost cloned the placeholder.

Cause (decompiled, KSP 1.12.5). Stock builds the rock at runtime. `ModuleAsteroid.OnStart` runs
`Random.InitState(seed)`, `radius = paPrefab.radius * Random.Range(minRadiusMultiplier,
maxRadiusMultiplier)` (config 0.75 / 1.25 by default), `paPrefab = Resources.Load<ProceduralAsteroid>
(prefabBaseURL)` (`"Procedural/PA_" + DiscoveryInfo.objectSize` when empty), `paPrefab.Generate(seed,
radius, part.transform, Rangefinder, OnGenComplete, currentState == 2)`, then destroys
`FindModelTransform("potatoroid")`. Persisted MODULE fields: `seed`, `AsteroidName`,
`prefabBaseURL`, `currentState` (comet: `seed`, `CometName`, `CometType`, `prefabBaseURL`,
`currentState`, `utFragmentSpawned`). The radius is not persisted; it is a function of the seed.
`ModuleComet.OnStart` is the same with `ProceduralComet.Generate(..., optimizeCollider, isSecondary)`
for a `Procedural/PC_` URL and an instantiated hand-made prefab otherwise (its
`radius = cometVessel.radius` is overwritten by the same draw on the next line). `Generate` only
creates Unity objects (a `Visual` child with MeshFilter + MeshRenderer, a `Collider` child whose
`SpaceObjectCollider.Setup` starts a coroutine that first yields a frame), so it runs on a detached
object; `SetupPartParameters`, which needs a live Part, is a separate call. The comet tail / coma
(`CometVFXController`) live in scaled space and read `hostVessel`, its orbit driver, `CometVessel`
and the sun, so they cannot run without a live vessel.

Fix: `SpaceObjectGhostVisual.TryPlan` (pure half `SpaceObjectGhostModel`) repeats stock's draw from
the snapshot MODULE node with Unity's Random state saved and restored, calls the prefab's public
`Generate` with parent null, copies the visual mesh, deactivates and destroys the generated object
(no collider is ever built) and caches the mesh per (part, URL, seed, state) for the process
(a failed generation is cached too, so a rebuilt ghost goes straight to its fallback).
`GhostVisualBuilder.AddPartVisuals` skips the cloned `potatoroid` renderer and adds the rock at the
part origin, as stock does. Fallbacks: `scaled-prefab` (generator failed; placeholder scaled to the
drawn radius), `prefab-lump` (no seed, `seed = -1`, non-procedural comet URL or no procedural
prefab). `ProceduralComet.Generate` sorts its mod list after using it, so one throwaway generation
per comet prefab per session puts the ghost on the order stock's own comets use. Log:
`RockGhost built: path=stock-generator|scaled-prefab|prefab-lump kind=... seed=... url=...
radius=... cache=hit|miss|hit-failed [reason=...] [cometVfx=skipped-needs-live-comet-vessel]`. Tests:
`SpaceObjectGhostModelTests` (MODULE parse, URL default, path choice, multiplier source, placeholder
scale, cache key, culture-invariant line); the generator `VesselSnapshotBuilder.ClawedAsteroidShip`
now writes the ModuleAsteroid fields and `LoneComet` the ModuleComet ones; the in-game
`ClawedAsteroidSnapshot_SurvivesGhostVisualBuild` now asserts the asteroid and a lone comet ghost
carry the generated rock (no placeholder, no collider) with bounds within 1% per axis of the rock
stock's own `Generate` builds for the seed. ClawCouple keeps 2 cells. H41 flown 2026-11-15 printed
`roidGhostRenderers=2` (the generated rock beside the one prefab renderer the ghost still clones, which
is not under a `potatoroid` transform), so its pin is `[12]` and the cell now checks every kept prefab
renderer against the live rock part (`droppedByStock=0`): if stock destroyed it, the ghost shows a lump
stock does not, and the cell fails.

Residue: (a) H42 flew green on this fix 2026-11-15 (`2026-11-15_1904`); H41 re-flies with the live-rock
check. (b) Not reproduced: the comet tail, coma, geysers and near dust; map /
Tracking Station ghosts (ProtoVessel stand-ins, unchanged). (c) Unverified: a secondary
(`currentState = 2`) comet's glow colour is drawn after the collider meshes; the ghost passes
`optimizeCollider = false` (the persisted value lives on the `CometVessel` vessel module, not the
part), so if stock built that comet with the optimized collider and the collider build consumes
Random draws, the ghost's glow colour can differ. The mesh does not depend on it.

## ~~ROCK-SPAWN-BOUNDS-TOO-SMALL~~: the spawn space check sized a grabbed asteroid or comet like any 2.5 m part [FILED 2026-11-15 by the asteroid / comet review (owner rulings 2026-11-15), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-15, branch `ast-fixes`; xUnit; no lane spawns a rock-carrying ship; low (a big rock could materialize inside a nearby vessel)]

What the player saw: a recorded ship holding a grabbed rock becomes real at its tip (and a
released rock at its own tip). `SpawnCollisionDetector.ComputeVesselBounds` gives every snapshot
part the same 1.25 m half extent, so a ship carrying a 40 m class E asteroid was checked for
room as a few metres and could spawn into a loaded vessel inside the rock. The same bounds feed
the Real Spawn Control time-jump placement.

Decompile (KSP 1.12.5). No rock radius is persisted. `ModuleAsteroid` / `ModuleComet` persist
`prefabBaseURL`, set on first start to `"Procedural/PA_" + objectSize` (comet `"Procedural/PC_"`),
and build the rock at `prefab.radius x Random(minRadiusMultiplier 0.75, maxRadiusMultiplier
1.25)`, then a procedural mesh whose PQS mods add relief scaled by the radius. The class radii
are `DiscoveryInfo.GetClassRadius`: A 3.24, B 5.4, C 9, D 15, E 25, F 41.7, G 69.5, H 115.8,
I 193 m. The VESSEL's `DISCOVERY size` is the int class (`DiscoveryInfo.Save`), the rock's own
only on a bare rock vessel (a ship keeps its own discovery info).

Fix: `SpawnCollisionDetector.ResolvePartHalfExtent` sizes a rock part (part name PotatoRoid /
PotatoComet or a ModuleAsteroid / ModuleComet MODULE, `VesselSnapshotOps.IsRockPartNode`) at
`class radius x 1.25 (max multiplier) x 1.25 (relief margin)` (class E: 39.1 m), the class from
the part's `prefabBaseURL` (`source=prefab:E`), else, for a bare rock vessel, its `DISCOVERY
size` (`source=discovery:C`), else the largest class I (301.6 m, `source=fallback-largest`,
logged at Info). Ordinary parts keep 1.25 m. Logs: `[SpawnCollision] ParsePartPositions: rock
part 'PotatoRoid' half extent 39.1m source=prefab:E` (rate-limited). Tests:
`RockSpawnBoundsTests`. Not covered: the 1.25 relief margin is a judgment (the PQS mod ranges
live in the prefab assets, not the code), and a comet built from a custom prefab URL has no class
letter, so it reads as the largest class.

## ~~ROCK-DRILL-HARVEST-UNCAPPED~~: a mining window with an asteroid or comet aboard had no plausibility cap [FILED 2026-11-15 by the asteroid / comet review (owner rulings 2026-11-15), by code reading; the gap was known since HV-2 (2026-10-16) and left open there. FIXED 2026-11-15, branch `ast-fixes`; xUnit + the HV-2 rate cell flipped to "modeled"; HV-2 re-flight owed; low (a route built on rock mining could credit a catch-up burst every run)]

What the player saw: a supply route whose recorded ship drilled a grabbed asteroid or comet
credited the whole witnessed harvest every run, including a stock catch-up burst (hours of
mining landing in one frame on load), because `FlightRecorder.ReadHarvestConverterRate` left
`ModuleAsteroidDrill` / `ModuleCometDrill` with a rock aboard `Unmodeled`, which makes the whole
window unbounded (HARVEST-ROUTE-PLAUSIBILITY-CAP).

Decompile (KSP 1.12.5). `ModuleAsteroidDrill.PrepareRecipe` (`ModuleCometDrill` is identical modulo names and strings):
the rock is the LAST part of the drill's own vessel carrying `ModuleAsteroid` (`ModuleComet`)
(`GetAttachedPotato`); per `ModuleAsteroidResource` (`ModuleCometResource`) on it, the output
ratio is `abundance x Efficiency x GetEfficiencyMultiplier()` units/s, `min`'d against the
rock's remaining minable mass (`(currentMass - massThreshold) / density`, only lowers it); the
drill sets `_preCalculateEfficiency`, so `BaseConverter` applies no second multiplier.
`GetEfficiencyMultiplier = EfficiencyBonus x heat throttle x _totalEfficiencyModifiers x crew
bonus`, the same factors the surface drill model reads (heat only lowers it; the margin covers
the modifiers). The persisted `abundance` is `max(0.01, mass share) x purity`, purity from the
resource's `lowRange..highRange` percent (`ModuleSpaceObjectInfo.SetupSpaceObjectResources`).

Fix: a new `HarvestConverterKind.SpaceObjectDrill` folded in `RouteHarvestCapture.
ComputePlausibleRates` as `abundance x Efficiency x multiplier` per rock resource. The live reader
gets the rocks' (resource, abundance) pairs per kind (`FlightRecorder.ReadRockAbundances`, every
`ModuleAsteroidResource` / `ModuleCometResource` on a part with `ModuleAsteroid` /
`ModuleComet`); the pure `RouteHarvestCapture.BuildSpaceObjectDrillRate` takes the per-resource
maximum over the rocks aboard (the drill mines one), credits an unreadable abundance
`RockAbundanceFallback = 1.0` (at or above any stock value) and logs it as a Warn, and reads no
rock of the drill's kind as `NoResourceOutput` (an asteroid drill no longer reads a comet as
aboard, or the reverse). Log: `[Recorder] Harvest rate: ModuleAsteroidDrill part=... kind=...
rock=[Ore:...] substituted=N`. Tests: `RouteHarvestCaptureTests` (`SpaceObjectDrill_*`); the
HV-2 rate cell `StockDrillAndIsruRatesAreModeled` now requires each stock rock drill modeled at a
synthetic abundance with a rock of its kind aboard and no output for the other kind (tally
`total=3` unchanged). Open: HV-2 must re-fly to prove the flipped cell; no lane mines a real rock.

## ~~ROCK-RELEASE-REFLY-SLOT~~: a released asteroid or comet counted as a controllable split child, so releasing one authored a Rewind Point and offered the rock as a Re-Fly slot [FILED 2026-11-15 from the owner rulings of 2026-11-15 ("No Re-Fly for rocks"), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-15, branch `ast-fixes`; xUnit; no lane flies a Klaw release yet; low (a Re-Fly that cannot be flown, on a rare path)]

What the player saw: grab an asteroid with the Klaw, then release it. The split had two
"controllable" children (the ship and the rock), so Parsek wrote a Rewind Point, and the rock's
recording could show in Unfinished Flights as a slot to re-fly, which a rock cannot be.

Cause. `ParsekFlight.IsTrackableVessel` returns true for a SpaceObject (right for recording: the
released rock gets its own branch and spawns real at its tip), and the same predicate fed the
controllable-children classifier behind every Rewind Point (`SegmentBoundaryLogic.
IdentifyControllableChildren`'s default predicate) and the background split RP hook
(`BackgroundRecorder.SplitDetection`, parent and child checks).

Fix: a second predicate, `ParsekFlight.IsReFlyControllableVessel` (pure core
`IsReFlyControllable`): EVA kerbal yes; SpaceObject type no (`space-object`); a vessel whose every
part is a rock no (`space-object-parts`); a command module yes (`command`, or
`command-carrying-space-object` for a ship holding a grabbed rock); else no. The RP classifier and
the background RP hook read it; `ShouldRecordAsOwnBranch`, the breakup / decouple capture and
`IdentityLossClassifier` keep `IsTrackableVessel` (recording identity, not Re-Fly). Releasing a
rock alone is therefore a single-controllable split (no RP). `UnfinishedFlightClassifier.TryQualify`
also refuses a rock's own recording (snapshot `type = SpaceObject`, or rock parts only) held by a
legacy RP with `spaceObjectNotFlyable`, before the `notControllable` check. Logs:
`[Rewind] Re-Fly controllability: ... controllable=False reason=space-object (asteroid / comet: no
Re-Fly slot)`, `[UnfinishedFlights] IsUnfinishedFlight=false ... reason=spaceObjectNotFlyable
rule=...`. Rock identification is shared in `VesselSnapshotOps` (`IsRockPartName`,
`IsSpaceObjectOnlySnapshot`, ...). Tests: `RockReleaseReFlySlotTests`.

## ~~RESTORE-ATTEMPT-RECORD-FOLDS-INTO-HISTORY~~: a world-record award made while a committed flight is resumed folds into that recording's stored history event and is lost on discard [FILED 2026-11-15 from SE-1's nightly red, run `2026-11-15_0704_SE-1-editor-round-trip` (build b548a42c1, PARSEK-FAIL(expectation) attempt 1, ledger actions=17 where the spec pins 15), against the last pass `2026-11-10_1631` (e5b47f33). FIXED 2026-11-15, branch `claude/project-thread-lkzj01-item27`; xUnit; SE-1 re-flight owed; medium (career ledger rows and stock's record band, every record node)]

What the player sees: fly a recorded ship again (the committed-spawned-vessel restore), break a
distance / altitude / speed / depth record threshold, then discard the new flight. The award is
dropped with the discard, stock's record is patched back below the thresholds, and stock pays them
again a frame later as fresh untagged career rows (SE-1: one repay row and two completion rows).

Cause. `GameStateRecorder.TryCoalesceWorldRecordReward` picked its seed by (milestone id,
recording id) only. The SE-1 host's `events.pgse` holds two stored RecordsDistance events at UT
1276.4236 tagged to the resumed recording (an award and stock's completion at the splashdown, with
no ledger row). The load-time optimizer split moves them onto the chain tail, and since PR #2588
(053eb7cd8, COMMITTED-RESTORE-APPENDS-TO-ROOT, intended) the restore attempt resumes on that tail,
so the live threshold 4 / 5 awards folded into the stored history event (rewriting its detail to
`thresholds=N;band=-`) instead of starting the attempt's own seed.
`LedgerOrchestrator.PreserveIrreversibleRestoreAttemptTailsOnDiscard` re-homes only events past
the attempt's cutoff, so it found only the completion (`re-homed 1`, PASS read `re-homed 2`), and
the recalc left `RecordsDistance hits=3 complete=False`. A defect older than #2588: any resumed
recording that already carries a stored event of the same record node hits it; #2588 moved the
SE-1 events onto the recording the attempt now resumes. Not timing: both runs had the same vessel
state and the same splits.

Fix: under an armed committed-tree restore attempt the coalescer skips a candidate seed at or
before the attempt's cutoff for that recording (`CommittedTreeRestoreAttempt.TryGetEventCutoff`,
the same boundary as the persistence suppression, the tail purge and the re-home), so the first
live award starts the attempt's own seed and later awards fold into it. The ledger-row half of the
fold takes the same guard: a committed history row of the scope at or before the cutoff is never
the seed's row, even inside the 0.1 s match window (without it a seed just past the cutoff added
every later award to that history row as well as to its own event, booking it twice: 900 for 600
paid, on a discard and on a commit). Log:
`TryCoalesceWorldRecordReward: ... skipped N restore-attempt history event(s)`. Tests:
`RestoreAttemptRecordCoalesceTests` (red on the old code: history detail rewritten, re-homed 1;
red without the row guard: history row 400 instead of 100; the cutoff boundary pinned in both
loops), covering the discard and the commit (`OnRecordingCommitted`) of the attempt.

Known residue, not built (from the fix's second review; neither reproduced):
  (a) `GameStateRecorder.EnrichPendingMilestoneRewards`
      (`Source/Parsek/GameActions/GameStateRecorder.Handlers.cs`, the ledger loop at lines
      1599-1619) picks a MilestoneAchievement row by milestone id and capture moment within 0.1 s
      (line 1608) with no recording-id or cutoff check, and SETS that row's rewards. No concrete
      failing sequence was found: `Complete()` is terminal for the node and the pending event is
      tagged, so it has no direct row.
      FIXED 2026-11-16 (branch `fix-residuals-limbo-enrich`): the row must carry the event's own
      scope (both untagged, or both tagged to the same recording) and, under an armed restore
      attempt, lie past that recording's cutoff (`IsMilestoneEnrichLedgerRowMatch`). A tagged
      event does have a direct row: a recovery-owned milestone is written TAGGED to the
      committed recording before stock's AwardProgress (`WriteRecoveryOwnedMilestoneIfAny`), so
      the loop is kept for tagged events. Tests: `MilestoneRewardCaptureTests` (other scope,
      KSC event past a newer tagged row, table), `RestoreAttemptRecordCoalesceTests`
      (`MilestoneEnrich_LeavesTheResumedRecordingsHistoryRowUnchanged`),
      `RecoveryScopedMilestoneTagTests` (`..._RealEnrichmentSetsTheTaggedRowsRewards`, red under
      a skip-tagged-events guard).
  (b) An award at exactly the restore attempt's cutoff UT is history to every consumer (not
      re-homed, not purged), so repeated awards at that identical UT would each start their own
      seed. Bounded and not seen in a flight; pinned only as a boundary in
      `RestoreAttemptRecordCoalesceTests`
      (`Boundary_AnEventAtTheCutoffIsHistory_OneJustAfterIsTheAttemptsOwn`). ACCEPTED 2026-11-16 (bounded, pinned by that boundary cell).
      For a resumed recording whose end lies ahead of the clock the cutoff is now just below the
      resume UT, so a resume-frame award is the attempt's (RESTORE-ATTEMPT-CUTOFF-AHEAD-OF-CLOCK);
      the residue stays for an end in the past.

## ~~FAR-SWITCH-INTENT-TTL-RACE~~: a fast far Switch-To starts a switch segment on the target, which the design says it must not [FILED 2026-11-14 from S0.14's third flight (PC, head a3624e48f, PARSEK-FAIL on its pre-registered P6), branch `item20-switch-pending-merge-lane`; code and decompile reading. FIXED 2026-11-14 on the same branch (PR #2609): no intent is armed for an unloaded target; xUnit + mutation; FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-15: S0.14 `2026-11-15_0011_S0.14-far-switch-merges-before-reload` PASS attempt 1; low (a recording the player did not ask for, on a rare path)]

What the player sees: with Parsek recording, a Switch-To (map menu, or the stock alarm's Jump in
FLIGHT) to a vessel outside the physics bubble reloads the flight scene, and on a fast machine the
new scene starts recording the target at once, as if the player had used Fly on it. On a slower
load it does not. The design says it never should.

The designed outcome. `docs/dev/done/plans/segment-scoped-switch-fly-autorecord.md`, "Unloaded-vessel
branch outcome": "The deliberate outcome for this case is that Map Switch-To to an unloaded vessel
does NOT immediate-start a segment; the player falls back to the first-modification watcher ... do
not write code that pretends to 'rearm fresh' in the new scene." The TTL line in the same plan sizes
the Map marker for the in-scene consume only: "2 seconds wall-clock for Map Switch-To (consume
happens same-frame in stock; anything longer is a stuck marker)", and "Marker lifetime: cross-scene
vs in-scene asymmetry" ends "Do not treat the Map-source marker as durable cross-scene state."
`StockActionIntentMarker.MapSwitchToTtlSeconds` carries the same comment. Round 3 (the no-session
Case B handlers) kept that outcome ("the new vessel got the first-modification watcher").

Why it records anyway. The plan assumed the map Postfix's `refused-no-switch` clear removes the
marker before the reload. Decompiled `FlightGlobals.setActiveVessel` (Assembly-CSharp 1.12.5,
ikdasm): the unloaded branch (`Vessel.loaded` false at IL_021d) fires
`onVesselSwitchingToUnloaded`, then `GamePersistence.SaveGame("persistent", ...)` (IL_0248) and
`HighLogic.CurrentGame.Updated()` (IL_0257, which calls `ScenarioRunner.GetUpdatedProtoModules`),
then `FlightDriver.StartAndFocusVessel` with that updated Game (IL_026c), all before it returns. Both
serializations run `ParsekScenario.OnSave`, which writes the still-armed intent
(`SaveRewindStagingState`), so the far scene's OnLoad reads it back from the node
(`LoadRewindStagingState` -> `ValidateLoadedStockActionIntentFreshness`). Any clear after
`SetActiveVessel` returns (the map Postfix, `AlarmJumpSwitchPatch.Postfix`) only clears the old
scene's copy, and `ArmIntentAndSwitchTo` (the Case A / B / C dialog and auto-resolve finisher, which
S0.14 drives through `AlarmJump`) has no clear at all. What stops a segment today is only the wall
clock: OnLoad clears `stale-intent` past 2 s, and the OnFlightReady consume clears
`stale-intent-ttl` past 2 s; a target on the surface is declined `on-surface-defer-to-trigger`. A
far scene that reaches OnFlightReady within 2 s of the click passes every check
(`StockActionIntentConsumeDecision.Evaluate`: same process, inside the TTL, target matches the new
active vessel) and gets a standalone segment.

The flight. S0.14 on `jool-park-nerv`: `pre-switch auto-resolve: resolution=Merge case=B-unloaded`
at 12.292, `CommitTreeFlight` 12.293, `[SwitchIntent] armed: intentId=30a51d77... action=MapSwitchTo
targetPid=4267147709 ... capturedRealtime=56.52705` 12.404, `Scene change requested: FLIGHT` 12.527,
`intent kept-armed on OnLoad` 12.983, `[OnFlightReady]` 13.741 (1.34 s after the arm), `[SwitchSegment]
created ... parentRecId=<standalone> ... focusedPid=4267147709 focusedName='Duna Rocket Debris'
reason=MapSwitchTo` 13.744, `cleared ... reason=consumed-into-segment` 13.754, then `recordingstate
recording=true ... points=1` (recordings 2 > max 1). The second flight of the same lane reached OnLoad
0.7 s after the arm and quit before OnFlightReady, so it does not say which way that run would have
gone; this host reloads well inside 2 s, so before the fix S0.14 would red on every flight.

Fix: a MapSwitchTo intent is armed only for a LOADED target, so nothing crosses the reload. The
pure predicate `MapFocusObjectOnSelectPatch.ShouldArmIntentForSwitchTarget(targetLoaded)` is read
through `DeclineArmForUnloadedTarget` by both FLIGHT arm sites, `PrepareOwnedVesselSwitch` (the map
Prefix, also reached from the alarm Jump in FLIGHT) and `ArmIntentAndSwitchTo` (the Case A / B / C
dialog and auto-resolve finisher). An unloaded target logs one Info line, `[SwitchIntentPatch]
<label> intent not armed: reason=far-switch-target-unloaded targetPid=<pid> ...`, arms nothing and
still switches; the map and alarm Postfix refunds see an empty intent id and log nothing. The third
arm site, the automation seam `SimulateStockSwitchClick`, already refused an unloaded target
(`target-unloaded`); its gate now reads the same predicate. A loaded target arms exactly as before
(2 s TTL, same-frame consume), so S0.8 / S0.12 / S0.13 / CI-1 / GS-3 / FAR-4 keep their pins. No
OnLoad clear was added, and the TS / KSC Fly markers and every TTL are unchanged. Tests:
`FarSwitchIntentArmTests` (predicate truth table, the log line through the sink, the empty refund,
the seam gate, source gates on both sites read comment-stripped, and the set of every
`ArmStockActionIntent` call site in production). Mutation: the predicate forced to always arm reds
five cells (the truth-table row, the decline cell, the seam-gate cell and the two existing
`Gate_UnloadedTarget_*` cells); removing either site's call reds that site's source gate. S0.14 now
requires the not-armed line before the reload and forbids every MapSwitchTo intent line for the
debris, `intent kept-armed on OnLoad` and the segment, with recordings {1,1}. The 10 s scene-load TTL
alternative was rejected: it contradicts the plan's stated outcome.

Flown green 2026-11-15: `2026-11-15_0011_S0.14-far-switch-merges-before-reload` PASS attempt 1 (PC,
head 94f5b8df9, DLL sha256 aa34bc87...3d22 carrying the fix's literals, wall 56 s). KSP.log order:
`CommitTreeFlight` at UT=27787328.0, `[SwitchIntentPatch] pre-switch-dialog intent not armed:
reason=far-switch-target-unloaded targetPid=4267147709` (line 12263), `Scene change requested: FLIGHT
at UT=27787328.00` (line 12375), the far scene flight-ready; zero `action=MapSwitchTo`, `intent
kept-armed on OnLoad` and `[SwitchSegment] created` lines; one recording in one committed tree.

Known residue, not built (from the fix's review):
  (a) A decline neither clears nor supersedes a still-armed EARLIER MapSwitchTo marker (before the
      fix the new arm superseded it), and `ArmIntentAndSwitchTo` has no Postfix refund when stock
      refuses its switch (a pre-existing gap). So in a contrived sequence a marker for another target
      could survive up to 2 s, be saved by the far branch and be consumed on the far side. The
      optional OnLoad clear of any loaded MapSwitchTo marker (no Map marker has a designed
      cross-scene consume) would close it.
  (b) When `FlightGlobals.ActiveVessel == null`, stock skips the ClearToSave and loaded checks and
      switches in-scene even to an unloaded target (decompiled `setActiveVessel`: IL_0089 branches
      to the in-scene IL_02be), so Parsek now declines where it used to arm. Degenerate: a FLIGHT
      Switch-To with no active vessel.

## PARALLEL-RUNNER-INSTANCE-BUSY-ON-EXITING-SIBLING: a slot's preflight refuses instance-busy on a sibling slot's KSP that is still exiting [FILED 2026-11-14 from a parallel daily run on the PC (2 slots); harness, no fix yet; low (one lane INVALID per occurrence, passes when re-flown)]

`RVR-3` was dispatched on slot 1 9 ms after slot 1's previous lane finished, and its zombie preflight
refused `INVALID(instance-busy)`: "a live KSP_x64.exe (pid=12408) is running on this machine; the
probe cannot tell which install it belongs to". pid 12408 was slot 2's KSP (launched for `S0.7`),
which had logged `Application.Quit` 0.4 s earlier and was mid-exit, so
`QueryFullProcessImageNameW` could not read its image path. The lane passed when flown alone.

Why: a slot child scopes the probe to its own instance (`Runtime.ksp_running` ->
`slotrun.blocking_ksp_pid`), but `slots.exe_belongs_to_instance` treats an unreadable path as busy
(fail-closed, deliberately), and an exiting process is exactly the one whose path stops being
readable. The only wait in front of the refusal, `_wait_for_prior_ksp_exit`, runs only after a lane
whose KSP this run killed on the same slot (`defer_post_quit and wait_for_prior_ksp`), so a sibling
slot's exiting KSP refuses at once.

What a fix needs, either of:
  1. A short bounded re-probe when every blocker has an unreadable path (a few seconds, polling
     `ksp_running`): an exiting process vanishes, and a live one reads its path again, so the
     verdict then attributes it. Keep the fail-closed reading at the end of the bound. Pure
     decision in `slotrun` (blockers all unknown-path -> wait), unit cells for: unknown path that
     vanishes (clear), unknown path that becomes another slot's exe (clear), unknown path that stays
     unknown (refuse), a known own-instance exe (refuse at once, no wait).
  2. Attribution by slot pid files: each `run.py --slot` child writes the pid of the KSP it launched
     (and removes it after the exit wait), and the probe treats an unreadable-path pid listed by
     ANOTHER slot as that slot's, not busy. Exact, but adds a file contract every launch path and
     crash path must keep.
The first is smaller and needs no new state.

Seen again 2026-11-15 (1.0.2 release check; noted there as PARALLEL-RUNNER-BUSY-PROBE-RACE and
folded in here): parallel run `fix-check` (2 to 3 slots, PC), lane `RVR-3-route-lifecycle` on slot
`stock-minimal-2`, run `2026-11-15_1047_RVR-3-route-lifecycle`, `INVALID(instance-busy)` before boot,
wall 2 s: `[Harness][Warn][Preflight] instance-busy: a live KSP_x64.exe (pid=16640) is running on
this machine; the probe cannot tell which install it belongs to, so refusing before
...\automation\stock-minimal-2 (INVALID instance-busy).` pid 16640 was the run's own sibling, the KSP
of lane `S0.7-exit-auto-commit` on slot `stock-minimal` (its lane log: `launch
exe=...\automation\stock-minimal\KSP_x64.exe pid=16640`), the same sibling lane as on 2026-11-14.
RVR-3 passed on the runner's own resume (`2026-11-15_1050_RVR-3-route-lifecycle`, 52 s). Not a
Parsek defect. Evidence on the PC: `logs\console\2026-11-15\RVR-3-route-lifecycle.65.log` and
`S0.7-exit-auto-commit.64.log`. Not investigated on the PC: whether that KSP was exiting at the
probe moment, so this second case is not shown to be the exiting shape above.

What the code says (main 76d3f23c5): the line is printed by `run_attempt` (`harness/run.py`, the
zombie preflight, Warn at line 4831) when `Runtime.ksp_running` (line 390) returns a pid. A slot
child runs with `scope_ksp_to_instance` set (line 6446), so `slotrun.blocking_ksp_pid`
(`harness/lib/slotrun.py`, line 167) already treats a KSP whose exe path lies in another slot's
install as not busy, through `slots.exe_belongs_to_instance` (`harness/lib/slots.py`, line 173).
The only way a sibling slot's KSP refuses is a path that reads as None:
`_windows_image_path` (`run.py`, line 684) failing `OpenProcess` or `QueryFullProcessImageNameW`,
or the Toolhelp snapshot failing so `_tasklist_ksp_processes` (line 411) lists every KSP with no
path. Which of those happened here is unknown. So the fix is the one above (a bounded re-probe of
unreadable-path blockers, or slot pid files), not new path mapping. Small addition for the next
occurrence: the Warn should say whether the blocker's path was unreadable or in this instance; its
wording ("the probe cannot tell which install it belongs to") is the serial-run wording.

## PARALLEL-RUNNER-SUMMARY-RENAME-ABORT: on Windows the parallel runner aborts when another process holds summary.txt open, and kills the lanes still flying [FILED 2026-11-15 from two parallel runs on the PC the same day, each with a `tail -F` watcher on the run's `summary.txt`; harness, no fix yet; medium (a run dies mid-way and its in-flight lanes re-fly on resume)]

Seen twice on 2026-11-15: `harness/tools/parallel_runner.py run` stopped with `runner internal
error: ... PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` from the rename that writes
`summary.txt`, while a `tail -F` held that file open, and the lanes then in flight were killed and
flew again on `resume`.

Why, by code reading: `RunFolder.write_summary` (`parallel_runner.py`, line 651) writes through
`write_text_atomic` (line 159), whose `os.replace(tmp, path)` (line 164) cannot replace a file
another process holds open on Windows without delete sharing. `_dispatch` calls it after every lane
end (line 885) and once at the end (line 940), outside any try, so the `PermissionError` leaves
`_dispatch`; `dispatch_loop`'s `except BaseException` (line 847) then runs `_kill_running` (line
1150) on every running child, logs an `abandon` event for each and re-raises, and `main` (line
1274) reports `runner internal error`. A summary write is bookkeeping, yet it takes the run and its
live lanes down with it.

Fix: retry the rename with a short backoff (a few tries over about a second); if it still fails,
log one Warn, keep the run alive and write the summary again on the next lane end (and at the end
of the run). Never kill in-flight lanes for a summary write. Unit cells: a replace that fails once
then succeeds writes the summary; one that always fails leaves the run and its children running
and retries on the next lane end; the end-of-run write failing still returns the run's real exit
code. Until then, the operator rule: watch a run through `parallel_runner.py status --name <run>`
or `events.jsonl`, never through an open handle on `summary.txt` (no `tail -F`, no editor that
keeps it open).

## B7-DUNA-FLYBY-IKE-EJECTION: B7's Duna flyby enters Ike's SOI and ends its first attempt, costing a retry of a long lane [FILED 2026-11-15 from the 1.0.2 release check (v1.0.2 released from main 76d3f23c5); mission library, no fix yet; low (one extra B7 flight per occurrence, not a Parsek defect)]

`B7-duna-flyby` needed a second attempt in three separate runs on 2026-11-15 and passed on
attempt 2 each time:
  - `main-early-nightly`: attempt 1 INVALID(mission) (loss reason not recorded here).
  - `final-nightly`: attempt 1 run `2026-11-15_0407`, INVALID(mission): `flyby ejected the craft
    off-course: body='Ike'`.
  - `fix-check`: attempt 1 run `2026-11-15_0926`, INVALID(boot-hang), a harness boot stall, a
    different cause.
The Ike case is a mission-autopilot issue, not a Parsek defect. It is the finding first filed
2026-07-25 ("B7 AT HEAD FAILS: the 300 km Duna approach gets captured by IKE",
`done/todo-and-known-bugs-v8.md`; the `autotest-status.md` B7 row says the lane is intermittent and
needs a spec decision); it was archived open with v8, has had no entry in this file since, and
was never fixed. Its
evidence then: the 300 km target was hit (`pe=310089`), the inbound leg crossed Ike's orbit and the
next window read `body=Ike` (`window[19] body=Duna alt=3,687,346` -> `window[20] body=Ike
alt=897,085`); whether Ike is close enough depends on its phase at arrival.

Where it ends, by code (main 76d3f23c5): B7 runs `mlib.b5_decide`
(`harness/missions/lib/mlib.py`, line 15657) through the alias `harness/missions/b7_duna_flyby.py`.
In the `B5_TARGET_FLYBY` branch (line 16852), any telemetry frame whose body is not blank, the
target (`Duna`) or the return body (`Sun`) ends the mission `MISSION_ASSERT_FAIL` with that loss
reason (line 16915). So the terminal fires on entering Ike's SOI, before anything shows whether
Ike would have thrown the craft off course. ASSERT-FAIL maps to subkind `mission`, which the
harness retries.

The aim: the correction rounds (`_b5_enter_plan_correction`, line 14303, and the
`B5_PLAN_CORRECTION` branch, line 16162) emit `ACTION_MJ_PLAN_COURSE_CORRECT` with
`courseCorrectPeriapsisMeters` (`harness/scenarios/B7-duna-flyby.toml`, line 134, 300000). The
runner (`harness/missions/mission_runner.py`, line 1819) passes it to MechJeb's
`operation_course_correction` as `course_correct_final_pe_a`, the Duna periapsis altitude only;
nothing in the plan looks at Ike or the arrival time.

Where a fix would go (a choice for whoever takes it; no code changed):
  1. Spec only, the V3C precedent (V3C-CAPTURE-AIMS-INTO-IKE, `done/todo-and-known-bugs-v11.md`):
     raise B7's `courseCorrectPeriapsisMeters` so the arrival periapsis clears Ike's orbital shell
     (about 1,734 - 4,026 km altitude per that entry; V3C moved 300 km -> 10,000 km and its next flight was MISSION-OK with no Ike encounter).
     A hyperbola whose periapsis is above the shell never enters it. B7's flyby floor
     (`targetPeriapsisFloorMeters`, 15 km, a minimum sampled altitude) still passes; the header's
     300 km rationale (finding 16d, the corrector under-delivers low targets) would need rewording.
  2. Machine: before the last correction round, read the patched conics and re-plan when the
     arrival reports `nextBody=Ike` (V3C named this option and did not take it: no flown precedent).
  3. Spec contract: accept an Ike transit as part of a Duna-system flyby (the B5_TARGET_FLYBY check
     would need a tolerated-moon list, like `viaBodyNames` for the coast). This changes what B7
     asserts, so it is an owner call.
Option 1 is the smallest. Done when B7 flies attempt 1 green across several nightlies.

## ~~B43-VALL-TYLO-FLYBY-SUBSURFACE~~: B43's first flight reaches Tylo on an impact course and never arms the capture [CLOSED 2026-11-16: B43 flew green with fix 3, `2026-11-16_1638` PASS attempt 1 (1,097 s, automation DLL 5bc76f4a; the last correction refined MechJeb's node, predicted Tylo pe -578,497 m, to an 8.12 m/s radial-out burn whose read-back predicted pe was 101,389 m, inside the window), and `vall-tylo-recorded` is harvested and committed, V43M handed over. FILED 2026-11-15 from B43's first flights; FIX 1 (cap 120) FLOWN 2026-11-16, still INVALID; FIX 2 (cap 250) FLOWN 2026-11-16, still INVALID; FIX 3 AUTHORED 2026-11-16 (node search, mission library, not flown); low (the forge cannot harvest `vall-tylo-recorded`, so V43M stays unflyable; not a Parsek defect)]

`B43-vall-tylo-transfer` flew twice on 2026-11-15 (runs `2026-11-15_1617` and `2026-11-15_1632_a2`)
and read INVALID(mission) both times: TARGET-FLYBY logged `flyby impact certain,
capture-never-armed (periapsis-subsurface)`, Tylo periapsis about -579,788 m on both attempts.
Cause (the two `_mission.stdout.log`s): every mid-course correction round was priced at 85.6 to
169 m/s and refused by the spec's `maxCorrectionDvMps = 50`, so no correction ever burned and the
raw stage-2 aim reached Tylo below the surface. Fix: the cap is 120 m/s (the first round's 85.6
m/s with 25% margin; 130.5 LF, about 683 m/s, was left after stage 2, enough for one round plus
the 161-201 m/s elliptical capture). Pinned by `test_moon_forge_fixes.B43CorrectionCapTests`.
Re-flown 2026-11-16 (runs `2026-11-15_2243`, `2026-11-15_2300_a2`), INVALID(mission) both, one
step further: round 0 flew its 85.6 m/s node in full, but the Tylo periapsis moved only from
-580 km to -323 km (the MechJeb node under-delivered; the burn's own telemetry shows the node
consumed to 1.4 m/s), and every later round priced 200.6-265.5 m/s and was refused at 120.
Fix 2: the cap is 250, so round 1's 200.6 m/s flies; 114.1 LF (~600 m/s) was left after round
0, enough for it plus the capture, while a 265 m/s round stays refused. Re-flown 2026-11-16 with
cap 250 (runs `2026-11-16_0002`, `2026-11-16_0022_a2`), INVALID(mission) both: every round flew to
within 2 m/s of its node, but MechJeb's node did not deliver the asked 500 km periapsis; the Tylo
periapsis went -580 -> -327 km (85.6 m/s), -326 -> -568 (199.5), -568 -> -483 (168.8), -483 -> -381
(111.1), and the arrival was subsurface. At v_inf ~245 m/s Tylo focuses the approach hard (aim
offsets under ~7.5 Mm hit the surface, 500 km needs ~10 Mm of the 10.86 Mm SOI), MechJeb's linear
model misjudges it, and its nodes sat 1,700-10,450 s before the SOI where the lever is small.
Fix 3: new opt-in mission param `correctionNodeSearch` (`b29_jool_kerbin` schema, with
`correctionNodeSearchPeWindowMeters` and `correctionNodeLeadSeconds`; off by default, so no other
lane changes). The runner logs the MechJeb node's predicted next body and periapsis; outside the
window it moves the node to now + 900 s and `mlib.search_correction_node` steps dv along ten
node-frame directions (crossing the V when the aim sweeps through Tylo's centre), bisects to the
smallest in-window dv and keeps the cheapest under the cap; a node whose read-back prediction is
outside the window or over the cap is removed, not flown. B43 now aims at 150 km with window
[100, 1,000] km. Pinned by `test_correction_node_search`.
Closed 2026-11-16: fix 3 flew green (`2026-11-16_1638`), the fixture is harvested.

## ~~B44-LAYTHE-TYLO-NODE-EDIT-UNAVAILABLE~~: B44's second transfer burn cannot edit its maneuver node and the craft is lost [CLOSED 2026-11-15: B44 flew green on its first flight with the fix, `2026-11-15_2243` PASS attempt 1 (888 s, origin/main c522ea549), and `laythe-tylo-recorded` is harvested and committed, V44M handed over. `B44-laythe-tylo-transfer` flew twice on 2026-11-15 (runs `2026-11-15_1617` and
`2026-11-15_1622_a2`) and read INVALID(mission) both times. The kRPC `Maneuver node editing is not
available` error was a symptom. Cause: the parent relay's stage 1 is an unaimed prograde escape at
the first periapsis pass the min-lead rule accepts, and on `laythe-park-nerv` that pass left
Laythe almost RADIALLY, so the Jool-frame orbit (pe 19.9 Mm, ap 23.5 Mm) straddled Laythe's own
orbit and the coast to the stage-2 node met Laythe again (next patch periapsis -266 km) and the
craft was lost. Fix: new mission param `escapeExtraParkOrbits` (`b29_jool_kerbin` schema, default

escape direction about 13.2 deg per 1,941 s pass, and the B44 spec sets 5, which leaves prograde
(Jool-frame pe 23.45 Mm, ap 73.9 Mm, no encounter in 400,000 s; passes 4 and 6 also prograde).
A patched-conic model that reproduces flight 1 pins the choice in
`test_moon_forge_fixes.B44EscapePassGeometryTests`. Closed by the green flight
`2026-11-15_2243` (PASS attempt 1) and the `laythe-tylo-recorded` harvest from its own snapshot.

## ~~B46-MINMUS-MUN-COAST-TIMEOUT~~: B46's Minmus -> Mun transfer never reaches the Mun before its coast phase times out [CLOSED 2026-11-16: B46 flew green with fix 2, `2026-11-16_0001` PASS attempt 1 (1,569 s, automation DLL 5bc76f4a), and `minmus-mun-recorded` is harvested and committed, V46M handed over. FILED 2026-11-15 from B46's first flights; FIX 1 (relative burn floor) FLOWN 2026-11-16 and worked, still INVALID one step later; FIX 2 AUTHORED 2026-11-16 (spec floor 20 Mm, not flown); low (the forge cannot harvest `minmus-mun-recorded`, so V46M stays unflyable; not a Parsek defect)]

`B46-minmus-mun-transfer` flew twice on 2026-11-15 in the analysis thread's `final-operator` run
(runs `2026-11-15_1638` and `2026-11-15_1743_a2`) and read INVALID(autopilot-flake) both times:
`phase COAST-TO-TARGET timed out`. Cause: dropping off rails warp before the stage-2 node
re-derived the orbit and moved a 45.55 Mm apoapsis by 39.5 km with no thrust; the burn tracker's
absolute "apsis changed" floor read that as a burn already done, the apoapsis floor was met, and
TRANSFER-BURN exited 478 s BEFORE its node, so the transfer was never flown and the coast waited
for a Mun encounter that could not come. Fix: `mlib._burn_apsis_changed` takes the larger of the
old absolute floor and 0.5% of the entry apsis (used by the burn stagnation tracker and the
correction-burn timeout); small orbits keep the absolute floor. Pinned by
`test_moon_forge_fixes.BurnChangedFloorTests` with B46's own frames. Re-flown 2026-11-16 (runs
`2026-11-15_2243`, `2026-11-15_2308_a2`), INVALID(autopilot-flake) both: stage 2 now burned at its
node and did the transfer (Kerbin pe 28.8 -> 10.76 Mm, a Mun encounter), but MechJeb's burn sat
mid-orbit at 29.9 Mm altitude, so it lowered the apoapsis too (45.55 -> 30.16 Mm) and the spec's
40 Mm `transferMinApoapsisMeters` read the finished transfer as an under-burn. Fix 2: the floor
is 20 Mm, under the burn-point bound (the new apoapsis is at least the old periapsis, ~29 Mm)
and above the Mun's orbit plus SOI (13.8 Mm); pinned by `test_moon_forge_fixes.B46InwardFloorTests`.
Closed 2026-11-16: fix 2 flew green (`2026-11-16_0001`), the fixture is harvested.

## ~~FAR-SWITCH-CASE-B-UNFLOWN~~: no lane flew a far vessel switch while recording, so the commit before stock's reload was never checked in game [CLOSED 2026-11-15: S0.14 LIVE-PROVEN on its fourth flight, `2026-11-15_0011_S0.14-far-switch-merges-before-reload` PASS attempt 1, tier daily; the residue below is the #266 stash, still unreached. FILED 2026-11-14 from a lane gap audit (the vessel-switch stash family). LANE AUTHORED 2026-11-14, branch `item20-switch-pending-merge-lane`: `S0.14-far-switch-merges-before-reload`, operator (flight 1 INVALID on its host, re-hosted on `jool-park-nerv`; flight 2 red on a spec error, fixed; flight 3 PARSEK-FAIL on a product defect, FAR-SWITCH-INTENT-TTL-RACE, now fixed and the lane re-pinned to it); the two-switch reading lane S0.15 flew once and was WITHDRAWN (no committed host). Closes when S0.14 flies green with the fix; the #266 stash stays unreached by any flown lane until a host is harvested; test gap]

Shape: the player records a vessel, then switches to a vessel OUTSIDE the physics bubble (map
Switch-To, or the stock alarm's Jump in FLIGHT). Stock's `setActiveVessel` fires
`onVesselSwitchingToUnloaded`, saves `persistent` and reloads FLIGHT through
`FlightDriver.StartAndFocusVessel`; it never fires `onVesselSwitching`, so the #266 pre-transition
stash (`StashActiveTreeForVesselSwitch`) cannot see it. Parsek decides first: pre-switch Case B
(no session, a live recording, `target.loaded == false`) in
`MapFocusObjectOnSelectPatch.PrepareOwnedVesselSwitch`, then `TryAutoResolvePreSwitch` ->
`MergeActiveTreeAndSwitchTo` (`CommitTreeFlight`) or `DiscardActiveRecordingAndSwitchTo`, then
