## ~~LAUNCH-SITE-WOUND-LONGITUDE~~: a flight parked on the pad or runway spawned there when its stored longitude was wound past the date line [FILED 2026-11-14 by the multiplayer implementation plan (`docs/dev/plans/multiplayer/r0b-prep-small.md`, P1-02, question 10.1; owner answer "Fix both"), by code reading and the committed fixtures. FIXED 2026-11-14, branch `claude/project-thread-xgsu2i` (PR #2605); xUnit; FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-14 on the PR DLL: EX-1 (`2026-11-14_2025`, pad retirement), PADG-1 (`_2030`), LF-1 (`_2027`), LF-2 (`_2028`), MC-4 (`_2020`), all first attempt; no committed lane stores a wound longitude, so the wrap itself is proven by xUnit only; low]

Recorded longitudes are not always in [-180, 180]: 2,686 of 118,819 `lon =` values in the committed
fixtures are outside it, and two `.prec.txt` points over the KSC read -434.4 / -434.5. The
launch-site circles (`SpawnCollisionDetector.ClassifyKscExclusionZone` /
`IsWithinKscExclusionZone`, `LaunchSiteExclusionZones.Classify`) used the flat-earth
`SurfaceDistance`, which does not wrap, so such a point was 360 degrees from the pad: the
end-of-flight retirement missed it (the vessel spawned on the pad) and `LaunchSiteOnlyGhost` did
not see it as launch-site ground.

Fix: the three launch-site callers use `SpawnCollisionDetector.LaunchSiteSurfaceDistance`, the
same formula with the longitude difference wrapped into (-180, 180]
(`WrapLongitudeDeltaDegrees`); a difference already in range is used unchanged, so every
decision on an unwound longitude is bit-identical. `SurfaceDistance` and its other callers
(not launch-site rules) are unchanged. Tests: `LaunchSiteWrapAndCacheTests` (the wrap table, a
bit-equality grid, wound pad / runway / Desert / Woomerang hits, a wound pad recording retiring
and a wound one 2 km off still spawning).

## ~~LAUNCH-SITE-PARTIAL-READ-CACHED~~: a first read of the Making History launch sites made before they were built kept fallback positions for the process [FILED 2026-11-14 by the multiplayer implementation plan (`r0b-prep-small.md`, P1-04, question 10.1; owner answer "Fix both"), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-14, branch `claude/project-thread-xgsu2i` (PR #2605); xUnit; FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-14 with the four lanes above and MC-4 (`2026-11-14_2020`, Desert pad): every run logged `Launch-site retirement circles resolved: runtime=8 fallback=0` once and no partial read, so the partial path is proven by xUnit only; low]

`LaunchSiteExclusionZones.GetAltSiteCircles` cached its merged list for the process whenever the
runtime read returned at least one circle. The runtime read keeps the KSC `LaunchPad` / `Runway`
too, so a read made while a Making History site's spawn transform was not built yet still
cached, with that site's fallback coordinates merged in, until KSP restarted.

Fix: a pure `ShouldCacheRuntimeRead(runtimeCount, fallbackMerged)` caches only a read with at
least one runtime circle and no fallback row merged in. A partial read is still used for that
call and logs `Launch-site retirement circles partial read: ... missing=<sites>; not cached`
(Info, rate-limited per missing set); the next call reads again. Without Making History the
fallback table is empty, so a KSC-only read still caches at once. A test seam
`RuntimeAltSiteReaderForTesting` replaces the runtime read. Cost while partial: one walk of
`PSystemSetup.LaunchSites` per call; the callers are spawn decisions, the ledger walk (once per
surface-terminal home-world recording per recalculation) and the `LaunchSiteOnlyGhost` cache,
which recomputes only when `RecordingStore.StateVersion` moves, so nothing reads it per frame. A
read stays partial only while a site is not set up yet (normally the load window), or forever if
a mod broke a site's setup, in which case the fallback circle keeps being used as before.

## ~~WINDOWS-TEST-HOST-ONLY-REDS-2026-11-14: 16 xUnit tests red on the owner's Windows PC and green on CI~~ [FILED 2026-11-14 from a Windows run of main 37a6c6101 (Debug and Release, OS culture ro-RO). FIXED 2026-11-14, branch `claude/project-thread-lkzj01`; xUnit on mono, the Windows re-run owed; tests only, no player-visible change]

Two defects, one gap.

1. Culture (3 tests, `MergeFlowDecisionTests`). `ParsekFlightMergeFlow` wrote
   `CommitTreeFlight: starting tree commit at UT=` and `CommitTreeSceneExit: finalizing tree at UT=`
   with the thread culture, so ro-RO printed `300,0` where the tests read `300.0`. Fix: both lines
   format with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture`. Reproduced red on mono with `LANG=ro_RO.UTF-8`
   (the 3 tests, nothing else in a whole-suite ro_RO run), green after.
2. Unity native call (all 13 tests of `AnchorEpsilonResidualTests`). The class constructor
   Harmony-patched Unity's `Quaternion.LookRotation(Vector3, Vector3)` and `AngleAxis`. Both are
   managed wrappers whose body calls a native `_Injected` method, and Harmony must JIT the original
   to patch it, which the .NET Framework host refuses ("ECall methods must be packaged into a
   system module"), so every test died in the constructor. Fix: no Harmony; the orbital pose code
   (`ParsekFlight.ComputeOrbitalRotation`, `ParsekFlightGhostPositioner.SafeOrbitalLookRotation`,
   `ProductionAnchorWorldFrameResolver.TryComputeBoundaryInstantOrbitalAnchorPose`) calls
   `ParsekFlight.OrbitalLookRotation` / `OrbitalAngleAxis`, which use a `*OverrideForTesting`
   delegate when a test sets one and otherwise Unity's call inside a `NoInlining` wrapper. A
   `mono --trace` of the class, audited for direct native callees of every method it enters,
   lists the two patched Unity originals before and none after (the two remaining entries are the
   deliberate probes `RecordingStore.ReadUnityApplicationIsPlayingCore` and
   `UnityEntryFactAttribute.TouchUnityNative`, both caught), and no entered method calls a small
   Unity wrapper a Release JIT could inline.
3. The gap: CI runs the suite on mono only. Mono takes its culture from the environment (C /
   invariant on CI) and refuses a native call only when it executes, so both kinds of failure show
   only on a Windows run (a PC `dotnet test` or `release.py`, which runs Debug and Release).

## PARALLEL-HARNESS-RUNS: fly harness lanes on 2-3 KSP copies at once while the owner keeps using the PC [FILED 2026-11-14 (owner request). BUILT 2026-11-14: C# part (xUnit only) and harness part (slots, locks, provisioning copies, the parallel runner; unit suites only); LIVE-PROVEN 2026-11-14 on the owner's PC: daily tier 28/28 PASS on 2 and 3 slots]

**Plan.** `harness/parallel-runs-plan-2026-11-14.md` in the project files (sections 1-6 and the
v2 overrides): slots `automation/<profile>-<k>`, a per-slot lock under the machine lock, stamped
kRPC ports, path-scoped process checks, per-copy `-logFile`, Unity prefs snapshot / restore,
and `harness/tools/parallel_runner.py`.

**C# part (done, automation only, inert unless `PARSEK_TEST_COMMANDS=1`).**
- Focus-lock suppression: `TestCommands/AutomationFocusLockSuppressionPatch.cs` prefixes the
  private `OnApplicationFocus(bool)` of `FlightDriver`, `EditorDriver`, `SpaceCenterMain`,
  `UISpaceCenter` and `MainMenu` and skips stock on focus loss, so an unfocused copy no longer
  takes the `ControlTypes.All` lock that made `WarpToUT` answer `warp-locked`, stalled the editor
  launch and paused the KSC Planetarium. `Prepare()` reads the env, so a player build applies
  zero targets. Log: rate-limited `focus lock suppressed scene=... lockId=...`.
- Window lookup by process: `TestCommands/OwnProcessWindowFinder.cs` (`EnumWindows` + own pid,
  `UnityWndClass` preferred) replaces the title lookups in `UiAction op=pointer`
  (`via=own-process`) and `DisabledHoverEchoImguiTest` (`window=own-process`).
- Boot window placement: `PARSEK_AUTOMATION_DESKTOP_ID` / `PARSEK_AUTOMATION_RETURN_FOREGROUND`;
  the seam moves its own window with `IVirtualDesktopManager.MoveWindowToDesktop` and hands the
  foreground back, ending with one Info line `window placement desktop=<moved|failed hr=..|
  skipped|no-window> foreground=<returned|not-foreground|failed|skipped> ...` (grammar in
  `design-autotest-command-seam.md`, "Addon lifecycle"). The harness minimises the window
  whenever the line does not say `desktop=moved`.

**Harness part (done, unit-tested, not flown).**
- Slots: `harness/lib/slots.py` (copy 1 = `automation/<profile>`, copy k = `automation/<profile>-<k>`;
  per-profile kRPC port blocks 50000 / 50020 / 50040, `+2*(k-1)`), run.py's decisions in
  `harness/lib/slotrun.py`.
- `run.py --slot <s>` (child of the runner): no machine lock, the runner token
  (`PARSEK_HARNESS_RUNNER_TOKEN` / `_PID`) re-checked at every attempt boundary, its slot lock,
  serial verify, no prune sweeps / run-index append / coverage refresh, stop request read-only;
  `--tests-prebuilt`, `--report-json` (`parsek-run-report/1`), `--window`, `--desktop-id`, and the
  maintenance flags `--sweep-results` / `--refresh-coverage`. New flake-exempt INVALID subkinds
  `port-busy`, `runner-token`, `slot-locked`, `slot-profile-mismatch`.
- Every run.py (serial too): holds the slot lock of each instance it flies, stamps the slot's kRPC
  ports before every launch (copy 1 of stock-tree / modded-compat moves to 50020 / 50040 on its next
  run or provision) and refuses `port-busy` on a listening port, writes `Player.log` into the instance
  (`-logFile`, plus `-screen-*` from settings.cfg), and as machine-lock holder snapshots / restores the
  shared Unity screen prefs (`HKCU\Software\Squad\Kerbal Space Program`; crash marker restored on the
  next start). Slot children are spaced 15 s apart at launch and count only their own instance's KSP.
- Provisioning: `provision.py --copy K` (manifest keys `slot` / `copy` / `krpcRpcPort` /
  `krpcStreamPort`, VERIFY expects the slot stamp, 8 GiB free-space margin for K >= 2),
  `--copy K --remove` (junctions unlinked first), `EC-10` while any slot lock is live.
- `harness/tools/parallel_runner.py` (pure `harness/lib/parallel.py`): `run` / `resume` / `set-slots`
  / `stop` / `status`, longest p50 first, 15 s dispatch gap, a memory guard that keeps 1.5 GB RAM
  / 1.5 GB VRAM free after the new copy loads (footprint 4.5 GB RAM / 2 GB VRAM, a booting copy's
  remaining footprint ramped down over 60 s), exclusive lanes skipped unless
  `--include-exclusive`, run.py's exit rule.
- Throughput fix (2026-11-14, after the first PC daily run, 28 lanes, 2 slots then `set-slots 3`
  at minute 10): the runner held every start 45 s after the previous one, and daily lanes take
  46-90 s, so the run took 21m46s against 25 min serial (1.2x) and slot 3 never got a lane; the
  wait was not logged. Fix: the gap is now the 15 s launch spacing
  (`parallel.DISPATCH_GAP_SECONDS`), the memory guard accounts for copies still booting, and
  every wait kind is logged once per change.
- Memory guard recalibrated (2026-11-14, after daily-par-3: 28 lanes, 3 slots). The run took
  15m24s against 21m46s for the first parallel daily run, but on 2 effective slots: the third
  slot never ran. 66 memory holds, 56 of them "2 running, 2 booting", typically
  `free RAM 10.4 GB - 2 booting x 4.5 GB = 1.4 GB < 6.0 GB; free VRAM 13.7 - 2 x 5.0 = 3.7 < 5.5`.
  Measured: free
  RAM 14.8 GB with no KSP, 6.07 GB at its lowest with two copies flying, one copy peaks at
  4.25 GB RAM and about 1 GB VRAM in the 1280x720 window (peak 3.7 GB VRAM used with 2 copies on
  a 1.8 GB baseline; the ~5 GB figure was fullscreen), an earlier trial ran 3 copies at full
  speed with 1.7 GB RAM free. Findings: daily lanes last 48-60 s, so the 75 s window marked a copy
  as booting for its whole life, and the reading already holds part of a booting copy's memory,
  so a full reserve on top counted it twice, against floors (6 / 5.5 GB) sized as if the new copy
  were not yet subtracted. Fix: projected = reading - remaining footprint of each booting copy
  (`footprint * max(0, 1 - elapsed / 60 s)`) - one full footprint for the new copy, held under
  1.5 GB (`COPY_FOOTPRINT_RAM_GB` 4.5, `COPY_FOOTPRINT_VRAM_GB` 2.0, `MIN_FREE_RAM_GB` /
  `MIN_FREE_VRAM_GB` 1.5, `BOOT_WINDOW_SECONDS` 60). The daily-par-3 hold (copies 50 s and 20 s
  in) now starts (RAM 10.4 - 3.75 - 4.5 = 2.15 GB); two booted copies at 6.07 GB free start a
  third; 5.5 GB RAM or 3.0 GB VRAM free hold (`DispatchTests` `test_pc_*`).
- Docs: `harness/README.md` ("The machine lock", "Install slots", "Parallel runs"),
  `design-autotest-harness-core.md` ("Install slots and parallel runs"),
  `design-autotest-stack-setup.md` ("Provisioning slot copies"), `autotest-status.md`.

**Measured basis (owner's PC, 2026-11-14).** Per copy about 1 CPU core, ~4.3 GB RAM at peak,
~9.4 GB commit, ~1 GB VRAM in a 1280x720 window; 1, 2 and 3 copies all at full speed; RAM is the
limit, so 2 copies while the owner uses the PC and 3 when away. Unity's Screenmanager prefs are
one registry key shared by every KSP on the PC.

**PC validation (done 2026-11-14, owner's PC, daily tier, 28 lanes, every lane PASS first attempt).**
- 2 slots then `set-slots 3` (360e486): 21m46s; slot 3 never ran (45 s settle, fixed in 47562f0).
- 3 slots (47562f0): 15m24s; slot 3 still idle (memory guard too strict, recalibrated in 2b118be).
- 3 slots (2b118be): 12m35s, lanes 10 / 9 / 9 per copy, peak 3 at once, min free RAM 3.65 GB, peak
  VRAM 9.0 / 16.3 GB, PC responsive. Serial p50 sum for comparison: about 25 min.
- Every lane logged `window placement desktop=moved` (foreground `returned` or `not-foreground`
  when the copy never took it), each copy wrote its own `Player.log`, ports 50000 / 50002 / 50004,
  and the Unity screen prefs matched the pre-run values afterwards.
- Reports: `logs/console/2026-11-14/parallel-daily-check*.txt` on the owner's PC.

## ARCH-COLD-RESET-HOLDERS: save-scoped statics are reset field by field, so a new field can be forgotten [FILED 2026-11-14 for refactor plan item 15 ("B1", as corrected by the 2026-11-11 architecture review), branch `item15-cold-reset-holders`. IN PROGRESS; refactor, no product change]

The mod keeps the loaded save's state in statics spread over many stores, and a Cold load
must forget all of it (`ParsekScenario.ResetSaveScopedSessionState`, then each store's own
Cold-path loader). A static the reset forgets leaks from one save into the next (PR #2568
fixed one: a stale Warp to time request). The agreed shape is NOT state owned by the scenario
module (KSP destroys it on every scene request) but a process-lifetime holder per store: the
store keeps its static facade, its save-scoped fields live in one nested `ColdResetState`
object, and the store's Cold reset replaces that object, so a new field is reset by
construction.

**Step 1, the cells (test-only).** `SaveScopedSessionResetTests` now covers every store
`scripts/arch/lifetimes.toml` tags save or load-transition, not only the 22 types
`ResetSaveScopedSessionState` resets:

- `ColdResetCells_CoverEverySaveScopedType` reads the lifetime map and reds on a tagged type
  with no cell (and on a cell for a type the map no longer tags).
- `ColdLoader_ResetsEverySaveScopedStatic` (one row per store the helper does not reset, 18
  rows) dirties every save / load-transition static of the store (lifetime resolved as
  `lifetimes.py` does: field entry, pattern, type default), runs the helper and then the
  store's own Cold-path call with a save that holds nothing (`VesselNameStore.Load`,
  `RouteStore.LoadRoutesFrom`, `LedgerOrchestrator.OnLoad`, `SaveFileLoadIntent.TryConsume`,
  ...), and reads each back. What it leaves set is pinned in `ColdLoaderKnownGaps`, and a
  pinned gap that closes reds until its entry goes; the list is empty since
  COLD-RESET-LEFTOVERS (below) closed its four.
- Both reset cells read through a `ColdResetState` holder: each field of the holder the reset
  leaves current is a slot keyed `Store.field`, so a field moved into the holder keeps its
  allowlist key and a field added to it is covered with no test edit.

**Step 2, the holders.** One store per commit, smallest first; listed here as they land.

- `WarpToTimeRequest`: both requests (9 fields); `DropAll` logs what it drops, then swaps.
- `RouteRunPrompt`: the pending prompt (2 fields); `ResetForSaveLoad` logs the cleared prompt, then swaps.
- `SceneEntryVesselScope`: the scene-entry and rewind-replay-target pids (5 fields, now properties); `ResetForLoad` swaps.
- `CommittedTreeRestoreAttempt`: the armed attempt (4 fields, private accessors keep the old names); `ResetForLoad` swaps.
- `InertRecordingTrees`: the held trees, their id sets and the notice latch (4 fields); `Clear` (BeginLoad, `ResetForLoad`, the test reset) swaps. No caller keeps a reference to the old lists.
- `RewindContext`: the plain-rewind context (16 properties, the three save-clock UTs start at NaN in the holder); `ResetForTesting` (which `ResetForSaveLoad` calls after its Warn) swaps. `EndRewind` still clears its subset.
- `RewindInvokeContext`: the Re-Fly invoke context (11 fields, now properties); `Clear` swaps to a holder naming no slot (-1). The arch IL cells that named `::Pending` and `::CapturedBundle` re-anchor (no save static is cleared by `ldsflda` + `initobj` any more; the fixture cells keep that rule covered).
- Re-pin: `facts_pins.toml` `crossTypeStaticWrites` stays at 55 with the same keys. The extractor now counts another type's call to a static property setter that reads a `ColdResetState` holder as a cross-type static write keyed by the property, so the 14 keys the holders moved (`RewindInvokeContext` x11, `SceneEntryVesselScope` x3) are still seen (a first re-pin to 41 had let the gate go blind to them). A call to a holder type's method that assigns holder fields is not counted. The lifetime gate still reads every holder field as save-scoped (7 holders, 51 fields), findings 0, `lifetime_pins.toml` unchanged.

## ~~COLD-RESET-LEFTOVERS~~: four save / load-transition statics a Cold load leaves set [FILED 2026-11-14 from the ARCH-COLD-RESET-HOLDERS cold-loader cells, by a headless test; none reproduced in play, low. FIXED 2026-11-14 on branch `item23-cold-reset-leftovers`, headless only]

- `RevertDetector.pending` and `revertTargetVesselPids`: consumed only by `OnLoad`'s
  in-session branch (`RevertDetector.Consume`, `ConsumeRevertTargetVesselPids`); the Cold
  branch, the reset helper and the main-menu transition never read or clear them. A revert
  that armed them and then did not load (stock fires the event inside
  `FlightDriver.RevertToLaunch` / `RevertToPrelaunch`, before `HighLogic.LoadScene`) would
  carry into the next save, where the first in-session load would classify as a revert. The
  lifetimes gate passes them by reachability only (the in-session consume is in the closure).
- `DiscardReFlyLoadIntent.armedTarget`: `Clear` and `TryConsume` drop `armed`, the session and
  the UT but keep the target. Inert while `armed` is false (every reader checks it); the
  lifetimes gate passes it through `ResetForTesting` reachability (docs/dev/arch/README.md,
  "Static lifetimes", Limits).
- `VesselNameStore.lastPostInitState`: tagged `save` by the type default, but `Load` keeps it
  with the flight epoch on purpose (`ClearRevertUndoState(resetEpoch: false)`); the tag is the
  thing to fix (a `process` field entry, beside `FlightEpoch`), not the code.

**Fix.** All four closed through the existing paths; `ColdLoaderKnownGaps` is empty.

- `RevertDetector.DropForColdLoad(reason)`, called by `ResetSaveScopedSessionState` after the
  load is classified, clears both fields and logs one line (Warn
  `Cold load dropped a stale pending revert: kind=.. targetPids=.. reason=..` when either was
  set, Verbose otherwise). Only a Cold load drops it: a load from the main menu or of another
  save folder. A load of the same save that finds `initialLoadDone` true (F9, the pause-menu
  Load into the same folder) with a revert pending still classifies in session by design
  (`ClassifyEarly` treats it as the revert's own load) and consumes the revert there. No race
  with the consumer: `ClassifyEarly` reads the kind before the reset, and `Consume` runs only in
  the in-session branch, which a Cold load never enters. The pending kind
  is also read at scene exit (`SceneExitInterceptor` persistent-write skip, the merge flow's
  save-file stash), so a stale one would have misled those too.
- `DiscardReFlyLoadIntent`: `TryConsume` and `Clear` (both paths) now reset every field, the
  target included, through one `Disarm`. Every OnLoad consumes the intent while it classifies, so
  the target was left by the consume, not only by `Clear`. Inert before (every reader checks
  `armed`); hygiene only.
- `VesselNameStore.lastPostInitState`: retagged `process` in `scripts/arch/lifetimes.toml`
  beside `FlightEpoch`; no code change. Stock rebuilds `FlightDriver.PostInitState` on every
  flight start, so the first flight ready after any load bumps the epoch whether the field is
  kept or cleared.
- Cells: `SaveScopedSessionResetTests` (`ColdLoader_ResetsEverySaveScopedStatic` rows for the
  three stores with no known gaps, `StaleRevert_IsDroppedByTheColdReset_WithAWarn`,
  `DiscardIntent_ConsumeAndClear_DropTheTarget`,
  `VesselNames_FlightEpochAndItsRevertTarget_SurviveTheColdLoad`) and, over the real OnLoad,
  `ParsekScenarioOnLoadStepOrderTests.AColdLoad_DropsAStaleRevertAndTheDiscardIntentTarget` and
  `TheRevertAndDiscardReFlyLoads_StillConsumeTheirMarkers`. Each fix reverted alone reds its
  cells; a clear moved before the classification reds the in-session cell.

## LOOP-SUN-LEG-DRAWN-OFF-PATH: a looped interplanetary ghost's short legs recorded around the Sun are drawn far from the ship and off its path [FILED 2026-11-12 from the TP-8 dumps, runs `2026-11-11_2243` and `2026-11-12_2110`; ~~FIXED 2026-11-14~~, branch `claude/project-thread-5ijjc4`]

**Measured.** `interbody-route-recorded`, the Duna supply ship "Duna Supply 1" (recording
`36c7688b8e5141f7809e2d4dbe9dc094`, treatment StockConic, body Sun), flight map at the save
clock (live UT 87,625,328, loop head UT 67,972,252). The ghost polyline pass reports
`fwdLegs=2` and the dump holds two `polyline` lines with body Sun: recorded UT
68,378,174.9 to 68,378,180.1 (20 points, 39 km long) and 68,378,239.0 to 68,378,311.3 (26
points, 521 km long), both about 406,000 s AHEAD of the head, so the forward pass is right to
pick them. Where they are drawn is not on the ship's path:
- 12.4 million km from the ship's icon (which sits on its own orbit line, within the line's
  sampling);
- 3.06 million km from the nearest point of the drawn transfer orbit line;
- at the right distance from the Sun (19.88 million km against 19.78 computed from the drawn
  conic for that instant) and the wrong angle: about 37 degrees BEHIND the icon along the
  orbit, where the instant is about 9 degrees ahead of it.
Both flights dumped the same two lines at the same place, so it is not from the supply route
overview line or its removal.

**On screen.** At the whole-system zoom the two legs are far below one pixel (the longer is
521 km on a map 40 million km wide), so no TP-8 picture shows them. A player would see a
short stray line only by zooming in on that empty spot.

**Not established.** The cause. Right distance with wrong angle fits a leg stored against the
Sun's own rotating frame and placed with the Sun's rotation at the live clock, or a leg left
in the recorded frame while the transfer conic is re-aimed; neither was checked in the code,
and the leg anchoring to the bracketing conic (`TryAnchorLegToConicSeam`) left no line in the
carried log slice. Also not checked: where the ship's ICON goes while the loop head is inside
those 77 s, and whether a looped mission outside a supply route does the same (the pass is the
same, so it should).

**Next.** Read why the forward legs of a Sun-bodied section are not anchored to the drawn
conic; a lane needs an instant with the head just before those legs, which
`interbody-route-recorded` cannot give (no derivable dispatch instant, see above), so a looped
Duna mission host with an off-rails stretch in solar orbit is the likely subject.

**Cause (2026-11-14).** The loop unit is a RE-AIM: `GhostMapPresence.ResolveEffectiveMapOrbitSegments`
replaces the three recorded Sun segments [63,901,473.6 .. 68,378,174.7], [68,378,180.4 ..
68,378,236.0], [68,378,313.4 .. 72,258,643.3] with ONE synthesized transfer conic over
[63,901,473.6 .. 72,258,643.3] (drawn LAN 208.18, argPe 2.40 against the recorded 156.18 /
12.72). The two burn legs sit in the gaps between the recorded segments, so they are geometry
of the transfer the re-aim replaced; the forward pass drew them from their recorded frames
(and `TryAnchorLegToConicSeam` anchors to the RECORDED segments), which is the recorded
inertial position, 37 degrees behind the re-aimed icon. Not a frame-rotation bug.

**Fix.** `GhostTrajectoryPolylineRenderer.IsLegSupersededByReaimedConic` (pure): a leg on the
re-aim's common-ancestor body lying wholly inside one synthesized segment of the effective list
is not drawn. `TryResolveReaimedLegFilter` turns it on only when the unit is a re-aim and the
resolver returned a list other than the recorded one, so faithful members and declined windows
draw exactly as before. Read by the head-gated pass, the head-leg bridge candidate and the
forward run legs; each skip logs `Leg hidden (inside re-aimed conic): ... pass=<head|forward>`.
Tests `ReaimSupersededLegTests` (TP-8 numbers); TP-8 gates the forward-pass line for the two
legs. Not covered: the icon while the loop head is inside those 77 s (no lane instant).

## ROUTE-CREATION-TREE-IDS-UNREAD: `Route.CreationTreeRecordingIds` is saved and loaded but nothing reads it [FILED 2026-11-12 with ROUTE-LINE-DETACHED-SEGMENTS; OPEN]

**Fact.** `Route.CreationTreeRecordingIds` (persisted as `CREATION_TREE_RECORDINGS` by
`RouteCodec`) had one runtime reader, the supply route overview line. That line is retired, so
the field is written at route creation, saved and loaded, and read by nothing at runtime. It is
also present in the format golden and the committed route fixtures.

**Allowed fix.** Remove the field and stop writing and reading the key. The save-format policy's
retired-key precedent covers it (`docs/dev/design-save-format-policy.md`: deleting a retired
feature's keys is not a shape change when their absence already means the feature-off default):
old saves load with the key ignored and drop it on the next save, committed fixtures and the
frozen golden keep the inert lines, and no format number moves.

**Why it is not done yet.** The retirement was kept to the map line; the field and its save /
load are untouched there.

## ~~REFLY-ANCHOR-EPSILON-1300KM~~: Re-Fly render anchors in RW-5 / RW-6 / RW-7 carried offsets of 64 km to 22,820 km [FILED 2026-11-12 from the first real run index (`run_index.py health-regressions`), runs `2026-11-11_0218_RW-5`, `2026-11-10_2237_RW-6`, `2026-11-11_0140_RW-7`. CAUSE FOUND 2026-11-12 (a frame defect in the seed epsilon, reproduced headless and confirmed from the PC logs). FIXED 2026-11-12 headless; open only for the live proof below]

**Symptom.** The three lanes pass, and their WARN count rose from 19 / 31 / 55 (runs of
2026-11-06) to 357 / 533 / 558. Every extra line is one message on the tag `Pipeline-Anchor`:
`Anchor <epsilon> exceeds bubble radius: recordingId=... sectionIndex=... side=... anchorSource=...
epsilonMagnitudeM=... bubbleRadiusM=2500`, 336 / 504 / 504 lines over 2 / 3 / 3 session rebuilds
(UT about 185,800.5 and 185,786.9), one per seeded anchor per rebuild (sources BubbleExit,
BubbleEntry, OrbitalCheckpoint and the DockOrMerge anchors that inherit them). The PC logs show
the magnitudes SPREAD from 64 km to 22,820 km, and the same anchor reads differently at each
rebuild (the earlier "1,308 to 1,311 km" reading was one anchor, the CS Orbiter LKO exit
`e312c6a9...` section 6/7, at 1,307.87 km). The warning was new visibility (commit 334b6cfd2,
2026-11-07, calls it from `PutAnchorWithPriority`), not new behaviour: the values were wrong and
applied.

**Cause.** `AnchorPropagator.TryResolveSeedEpsilon` computed `epsilon = worldRef - smoothed` with
one side a Kepler position at the boundary UT placed through the CURRENT `Planetarium.Zup` and the
other a body-fixed point placed through the body's CURRENT rotation, both read at the session
rebuild rather than at the boundary UT `t_b`. Every seed carried the body's rotation since its
boundary: a chord `2 r cos(lat) |sin(pi (now - t_b) / T_rot)|`, each seed with its own phase. The
recorded data are sound: on `cs-career-mun4` the stored-frame Kepler point and the physics sample
agree within 5 m at `t_b` on all 115 Kerbin and Mun bubble boundaries.

**What the player saw.** During a Re-Fly session only, in FLIGHT: the positioner adds the anchor
epsilon as a world translation through `allowRenderAnchorCorrectionInterval` (PointInterp, spline
and checkpoint paths, and the LateUpdate re-apply in `ParsekFlightPlaybackHost`). The correction
covers the whole TrackSection that owns the anchor: a Start-only or End-only anchor is a constant
offset over the section, an anchor on both ends is lerped between them
(`RenderSessionState.LookupForSegmentInterval` -> `AnchorCorrectionInterval.EvaluateAt`). So a
committed ghost playing such a section (an orbital coast, or the launch / re-entry leg next to
one) was drawn tens to thousands of km from its true place while in view or watched. Map
proto-vessel orbits never read the epsilon. The RW lanes assert no rendered position.

**Fix (2026-11-12).** BubbleExit, BubbleEntry and OrbitalCheckpoint seeds no longer go through the
world-frame resolver. `AnchorPropagator.TryResolveBoundaryInstantEpsilon` takes both sides of the
boundary from recorded data at `t_b` and in one frame: the Kepler side is read in the STORED
element frame (`TwoBodyOrbit.TryCreateFromSegmentStoredFrame`, no Zup) and turned into body-fixed
lat / lon / alt by `TrajectoryMath.BoundaryFrame` (body-fixed lon = inertial lon -
`rotationAngle(t_b)`, `rotationAngle = initialRotation + 360 t / T_rot`, from decompiled
`CBUpdate`); the other side is the recorded physics sample (Bubble) or the spline at `t_b`
(OrbitalCheckpoint; tag 1 lowered by `lon - 360 t_b / T_rot`). Both body-fixed points are then
placed through the same surface lookup at the rebuild, so `|epsilon|` is independent of when the
rebuild runs; the stored vector is a world-frame translation oriented by the body's rotation at the
rebuild (the orientation playback uses to lower a body-fixed sample), and its later drift as the
body turns is at most `2 |epsilon|`, i.e. metres. The DAG summary line gains
`boundaryInstantMaxEpsilonM=`. Measured on the fixture: the LKO exit 1,307.87 km -> 0.02 m, worst
seed 4.97 m, zero over the bubble radius, magnitudes equal across rebuild clocks to 1e-7 m. Tests:
`AnchorEpsilonRebuildClockTests` (the flipped characterization), `AnchorBoundaryInstantEpsilonTests`,
`AnchorWorldFrameResolverTests.BoundaryInstantSources_NeverConsultTheResolver`; the H11 / LT-1
in-game cells `Pipeline_Anchor_OrbitalCheckpoint` / `BubbleExit` / `BubbleEntry` now run the real
propagator against a live body and assert `0 < |eps| < 5 m`. RW-5 / RW-6 / RW-7 forbid the
`exceeds bubble radius` line.

**The two residuals, fixed 2026-11-12 (headless).** Both are the same mixed-frame class, on synthetic
recordings (no committed fixture has either shape, see (5)); the failing-first cells read, at
rebuild clocks of 0 / T/4 / T/2 after the boundary (T the Absolute body's day):

## ~~REAIM-PARKING-ICON-AFTER-LANDING: after a time jump over a looped re-aimed landing, the ship shows in the parking orbit a month later~~ [FILED 2026-11-11 from the TP-4 pictures, runs `2026-11-11_2238` and `_2316`; NARROWED 2026-11-11 by run `_2332`: after a landing that PLAYED the map is clean. FIXED AND FLOWN 2026-11-12 (PR #2579): the destination transfer member stays hidden from the end of the landing to the next cycle, on the map and in flight; xUnit, and four check lanes green on the first attempt (`2026-11-12_0700` TP-9, `_0701` TP-4, `_0704` V25M, `_0705` AT-1). Not measured: the 3D flight ghost near Duna after the landing (unit tests only) and a watched transfer ghost; low]

**What the player saw.** Loop a Kerbin -> Duna landing and watch it land: the ghost
arrives, parks, deorbits and lands, and the map at Duna stays empty from then on, as it should
(photographed right after the landing and a month later). The leftover needs a time jump that
skips the whole landing (a Parsek jump across the 5.7 hour descent window): the lander is then
never shown, and about a month of game time later the ship's icon and orbit line sit in the low
Duna parking orbit for about 13.6 hours. Stock fades a vessel's line and icon with camera
distance, so it shows only with the map camera within about 12 Mm of Duna.

**Evidence.** Fixture `duna-park-recorded`, tree `ced78481...`, re-aim engaged with
`captureShift=-2860032.857s`. The descent window is `[5357413107.29558,5357433620.6203632]`.
- Run `_2238` jumped from the transfer straight to live UT 5,360,144,085 and printed `DESCENT
  SKIPPED cycle=0 ... cause=frame-stepped-over-window`. There the log reads `transfer/loiter
  member=11 cycle=0 unitDescentPhase=Done baseDecision=Render ... -> kept (loiter/normal icon)`,
  the map trace reads `Orbit line decision: pid=3322786469 reason=director-stockconic-visible
  lineActive=True drawIcons=OBJ ... bounds=[5360095095.6,5360144182.0]` for recording
  `aa48920e...`, and the three dumps list a `Kerbal X` proto ghost on a Duna conic (sma
  495,883 m, ecc 0.042) with its icon 516 km from Duna's centre. Those views sat 1.05e8 m out,
  where stock had faded line and icon, so the screenshots show nothing; the bounds are the
  49,086 s parking conic at the RECORDED loop-clock slot.
- Runs `_2316` and `_2332` played the landing (no `DESCENT SKIPPED`). At 5,357,413,167 the
  descent member took the chain's map presence and the transfer member's proto ghost went
  (`destroy: rec=aa48920e... ghostPid=3667796649 ... reason=chain-segment-replaced`,
  `RemovePreviousChainMapVessel`); nothing creates it again. `tp4-c1-after-duna-low-top`
  (6,380 s after the window closed) and `tp4-c1-late-duna-low-top` (5,360,120,010, inside the
  recorded slot, Duna from 1.5e6 m) each list one ghost, the probe left at Kerbin, and the
  screenshots show Duna with the fixture's two landed vessels and nothing in orbit
  (`lifecycle-summary ... vesselsTracked=1`).

**Cause.** One rule decides whether a member of a looped re-aimed unit is hidden for the
descent, `GhostPlaybackLogic.ShouldHideNonDescentMemberForDescentHandoff`
(`GhostPlaybackLogic.SpanClock.cs`), read by the map / Tracking Station resolver
(`ResolveTrackingStationSampleUT`) and by the flight engine
(`GhostPlaybackEngine.ApplyDescentHandoffHide`). It hid a non-descent member only while the unit
phase was `Descent`. In `Done` (the landing's clip has ended; the phase lasts until the cycle
index changes) the transfer member's raw span clock is still inside its window, so both
surfaces kept it and the loiter-gap clamp wrapped its head back onto the parking conic. After a
played landing the chain dedup had already removed its map presence, so only the 3D ghost was
left circling; after a skipped landing nothing had removed anything, and the conic, the icon
and the ghost all showed at the recorded slot.

**Fix.** The rule also answers true when the phase is `Done` and the member is the unit's
`TransferMemberIndex`. Nothing else moved: both call sites keep their gate (the unit has a
descent trigger and the member's own decision is Render) and their place before the loiter-gap
clamp, so a hidden member is never clamped. Inert and Loiter are unchanged, the next cycle
starts Inert and shows the member again, a ride-along that is not the transfer member (member
7 of this fixture, the probe left at Kerbin) keeps rendering in `Done`, and a unit with no
descent trigger never reaches the rule. This is also the answer for the skipped case: the
landing is over whether or not it was drawn, so the ship is not shown in orbit after it.
- The resolver's and the engine's rate-limited lines keep their two wordings and gain a third
  for this case, `-> HIDDEN (landed; journey over until the next cycle)`
  (`DescribeDescentHandoffOutcome`); the engine's hide line and destroy reason read `landed`
  instead of `descent handoff` (`DescribeUnitMemberHide`).
- No map consumer needed a change, by reading: every one reads the resolver's hidden answer
  before it reaches a loiter-gap or line-hold call. Flight map: the pending-create pass skips
  (`GhostMapPresence.FlightMapLifecycle.cs`), the reseed and state-vector passes tear the proto
  down, and the teardown's requeue is skipped again on the next pass. Tracking Station: the
  create and startup passes skip and the refresh returns `mission-loop-out-of-window`
  (`GhostMapPresence.TrackingStationLifecycle.cs`). The chain sampler returns an outside
  sample, the two marker sites skip, and the polyline's primary does not render. The orbit-line
  patch's loiter icon drive and the parking-conic line hold act on a live proto only; the hold
  expires at the live trigger UT and its stamp goes with the proto.

**Tests (xUnit, headless).** `DescentTriggerTests` (the rule in `Done` for the transfer
member, the ride-along and the owner; the resolver across the whole of `Done`, at the next
cycle's Inert, on a skipped descent, and on a unit with no trigger; the two existing handoff
facts now expect the transfer member hidden in `Done`), `DescentHandoffResolverLogTests` (the
three wordings and their rate keys), `UnitMemberPlaybackCharacterizationTests` (the engine
call, its log line, the hide and destroy wording, and a drive through the whole member update:
transfer hidden, ride-along rendered, next cycle rendered), `TrackingStationRefreshPhaseTests`
and `FlightMapPassPhaseTests` (the two lifecycle answers named above). The in-game cell
`DescentHandoffVisibility` now asserts the hide in its `Done` section; no committed lane runs
it on a unit with a descent trigger (H54's fixture has none, so the cell skips there).

**Flown 2026-11-12, flown head 748e20428** (automation DLL sha256 `0447f7da...`, provisioned
from worktree `Parsek-reaim-landed`; outputs on branch `carrier/reaim-landed-2026-11-12`,
commit ec9adc0e6, dir `carrier/reaim-landed/`). Four lanes, each PASS on attempt 1:
- **The skipped landing: `2026-11-12_0700_TP-9-duna-reaim-skipped-landing-map-pictures`**
  (wall 65 s). The jump stepped over the window: `DESCENT SKIPPED cycle=0: reached Done at
  liveUT=5360120000 with NO frame inside the descent window
  [5357413107.29558,5357433620.6203632] ... prevFrameUT=5355451931.8601112 frameStep=4668068s
  cause=frame-stepped-over-window`. Both surfaces hid the ship: `engine transfer/loiter
  member=11 cycle=0 unitDescentPhase=Done baseDecision=Render liveUT=5360120000
  loopUT=2570430990.486022 -> HIDDEN (landed; journey over until the next cycle)` and the
  resolver's twin. The log holds 12 `unitDescentPhase=Done` lines, 6 for member 11 (hidden)
  and 6 for member 7, the Kerbal X Probe at Kerbin (kept); no `loiter-circle` line and no line
  with `bounds=[5360095095.6,5360144182.0]`. The map dump lists one ghost, the Kerbal X Probe
  (index 7, body Kerbin), and nothing at Duna; the picture shows Duna with the fixture's two
  landed vessels and nothing in orbit.
- **The played landing: `2026-11-12_0701_TP-4-duna-reaim-landing-map-pictures`** (wall 149 s,
  14 views). `DESCENT RENDERED cycle=0 member=12`. The `c1-after` and `c1-late` dumps list
  only the Kerbal X Probe at Kerbin and nothing at Duna, as before the fix. The resolver and
  the engine print `member=11 ... unitDescentPhase=Done ... -> HIDDEN (landed; ...)` at
  liveUT=5357440000 (8 such lines in the log, none kept for member 11, no `loiter-circle` line). The
  log has no destroy line with a `landed hide` reason: member 11's ghost was not active when
  the unit reached `Done` in this map-view flight.
- **`2026-11-12_0704_V25M-duna-park-player-loop`** (wall 47 s). Its third window is `Done`
  inside the recorded slot after a jump over the descent window, so the transfer member it used
  to observe there is now hidden. The armed block still passes: `status=PASS gating=True ...
  dwells=2 cycles=0 unevaluable=68 findings={'FAIL': 0, 'WARN': 0, 'INFO': 1} mismatches=0`,
  seam kinds rigid 8 and flexible-soi 2; the expectations row reads PASS with no mismatch. The
  census in the spec header was re-read off this run. Its log holds the hide itself: `engine
  transfer/loiter member=11 cycle=0 unitDescentPhase=Done ... liveUT=5360143765 ... -> HIDDEN
  (landed; journey over until the next cycle)`, and no kept line for member 11 in `Done`.
- **`2026-11-12_0705_AT-1-duna-atmospheric-descent`** (wall 47 s). It never reaches `Done`
  (4 Loiter and 3 Descent phase lines), so the fix does not touch it.

**Correction (clean review, 2026-11-12).** The bounds quoted above from run `_2238`,
`[5360095095.6,5360144182.0]`, are not a fixed "recorded slot": they are the parking conic
with its head wrapped onto the last parking period at the frame that printed them, so they
move with the instant. Before the fix the ship showed in the parking orbit for the whole of
`Done` after a skipped landing (about a month, until its recording ran out), not only inside
one window; the wording "recorded loop-clock slot" in this entry, the TP-4 and TP-9 headers and
the status rows should be read that way. TP-9's third forbidden pin was a literal on those
bounds and could not fire at its own instant; it now keys on the transfer recording's proto
orbit line switching on after the jump, read against the first flight's log (0 matches) and
run `_2238`'s (42).

**Not measured.**
- The 3D flight ghost near Duna after the landing. No flight has photographed it and no flown
  log holds its teardown: in all four lanes the active vessel sits at Kerbin, and in TP-4 the
  transfer member's ghost was not active at `Done`. That the engine hides and destroys the
  ghost there is proven by the unit tests only. A lane with the active vessel in low Duna orbit
  would settle it.
- A watched transfer member. The watch camera's owner is kept alive hidden through `Done` the
  same way it is through `Descent`; whether the camera should move to the landed vessel's site
  instead has no test and no picture.

**Follow-up (test only, not started).** V25M's third window was written to watch the Duna
arrival and sits at the RECORDED loop-clock slot, which since the re-aim is a month after the
landing: it now looks at an empty Duna (dwells 3 -> 2). Move its three jumps to the live
arrival and parking window TP-4 uses (5,357,320,632 onward) to give the lane its Duna subject
back; that needs a reading flight before its armed windows are trusted again.

## MAP-PICTURE-LANES-FIRST-FLIGHT: the eight map picture lanes TP-1..TP-8 flew green twice; TP-4 photographed the wrong Duna instants and is re-pinned [FILED 2026-11-11 with the lanes; FIRST FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-11; dump fix and `MapCamera hold` RE-FLOWN GREEN 2026-11-11 (PR #2570); TP-4 Duna instants re-pinned and FLOWN GREEN (`2026-11-11_2316`), and again with closer arrival views and a late-slot view (`2026-11-11_2332`). OPEN for the dump's icon fade and the efficiency check; no flight owed]

The first lanes wired to the `DumpMapGeometry` / `MapCamera` seam verbs: operator-tier picture
lanes that copy a model lane's fixture, loop setup and measured jumps (TP-1 V6M, TP-2 V6T, TP-3
V7M, TP-4 V25M, TP-5 V17M, TP-6 V23M, TP-7 V18T, TP-8 V26M; V26M was deleted 2026-11-12 with
the supply route overview line, ROUTE-LINE-DETACHED-SEGMENTS, which also took the route-line
step and tokens of TP-7 and TP-8) and take 85 views
(`MapCamera` -> `CaptureScreenshot` -> `DumpMapGeometry`, one label per view) for the map mirror
page (`docs/dev/design-map-mirror.md` -> "How to get the pictures").

**First flight, 2026-11-11, flown head c158d338a: all eight PASS.** Runs `2026-11-11_2146` TP-1,
`_2148` TP-8, `_2149` TP-2, `_2150` TP-3, `_2151` TP-5, `_2153` TP-6, `_2154` TP-4, `_2155` TP-7
(wall 56 to 91 s). 85 views, every `mapcamera ok` with `pitchClamped=false distanceClamped=false`;
TP-2 and TP-7 loaded the Tracking Station three times in one process without a refusal.

**Defect found on the page: ghost orbit lines dumped `active:true` with stale points.** Read from
the KSP 1.12.5 IL (`docs/dev/design-map-geometry-dump.md` -> "Stock's orbit-line fade"): a
vessel orbit line fades by camera distance in `OrbitRendererBase.SplineOpacityUpdate` (toward 1
inside a camera-distance / SMA window, toward 0 outside it, `0.25 * Time.deltaTime` per frame,
so 4 s per full fade); at `lineOpacity == 0` `DrawOrbit` returns before `UpdateSpline`, so the
points freeze where they were last drawn, and Parsek's `GhostOrbitLinePatch` keeps the line
object active. The dump took that as drawn. On the first-flight dumps the page's conic check
flags 24 lines in 21 captures as off their own conic (TP-1 and TP-3 Kerbin / Minmus arrival
views, most of TP-4 from the Duna transfer to the landing, TP-5 Jool arrival in both cycles,
`tp8-save-clock-duna-top`), every one `clipped:false`; `tp1-c1-arrival-kerbin-top` draws a
hyperbola's points at 3.79e7 m whose periapsis is 3.4e5 m, and `tp1-c2-arrival-kerbin-top` has
points on the right conic but the shape of an earlier clipped arc.

Fix (this branch): the dump reads `lineOpacity` (fail soft) and the effective draw mode and
writes an orbit line drawn only when `active && enabled && drawMode != OFF && opacity > 0`
(`MapGeometryDecisions.ClassifyOrbitLine`; an unreadable opacity keeps the old rule and is
counted); a faded line is `active:false` with no points, every orbit line carries the additive
`opacity` / `drawMode` keys, and `dumpmapgeometry captured:` counts `orbitLinesFaded=` /
`orbitOpacityUnknown=`. The page draws a part-faded line lighter, lists a faded one as "not drawn
(stock fade)" and flags a drawn line off its conic in red on the lane rail. Not handled, by
design: a line in REDRAW_ONLY / REDRAW_AND_FOLLOW draws its stored points without recomputing them
(Parsek sets REDRAW_AND_RECALCULATE on every ghost renderer; the dump names the mode), and a
debris line without mouse-over or a map-filtered line does not update its opacity. `MapCamera`
gains `hold=<seconds>` (0..10, real time; settle budget = step budget minus hold), and every TP
view holds 4.5 s so a fade started by the new frame finishes before the screenshot.

**Re-fly with the fix, 2026-11-11, flown head 3fdcfc1b6: all eight PASS on the first attempt.**
Runs `2026-11-11_2236` TP-1, `_2238` TP-4, `_2240` TP-3, `_2243` TP-8, `_2244` TP-2, `_2246` TP-5,
`_2248` TP-6, `_2250` TP-7 (wall 88 to 150 s). All 85 `mapcamera ok` lines carry `hold=4.5`, none
clamped; 39 orbit lines read faded, `orbitOpacityUnknown=0` on every capture; the page's conic
check flags no drawn line. Outputs: branch `carrier/tp-pictures-2026-11-11-run2`.

Read from those pictures:
- EXPLAINED, by design: the 46.6 km gap at `tp1-c1-arrival-mun-top` between the end of the Mun
  arrival orbit line and the start of the descent polyline. The polyline leg is drawn fixed to
  the rotating body and the conic is inertial, so before the ghost reaches the seam the two sit
  apart by the body's rotation over the time still to go, and they meet at the seam instant. The
  leg's first point moved 202 m in the 9.46 s between the two flights' captures (the Mun's
  rotation at that radius), and TP-6's three Mun instants read 8.700, -0.352 and -3.025 degrees
  about the spin axis at UT 1,268,422 / 1,271,916 / 1,272,948: the Mun's rate to three digits,
  through zero at the seam. The same shape reads at Vall (`tp5-c1-arrival-vall-edge`, 11.4 deg).
- The other derived instants show the ghost where their names say: TP-1 / TP-2 park at 140 km
  over the Mun, TP-3 park at 38 km over Minmus, TP-6 approach at 1,335 km, descent at 134 km and
  landing at 8 km, TP-7's `60,149` near the dock.
- WRONG, re-pinned: TP-4's arrival, descent and landing instants. Both flights jumped to the
  RECORDED loop-clock slots (5,360,144,085 / 5,360,227,434 / 5,360,227,534) and the six descent
  and landing views hold no lander (`legs=0 markersDrawn=0`, only the Kerbin-side probe; the two
  icons on Duna in the screenshots are the fixture's own landed vessels). A re-aimed landing does
  not play there: the transfer is shorter than recorded (`captureShift=-2860032.857s`), the ghost
  reaches Duna early and `Reaim/DescentTrigger.cs` plays the descent from its own window, which
  run `_2238` printed: `DESCENT SKIPPED cycle=0: reached Done at liveUT=5360144085 with NO frame
  inside the descent window [5357413107.29558,5357433620.6203632] ...
  cause=frame-stepped-over-window`. TP-4 now jumps to 5,357,320,632 (600 s before the re-aimed
  capture), 5,357,413,167 and 5,357,413,297 (60 s and 190 s into the window) and adds
  `tp4-c1-after-duna-low-top` at 5,357,440,000 (13 views). The model lane V25M is untouched (its

- Stock fades a vessel orbit line out once the camera is more than 25 SMA away, so the SOI-scale
