## ~~WARP-REQUEST-SURVIVES-A-FAILED-REWIND: a Warp to time request stays armed after its rewind fails to launch, and the next Space Center load jumps forward~~ [FILED 2026-11-11 from the static lifetimes gate (coldLoadMisses, the nine `WarpToTimeRequest` fields), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-11, branch `claude/project-thread-lkzj01`; xUnit (headless, the real `InitiateRewind` failure paths included) + the static lifetimes gate (coldLoadMisses 9 -> 0); not flown (no committed lane drives Warp to time through a rewind); low]

The chain, read in the source (line numbers as of the static lifetimes branch):

1. `WarpToTimeController.StartRewind` arms the request (`WarpToTimeRequest.Set`,
   `WarpToTimeController.cs:345`) and then calls `RewindLauncher.InitiateRewind(ownerNow)`
   (`:349`), which returns void (`RewindLauncher.cs:416`), so the caller cannot see a failure.
2. `InitiateRewind` returns early when the rewind owner does not resolve
   (`RewindLauncher.cs:421-428`) and when a re-fly merge journal is unfinished (`:443-451`;
   `CanRewind`, `:239`, which `StartRewind` checks first, does not look at the journal). When
   `ExecuteRewindSaveLoad` fails (LoadGame returned null, `:614`, or threw, `:683`) it returns
   false and `InitiateRewind` only undoes the live-tree drop (`:469-470`). None of these paths
   clears the request; `ResetRewindFlags` (`:403`) does not touch it. The career-start branch
   does clear on a refused launch (`WarpToTimeController.cs:318-322`).
3. Nothing else clears it: its only writers are `Set`, `Clear` and `ResetForTesting`, and `Clear`
   is called only by `StartRewind`'s own abort paths and by the consumer. The lifetimes gate
   shows no Cold load path clears it, and no main-menu transition does either.
4. `WarpToTimeConsumer.HandleLevelWasLoaded` (`WarpToTimeConsumer.cs:60-108`) runs on every
   `onLevelWasLoaded(SPACECENTER)`: with `HasPending` and the same process session it starts
   `ConsumePendingWarp`, which calls `TimeJumpManager.ExecuteForwardJump(target)` when the clock
   is behind the target (`:166-215`). `IsStale` (`WarpToTimeRequest.cs:48-51`) rejects only a
   request from another process.

So after a failed launch the next Space Center load of the same process jumps the clock forward
to the old target: a return from the VAB / SPH in the same save, or another save loaded from the
main menu. The deferred flight warp (`SetDeferredKscWarp`) has the same no-clear property at the
Cold load and the main-menu transition.

**Fix.**
1. A rewind that does not launch drops the pending jump. `RewindLauncher.InitiateRewind` returns
   whether the Space Center load was requested (false on no owner, an unfinished merge journal,
   a null or throwing `LoadGame`), as `InitiateRewindToCareerStart` does. `StartRewind` arms
   the request through `WarpToTimeController.ArmPendingWarpAndLaunch` for both rewind kinds: arm,
   launch, and on false (or a throw) `WarpToTimeRequest.DropPending(reason)`, which logs
   `[WarpTime] Pending warp dropped: targetUT=<ut> reason=<rewind|career-start-reset>-not-launched`.
   The Recordings table ignores the result; the InvokeRewindToLaunch seam reads it beside
   `RewindContext.IsRewinding`.
2. A Cold load and the main-menu transition drop both requests (`WarpToTimeRequest.DropAll`,
   `reason=cold-load:<coldReason>` / `main-menu`, one Info line per dropped request), in
   `ParsekScenario.ResetSaveScopedSessionState` and the MAINMENU branch of `OnMainMenuTransition`.
   Neither site is on a path a legitimate request crosses: the request is armed in the Space
   Center right before a plain rewind (Rewind-to-Launch or the career-start reset), whose load
   classifies PlainRewind (`ClassifyEarly` checks `RewindContext.IsRewinding`, set before the
   `LoadGame`, ahead of the save-file rule; `GamePersistence.LoadGame` never arms
   `SaveFileLoadIntent`), and the deferred flight warp crosses a FLIGHT -> SPACECENTER scene exit
   (`HighLogic.LoadScene`, InSession); its backward case then arms the pending jump for the
   rewind's own PlainRewind load. All of them load the Space Center, never the main menu. The
   one Cold rewind load is the one `ClassifyEarly` documents (a rewind whose load finds
   `initialLoadDone` false after an earlier cold load threw), where the reset already discards
   the rewind context as stale; dropping the warp there is consistent.
3. The consumer re-reads the request after its first yield
   (`WarpToTimeConsumer.RequestDroppedWhileSettling`). `onLevelWasLoaded` fires before the
   scene's Start methods, so the scenario's OnLoad (and its Cold reset) runs between the
   handler's check and the coroutine's resume; without the re-read a dropped deferred warp would
   run `ExecuteAtKsc(0, 0, 0, 0)`.
4. `WarpToTimeRequest` joined `SaveScopedSessionResetTests`' type list (no allowlisted field: the
   reset clears all nine statics; the Guid fields mutate through the struct path), so the C#
   reset gate and the IL lifetimes gate both hold the clear. `lifetimes.toml` keeps its
   `load-transition` default; `lifetime_pins.toml` re-pinned coldLoadMisses 9 -> 0, and
   `test_a_swap_inside_a_finding_bound_passes` now builds its own one-key bound (it read the
   first pinned miss, which no longer exists).

**Validation.** `WarpToTimeRequestTests` (drop / keep, the launch wrapper launched / refused /
throwing, the consumer re-read and its wiring after the first yield, the plain-rewind and
flight-exit loads classified non-Cold, `DropAll` called only by the two sites, `StartRewind`
arming only through the wrapper); `RewindLauncherUnitTests` (the real `InitiateRewind` no-owner,
journal and load-failure paths return false and drop the pending warp through the wrapper; the
career-start refusal too); `SaveScopedSessionResetTests` (the Cold reset drops both with the
reason; the generic gate covers the new type). Not covered headless: the coroutines themselves
and the in-game ordering of `onLevelWasLoaded` before OnLoad (taken from the decompile note in
`FlightCameraReloadPin`); the main-menu clear is pinned by source, not driven. No committed
harness lane drives Warp to time through a rewind or the deferred flight warp (LT-2 runs only
the read-only `WarpToTime` ResolvePlan cell); the InvokeRewindToLaunch lanes (H58, RB-4, RF-15,
FLG-1 and the rest) exercise the touched `InitiateRewind` return.

## ROUTE-SOURCE-OPTIMIZER-REWRITE: the optimizer merged, split and trimmed recordings a supply route was built from, breaking the route [FIXED 2026-11-14, found by the C8 test of NEXT-TESTS-TO-BUILD-2026-11-11]

`CommittedListOptimizer.RunOptimizationPass` runs after every commit and on every load. It merged,
split and tail-trimmed recordings a route names in its `SourceRefs`, each of which moves a field the
route captured (the id on a merge, `EndUT` on a split or trim), so the next
`RouteStore.RevalidateSources` set the route to `SourceChanged` (a dormant route to
`MissingSourceRecording`), neither of which recovers. Realistic trigger: creating a route clears the
manual loop on its tree (`RouteTreeGuard.ForceClearManualLoopForRoute`), the loop was the only thing
holding a chain pair apart, and the next pass broke the route the player had just built.
Fix: `RouteStore.CollectSourceRecordingIds` (committed + dormant routes) is collected once per pass;
the merge (`ChooseMergeCandidateIndex`), split (`ChooseSplitCandidateIndex`) and tail-trim passes
skip those recordings and log one Verbose summary each. Design section 10.16 updated (source refs
stay immutable, section 4.7). Tests: `RouteSourceOptimizerTests` (6 of the first 7 facts red before
the fix). Not covered: any `FilesDirty` flush of a source recording still advances its sidecar
epoch; `FindSplitCandidatesForOptimizer`'s `EnsureCheckpointSectionsForTopLevelOrbitSegments
(markDirty: true)` runs over sources too. Whether that can drift a source ref to SourceChanged is
unproven (follow-up below).

## ~~ROUTE-DOCKED-ORIGIN-IGNORES-ESCROW~~: a route whose docked origin is a depot may drain cargo another route reserved there [SUSPECTED 2026-11-14 by code read. CONFIRMED by code trace and FIXED 2026-11-16, branch fix-route-origin-escrow; xUnit; medium]

`LiveRouteRuntimeEnvironment.OriginProvenanceHasCargo` probes `route.Origin` without
`RouteStore.OtherRoutesReservedFor`; only `PickupSourcesHaveCargo` nets the escrow. So route A
whose docked origin is depot D can take fuel an in-flight multi-stop route B reserved at its later
pickup window at D. B's pickup debit then comes up short, but B's delivery still writes its full
recorded `DeliveryManifest` (`RouteDeliveryPlanner` never reads what was picked up): cargo is
created. Proving it needs a live origin resolve (FlightGlobals), so an in-game test or a seam.
Also check here: whether a sidecar flush of a source recording (see ROUTE-SOURCE-OPTIMIZER-REWRITE)
can move a route to SourceChanged.

Confirmed by trace (no live run): `OriginProvenanceHasCargo` gated `route.CostManifest` on the raw
origin probe, and a multi-stop cycle reserves its pickup escrow at dispatch
(`ProcessMultiStopCrossings` -> `ReserveCycleEscrow`) but debits the source only at the pickup
window, so in that gap a docked-origin route A at depot D passed its gate on B's reserved cargo and
its loop-path dispatch physically drained D (`EmitDispatchDebit` -> `ApplyOriginDebit`, clamped
to stored). B's later `EmitPickupHalf` then clamped short (row actual < requested), while B's
delivery (`ApplyDelivery` -> `RouteDeliveryPlanner.PrepareDelivery`) planned from the stop's
recorded `DeliveryManifest` only and wrote the full amount. The same short-pickup-full-delivery
path was reachable without a second route (the player draining the depot between B's dispatch and
its pickup window, or a pickup / origin endpoint unresolved at the debit).

Fix, two halves. (1) The origin gate nets other routes' escrow on the origin pid exactly as the
pickup gate does: the pure `RoutePickupSourceGate.OriginCoversNetOfOtherRoutes` (raw reader +
`RouteStore.OtherRoutesReservedFor` reader, `NettedAvailable` net, own reservation not netted,
`IsEscrowCausedShort` classification); an escrow-caused origin short holds with the existing
`source-reserved:` token, so the Logistics window says "<depot> has <resource> reserved by route
'<name>'"; one `OriginHasCargo ... short-cause=` Verbose line per blocked check. (2) A delivery
never writes more than the cycle put on board: `RouteOrchestrator.ComputeCycleSupplyDeficit`
walks this route and cycle's persisted debit / pickup / delivery rows in Sequence order (a debit
or pickup row adds `requested - actual`, an earlier delivery row subtracts what it kept on board,
floored at zero); `RouteOrchestrator.ComputeDeliveryHoldback` turns that deficit into what THIS
delivery holds back, the deficit less what the route's later deliveries of the resource can
absorb (`LaterDeliveriesAbsorbable`: the largest running total, over the later stops in window
order, of recorded deliveries minus recorded pickups, read at each later delivery; a later
pickup feeds the delivery after it, so it cannot absorb a shortfall from before it), and
`PrepareDelivery(..., supplyHoldback)` caps each resource at recorded minus holdback (the line
keeps the recorded amount as Requested, so it reads as a partial delivery in the row and the
existing last-partial-delivery line). So the cargo aboard goes to the first stop that wants it
and the shortfall lands on the last ones (debit 40 short of 100, stops of 50 and 50: 50 then
10), the cycle never delivers more than it took on, and a harvest route, which books no row
for harvested cargo, is never capped while its debit and pickups are met. `ApplyDelivery`
computes both from `RouteEventLog.Events` and the route's stops and logs a
`supply short this cycle - capping delivery` Warn with the deficit and the part held back here
(a review of the first cut, which put the whole deficit on the first delivery, found it starved
the first stop and could lose cargo a full later destination refused). Both halves
are pure and headless; the live origin resolve stays in `LiveRouteRuntimeEnvironment`. Tests:
`RouteDockedOriginEscrowTests` (16: the netted origin gate incl. own-reservation, physical vs
escrow cause, other pid / resource, ordinal first-short, null readers; the deficit walk for a
short pickup, a short or unresolved origin debit, full supply, other cycle / route / later
window, an earlier capped delivery absorbing its share, an earlier capacity clamp flooring at
zero; the planner cap; two source pins for the live wiring) plus the holdback cells
`Holdback_ShortDebit_FirstStopGetsWhatIsAboard`, `Holdback_FullFirstDestination_*`,
`Holdback_FullSecondDestination_*`, `Holdback_LaterPickup_DoesNotAbsorbTheEarlierDeficit`,
`LaterDeliveriesAbsorbable_ReadsTheRunningTotalInWindowOrder`, `Holdback_HarvestRoute_IsNeverCapped`,
`Holdback_SingleDelivery_HoldsBackTheWholeDeficit` and `Holdback_SaveReloadMidCycle_*`
(mutation-checked: no later absorption reds six, ignoring later pickups reds three). The first test asserts the pre-fix
raw gate passes the scenario the netted gate holds.

Left open: (a) a route whose OWN docked origin and OWN later pickup are the same vessel is gated
per provenance (cost and pickup each against the full tank, not their sum); the delivery cap now
keeps that conservation-safe, but the gate can still dispatch a cycle that comes up short.
(b) Inventory: no delivery row carries its stored-part actuals, so the cap covers resources only;
a short stored-part pickup still delivers the recorded parts. (c) Live proof: AUTHORED 2026-11-16 (branch route-escrow-ingame), NOT YET FLOWN. Two
`RouteEscrowContention` FLIGHT cells gated by H60: `docked-origin-holds` (a docked-origin
competitor on the depot the multi-stop holder reserved at holds with `source-reserved:` from the
ORIGIN gate and debits nothing; the holder's second pickup and its delivery both read full,
delivered == picked up == 10) and `short-pickup-caps-delivery` (the depot drained to 2 LF between
the holder's windows; the delivery is capped at 6 == picked up, with the supply-cap Warn). Flown green
2026-11-16 (`2026-11-16_2354_H60-route-escrow-contention`, 5/5/0/0, pinned whole). Still open: a lane-level conservation read like
RCN-1's on a recorded host.

Side question (sidecar flush -> SourceChanged): the mechanism is real and by design (section
10.16 lists a sidecar epoch change): `RouteStore.FirstDifferingField` compares
`RouteSourceRef.SidecarEpoch`, and any `FilesDirty` source re-saved by OnSave bumps
`Recording.SidecarEpoch` (`RecordingSidecarStore.SaveRecordingFiles(incrementEpoch: true)`), which
reads as `SourceChanged/sidecar-epoch-drift` and never auto-recovers. The specific case named
above cannot fire in practice: `FindSplitCandidatesForOptimizer`'s
`EnsureCheckpointSectionsForTopLevelOrbitSegments(markDirty: true)` dirties a recording only on
an actual mutation (true only since 2026-11-24, CHECKPOINT-BRIDGE-COVERED-IS-NOT-A-CHANGE: until
then a checkpoint wider than its section dirtied on every pass), Ensure is idempotent (pinned by
`EnsurePassIntegrityTests.AnalysisPass_WhenEnsureIsANoOp_LeavesRecordingClean`), every recording runs through that pass at
its own commit before a route can name it, and the route captures the pending advance of that
pass's flush (`RouteSourceRef.EffectiveSidecarEpoch`). Other post-creation dirty sites on a
committed source are filed as ROUTE-SOURCE-EPOCH-ON-METADATA-REWRITE.

## ~~COLD-LOAD-UNSTAMPED-LEAF-RESTORE-SILENT-NO-MATCH~~: a real vessel whose committed leaf carries no spawn stamp is never resumed into its tree after a Cold FLIGHT load, and nothing logs why [FOUND 2026-11-16 by RSF-1's first flight; headless probe; low. FIXED 2026-11-17, branch coldload-fix; xUnit; RSF-1 reshaped to fly it]

On `rover-relay-c-recorded` the transport C (pid 612987736) has a committed leaf `ec4bf428`
with a vessel snapshot, `vesselPersistentId` and `recordedVesselGuid` equal to the live vessel,
and no `spawnedPid`. Before the crew pass, `TryFindCommittedTreeForSpawnedVessel` matches it
(direct pid + guid branch). On every Cold load into FLIGHT,
`ParsekScenario.OnLoadPhaseAutoUnreserveCrewPastEndUT` sees UT past EndUT on a leaf not marked
spawned, nulls its snapshot and sets `VesselSpawned=true` with no spawn pid. After that neither
branch matches (the spawn-stamp branch needs `SpawnedVesselPersistentId == livePid`, the direct
branch needs `!VesselSpawned`), and neither counts a refusal, so OnFlightReady and the 1 Hz
retry return silently; the player's next flight of C opens a new tree. `VesselSpawned` is
rebuilt from `spawnedPid` on load, so every Cold FLIGHT load repeats it. Normal in-flight
commits stamp the active leaf (`CommitTreeFlight`), so the reach is a leaf committed by another
path while its vessel stays real. Fix options: the crew pass stamps the live pid when the
recorded vessel exists (guid-gated), or the finder treats spawned-with-no-pid (not
`SpawnAbandoned`) as unstamped; either way the finder counts and logs the refusal. Evidence:
RSF-1 run `2026-11-16_2349` (INVALID, CommitTree `no-active-tree`); a headless probe over the
fixture's trees reads `found=True` before the crew pass and `found=False` after it.

**Fix (2026-11-17, branch `coldload-fix`):** the finder takes the second option.
`ParsekFlight.TryFindCommittedTreeForSpawnedVessel` adds a third match,
`IsUnstampedSpawnedLeafOfLiveLaunch`: spawned, no spawn pid, not `SpawnAbandoned`, and the live
vessel POSITIVELY the recorded launch (`VesselLaunchIdentity.LiveVesselIsPositivelyRecordedLaunch`:
pid equal and both launch guids known and equal; the mark carries no pid, so an unknown guid is
never enough). A match logs `matched unstamped spawned leaf '<id>' in tree '<id>' for pid=N`
(Info); a pid match the guid does not prove is counted and logged rate-limited
(`refused N committed recording(s) ... marked spawned with no spawn pid ...`). The take path's
existing clear-flags block resets the mark on the resumed clone, and the commit refreshes the
nulled snapshot from the live vessel. The crew pass is unchanged. Offline, through the
production codecs over every committed fixture save, the new match changes the active vessel's
restore on four hosts only: `rover-relay-c-recorded` (+career) C, `rover-relay-recorded` rover C
and `rover-route-recorded` (+career) B; every lane on them but GUI-13 / GUI-26 (operator) starts
with the StopRecording / DiscardTree pair. Tests: `ColdLoadUnstampedLeafRestoreTests` (5,
the two match cells red without the branch). RSF-1 is reshaped back to its first shape (the
restore re-opens the route's tree and the merge re-commits it), owed a flight.

**Follow-up (2026-11-17, same branch): the route-source guard on a tree with no committed copy.**
The first flights (run `coldload-fix2`) passed RSF-1 and eight more lanes but red H59
(`2026-11-17_1602`, PARSEK-FAIL: no `KSC SURFACE playback resolved` line, saveParse
`routes.statuses.Active 0 < min 1`). The in-game batch's final baseline restore is a Cold load in
FLIGHT with rover B active, B's leaf in route tree 73e50f1e is the unstamped one, so the new
match takes a restore clone; OnSave writes it as the active tree over the committed copy; the
load into the Space Center then stashes it pending and auto-commits it as a fresh tree. With no
committed copy in memory, `TreeCommitService.CollectUnchangedRouteSourceIds` counted both route
sources `notCommitted` (`keptUnchanged=0 notCommitted=2`), so the commit re-merged them and
marked them dirty, the flush deferred an epoch advance, and the route flipped
`Active->SourceChanged ... sidecar-epoch-drift`. Any save holding a route's tree only as the
active tree reaches the same commit (a stamped leaf resumed and saved mid-flight too), so the
guard is the fix, not the match: a source with no committed copy is kept unchanged when it is
clean (not dirty, no deferred advance) and `RouteStore.RecordingMatchesCapturedSourceRef` finds a
committed or dormant route whose captured ref equals, field for field, the ref the revalidation
would build from it now. The summary line gains `keptAtRouteCapture=N`. Tests: four cells in
`RouteSourceEpochMetadataRewriteTests` (the predicate tables, the H59 shape staying Active, and
an edited source on that path still flipping SourceChanged).

**Second flights (run `coldload-fix3`, 1c677cd059, 2 slots): 6 PASS of 9.** H59
(`2026-11-17_1805`, 6 `KSC SURFACE playback resolved` lines, `keptAtRouteCapture=2`), V27M
(same guard line), RSF-1, RVR-1, RVR-3 and RVR-21 PASS; no `->SourceChanged` in any lane. H56,
H57 and H69 (all on `rover-route-recorded`) red: the lane's `StopRecording` / `DiscardTree`
suppresses the committed-tree restore for rover B only until the scene ends, and the isolated
batch's FLIGHT baseline prime and post-test restores are fresh scenes, so each one re-adopted B's
tree through the new match and started recording (`matched unstamped spawned leaf '4370a799'`
12 / 14 / 8 times). The AutoRecord tests then skipped as "recording already active" and the dock
capture's undock never bound its origin proof. On main the crew pass's silent no-match had kept
B idle for them. Test-runner fix: a FLIGHT baseline captures the restore suppression the active
vessel carried (`FlightBatchBaselineState.CommittedRestoreSuppressedPid`), and
`ReapplyBaselineCommittedRestoreSuppression` runs after every FLIGHT baseline restore lands:
when it names the restored active vessel, it stops the recorder and discards a re-adopted clone
in memory, suppresses again and logs `re-applied the captured committed-tree restore
suppression for pid=N discardedReadoptedTree=<bool>`. Pure helpers in `InGameTestRunnerTests`; the
setter's caller gate (`CommittedSpawnedRestoreSuppressionTests`) now names the seam verb and this
automation-only restore. Re-flown as run `coldload-fix4` (e2252c2054, copy 1, serial): H56
(`2026-11-17_2045`, `total=6 passed=6`), H57 (`2026-11-17_2047`, `total=3 passed=3`), H69
(`2026-11-17_2048`, `total=10 passed=4 skipped=6`, the pinned tally) and H59 (`2026-11-17_2049`)
all PASS attempt 1; the re-apply line fired before every restore with
`discardedReadoptedTree=True` for pid 313889796; no `->SourceChanged` in any lane.

## ~~ROUTE-SOURCE-EPOCH-ON-METADATA-REWRITE~~: a content-neutral rewrite of a route's source recording may pause the route as SourceChanged for good [SUSPECTED 2026-11-16 by code read. CONFIRMED by code trace and FIXED 2026-11-16, branch fix-route-source-epoch; xUnit; low]

A route compares each source's `SidecarEpoch` (`RouteStore.FirstDifferingField`), and the next
OnSave advances the epoch of any recording marked `FilesDirty`, whatever changed. Several sites
dirty an already-committed recording without touching what a route reads (window, manifests, UT
bounds, proof hash): `RecordingGroupStore.RepairAutoGroupMembership` (group list, a .sfs-side
field), `RecordingFinalizationCacheApplier`, the hydration repairs in
`ParsekScenario.HydrationRepair.cs`. If any of them fires on a route source after the route is
built, the route turns SourceChanged at the next save and stays there (design 10.16 lets only a
recreate clear it). Not audited per site and not reproduced. Options for the owner: compare the
route proof hash and UT bounds only (drop the epoch from the drift check; the epoch is a cache
counter, not a content fingerprint), or audit and gate each dirty site against route sources as
ROUTE-SOURCE-OPTIMIZER-REWRITE did for the optimizer.

Audit (code trace, no live run). The epoch advances only when a sidecar is rewritten:
`ParsekScenario.EnsureRecordingFilesCurrentForSave` calls `SaveRecordingFiles(incrementEpoch:
true)` for a recording that is `FilesDirty`, owes a deferred advance
(`SidecarEpochAdvancePending`, set by the commit / optimizer flush) or whose files are not
current; `tree.Save` writes every recording's .sfs node on every OnSave regardless. So a
metadata-only edit moves the epoch only when its site also sets `FilesDirty`. No UI rename does:
group rename (`RecordingGroupStore.RenameGroup` / `ReplaceGroupOnAll`), mission rename
(`MissionGroupLink.RenameMissionGroup`), the vessel-name apply pass (`VesselNameStore.ApplyAll`),
ledger tagging and loop settings never dirty or re-save a sidecar (grep of `FilesDirty` /
`MarkFilesDirty` / `SaveRecordingFiles` over `Missions`, `UI`, `GameActions`, `Crew` and the
vessel-name files: no hit). Of the ~70 dirty sites, every one but four acts on the active or
pending tree, the recorders, a Re-Fly supersede / split (a designed source change) or a load-time
repair of a broken sidecar (the malformed-flat-fallback heal already keeps the epoch). The four
that dirty an already-committed route source with no sidecar change:
(1) `TreeCommitService.MergeTreeRecordingsIntoCommitted` forced `FilesDirty` on every member of a
re-committed tree, so a resumed committed vessel merged back (committed-spawned-clone restore of
the run's tree, e.g. flying the transport again after building the route) or a Re-Fly union of
that tree advanced every [root..dock] source's epoch through the commit flush; reachable in
ordinary play. (2) `MarkSupersededTerminalSpawnsForContinuedSources` and (3)
`MarkTerminalSpawnSupersededByDockMerge` set `FilesDirty` for .sfs-only spawn fields; they reach a
source only when it is a spawned / adopted leaf (a run that ended docked), and (2) also runs over
every committed tree on a rewind (`ResetAllPlaybackState`). (4)
`RecordingGroupStore.RepairAutoGroupMembership` (group list, .sfs) runs only from the Re-Fly
discard restore of a detached tree and only when membership drifted. Not changed:
`RecordingFinalizationCacheApplier` and the `ParsekScenario.HydrationRepair.cs` sites act on the
live / loaded active tree (finalization moves `EndUT` anyway; the hydration copies are real
restores); the hydration refresh of a quickloaded resumed-tree member is a possible narrow edge
(it re-dirties a member copied from the committed copy) and is left open.

Fix: (1) `CommitTreeCore` collects, before the session merge, the route sources the incoming
tree carries unchanged (`TreeCommitService.CollectUnchangedRouteSourceIds` over
`RouteStore.CollectSourceRecordingIds`, read through `CommittedListOptimizer.CollectUnchangedRouteSourceIds`,
the type that already reads the route source set for its own pass, so no new Recording ->
Logistics layer pair; pure `IsUnchangedCommittedRecording`: neither copy dirty
nor owing an advance, and the same instance or the same epoch, `PrecHash`, vessel / ghost
snapshot hashes, start and end UT); those skip the session merge overwrite and the forced dirty in
`MergeTreeRecordingsIntoCommitted`, so memory keeps exactly the bytes on disk; one Verbose
`route sources in tree ... keptUnchanged=` summary per commit. A changed source (dirty, re-saved,
extended) and every non-source member are merged and rewritten as before. (2)-(4) no longer set
`FilesDirty` (comment at each site: .sfs metadata only). The epoch comparison stays, so a real
sidecar change still reads as SourceChanged. Tests: `RouteSourceEpochMetadataRewriteTests` (10: the re-commit
keeps sources clean and the route Active, the kept source keeps its committed lists, a changed
source still flips SourceChanged through `sidecar-epoch`, a non-source member is still rewritten,
the two predicates, the two supersede marks and the group repair); with the fix reverted 6 red.
The tenth pins that the source set never grows: after two continuations of the route's
transport are merged back into its tree, `SourceRefs`, `RecordingIds` and
`CollectSourceRecordingIds` are exactly the creation set, and the continuations stay ordinary
optimizer input (merge / split candidates; a pair with the dock leaf is held for the leaf only).
Audit: a route's source set is written only by `RouteBuilder` (creation) and `RouteCodec` (load),
and every runtime reader (ERS presence, revalidation, transport identities, the backing mission
frozen to creation members by `ComputeAutoExcludedNewIntervalKeys`) reads that fixed set, never
a later recording of the vessel; `RouteCandidateFinder` leaves a continuation analysable.
Live proof flown green 2026-11-17 (`2026-11-17_0049`, PASS attempt 1): lane `RSF-1-route-source-fixed-across-transport-reflight` on
RCN-1's host creates and activates the route, F5 / F9, takes the real transport C out again in
a NEW tree, drives C 5 s, merges, F5 / F9 again and runs the cycle; the route must stay Active
with no SourceChanged flip. It cannot re-commit the route's own tree: the host's leaf
`ec4bf428` has no spawn stamp, so a Cold FLIGHT load's crew pass
(`OnLoadPhaseAutoUnreserveCrewPastEndUT`) marks it spawned with no pid and
`TryFindCommittedTreeForSpawnedVessel` silently matches nothing. The re-commit path stays
xUnit-proven. `ListHandles kind=routes` gained `sources` / `sourceIds` / `sourceEpochs` (captured/live) /
`sourceDrift` (read-only `RouteStore.DescribeSourceState`) so the lane compares the source set
taken at creation with the one after the merge, the F9 and the cycle by regex backreference.
Known remaining case (review 2026-11-16, fails safe): `SessionMerger.MergeTree` still runs
`EnsureCheckpointSectionsForTopLevelOrbitSegments(markDirty: true)` on every member after the
unchanged set is collected, so an orbital source that lacks checkpoint sections would still be
rewritten and pause its route. It errs toward pausing, never toward replaying changed data.

## ~~PRESWITCH-CASE-C-LIVE-TREE-MEMBER~~: switching back to the ship a kerbal just left ended the recording when that ship ended an earlier committed flight [FILED 2026-11-14 from lane FAR-4's first flight, runs `2026-11-14_1525` and `_1526_a2` (INVALID driver-gate, the seam refused `dialog-required case=C-loaded-separate-committed`). FIXED 2026-11-14, branch `pc-lanes-fix`; xUnit; FAR-4 green `2026-11-14_2324`; medium]

Shape: a recording is started on a vessel that an earlier committed flight also recorded (the
committed tree's spawned leaf), a kerbal goes on EVA (the vessel becomes a background member of
the live tree), then the player switches back to it from the map. The pre-switch gate's Case C
looked the target up among committed trees, found the OLDER tree, saw its id differ from the live
tree's and called the target a separate committed vessel. With auto-merge on (every player
build: `ClampHiddenSettingsToShippingValues`) `TryAutoResolvePreSwitch` then silently merged
(or, for a no-op, discarded) the live recording and the switch restored the older committed
tree; with auto-merge off (the harness) the Merge / Discard dialog opened, and either answer
ends the live recording.
Fix: `MapFocusObjectOnSelectPatch.IsSeparateCommittedTarget` also requires that the target is not
in the live tree's `BackgroundMap` (`IsLiveTreeBackgroundMember`); the switch then takes the
ordinary background-member continuation. `SimulateStockSwitchClick`'s seam evaluator reads the
same two helpers. A skipped Case C logs one Verbose `pre-switch Case C skipped: target is a
background member of the live tree`. Tests: `PreSwitchCaseCLiveTreeMemberTests` (6 facts).
Live proof: FAR-4's second flight `2026-11-14_1638` (head 37a6c6101) read
`targetIsSeparateCommittedVessel=false dialogDecision=NoPriorSession` and
`route=bg-member-continuation`; the lane itself red only on two first-reading counts (re-pinned,
re-flight owed).

## ~~FAR1-CAREER-FIXTURE-EMBEDDED-LEDGER~~: the `duna-ike-recorded-career` host kept its SANDBOX ledger, so FAR-1's rewind patched funds up 9120 [FILED 2026-11-14 from FAR-1's second flight, run `2026-11-14_1642` PARSEK-FAIL(expectation). FIXED 2026-11-14, branch `pc-lanes-fix-2`; harness fixture builder, not a Parsek defect; FAR-1 green `2026-11-14_2321`]

`build_route_career.py` strips the SANDBOX seeds and the milestone award rows from the
`ledger.pgld` sidecar. Its sixth source, `duna-ike-recorded`, also embeds a `GAME_STATE` node
in the ParsekScenario node, and a load reads that copy (`Ledger.LoadFromNodeCore`,
`GAME_STATE/LEDGER`), so FAR-1 booted with the 12 award rows and the SANDBOX
`ScienceInitial` (science 0) still live. Readings: the boot filed adopted-gap pool adjustments
(funds -160680, science +95) and logged no `Seeded initial science: amount=100,`; after the
Rewind-to-Launch the walk topped up two older rows, `Milestone 'Orbit' topped up` at
UT 4742953.2 (6240) and 9160199.4 (2880), and `PatchFunds: 500000.0 -> 509120.0`. Those rows are
the Sun and Duna orbits captured with the bare id `Orbit` before #2301 (the same pre-1.0 shape as
CS-FIXTURES-CARRY-BARE-ORBIT-MILESTONE), so they collide with Kerbin's `Orbit` and the rewind's
timeline break lets the top-up (owner ruling 2026-11-04) pay the differences. A 1.0+ save
qualifies every body milestone, so no player save collides this way. Fix: the builder applies
the same strip to the embedded `GAME_STATE/LEDGER` (`strip_embedded_ledger`, 2 seeds and 12 award
rows out, the 6 zero-award rows kept) and `verify_sfs` refuses a leftover; the fixture is
rebuilt (`--check` OK for all six). Test: `test_route_career.test_the_embedded_ledger_gets_the_same_strip`.

## ~~POSITIONER-BODY-LOOKUP-AND-SEGMENT-INDEX-PER-FRAME-COST: every ghost allocates closures for its body lookups, and orbit ghosts box their segment list, every frame~~ [FILED 2026-11-10 from the read of the positioner InterpolateAndPosition core (refactor branch `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr` at e29de7161), by reading the source and IL. FIXED 2026-11-10, branch `refactor-w0-bodylookup`; xUnit + il_compare; performance, low]

**What is true.** `ParsekFlightGhostPositioner` looked every body up with
`FlightGlobals.Bodies.Find(b => b.name == x)` (27 sites, plus 4 `b != null && b.bodyName == x`
sites and the tail-lift terminal lookup). Each lambda captures a local or a parameter, so the
compiler hoists it into a display class allocated when its scope starts (26 `newobj
<>c__DisplayClass` in 25 methods), including the point-interpolation core that runs per frame
for every ghost. Separately, the orbit-segment path of `InterpolateAndPosition` called
`segments.IndexOf(seg.Value)` every frame for its orbit cache key; `OrbitSegment` has no
`Equals`, so the default comparer boxes each element it compares and compares fields by
reflection.

**Fix.** Each lookup goes through `ParsekFlightGhostPositioner.FindFirstMatching<T>(IList<T>, name,
matcher)`, a `List.Find` loop over a static, non-capturing matcher that keeps the replaced
lambda's predicate with the name passed as an argument (`FindBodyByName` / `FindBodyByNameOrNull`
/ `FindLiveBodyByBodyNameOrNull` keep the `.Find` versus `?.Find` null-list behavior). The orbit
path takes the index from `TrajectoryMath.FindOrbitSegmentIndex` (which `FindOrbitSegment` now
reads) and `TrajectoryMath.ResolveOrbitSegmentIndexOfFound`, which returns the found index except
at the one point where `IndexOf` can differ: the last segment repeats an earlier one field for
field and the UT is its endUT. That point still calls `IndexOf`, so the cache key is unchanged.

**Fixed.** il_compare shows no display-class `newobj` left in the positioner (26 before) and no
`IndexOf` on the per-frame path; the box-opcode count of every changed method is unchanged
(all inside the once-per-key log interpolations). `PositionerNoAllocLookupTests` pins the lookup
against `List.Find` for every matcher, name and null-entry layout, and the segment index against
`IndexOf` over 400 random lists with repeated segments.

## ~~B13-LANDER-NEVER-STATIONARY: the B13 Mun lander records Approach -> SurfaceMobile and never reaches SurfaceStationary~~ [SUPERSEDED 2026-11-10 by the fixed main entry of the same id below (#2535, merged from main). FILED 2026-11-08 from the wave-2 overnight flights (refactor branch `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr` at f28324df0, DLL sha256 bde5f2b3...), runs `2026-11-08_0139_B13-mun-landing` and re-fly `2026-11-08_0422`, both PARSEK-FAIL(expectations). OPEN; not yet placed (refactor or pre-existing), medium]

**What is true.** Both flights were MISSION-OK and every verifier but expectations was PASS or
REPORT. The one failing row is the required log contract
`Environment transition: \w+ -> SurfaceStationary at UT=`. In both flights the lander logs
`Approach -> SurfaceMobile` at about UT=23020-23024 and never a later `-> SurfaceStationary`.
`EnvironmentDetector.Classify` reads a landed vessel as SurfaceMobile while `srfSpeed > 0.1`,
so the recorder saw the lander above 0.1 m/s from touchdown to the commit. The mission's own
LANDED-SETTLE gate uses its own speed thresholds, so it can pass while the recorder still reads
Mobile. B13 last passed with `SurfaceStationary` on the 2026-11-06 full run on main.

**Not the refactor, by code reading.** No wave-2 PR between the pre-wave tip 088feb067 and
f28324df0 changed `EnvironmentDetector.cs`, the environment hysteresis or the recorder's

## ~~FLG-1-SAME-FRAME-PLANT-AND-PICKUP: FLG-1 reds when the replayed plant and pick-up land in one frame~~ [FILED 2026-11-08 from the wave-2 overnight flights (refactor branch at f28324df0), run `2026-11-08_0248_FLG-1-pickup-rewind` PARSEK-FAIL(expectations); the re-fly `2026-11-08_0442` PASSED. FIXED 2026-11-10, branch `refactor-flg1-spec` (spec only, offline-proven, not re-flown); harness (spec), low; the product end state is right]

**What is true.** The recorded plant is at ut=33.84 and the pick-up at ut=33.90, 0.06 s apart.
`GhostPlaybackLogic.ApplyFlagEvents` applies recorded pick-ups BEFORE plants by design (its
comment: a walk past both must not plant a flag only to take it down again). In the red flight
one replay frame passed both UTs: the pick-up tombstoned the spot and took down 0 flags, then
the plant was skipped with `Flag replay skipped ... removed by the player at ut=33.90`. No flag
stood afterwards, which is the ruled end state (owner ruling 2026-11-04). In the green flight the
frames split the two UTs, so the plant spawned and the pick-up took down 1 flag.

**Fix (spec).** FLG-1 requires the plant-then-take-down chain and forbids every
`Flag replay skipped` line, so it depends on frame timing. Accept either chain: the existing one,
or a pick-up line naming the same flag followed by a skip whose `removed ... at ut=` equals the
recorded pick-up UT, and keep forbidding a skip with an earlier removal UT and any second
`Spawned flag vessel` after the take-down. A cheaper alternative is to space the plant and the
pick-up further apart in the lane's act (a dwell of a few seconds before `PickUpFlag`).

**Fixed.** `harness/scenarios/FLG-1-pickup-rewind.toml` now accepts either chain after the
rewind mark: `Spawned flag vessel` then `took down 1 standing flag(s)`, or a replayed pick-up
that `took down 0` followed by `Flag replay skipped: '<same flag>' ... at ut=<the pick-up's ut>`
(regex back-references; both lines print the one double with "R", so equality is byte-equal).
Three forbidden patterns replace the old one: a skip before any replayed pick-up (the live
tombstone survived the rewind), a skip after one that names another flag, body or UT, and a
replayed plant followed by `took down 0` (the take-down missed the flag, which stays standing).
A plant after the take-down stays forbidden. Proof: 18 synthetic logs through
`hlib.evaluate_expectations` (both chains green, every other shape red); one re-fly confirms.

## ~~UNIT-MEMBER-PLAYBACK-CLOSURE-PER-FRAME: every loop-unit member allocates a closure object every frame~~ [FILED 2026-11-08 from the UpdateUnitMemberPlayback extraction (refactor branch `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr`, branch `refactor-w9a-unit-member`), by reading the IL. FIXED 2026-11-08, branch `refactor-w9a-handoff-closure`; xUnit + il_compare; performance, low]

**What is true.** The descent-handoff log in `GhostPlaybackEngine.UpdateUnitMemberPlayback`
passes a `() => ...` message lambda to `ParsekLog.VerboseRateLimited`, and that lambda captures
the parameter `i` and the local `unitCycle`. The compiler hoists both into a display class that
it allocates at method entry (`IL_0000: newobj <>c__DisplayClass_0::.ctor`), so every call
allocates one object, for every unit member on every frame, even though the lambda runs only
for a rendering non-descent member of a unit that has a descent trigger. The extraction kept
the block inline so the allocation is unchanged.

**Fix.** Move the descent-handoff block (from `bool hiddenForDescentHandoff = false;` through
its closing brace) into its own method, called only under the existing gate, so the display
class is allocated only when the lambda can run. The `UnitMember_DescentTrigger_HandoffAndLoiter`
golden in `UnitMemberPlaybackCharacterizationTests` pins the block's output.

**Fixed.** The block is now `GhostPlaybackEngine.ApplyDescentHandoffHide`, called only under the
existing `!descentMember && decision == Render && unit.HasDescentTrigger` gate, with the log text,
rate-limit key and order unchanged. `UpdateUnitMemberPlayback` no longer opens with the display
class `newobj` (il_compare); the closure is allocated only inside the new method.
`DescentHandoffHide_HidesTheTransferMemberWhileTheDescentPlays_AndPinsItsLogLine` pins both log
lines and the key.

## ~~B13-LANDER-NEVER-STATIONARY: B13 reds because the lander is still sliding when the tree commits~~ [FILED 2026-11-10 from the 1.0.1 and refactor-branch B13 reds. FIXED 2026-11-10 (owner picked "accept landed and sliding"); harness only, no Parsek defect]

- Symptom: `B13-mun-landing` MISSION-OK but PARSEK-FAIL(expectations) on `\w+ -> SurfaceStationary` (run `2026-11-09_2132`). The untargeted landing put the lander on a slope where it crept at 0.55-0.65 m/s horizontal for the whole LANDED-SETTLE window, so Parsek's `Approach -> SurfaceMobile` (srfSpeed > 0.1 m/s) was the correct reading; the 3 s Mobile/Stationary debounce never saw a still lander. Before #2391 shortened the park dwell the lander usually settled first, so the old token was a coin flip on the landing site.
- Fix: the lane no longer demands Stationary. With `landedSurfaceClassMark = true` the B5 machine measures the lander's own kRPC surface speed over the last 6 s before the commit and writes a `MISSIONMARK label=b5-landed-expect-<SurfaceStationary|SurfaceMobile|either>` (all <= 0.05 m/s parked, all >= 0.2 m/s sliding, otherwise either). The required token pairs the LAST `-> Surface*` transition before the mark with the mark, so Parsek must agree with the mission's independent speed reading: a misclassification in either clear band still reds. The `surface-stationary` D4 claim moved to RVR-21, whose required token proves it. The new `surfaceClassMarked` mission assertion fails the mission (INVALID, never PARSEK-FAIL) when the mark was not written.
- Residual: B14 pins `-> SurfaceMobile` the same way and could red if a Minmus landing ever parks perfectly still; not seen yet.

## ~~REPLACE-COPIES-DESTROYED-FLAG-ONTO-LIVE-REPLACEMENT~~: a replace commit can mark a surviving replacement destroyed and keep a stale situation [FILED 2026-11-07 from the review of the TreeCommitService unit tests (refactor branch `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr`, PR #2452), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-16, branch fix-treecommit-trio; xUnit; low]

**What is true.**
- `TreeCommitService.PreserveFinalStateDiagnosticsOnReplace` (the last cluster of
  `PreserveLiveRuntimeFieldsOnReplace`) copies each field from the committed recording onto its
  replacement when the replacement holds the default. `VesselDestroyed` defaults to false, so a
  destroyed committed recording always hands `VesselDestroyed = true` to its replacement, even
  when the replacement flew on and survived.
- The guard on `SceneExitSituation` reads `!incoming.VesselDestroyed` BEFORE that copy and the
  guard on `VesselSituation` reads it AFTER, so with existing `VesselDestroyed=true,
  SceneExitSituation=2` and a default replacement the result is `VesselDestroyed=true`,
  `SceneExitSituation=2`, `VesselSituation=null`: destroyed, with a live situation code.
- `MarkDestroyedAtTerminal` clears both situation fields on the destroyed side, so the mixed
  result needs a destroyed recording that still carries a situation code. Whether a Re-Fly
  replace can hand a destroyed committed copy to a surviving replacement is not established.

**Fix.** Decide whether `VesselDestroyed` should copy at all onto a replacement whose own
terminal is not Destroyed (the spawn claim already refuses a vesselless terminal the same way),
and read the destroyed state once before the cluster so both situation guards agree. The unit
tests in `TreeCommitServiceUnitTests` cover each field alone and do not pin the mixed case.

Fix: `TreeCommitService.ShouldCopyDestroyedFlagOnReplace` copies `VesselDestroyed` only when the
replacement's own `TerminalStateValue` is unset or Destroyed (a set terminal that is not
Destroyed is the replacement's verdict that the vessel did not die; an Info line names the
refusal). `PreserveFinalStateDiagnosticsOnReplace` decides the destroyed state the replacement
ends with once, before any copy, and both situation guards read it, so a copied flag never sits
beside a copied situation. Tests: `PreserveFinalStateDiagnostics_DestroyedCopyOntoUnterminatedReplacement_SituationsAgree`,
`PreserveFinalStateDiagnostics_SurvivingReplacementNotMarkedDestroyed`,
`ShouldCopyDestroyedFlagOnReplace_ByReplacementTerminal`.

## ~~TREE-START-UT-EMPTY-RECORDING-READS-ZERO~~: one empty recording pulls a continuation tree's start to UT 0 [FILED 2026-11-07 from the same review, by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-16, branch fix-treecommit-trio; xUnit; low]

**What is true.** `TreeCommitService.GetTreeStartUT` takes the minimum `Recording.StartUT` over
the tree, and `StartUT` reads 0.0 for a recording with no trajectory and no explicit start. One
such recording makes the tree start at 0, so the contiguity half of
`ShouldMarkSupersededTerminalSpawn` (`continuationTreeStartUT > prior.EndUT + 1e-3`) never
rejects and only the same-launch / same-name test and the prior-end-before-continuation-start
test stand between an unrelated later tree and a terminal spawn supersede mark.

**Fix.** Skip recordings without trajectory bounds or an explicit start in `GetTreeStartUT`
(NaN when none is left), with a unit test beside the existing `GetTreeStartUT_*` cells.

Fix: `GetTreeStartUT` skips a recording with neither `TryGetActualTrajectoryBounds` nor an
`ExplicitStartUT` and returns NaN when none is left. Its one caller,
`MarkSupersededTerminalSpawnsForContinuedSources`, logs a Verbose line for a NaN tree start;
`ShouldMarkSupersededTerminalSpawn` already refuses the contiguity branch on NaN (fails closed),
so only the spawned-pid match can mark such a tree. Tests:
`GetTreeStartUT_SkipsRecordingWithNoTrajectoryAndNoExplicitStart`,
`GetTreeStartUT_TrajectoryOnlyRecordingCounts`, `GetTreeStartUT_OnlyEmptyRecordings_NaN`,
`MarkSupersededForContinuedSources_EmptyRecordingDoesNotPullTreeStartToZero` (marked before the
fix), `MarkSupersededForContinuedSources_NoStartedRecording_LogsAndKeepsPidMatch`.

## TRACE-SEP-DEBRIS-ROW-MISREPORTS: the PositionDebris trace row can blame playback math or the recorder for a diagnostic artifact [FILED 2026-11-07 from the review of the ghost positioner unit tests (refactor branch `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr`, PR #2457), by code reading. OPEN; trace-only (`ghostRenderTracing`), low]

**What is true.** `ParsekFlightGhostPositioner.TraceDebrisBodyFixedPrimaryPlayback` (the Trace-Sep
`PositionDebris` row, moved verbatim out of `TryPositionFromBodyFixedPrimary`):
- `predictedWorld` stays `Vector3d.zero` when the bracket is one-sided (playback past the last
  body-fixed frame) or the body does not resolve, so `predictedVsActual` / `|predDelta|` log the
  ghost's whole world position, which the row's own triage rule reads as a playback-math defect.
- `recordedBodyFixedDist` subtracts the parent's last body-fixed sample at or before the playback
  UT from the debris bracket's before-frame without matching their UTs (a 0.9 s skew at orbital
  speed is about 1.8 km), resolves the parent sample on the debris sample's body, and
  `FindLastBodyFixedFrameAtOrBefore` takes the qualifying sample of the LAST section in list order
  rather than the latest by UT.

**Fix.** Log `predictedWorld` / `predDelta` as unresolved when no two-sided bracket resolved, and
compute the parent sample at the debris before-frame's UT on the parent's own body (or log the
two UTs side by side). Flight behaviour is unaffected; only the trace row is misleading.

## ~~SWITCH-SEGMENT-DISCARD-TOPOLOGY-RESIDUE~~: the scoped switch-segment Discard leaves three things the committed-tree prune repairs [FILED 2026-11-07 from the review of the discard-service unit tests (refactor branch `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr`, PR #2454), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-16, branch fix-treecommit-trio; xUnit; low]

**What is true.** `SwitchSegmentAttempts.TryDiscardActiveSwitchSegmentAttempt` (pending-tree-prune
disposition) removes the segment subtree from the tree it lives in, but unlike
`TreeDiscardService.PruneTaggedRecordingsFromTree` it:
- never calls `RecordingTree.RebuildBackgroundMap`, so `BackgroundMap` / `RecordedVesselPids` can
  keep a pid of a removed background-recorded child until something else rebuilds them;
- repairs a stale `ActiveRecordingId` (to the session parent or null) but never a stale
  `RootRecordingId`;
- with a null `PreSessionBranchPointIds` baseline (unknown, treated as "authored nothing") keeps
  the session's branch points after their child lists were scrubbed empty, and the parent's
  `ChildBranchPointId` still names them (the committed prune drops a branch point with an empty
  side).

None is known to reach a player: the pending tree is usually committed or dropped next, and the
background map is rebuilt on load. The unit tests in `DiscardServicesUnitTests` cover the
helpers as they are and pin none of the three.

**Fix.** After the removal, rebuild the background map, reset a stale root the way the active id
is reset, and drop branch points left with an empty side (reuse
`TreeDiscardService.ScrubBranchPointEndpointsAndDropEmpty` + `ClearRecordingBranchPointRefs`,
keeping the switch-segment restore of an overwritten continuing link). Each needs a unit cell.

Fix: after the removal, `TryDiscardActiveSwitchSegmentAttempt` runs
`SwitchSegmentAttempts.DropBranchPointsLeftEmptyAfterSegmentDiscard` (the committed prune's
empty-side drop rule, logged, SCOPED: only a branch point that named a removed recording before
the removal scrubbed the endpoint lists, read by `CollectBranchPointIdsNamingRecordings`, may be
dropped; a pre-existing branch point that already had an empty side, such as a focused breakup
whose debris all failed `ShouldRecordDebris`, stays untouched and the parent's overwritten link
to it is restored; the committed prune `TreeDiscardService.ScrubBranchPointEndpointsAndDropEmpty`
keeps dropping every empty-sided branch point and is not called from SwitchIntent, because a
direct SwitchIntent -> TreeDiscardService call raised the semantic cut residue from 124 to 140),
feeds the session-authored
plus dropped ids to `RepairBranchPointLinksAfterSegmentDiscard` (which plays
`ClearRecordingBranchPointRefs`'s role and keeps the overwritten-continuing-link restore),
resets a removed active AND root id through `RepairActiveAndRootAfterSegmentDiscard` (parent if
it survives, else null), and ends with `RebuildBackgroundMap` (pure over the tree, safe headless).
Tests: `DiscardServicesUnitTests.DropBranchPointsLeftEmpty_*` (including
`KeepsAlreadyEmptyBranchNamingNoRemovedRecording`),
`CollectBranchPointIdsNamingRecordings_EmptyOrNullInputs_Empty`,
`RepairActiveAndRootAfterSegmentDiscard_ResetsRemovedRootToParent`, and end to end
`SwitchSegmentDiscardScopeTests.Discard_RemovedBackgroundChild_LeavesBackgroundMap`,
`Discard_RemovedRootRecording_ResetsRootToSessionParent`,
`Discard_UnknownBaseline_DropsEmptiedContinuationBranch`,
`Discard_PreSessionEmptyBreakupBranch_SurvivesAndParentLinkRestored` (known and unknown
baseline; mutation-checked: dropping every empty-sided branch point reds both rows).

## ~~LOOP-SEAM-TRACE-INDEX-NOT-SHIFTED: two loop-seam trace dictionaries in ParsekFlight are keyed by committed index and never shift~~ [FILED 2026-11-07 from the ParsekFlight seam inventory (`plan-parsekflight-seams-2026-11-07.md`, refactor branch `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr` at f3400b90a), by code reading. FIXED 2026-11-07, branch `refactor-loopseam-index-shift` (base `claude/project-thread-bkwmrr`); xUnit; diagnostics only, low]

**What is true.**
- `ParsekFlight.reaimLastGhostFrame` and `ParsekFlight.loopSeamLastGhostFrame` are
  `Dictionary<int, ...>` keyed by the loop member's committed-list index (written by the
  re-aim seam trace and `TrackLoopSeamTeleport`, read on the next frame to log a seam jump).
- `OnCommittedRecordingRemoved` / `OnCommittedRecordingInserted` shift or clear every other
  index-keyed slot (engine, held ghosts, map presence, watch mode, orbit caches, the two
  `loggedOrbit*` sets) but neither of these, and nothing clears them at a scene change other
  than the MonoBehaviour going away.
- Effect: after a mid-list insert or removal, a member's first seam check compares against the
  previous frame of the recording that used to hold its index, so a `ReaimSeam` /
  loop-seam teleport line can report a jump that never happened (or miss one). Both are gated
  diagnostics (`ghostRenderTracing` for the loop-seam instrument, Verbose for `ReaimSeam`);
  nothing a player sees and no positioning reads them.

**Fix.** The dictionaries now live on `ParsekFlightGhostPositioner` and shift with the list
instead of being cleared: `ShiftLoopSeamTracesAfterDelete` / `ShiftLoopSeamTracesAfterInsert`
run both through `IndexShift.DictAfterDelete` / `DictAfterInsert` (delete drops the removed index
and moves higher keys down; insert moves keys at or above the index up and leaves the slot
empty), and log one Verbose `[Flight] Loop-seam traces reindexed after delete|insert at #N:` line
with per-dictionary shifted / dropped / count values. `ParsekFlight.OnCommittedRecordingRemoved` /
`OnCommittedRecordingInserted` call them right after `Positioner.ClearOrbitPlaybackCaches()`; no
service subscribes to the seam. Tests: `LoopSeamTraceIndexShiftTests` (delete, insert, log line,
empty no-op) and the call order pinned in
`CommittedListNotificationTests.FlightHandlers_StayOnParsekFlight_InOrder_AndNoServiceListensOrWrites`.
Not flown; the loop lanes that exercise the traces are listed in the PR.

Converters are exercised only through a FuelCell (H38, GS-6); drill and ISRU ghosts are built

docked-origin route across a rewind; a live-drill harvest-origin route; GS-6 revision 3 with an

(HARVEST-ROUTE-PLAUSIBILITY-CAP) and ledger resource-scan unlocks (RESOURCE-SCAN-UNLOCKS-NOT-LEDGERED).

## HARNESS-LEDGER-ORACLE-ROUTES-AND-REWIND: the ledger oracle knows no route actions and refuses every rewind lane [FILED 2026-10-06 for the logistics integration program (C1), branch `ccr-77f23eb2-dbqh6i`. OPEN, harness]

`harness/lib/oracle.py` models no route action types, and `hlib.validate_spec` refuses an
`[expectations.ledger]` block on any lane that rewinds (`InvokeRewind`, `InvokeRewindToLaunch`;
the L4 deferral, `hlib.py` around the ledger-expectation validator). Route funds are therefore
pinned only by log tokens (RVR-4 `DispatchDebit ... cost=7410`), and no lane can assert that a
rewind retired exactly the route rows after its cutoff.

Fix: add the route action types (dispatch debit, recovery credit, delivery, pickup) to the
oracle's expected model, and a rewind-cutoff model (rows strictly after the cutoff retired,
dormant routes, re-delivery exactly once) so route lanes can carry a gating ledger block.
Roadmap: "The logistics integration program", row C1.

Rewind half DONE 2026-10-17 (branch `claude/career-rewind-ledger-tlmab9`, TC-4): a ledger block
that declares `timeline = "rewind-aware"` may pair with `InvokeRewind`, `InvokeRewindToLaunch`
and `AnswerMergeDialog`. `oracle.compute_expected_rewind_aware` places every entry against the
produced save's clock (careerSave `universalTime`, analyzer version 5) and expects the design 3.9
AVAILABLE funds and science (running balance floored by every projected future balance, earnings
before spendings at one UT) and the running reputation; `attempt` + `retiredAttempts` drop rows
a Re-Fly tombstone retired, `onceKey` credits a milestone once. A missing clock is
INVALID(tooling), a window straddling the clock a hard `timeline-unplaceable` divergence. Cells:
`test_oracle.RewindAwareTimelineTests`, `test_ledger_timeline.py`, `LedgerGroundTruthParserTests`,
`ReportWriterTests`. Lane `L8-career-repeated-rewinds` (three Rewind-to-Launch on a career with
KSC spending, two recovered flights, LedgerGroundTruth after the third rewind) is authored; its
first reading run (`2026-10-17_0632`) was INVALID on driver gaps, now fixed: `InvokeRewindToLaunch`
runs from the Space Center as well as FLIGHT (`VerbSceneRequirement.RequiresRewindScene`, deferring
`not-in-rewind-scene` elsewhere), a `KscAction upgrade-facility` that stock did not apply reads
`upgrade-not-applied` and only a refusal by Parsek's guard reads `blocked-committed`
(`FacilityUpgradePatch.BlockedUpgradeCount`), and the lane commits each pad flight before
recovering it. The second flight (`2026-10-17_0700`) found HIRE-RECALC-BEFORE-STOCK-DEBIT; the
third, `2026-10-17_0930`, PASSED attempt 1 with the produced pools equal to the oracle's
(funds 216769, science 90, rep 0 at end clock 199.87). Still open: the route action types.
Update 2026-10-21 (LOGISTICS-WITHOUT-MONEY phase 2, branch `logistics-no-money-p2`): route events
are no longer ledger rows and routes move no funds, so the route half has nothing left to model in
the ledger oracle; a route-cutoff check would read the route event log (`ROUTE_EVENT_LOG`) instead.
Left open for the operator to close or re-scope.

## HARNESS-POST-FLIGHT-DIALOG-STALLS: harness runs sit behind KSP's post-flight screens until a timeout or the wall budget ends [FILED 2026-10-03, branch `todo-stuck-dialogs`. CONFIRMED in the collected logs; observability done on branch `post-flight-dialog-logging`; the paused-clock watchdog, the seam active-vessel-loss fail-fast and the CommitTree fast reject FIXED 2026-10-03, branch `harness-dialog-stalls`; the frozen-telemetry item FIXED 2026-10-04, branch `frozen-detector-fix`; the RB-1 chute-read item FIXED 2026-10-06, branch `harness-overhead`]

Operator observation: auto tests sometimes sit on the post-flight "Mission Summary" screen.
A scan of all 894 collected `_shots/KSP.log` files found two stock dialogs, neither of which
Parsek, `run.py` or the seam detects or dismisses (the old FlightResults patch is gone;
`UiAction op=dismiss` reaches only Parsek popups; `mission_runner.py` `_warp_watchdog`
clears a pause only while a warp is running). In every case something else held the run.

- **Crash screen (`FlightResultsDialog`, "Outcome: Catastrophic Failure!") pauses the game.**
  Stock `FlightLogger` opens it about 60 s after the active vessel's root part is destroyed.
  It calls `FlightDriver.SetPause(true)`, so `timeScale` is 0. KSP.log marker:
  `Game State Saved to saves/<x>/persistent` followed within about 10 ms by `Game Paused!`.
  The seam's `StockScreen` VAB open makes the same pair but unpauses within 0.1 s; exclude it.
  - RB-1 `2026-09-27_1353` (PARSEK-FAIL batch-crashed): the Flea crashed on descent, which
    the lane never intends. `Game Paused!` at 16:56:51, `Game Unpaused!` at 17:15:41: about
    1,130 s on the crash screen, 1,337 s wall against 410-422 s for passing runs. Nothing
    tripped earlier because every phase budget is game time and `mlib` `advances_frozen`
    deliberately ignores a stopped clock, so the mission polled frozen telemetry until its
    wall budget ran out.
  - EVA-8 x6 (2026-09-29, INVALID): Jeb died just after a seam `evagroundscience step move`.
    The pending two-phase step waited out its 120 s `step-timeout`, about half of it with the
    crash screen up. This was a lane-development defect; the lane passes since `_1819`.
- **KSC recovery screen (`MissionRecoveryDialog`, "Mission Summary for <vessel>").**
  The marker is the stock `[VesselRecovery]: ... recovered` line. 22 runs in 9 lanes, median
  1.7 s to the next scene. In 7 of them (L3 x5, L5, L6 x2) it stayed about 62 s, while the
  post-mission `CommitTree` was deferred `not-in-flight` until its 60 s timeout. That timeout
  is measured and non-gating by design in `L3-career-science-recover.toml`; the dialog is a
  bystander.

Lost: about 26 min with a dialog up, about 25 min of it avoidable (RB-1 is about 19 min).

- [x] Mission shell: an always-on paused-clock watchdog. If game time has not advanced for
  about 15 wall s while `krpc.paused` is true, with no seam step in flight, end the mission
  as vessel lost rather than waiting out the wall budget. This would have saved about
  1,100 s on RB-1.
  Fix: pure `mlib.paused_clock_step` (one debounced wall window: an unbroken run of polls
  with UT unchanged AND `KRPC.Paused` true lasting `PAUSED_CLOCK_WALL_SECONDS = 15`), fed
  every poll by `mission_runner._fly_loop_body`. A trip ends the mission through
  `mlib.paused_clock_terminal`: `MISSION-ASSERT-FAIL` with a `vessel-lost (paused-clock:
  ...)` reason, the class every machine's own vessel-lost terminal uses (INVALID(mission),
  retried once). A state with no `loss_reason` field (M3 only) gets a named `MISSION-FLAKE`
  so its frozen telemetry is never graded. Exempt, re-arming the watch: a running native
  warp (`_warp_watchdog` owns pauses then), the poll after any seam action (perform()
  blocks for the whole step), a machine state declaring `game_pause_owned` (no mission
  pauses the game; grep found no pause writer but `_warp_watchdog`'s unpause), an unread
  pause state, a non-finite UT. Not scoped to airborne phases: the seam exemption already
  keeps scene-straddling verbs out, and a pause this long is a stall in any phase. The pause
  RPC is issued only on a poll whose UT did not move. Log: `gate paused-clock armed` /
  `cleared` at Info, `gate paused-clock TRIP | frozenUt= pausedFor= limit=` at Warn. On
  RB-1 it would have tripped about 15.5 s after `Game Paused!` (16:57:07 instead of the
  wall reaper at about 17:15). Tests: `test_mlib.PausedClockWatchdogTests`,
  `test_shells.PausedClockWatchdogShellTests` / `KrpcPausedClockSeamTests`.
- [x] RB-1 also shows the frozen-telemetry detector NOT firing: from the crash (UT 98.72)
  to the pause (UT 157.86) UT advanced at 1x for about 60 s while the logged altitude,
  vertical speed, apoapsis and periapsis stayed identical to 3 decimals, yet B1's
  10-sample limit (inside `sbr_decide`) never tripped. Replaying the logged 3-decimal
  values trips at sample 11 and the sibling RB-2 `2026-09-27_1417` (same code) tripped
  live, so a sub-millimetre difference in one of the four fields kept resetting the count.
  Fix: three changes to the shared `mlib._advance_frozen_count`. (1) A poll whose UT did
  not strictly advance HOLDS the count, as a warp frame already did: a repeated or
  non-finite UT keeps the signature, a lower UT (load, rewind) re-baselines it. A stopped
  clock still never increments, so the paused-clock watchdog keeps sole ownership of a
  pause. (2) The airborne hop machines compare the four fields within a tolerance: new
  missionParams key `frozenToleranceAbs`, defaulting to `HOP_FROZEN_TOLERANCE_ABS = 1e-3`
  in the B1 (and so SBR), EVA-4, GS-1 and B4 params builders, NaN never matching; B4
  applies it only in REENTRY / SPLASHDOWN (`B4_FROZEN_TOLERANCE_PHASES`). Every orbit
  machine (B2 / R1, B5 / V1, B-DOCK, FORGE-LKO, KXRW) keeps the exact compare: near an
  apsis of a near-circular orbit a live craft can sit inside 1e-3 per poll. (3)
  Observability: the machine line and status dict now read the counter off a delegated
  sub-machine (`frozenCount=` was `-` on SBR, R1, V1 and S/R/T-DOCK), and the fly loop logs
  one `frozen-telemetry reset count=N->0 field=<f> <f>=<prev repr>-><curr repr> dUt= warp=
  tol=` line when a run of 1 or more breaks, plus a `frozen-telemetry within-tolerance`
  line when a tolerant machine counts a poll that was not bit-identical (capped at
  `FROZEN_NOTE_LIMIT = 20` per flight; silent on a healthy flight). The jittering field is
  still UNPROVEN: the logs print 3 decimals. The next crash names it in those lines.
  Tests: `test_frozen_detector.py`.
- [x] ~~RB-1's chute channel read nothing useful: of the 1,261 telemetry lines, 1,254 print
  `chute=-` and 7 `chute=Stowed`, and the Flea hit at about 230 m/s.~~ Cause: the fixture made
  kRPC read a clone's parts (fixed by 5ab868f0a); the arm logged `on 0 parachute(s)` and the
  chute never armed. Fixed 2026-10-06, branch `harness-overhead`: B1 / SBR / EVA-4 end the
  mission before the arm when the chute read returns nothing on the DESCENT-entry poll and
  the one before it (`mlib.chute_unobservable_at_descent`, `MISSION-ASSERT-FAIL` reason
  `chute unobservable (part identity?)`, INVALID(mission)), and `deploy_chute` logs
  `deployed N parachute(s)`. Over the 26 collected flights of these lanes it trips on RB-1
  and both RB-2 attempts (same defect) and on no other.
- [x] Seam: a two-phase pending step fails fast when the active vessel is destroyed or
  `FlightResultsDialog.isDisplaying`, instead of waiting its full timeout
  (`ParsekTestCommandAddon.EvaGroundScience.cs` step-move path first). Also log the
  dialog's display and the active-vessel loss so a scan can find the next case.
  Fix: one shared guard on the two-phase completion poll
  (`ParsekTestCommandAddon.ActiveVesselLoss.cs`, pure decision
  `TestCommandActiveVesselLoss`). A watched verb (`EvaGroundScience`, `PlantFlag`) captures
  the active vessel when it goes PENDING; each completion poll checks it before the verb's
  own completion and ends the step `ERROR active-vessel-lost` with one Warn line
  (`active-vessel lost id= cmd= vessel= pid= state=dead|destroyed elapsed=`). Lost means
  Unity-null OR `Vessel.State.DEAD`: decompiled `Vessel.Die` leaves the dead ACTIVE vessel in
  place, which is why the old `kerbal == null` check never fired and each EVA-8 run sat out
  the full 120 s. The kerbal's death precedes the crash dialog by about 60 s, so no dialog
  check is needed to fail fast; logging the dialog belongs to the observability item below
  and to game-side PR #1992. EvaChuteDeploy keeps its own debounced `eva-chute-kerbal-lost`;
  EvaBoard / EvaExit / scene-leaving verbs / WarpToUT are not watched. Saves about 120 s on
  each of the six EVA-8 runs. Tests: `TestCommandActiveVesselLossTests`.
- [x] Recovery-screen class: `CommitTree` returns a fast `REJECTED not-in-flight` in
  SPACECENTER instead of deferring 60 s, or L3 / L5 / L6 drop that step. L3 keeps the step
  verbatim as a tripwire, so its `expect` must change with it. Saves about 60 s on each of
  those runs (SE-1 hits the same deferral).
  Fix: option (a). `TestCommandDispatcher.RejectOutsideFlightVerbs` = {`CommitTree`}: in a
  settled non-FLIGHT scene it answers `REJECTED not-in-flight` at once; every other FLIGHT
  verb keeps its defer. A pending scene load still defers `not-safe-point` above the scene
  check (the transition flag is set synchronously by any load request, kRPC included), and
  the FIFO head blocks every other seam verb, so no deferral could bridge into FLIGHT. Caller
  audit: 38 specs drive CommitTree as a step (previous step StopRecording x20, the mission
  phase x15, WarpToUT x3) plus in-mission seam calls from the mission shells; across all 217
  collected runs that sent it, 213 dispatched straight to OK with no defer and all 10 that
  deferred `not-in-flight` ended TIMEOUT (L3 x5, L5, L6 x2, SE-1 x2), none executing after a
  defer. L3 / L5 / both L6 lanes now expect `REJECTED`. SE-1 needs no change: its two
  deferrals came after an upstream `LaunchFromEditor` failure left the run outside FLIGHT,
  which now rejects fast too. Tests: `TestCommandDispatchTests.CommitTree_*`.
- [x] Seam budgets that only ever paid out on failure: `EvaGroundScience` 120 s -> 60 s and
  `AnswerMergeDialog` 120 s -> 60 s (2026-10-06, branch `seam-timeout-budgets`). Measured
  over 859 collected runs (2026-09-10 to 2026-10-05): EvaGroundScience OK n=412, p99 5.5 s,
  max 5.5 s, its 37 timeouts all at the full 120 s (4,440 s); AnswerMergeDialog OK n=65,
  p99 6.6 s, max 7.2 s, its 6 non-OK outcomes all at 120 s. Rule: max(4 x OK max, 30 s),
  except EvaGroundScience at 60 s because its place ladder counts frames (about 1,000
  worst case, inside 60 s down to ~17 fps); AnswerMergeDialog's floor is twice its 30 s re-fly resume-settle fallback. The hlib
  `DISPATCH_DEFERRAL_BUDGET_SECONDS` mirror moved with them. Other verbs whose failures
  all sat at the budget while OK max was under a quarter of it: `StopRecording` (2 at the
  60 s default, OK max 0.1 s) and `TrackingStationRecover` (2 at 120 s, OK max 3.6 s, only 5
  OK samples); left unchanged (the default bounds a scene-settle defer for every verb, and
  5 samples are too few). `CommitTree` (10 at 60 s) is already fixed above. Tests:
  `TestCommandDeferralBudgetTests.MeasuredBudgets_ArePinned`.
- [x] ~~Observability: subscribe to `onGUIRecoveryDialogSpawn` / `Despawn` and log the crash
  dialog. Neither dialog logs its own close today, so a stall longer than about 62 s on the
  recovery screen cannot be confirmed from logs.~~ Fix: `PostFlightDialogLog` (pure state and
  formatting) writes four Info lines under the `[PostFlightDialog]` subsystem, each with the
  scene and the vessel name in quotes (`"?"` when unknown):
  `FlightResultsDialog shown: scene=FLIGHT vessel="..." paused=true exitControls=true outcome="..."`,
  `FlightResultsDialog dismissed: scene=... vessel="..." via=Close|Destroyed onScreenWallSeconds=N.NN paused=...`,
  `MissionRecoveryDialog shown: scene=SPACECENTER vessel="..."` and
  `MissionRecoveryDialog dismissed: scene=... vessel="..." onScreenWallSeconds=N.NN` (`unknown`
  for a dialog that opened before the subscription). Wall seconds come from
  `Time.realtimeSinceStartup` and format culture-invariant. `exitControls=true` is the crash
  screen; `false` is the F3 flight status screen, which is the same stock dialog. The flight
  results feed is three Harmony postfixes (`Patches/FlightResultsDialogLogPatches.cs` on
  `Display(string)`, `Close()` and the private `OnDestroy()`, since that dialog has no
  GameEvent); the recovery feed is `PostFlightDialogLogHost`, a process-lifetime addon on
  stock `onGUIRecoveryDialogSpawn` / `onGUIRecoveryDialogDespawn` plus
  `onVesselRecoveryProcessing` for the vessel name (stock fires the spawn inside the dialog's
  Awake, before the name is set). No harness cell reads these lines yet.

## HARNESS-FLIGHT-WALL-TIME: auto-flights spend ~40% of their mission wall time idle at 1x [FILED 2026-10-01, branch `flight-efficiency`. MEASURED; the warp-policy fix is a separate session]

MEASURED 2026-10-12/13 (daily + operator tiers on main `7cbe594c0`, 181 lanes, 189 attempt runs):
12.1 h of wall. Longest: B20 4,655 s, B21 3,045 s, B19 2,950 s, V24W 2,868 s, B22 2,247 s, B30
1,763 s, B16 1,536 s, BDOCK-2 1,299 s. Daily lanes are boot-bound (kspBoot ~24 s mean, KSPCF
FastLoader and the ModuleManager cache already active; preLaunch ~6 s, verifiers ~8 s). Operator
mission wall 34,927 s: idle at 1x 9,895 s, recoverable 4,640 s (low-warp 2,144 s, of which B20's
coast 1,315 s; waiting-for-node 1,963 s, of which the B19 / B20 / B21 park round-out ~1,773 s,
tried and dropped below), by design 6,064 s.

`harness/tools/flight_efficiency.py` (pure core `harness/lib/flighteff.py`, contract in its
docstring and `harness/README.md` "Flight efficiency") now measures where a run's wall time
goes. Over the 2026-10-01 nightly runs 39% of mission wall was 1x with a static orbit outside
the atmosphere; over all 165 mission runs in every worktree's results, 38%. The largest
recoverable causes: MechJeb NodeExecutor node waits (B11 CAPTURE-BURN ~600 s, TRANSFER-BURN
30-100 s on most B lanes, BDOCK RENDEZVOUS; with autowarp on, the executor warps only to
600 s before ignition and then holds 1x until the craft is within 1 deg AND turning slower
than 0.001 rad/s, decompiled MechJeb2 2.15.1 `StateWarpAlign` / `AlignedAndSettled`), the
1x PARK dwells (`parkDwellSeconds` of game time, ~170 s each, 1x by design so the recording
carries parked coverage), B4's DEORBIT retrograde slew at 1x
(~340 s per run; `apErr` is the autopilot pointing error, so rails warp cannot help it), and
the m3 HOLD-* observation windows (deliberate). The mission warp policy itself is being
changed in a separate session; re-run the tool over the next nightly to measure that fix.
